full_output.paper_title: A single membrane-embedded negative charge is critical for recognizing positively charged drugs by the Escherichia coli multidrug resistance protein MdfA.

mutations_found.validated_by: drug resistance assays and transport experiments

mdfA.notes: The E26K mutation abolishes resistance to positively charged drugs but retains chloramphenicol resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the glutamate residue at position 26 (E26) in the MdfA protein is crucial for recognizing and transporting positively charged drugs, while the E26K mutation affects this functionality.
full_output.methodology: The study used site-directed mutagenesis, drug resistance assays, and transport experiments to investigate the role of the E26 residue in MdfA-mediated drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Efflux-mediated aminoglycoside and macrolide resistance in Burkholderia pseudomallei.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the AmrAB-OprA multidrug efflux system in Burkholderia pseudomallei, which is responsible for aminoglycoside and macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis and susceptibility testing were used to identify the AmrAB-OprA efflux system.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activities of cephalosporins and quinolones against 195 strains of Escherichia coli isolated from diarrheic dairy calves, revealing varying levels of resistance to certain antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the agar dilution method according to NCCLS guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Use of an isogenic Escherichia coli panel to design tests for discrimination of beta-lactamase functional groups of Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various beta-lactamase genes in an isogenic E. coli panel to differentiate between functional groups of beta-lactamases in Enterobacteriaceae, identifying cefpodoxime and ceftazidime as effective agents for distinguishing between group 1 and group 2 beta-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution tests were used to assess the susceptibility of E. coli strains expressing different beta-lactamases to various beta-lactam antibiotics, including cefpodoxime, ceftazidime, cefotaxime, ceftriaxone, aztreonam, cefoxitin, and cefotetan, with and without beta-lactamase inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic analysis of the Serratia marcescens N28b O4 antigen gene cluster.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the Serratia marcescens N28b O4 antigen gene cluster, which includes genes involved in the biosynthesis of the O4 antigen. Key genes identified are wbbL, rmlD, rmlC, wzm, wzt, and wbbA, which are involved in dTDP-rhamnose biosynthesis, rhamnosyltransferase activity, and O-antigen export.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, DNA sequencing, and functional studies in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Mutational analysis of active-site residues of the enterococcal D-ala-D-Ala dipeptidase VanX and comparison with Escherichia coli D-ala-D-Ala ligase and D-ala-D-Ala carboxypeptidase VanY.

VanX.notes: Mutations in VanX affect substrate recognition and transition state stabilization.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies key residues in VanX involved in substrate recognition and transition state stabilization through mutagenesis experiments.
full_output.methodology: Mutagenesis and kinetic analysis of VanX mutants.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports an extremely high incidence of macrolide and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole resistance among clinical isolates of Streptococcus pneumoniae in Taiwan.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using agar dilution and disk diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: DNA Banding Pattern Polymorphism in Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcus faecium and Criteria for Defining Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates DNA banding pattern polymorphism in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREM) and establishes criteria for defining strains based on banding pattern similarities.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE), ribotyping, plasmid profile analysis, biotyping, pyrolysis mass spectrometry, and antibiogram analysis to examine genetic diversity among VREM isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibilities and plasmid contents of Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from commercial sex workers in Dhaka, Bangladesh: emergence of high-level resistance to ciprofloxacin.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA were associated with ciprofloxacin resistance.

parC.notes: Mutations in parC were associated with ciprofloxacin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the emergence of high-level resistance to ciprofloxacin in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from commercial sex workers in Dhaka, Bangladesh, with mutations in the gyrA and parC genes contributing to this resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using disk diffusion and agar dilution methods, and plasmid profiles were analyzed.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes a novel iron transport system, sit, encoded within the centisome 63 pathogenicity island of Salmonella typhimurium. This system is capable of complementing the growth defect of an enterobactin-deficient E. coli strain in iron-restricted medium, suggesting its role in iron uptake.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular cloning, DNA sequencing, and functional assays to identify and characterize the sit operon, including its ability to complement the growth defect of an E. coli strain in iron-restricted conditions.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pncA as a critical gene for pyrazinamide (PZA) resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Mutations in pncA lead to PZA resistance, while functional pncA allows PZA conversion to pyrazinoic acid (POA), which is essential for PZA's antibacterial activity. M. smegmatis exhibits high POA efflux, contributing to its intrinsic PZA resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, mutational studies, and functional complementation experiments were conducted to investigate PZA resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: A periplasmic D-alanyl-D-alanine dipeptidase in the gram-negative bacterium Salmonella enterica.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a periplasmic d-Ala-d-Ala dipeptidase, PcgL, in Salmonella enterica, which hydrolyzes d-Ala-d-Ala and is regulated by the PhoP-PhoQ system. The gene pcgL is specific to Salmonella and was likely acquired via horizontal gene transfer.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, enzymatic activity assays, and sequence analysis were used to characterize the PcgL protein and its function.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations That Confer Resistance to 2-Deoxyglucose Reduce the Specific Activity of Hexokinase from Myxococcus xanthus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hex1 and hex3 mutations in Myxococcus xanthus that confer resistance to 2-deoxyglucose by reducing the specific activity of a soluble hexokinase.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis and enzymatic assays to characterize hexokinase activity and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro and in vivo antibacterial activities of a novel glycylcycline, the 9-t-butylglycylamido derivative of minocycline (GAR-936).
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the in vitro and in vivo antibacterial activities of TBG-MINO, a novel glycylcycline, against various tetracycline-resistant strains, including those with tet(A), tet(B), tet(C), tet(D), tet(K), and tet(M) resistance determinants.
full_output.methodology: In vitro susceptibility testing and in vivo efficacy studies in mice.

full_output.paper_title: Exposure to metronidazole in vivo readily induces resistance in Helicobacter pylori and reduces the efficacy of eradication therapy in mice.

rdxA.notes: The rdxA gene was identified as being involved in metronidazole resistance through mutational inactivation.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that exposure to metronidazole in vivo readily induces resistance in Helicobacter pylori, and prior exposure to metronidazole is associated with failure of eradication therapy. Mutational inactivation of the rdxA gene was linked to metronidazole resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used a mouse model to investigate the development of metronidazole resistance in H. pylori and evaluated the efficacy of eradication therapy.

blaIMP.validation_method: overexpression and purification of the enzyme, biochemical characterization

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the IMP-1 metallo-beta-lactamase produced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa 101/1477, which was overexpressed in Escherichia coli and showed broad-spectrum activity against various beta-lactam antibiotics, excluding monobactams.
full_output.methodology: Overexpression of the blaIMP gene in E. coli, purification of the enzyme, and biochemical characterization of its activity against various beta-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Mitomycin resistance in Streptomyces lavendulae includes a novel drug-binding-protein-dependent export system.

mct.validation_method: expression in E. coli, reduced intracellular accumulation of MC

mrd.validation_method: expression in E. coli, reduced intracellular accumulation of MC

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mct and mrd as novel genes involved in mitomycin C resistance in Streptomyces lavendulae, functioning as a drug export system and a drug-binding protein, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, mutagenesis, and expression in E. coli to assess resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: The neutral cysteine protease bleomycin hydrolase is essential for epidermal integrity and bleomycin resistance.

Blmh.validation_method: generation of Blmh null mice and demonstration that Blmh is the sole enzyme required for BLM deamination

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bleomycin hydrolase (Blmh) as essential for epidermal integrity and bleomycin resistance, demonstrating that Blmh is the sole enzyme required for bleomycin deamination and that its absence leads to increased sensitivity to bleomycin toxicity.
full_output.methodology: Generation of Blmh knockout mice and assessment of their response to bleomycin treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genomic variation among Staphylococcus epidermidis strains infecting joint prostheses.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the phenotypic and genomic variation among Staphylococcus epidermidis strains infecting joint prostheses, highlighting the presence of multiple strains with distinct drug resistance patterns and macrorestriction profiles, indicating possible clonal relationships or polyclonal infections.
full_output.methodology: The study used macrorestriction patterns, drug resistance profiling, and ribotyping to analyze the genetic and phenotypic diversity of S. epidermidis strains from infected patients and healthy individuals.
full_output.sample_size: 54 strains from infected specimens and 23 strains from healthy individuals

full_output.paper_title: Cooperation between phosphorylation and acetylation processes in transcriptional control.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the transcriptional effects of histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitors, such as butyrate and trapoxin, are mediated through the activation of serine/threonine protein kinases and phosphatases. It highlights the importance of H7-sensitive protein kinase activity in the activation of the ChAT promoter and other viral promoters by HDAC inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized transient and stable transfections, luciferase assays, Western blot analysis, and Northern blotting to investigate the effects of HDAC inhibitors on gene expression and the role of protein kinases and phosphatases in this process.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro and in vivo antimicrobial activities of T-3811ME, a novel des-F(6)-quinolone.

mutations_found.origin: clinical isolates from various hospitals in Japan

GyrA.notes: Mutations in GyrA contribute to quinolone resistance in S. aureus and S. pneumoniae.
GyrA.evidence_note: The paper states that quinolone-resistant S. aureus with a GyrA GrlA double mutation, quinolone-resistant S. pneumoniae with a ParC mutation, and quinolone-resistant E. faecalis with a GyrA mutation were used in the study. The nucleotide sequences of gyrA and parC (grlA) in the quinolone resistance determining regions of these quinolone-resistant strains were determined by the dideoxy chain termination method.

mutations_found.origin: clinical isolates from various hospitals in Japan

ParC.notes: Mutation in ParC contributes to quinolone resistance in S. pneumoniae.
ParC.evidence_note: The nucleotide sequences of parC in the quinolone resistance determining regions of these quinolone-resistant strains were determined by the dideoxy chain termination method as previously reported.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial activity of T-3811ME, a novel des-F(6)-quinolone, against various bacterial strains, including quinolone-resistant isolates. It highlights the effectiveness of T-3811ME against gram-positive bacteria, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae, and identifies mutations in GyrA and ParC that confer quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted in vitro and in vivo antimicrobial activity tests, including MIC determinations and therapeutic efficacy evaluations in mouse models.

full_output.paper_title: Integron- and Carbenicillinase-Mediated Reduced Susceptibility to Amoxicillin-Clavulanic Acid in Isolates of Multidrug-Resistant Salmonella enterica Serotype Typhimurium DT104 from French Patients.

blaPSE-1.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC determination

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaPSE-1, a carbenicillinase gene, as the molecular mechanism underlying reduced susceptibility to amoxicillin-clavulanic acid in multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica serotype Typhimurium DT104 isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, cloning, and MIC determination were used to characterize the resistance mechanism.

full_output.paper_title: Heterogeneity in the vanB gene cluster of genomically diverse clinical strains of vancomycin-resistant enterococci.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three subtypes of the vanB gene cluster (vanB1, vanB2, and vanB3) in vancomycin-resistant enterococci, highlighting their molecular heterogeneity and implications for diagnostic primer design and epidemiological tracking.
full_output.methodology: PCR, RFLP analysis, DNA sequencing, and PFGE typing were used to analyze the vanB gene cluster in clinical isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the influence of antibiotics on the antibacterial activities of platelet microbicidal protein (tPMP-1) and neutrophil defensin (HNP-1) against Staphylococcus aureus. It shows that pretreatment with cell wall synthesis inhibitors (penicillin, vancomycin) enhances the staphylocidal effects of tPMP-1 and HNP-1, whereas pretreatment with protein synthesis inhibitors (tetracycline, novobiocin, azithromycin, quinupristin, dalfopristin) significantly reduces these effects.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro susceptibility testing, antibiotic pretreatment, and evaluation of bactericidal effects of tPMP-1 and HNP-1 against S. aureus under various conditions.

full_output.paper_title: From vanA Enterococcus hirae to vanA Enterococcus faecium: a study of feed supplementation with avoparcin and tylosin in young chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the vanA gene as responsible for glycopeptide resistance in Enterococcus hirae and Enterococcus faecium, showing that avoparcin and tylosin supplementation in chicken feed influences the selection and evolution of vanA-containing enterococci.
full_output.methodology: PCR, susceptibility testing, and PFGE analysis were used to characterize vanA-containing enterococci.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the in vitro activity of the carbapenem MK-0826 against clinical isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli producing broad-spectrum beta-lactamases (BDSBLs) and extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs). MK-0826 showed high potency against all tested isolates, with MIC ranges of 0.008 to 0.12 μg/ml. The study also highlights the importance of PBP binding affinity in determining the effectiveness of carbapenems against these resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution assays to determine MICs and competitive binding assays to assess PBP binding affinities of MK-0826 and other carbapenems.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro development of resistance to five quinolones and amoxicillin-clavulanate in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes mutations in parC, parE, gyrA, and gyrB associated with quinolone resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae, showing that these mutations contribute to increased MICs for various quinolones.
full_output.methodology: The study used serial subculturing in subinhibitory concentrations of quinolones and amoxicillin-clavulanate, followed by MIC determination and gene sequencing to identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: An inhibitor of exported Mycobacterium tuberculosis glutamine synthetase selectively blocks the growth of pathogenic mycobacteria in axenic culture and in human monocytes: extracellular proteins as potential novel drug targets.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the glutamine synthetase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis is highly sensitive to the inhibitors l-methionine-S-sulfoximine and d,l-phosphinothricin, leading to growth inhibition of pathogenic mycobacteria.
full_output.methodology: Purification and inhibition profiling of glutamine synthetase, growth inhibition assays, and analysis of cell wall components.

full_output.paper_title: Nasopharyngeal Carriage of Penicillin-Resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae among Children with Acute Respiratory Tract Infections in Thailand: a Molecular Epidemiological Survey
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae in Thailand, with 37.2% of isolates being penicillin-resistant. It highlighted the spread of international clones 23F and 9V, which are multidrug-resistant and contribute significantly to the increase in penicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular epidemiological methods including RFEL analysis, BOX PCR typing, PBP genotyping, serotyping, and drug susceptibility testing to analyze penicillin-resistant pneumococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of an archaic clone of Staphylococcus aureus with low-level resistance to methicillin in a pediatric hospital in Portugal and in international samples: relics of a formerly widely disseminated strain?

mecA.validation_method: molecular typing and hybridization with mecA probe

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a low-level methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus clone, characterized by the presence of the mecA gene, which confers resistance to methicillin. This clone was found in a pediatric hospital in Portugal and in international samples, suggesting it is an archaic strain that persisted in certain epidemiological settings.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing techniques, including PFGE, Southern hybridization, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, were used to characterize the MRSA strains.

full_output.paper_title: Erythromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae and oral commensal Neisseria spp. carry known rRNA methylase genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of known rRNA methylase genes (ermB, ermC, and ermF) in erythromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae and oral commensal Neisseria spp., which confer resistance to erythromycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and hybridization techniques were used to identify and characterize the erm genes in the isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 16 commensal Neisseria isolates and 4 N. gonorrhoeae isolates

full_output.paper_title: Use of microdilution panels with and without beta-lactamase inhibitors as a phenotypic test for beta-lactamase production among Escherichia coli, Klebsiella spp., Enterobacter spp., Citrobacter freundii, and Serratia marcescens.

blaSHV-2.role_in_paper: The study focuses on the detection of beta-lactamase production in clinical isolates of Enterobacteriaceae, including Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
blaSHV-2.genetic_context: The study includes strains producing SHV-2 beta-lactamase.
blaSHV-2.source: The study discusses the role of SHV-2 beta-lactamase in conferring resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics.
blaSHV-2.evidence_note: The paper mentions SHV-2 as a beta-lactamase producing strain in the context of resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the use of microdilution panels with and without beta-lactamase inhibitors to detect beta-lactamase production in various Enterobacteriaceae species. It identifies several beta-lactamase genes, including TEM, SHV, and others, which confer resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used susceptibility testing with microdilution panels and analyzed the effects of beta-lactamase inhibitors on antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activities of designed antimicrobial peptides (DAPs) against multidrug-resistant cystic fibrosis pathogens, demonstrating that D2A21 and D4E1 exhibit potent bactericidal activity against methicillin-resistant S. aureus, multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and Burkholderia cepacia.
full_output.methodology: The study used time-kill assays and broth microdilution techniques to assess the antibacterial activities of DAPs against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Outer membrane permeability barrier in Escherichia coli mutants that are defective in the late acyltransferases of lipid A biosynthesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the msbB mutant in E. coli, which produces penta-acylated lipid A, maintains an intact outer membrane permeability barrier against hydrophobic antibiotics and glycopeptides, indicating that hexa-acylation of lipid A is not necessary for normal barrier function.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the susceptibility of E. coli mutants defective in lipid A biosynthesis to various antibiotics using E-test strips.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of multidrug resistance in Streptococcus mitis.

mef.validation_method: PCR amplification and detection of amplicon

ermB.validation_method: PCR amplification and detection of amplicon

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of mef, ermB, and tet(M) genes in multidrug-resistant Streptococcus mitis isolates, contributing to resistance against macrolides, clindamycin, and tetracycline, respectively.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Southern blot hybridization, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic analysis of a chromosomal region containing vanA and vanB, genes required for conversion of either ferulate or vanillate to protocatechuate in Acinetobacter.

vanB.evidence_note: The paper describes spontaneous mutations in vanB, including a G-to-A substitution causing G269D in VanB, and insertions of IS1236. These mutations disrupt vanillate demethylase activity, as shown by the inability of mutant strains to grow on ferulate.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies vanA and vanB as essential genes for the conversion of ferulate and vanillate to protocatechuate in Acinetobacter, demonstrating their role in aromatic compound metabolism through mutant analysis and gene cloning.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, mutant analysis, and DNA sequencing were used to characterize vanA and vanB.

full_output.paper_title: Most Enterobacter aerogenes Strains in France Belong to a Prevalent Clone.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a prevalent clone of Enterobacter aerogenes in France, which is resistant to multiple antibiotics, including extended-spectrum beta-lactamase TEM-24, and highlights the role of outer membrane porin alterations in reduced susceptibility to certain antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing using RAPD and ERIC-PCR, sequencing of TEM-24 beta-lactamase, and immunodetection of outer membrane porins.

full_output.paper_title: Role in cell permeability of an essential two-component system in Staphylococcus aureus.

yycF.notes: The yycF1 mutation causes hypersensitivity to macrolides and lincosamides.

full_output.key_findings: The yycF1 mutation in Staphylococcus aureus leads to hypersusceptibility to macrolides and lincosamides, highlighting the essential role of the yycFG two-component system in cell permeability and survival.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, mutant isolation, complementation, and phenotypic characterization.

full_output.paper_title: noxR3, a novel gene from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, protects Salmonella typhimurium from nitrosative and oxidative stress.

noxR3.validation_method: expression in Salmonella typhimurium and survival assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies noxR3, a novel gene from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which confers resistance to nitrosative and oxidative stress in Salmonella typhimurium.
full_output.methodology: Functional characterization of the noxR3 gene through expression in Salmonella typhimurium and survival assays under various stress conditions.

full_output.paper_title: A novel means of self-protection, unrelated to toxin activation, confers immunity to the bactericidal effects of the Enterococcus faecalis cytolysin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cylI as a novel gene responsible for conferring immunity to the bactericidal effects of the Enterococcus faecalis cytolysin. This gene is located 3' to the cylA gene and is essential for immunity.
full_output.methodology: The study used deletion analysis, mutagenesis, and RT-PCR to characterize the role of cylI in cytolysin immunity.

acrAB.validation_method: purification and reconstitution into proteoliposomes

full_output.key_findings: The AcrAB multidrug efflux pump of Escherichia coli was purified and reconstituted, demonstrating its role in intrinsic resistance to solvents, dyes, detergents, and lipophilic antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Protein purification, reconstitution into proteoliposomes, and fluorescence measurements were used to characterize the AcrAB efflux pump.

dam.mechanism: confers resistance to 2-aminopurine and other mutagens by affecting DNA methylation and mismatch repair
dam.validation_method: complementation studies and mutagen sensitivity assays

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a dam mutant of Serratia marcescens, identifying the dam gene encoding a DNA adenine methyltransferase that affects DNA methylation and mismatch repair, leading to increased mutability and sensitivity to 2-aminopurine and other mutagens.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, complementation studies, and mutagen sensitivity assays were used to characterize the dam gene and its function.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of rpoS mutation on the stress response and expression of virulence factors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: hypersensitivity to stressors and altered virulence factor production

rpoS.evidence_note: The paper describes the rpoS mutation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and its effects on stress response and virulence factors.

full_output.key_findings: The rpoS mutation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa leads to hypersensitivity to stressors and altered production of virulence factors such as exotoxin A, pyocyanin, and pyoverdine.
full_output.methodology: Construction of rpoS mutants and assessment of stress responses and virulence factor production.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli mutants lacking all possible combinations of eight penicillin binding proteins: viability, characteristics, and implications for peptidoglycan synthesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that E. coli can survive with multiple deletions of penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), demonstrating that certain PBPs are nonessential for growth and that others can compensate for their loss.
full_output.methodology: The research involved constructing a set of E. coli mutants with deletions of various PBPs and analyzing their viability and growth characteristics.

pbpF.validation_method: expression in E. coli and penicillin binding activity

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes a new penicillin-binding protein, PBP2B, encoded by the gene pbpF in Staphylococcus aureus. This protein exhibits penicillin binding activity and is expressed in vivo.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, expression in E. coli, penicillin binding assays, immunoprecipitation, and sequencing were used to characterize PBP2B.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of TEM-59 (IRT-17), a novel inhibitor-resistant TEM-derived beta-lactamase in a clinical isolate of Klebsiella oxytoca.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TEM-59 (IRT-17), a novel inhibitor-resistant TEM-derived beta-lactamase in a clinical isolate of Klebsiella oxytoca, which shows resistance to penicillins and reduced susceptibility to beta-lactamase inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization through sequencing, isoelectric focusing, and kinetic studies.

full_output.paper_title: Roles of beta-lactamases and porins in activities of carbapenems and cephalosporins against Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several beta-lactamases (blaSHV-2, blaSHV-5, blaTEM-6, blaTEM-10, blaTEM-12, blaTEM-26, blaSHV-3, and blaAmpC) that confer resistance to various cephalosporins and carbapenems in Klebsiella pneumoniae. The role of porin OmpK36 in resistance is also highlighted, as its restoration reduces MICs of antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid introduction, MIC testing, and SDS-PAGE analysis were used to evaluate the role of beta-lactamases and porins in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Reversal of tetracycline resistance mediated by different bacterial tetracycline resistance determinants by an inhibitor of the Tet(B) antiport protein.

tet(B).evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that tet(B) encodes an antiport protein involved in tetracycline efflux and that it confers resistance to tetracycline. The organisms tested in the study are listed as Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Enterococcus hirae.

full_output.methodology: Examination of tetracycline efflux inhibition in everted membrane vesicles and bacterial growth assays.

Genetic Structure of Natural Populations of Escherichia coli in Wild Hosts on Different Continents

full_output.methodology: The study used multilocus enzyme electrophoresis (MLEE), antibiotic resistance testing, and plasmid profiling to analyze E. coli strains from wild mammals and birds.

full_output.paper_title: Construction and characterization of mutants of the TEM-1 beta-lactamase containing amino acid substitutions associated with both extended-spectrum resistance and resistance to beta-lactamase inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activities of ertapenem (MK-0826) against recent clinical bacteria collected in Europe and Australia.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of ertapenem against various clinical bacteria, highlighting its effectiveness against Enterobacteriaceae and other Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, while noting limited activity against certain species like Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter spp.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of IS1409, an insertion element of 4-chlorobenzoate-degrading Arthrobacter sp. strain TM1, and development of a system for transposon mutagenesis.

full_output.paper_title: Promoters of the CATG-Specific Methyltransferase Gene hpyIM Differ between iceA1 and iceA2 Helicobacter pylori Strains.

full_output.paper_title: Intra- and interspecies signaling between Streptococcus salivarius and Streptococcus pyogenes mediated by SalA and SalA1 lantibiotic peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Organization of Plasmid ColJs, Encoding Colicin Js Activity, Immunity, and Release Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the genetic organization of plasmid ColJs, identifying three genes: cja (colicin Js activity), cji (colicin Js immunity), and cjl (colicin Js release).

full_output.paper_title: Tuberculosis and drug resistance among patients seen at an AIDS Reference Center in São Paulo, Brazil.

full_output.paper_title: Selection and genetic characterization of Streptococcus pneumoniae mutants resistant to the des-F(6) quinolone BMS-284756.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of trypsin-like cysteine proteinases (gingipains) from Porphyromonas gingivalis by tetracycline and its analogues.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the cold shock gene cspA as critical for the susceptibility of Staphylococcus aureus to the antimicrobial peptide CG 117-136. Mutations in cspA increase resistance to this peptide.
full_output.methodology: The study used insertional mutagenesis, Southern hybridization, PCR, and RT-PCR to analyze the role of cspA in susceptibility to CG 117-136.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of residues critical for catalysis in a class C beta-lactamase by combinatorial scanning mutagenesis.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: reduced capability to convey antibiotic resistance
mutations_found.validated_by: in vivo antibiotic resistance assay and in vitro kinetic analysis

blaC.notes: Mutation at position 346 (N346D) in the active site of the class C beta-lactamase P99 leads to reduced antibiotic resistance.
blaC.evidence_note: The paper describes the mutation N346D in the class C beta-lactamase P99 and its effect on antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several mutations in the class C beta-lactamase P99 that significantly reduce antibiotic resistance, indicating the importance of specific residues in catalytic activity.
full_output.methodology: Combinatorial scanning mutagenesis, in vivo antibiotic resistance assay, and in vitro kinetic analysis were used to evaluate the impact of mutations on beta-lactamase activity.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular mechanisms of itraconazole resistance in Candida dubliniensis.

CdERG3.validation_method: identification of mutations in the alleles encoding this enzyme and their lack of functional complementation in a Saccharomyces cerevisiae erg3 mutant

CdERG3.notes: Frameshift mutations in CdERG3 lead to truncated proteins and loss of sterol C5,6-desaturase activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CdERG3 mutations as the primary mechanism of itraconazole resistance in six of seven C. dubliniensis derivatives, with altered membrane properties and absence of ergosterol.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, Southern hybridization, Northern blot analysis, and sterol analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Rod shape determination by the Bacillus subtilis class B penicillin-binding proteins encoded by pbpA and pbpH.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pbpA and pbpH as class B penicillin-binding proteins involved in rod shape determination in Bacillus subtilis. Both genes play redundant roles in maintaining rod shape during vegetative growth and spore outgrowth.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation, transcriptional analysis, and microscopic examination to investigate the roles of pbpA and pbpH in cell shape determination.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Streptococcus mutans strains deficient in EIIAB Man of the sugar phosphotransferase system.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the role of EIIAB Man in Streptococcus mutans, highlighting its involvement in sugar transport, catabolite repression, and regulation of virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, growth assays, PTS activity measurements, and proteomic analysis to investigate the functions of EIIAB Man.

full_output.paper_title: Coagulase-negative staphylococci: comparison of phenotypic and genotypic oxacillin susceptibility tests and evaluation of the agar screening test by using different concentrations of oxacillin.

mecA.validation_method: PCR detection of the mecA gene

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the oxacillin susceptibilities of 152 coagulase-negative staphylococcal (CoNS) strains and found that the mecA gene is responsible for oxacillin resistance. The agar screening test with 4 μg of oxacillin per ml and incubation for 48 h was highly effective in detecting oxacillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic oxacillin susceptibility tests, including disk diffusion, agar dilution, E-test, agar screening, and PCR for mecA gene detection.

23S rRNA.notes: associated with low-level resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a T2717C mutation in the 23S rRNA gene of Helicobacter pylori as a cause of clarithromycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and restriction analysis were used to detect the T2717C mutation in the 23S rRNA gene of H. pylori.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the Osiris expert system for identification of beta-lactam phenotypes in isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the Osiris expert system for identifying beta-lactam phenotypes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, focusing on resistance mechanisms such as beta-lactamase production, derepressed cephalosporinase, efflux systems, and porin deficiencies.
full_output.methodology: The study used disk diffusion tests and the Osiris expert system to analyze beta-lactam resistance phenotypes in 53 P. aeruginosa strains with well-characterized resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic identification of erythromycin-resistant campylobacter isolates as helicobacter species and analysis of resistance mechanism.

23S rRNA.notes: Mutation at position 2142 (A2142G) in 23S rRNA gene associated with erythromycin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a point mutation (A2142G) in the 23S rRNA gene of Helicobacter cinaedi and Helicobacter pullorum strains that confers erythromycin resistance, highlighting the importance of molecular methods for accurate identification of erythromycin-resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: Molecular techniques including 16S and 23S rDNA sequencing, PCR, and nucleotide sequence analysis were used to identify and characterize erythromycin-resistant Helicobacter species.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of sporadic isolates of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in hospitals and their similarities to isolates of community-acquired MRSA.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the genetic diversity and evolutionary relationships of sporadic methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates, identifying variations in SCC mec types and highlighting the presence of novel SCC mec structural variants.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular typing techniques including spaA typing, multilocus sequence typing (MLST), and SCC mec typing to analyze the genetic characteristics of MRSA isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports a case of empyema with infected ascites caused by Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, which was sensitive to meropenem and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Clinical case report and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Control of SXT integration and excision.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Xis as a novel recombination directionality factor (RDF) that facilitates SXT excision and inhibits SXT integration, highlighting its critical role in the regulation of SXT mobility.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular biology techniques including plasmid construction, mutagenesis, real-time quantitative PCR, and conjugation assays to investigate the roles of SXT genes in integration and excision.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of azithromycin administration for trachoma control on the carriage of antibiotic-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that azithromycin administration for trachoma control did not significantly increase the prevalence of macrolide-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae. Only one erythromycin-resistant isolate was identified, which carried the mef gene, indicating resistance due to an efflux pump.
full_output.methodology: PCR and susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize antibiotic-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Presence of the tet(O) Gene in Erythromycin- and Tetracycline-Resistant Strains of Streptococcus pyogenes and Linkage with either the mef(A) or the erm(A) Gene.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the tet(O) gene in erythromycin- and tetracycline-resistant Streptococcus pyogenes strains and shows its linkage with mef(A) or erm(A) genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, conjugal transfer experiments, and PFGE analysis were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: The Aminoglycoside 6′-N-Acetyltransferase Type Ib Encoded by Tn1331 Is Evenly Distributed within the Cell's Cytoplasm.

aac(6')-Ib.mechanism: modifies aminoglycoside antibiotics by adding an acetyl group, reducing their ability to bind to the ribosome and thus conferring resistance
aac(6')-Ib.validation_method: protein expression and localization studies, including fusion with phoA and CFP, and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the aac(6′)-Ib gene, which encodes an aminoglycoside 6′-N-acetyltransferase that confers resistance to kanamycin, amikacin, and tobramycin. The gene is part of the Tn1331 transposon and is localized in the cytoplasm of E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Expression and localization studies of the aac(6′)-Ib gene, including fusion with phoA and CFP, and MIC testing for aminoglycoside resistance.

full_output.paper_title: New Klebsiella oxytoca beta-lactamase genes blaOXY-3 and blaOXY-4 and a third genetic group of K. oxytoca based on blaOXY-3.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two new beta-lactamase genes, blaOXY-3 and blaOXY-4, in Klebsiella oxytoca, representing a third genetic group of the species.
full_output.methodology: Sequence comparison, phylogenetic analysis, and biochemical testing were used to characterize the new beta-lactamase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Arsenic sensing and resistance system in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. strain PCC 6803.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the arsenic resistance operon in Synechocystis sp. strain PCC 6803, identifying the genes arsB, arsC, and arsH. Mutant analyses revealed that arsB and arsC are involved in arsenic resistance, while arsH's role remains unclear.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation and mutant analysis were used to investigate the roles of arsB, arsC, and arsH in arsenic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Application of DNA microarrays to study the evolutionary genomics of Yersinia pestis and Yersinia pseudotuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes such as sepC, which is a putative insecticidal toxin, and btuB, a vitamin B12 receptor, which show variation between Yersinia pestis and Yersinia pseudotuberculosis strains.
full_output.methodology: DNA microarray analysis was used to compare the genomes of Yersinia pestis and Yersinia pseudotuberculosis strains.
full_output.sample_size: 22 Y. pestis strains and 10 Y. pseudotuberculosis strains

full_output.paper_title: Identification of cry1I-Type Genes from Bacillus thuringiensis Strains and Characterization of a Novel cry1I-Type Gene.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes a novel cry1I-type gene, cry1Ie1, from Bacillus thuringiensis, which exhibits toxicity against several insect pests including the diamondback moth, Asian corn borer, and soybean pod borer.
full_output.methodology: PCR-RFLP analysis, gene cloning, expression in E. coli, and bioassays to assess insecticidal activity.

full_output.paper_title: Population genetics of the nomenspecies Enterobacter cloacae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 12 genetic clusters and one sequence crowd within the E. cloacae complex through molecular phylogeny analysis of hsp60, rpoB, hemB, and ampC genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular phylogeny analysis of housekeeping genes and PCR-RFLP to investigate the genetic structure of the E. cloacae complex.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and serotype distribution of Streptococcus pneumoniae and molecular characterization of multidrug-resistant serotype 19F, 6B, and 23F Pneumococci in northern Thailand.

gyrA.notes: Mutation in gyrA gene associated with ciprofloxacin resistance.

parC.notes: Mutation in parC gene associated with ciprofloxacin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant serotypes 19F, 6B, and 23F of Streptococcus pneumoniae in northern Thailand, with specific mutations in gyrA and parC genes contributing to ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, serotyping, and molecular typing by pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal distribution of invasive pneumococcal isolates from children and selected adults in the United States prior to 7-valent conjugate vaccine introduction.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the clonal distribution of invasive pneumococcal isolates in the US before the 7-valent conjugate vaccine, identifying multiple clonal complexes and single ST lineages associated with different serotypes, highlighting the genetic diversity and resistance profiles of the isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) and multilocus sequence typing (MLST) to analyze the genetic structure of pneumococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Multiple CTX-M-type extended-spectrum beta-lactamases in nosocomial isolates of Enterobacteriaceae from a hospital in northern Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple CTX-M-type extended-spectrum beta-lactamases, including CTX-M-1, CTX-M-2, and CTX-M-15, in nosocomial isolates of Enterobacteriaceae from a hospital in northern Italy.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the CTX-M-type beta-lactamases.

full_output.paper_title: Community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus carrying Panton-Valentine leukocidin genes: worldwide emergence.

SCC mec type IV.validation_method: detection via PCR and PFGE analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the SCC mec type IV element and the PVL locus as common features among CA-MRSA isolates globally. These elements contribute to methicillin resistance and virulence, respectively.
full_output.methodology: PCR, PFGE, and MLST were used to analyze genetic characteristics and resistance mechanisms in CA-MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa-carrying VIM-2 metallo-beta-lactamase determinants, Croatia.

blaVIM-2.validation_method: PCR amplification and direct sequencing of the variable region of class 1 integrons

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the first clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Croatia carrying the blaVIM-2 gene, which confers resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and hybridization analyses were used to identify and characterize the blaVIM-2 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Listeria monocytogenes sigma B regulates stress response and virulence functions.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 54 sigma B-dependent genes in Listeria monocytogenes, highlighting the role of sigma B in stress response and virulence.
full_output.methodology: Combined HMM searches and microarray analyses to identify sigma B-regulated genes.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the use of genetic markers, specifically IS6110 and IS1081, for the epidemiological study of tuberculosis. These insertion sequences are used for DNA fingerprinting to trace the source of tuberculosis outbreaks and understand the transmission dynamics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) analysis and DNA fingerprinting techniques to analyze the genetic diversity of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex strains.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptional mapping of the promoter of the aminoglycoside acetyltransferase gene (aacC9) of neomycin-producing Micromonospora chalcea.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the promoter of the aacC9 gene encoding aminoglycoside acetyltransferase in neomycin-producing Micromonospora chalcea, showing that the transcription initiation point is at the translation start point with no conventional ribosome-binding site.
full_output.methodology: S1 nuclease mapping was used to analyze the promoter region of the aacC9 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical failure of vancomycin treatment of Staphylococcus aureus infection in a tertiary care hospital in southern Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a case of clinical failure of vancomycin treatment of Staphylococcus aureus infection, highlighting the emergence of vancomycin heteroresistant S. aureus (SAHV) with increased resistance after pre-incubation with vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Bacteriological cultures, disk diffusion, E-Test, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) were used to analyze the isolate's resistance mechanisms and genetic relatedness.

full_output.paper_title: Novel plasmid-borne gene qacJ mediates resistance to quaternary ammonium compounds in equine Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus simulans, and Staphylococcus intermedius.

qacJ.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC testing
qacJ.source: Novel Plasmid-Borne Gene qacJ Mediates Resistance to Quaternary Ammonium Compounds in Equine Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus simulans, and Staphylococcus intermedius.
qacJ.evidence_note: The paper states that qacJ was located on a 2,650-bp plasmid (designated pNVH01), and the 107-amino-acid protein, QacJ, showed similarities to known proteins of the small multidrug resistance family. The benzalkonium chloride MIC for a qacJ-containing recombinant was higher than those for otherwise isogenic recombinants expressing Smr, QacG, or QacH.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel plasmid-borne gene, qacJ, which mediates resistance to quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs) in equine Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus simulans, and Staphylococcus intermedius.
full_output.methodology: PCR, plasmid isolation, sequencing, and MIC testing were used to identify and characterize the qacJ gene.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in the DNA mismatch repair proteins MutS and MutL of oxazolidinone-resistant or -susceptible Enterococcus faecium.

mutS.notes: MutS mutations were found in linezolid-resistant and -susceptible isolates.

mutL.notes: MutL mutations were found in linezolid-resistant and -susceptible isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the DNA mismatch repair proteins MutS and MutL in oxazolidinone-resistant and -susceptible Enterococcus faecium isolates, suggesting a potential link between these mutations and linezolid resistance.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of mutSL genes and analysis of mutations in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A rifampin-hypersensitive mutant reveals differences between strains of Mycobacterium smegmatis and presence of a novel transposon, IS1623.

arr.validation_method: cloning in M. smegmatis and M. marinum + rifampin MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the arr gene in Mycobacterium smegmatis, which encodes a rifampin ADP ribosyltransferase that inactivates rifampin, leading to resistance. Disruption of arr results in rifampin hypersensitivity, and the gene is functional in M. marinum, increasing its rifampin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, cloning, and rifampin MIC testing were used to characterize the arr gene and its role in rifampin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance genes in enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli O149:K91 isolates obtained over a 23-year period from pigs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in ETEC O149:K91 isolates from pigs, including beta-lactamases (bla TEM, bla SHV, bla OXA-1), aminoglycoside resistance genes (aph (3′)-Ia, aph (3′)-IIa, aac (3)-IV), tetracycline resistance genes (tet (A), tet (B), tet (C)), chloramphenicol resistance gene (catI), trimethoprim resistance genes (dhfrI, dhfrV, dhfrXIII), and sulfonamide resistance genes (sulI, sulII). Additionally, class 1 integrons were found to play a significant role in the spread of these resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized colony hybridization, PCR, and sequencing to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in ETEC O149:K91 isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of XRP 2868, a new oral streptogramin, against Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus species, showing potent activity regardless of susceptibility to other agents.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar dilution and microdilution MIC testing to evaluate the antibacterial activity of XRP 2868 and other agents against various bacterial strains.
full_output.sample_size: 261 pneumococcal strains, 150 H. influenzae strains, and 26 H. parainfluenzae strains

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a DNA microarray to identify tetracycline resistance genes (tet) and successfully detected various tet genes in different bacterial species, demonstrating the effectiveness of the microarray technology for high-throughput screening of antimicrobial resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized DNA microarray technology to detect tetracycline resistance genes by hybridization with specific probes generated via PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemic and nonepidemic multidrug-resistant Enterococcus faecium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the esp gene as a significant marker for epidemic multidrug-resistant Enterococcus faecium, associated with hospital outbreaks and clinical infections. It also highlights the link between the purK-1 allele and the presence of the esp gene and ampicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping, susceptibility testing, PCR, sequencing, and AFLP analysis were used to investigate genetic relatedness and resistance mechanisms in Enterococcus faecium isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Fast and accurate quantitative detection of Helicobacter pylori and identification of clarithromycin resistance mutations in H. pylori isolates from gastric biopsy specimens by real-time PCR.

full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR with melting analysis for detection of H. pylori and identification of clarithromycin resistance mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Association between handling of pet treats and infection with Salmonella enterica serotype newport expressing the AmpC beta-lactamase, CMY-2.

blaCMY-2.validation_method: isolectric focusing, multiplex PCR, and sequencing

full_output.methodology: The study used isoelectric focusing, multiplex PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to identify and characterize the CMY-2 beta-lactamase.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of a point mutation associated with high-level isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis by using real-time PCR technology with 3′-minor groove binder-DNA probes.

full_output.paper_title: GeneHunter, a transposon tool for identification and isolation of cryptic antibiotic resistance genes.

aac(6')-Iaa.validation_method: experimental activation and identification via GeneHunter transposon

rma.validation_method: experimental activation and identification via GeneHunter transposon

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the identification of two cryptic antibiotic resistance genes, aac(6')-Iaa and rma, using the GeneHunter transposon tool. These genes were experimentally activated and characterized for their resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: Use of the GeneHunter transposon tool for activation and identification of cryptic resistance genes through transposition and subsequent characterization of resistance phenotypes.

full_output.paper_title: aph(3′)-IIb, a Gene Encoding an Aminoglycoside-Modifying Enzyme, Is under the Positive Control of Surrogate Regulator HpaA.

aph(3')-IIb.role_in_paper: The aph(3')-IIb gene is shown to form an operon structure with its upstream hpaA homologue and is activated by the HpaA homologue in response to the presence of 4-HPA, enabling P. aeruginosa to utilize 4-HPA as a sole carbon source.
aph(3')-IIb.validation_method: The study demonstrates that the aph(3')-IIb gene is regulated by HpaA and that its expression is induced by 4-HPA, leading to increased resistance to aminoglycoside antibiotics.
aph(3')-IIb.evidence_level: The evidence is based on experimental validation showing the regulation of the gene by HpaA and its role in conferring resistance to specific aminoglycoside antibiotics.
aph(3')-IIb.genetic_context: The aph(3')-IIb gene forms an operon with the upstream hpaA gene, and its expression is regulated by HpaA in response to 4-HPA.
aph(3')-IIb.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the aph(3')-IIb gene confers resistance to several aminoglycoside antibiotics, including kanamycin A and B, neomycin B and C, butirosin, and seldomycin F.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the aph(3′)-IIb gene, which encodes an aminoglycoside phosphotransferase, as a gene that confers resistance to aminoglycoside antibiotics in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The gene is regulated by the HpaA regulator in response to 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid (4-HPA).
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic approaches, including mutagenesis, lacZ fusion constructs, and β-galactosidase assays to investigate the regulation and function of the aph(3′)-IIb gene.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular mechanism of terbinafine resistance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies single point mutations in the ERG1 gene, which encode squalene epoxidase, as the cause of terbinafine resistance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. These mutations include L251F, F402L, F420L, P430S, and F433S.
full_output.methodology: Gene replacement experiments and PCR mutagenesis were used to validate the role of ERG1 mutations in terbinafine resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Biochemical, genetic, and zoosporicidal properties of cyclic lipopeptide surfactants produced by Pseudomonas fluorescens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes involved in the biosynthesis of cyclic lipopeptide surfactants in Pseudomonas fluorescens, which exhibit zoosporicidal activity against oomycete pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, Tn5 mutagenesis, and biochemical characterization were used to identify and validate the genes involved in surfactant production.

erm(B).validation_method: experimental validation through PCR, Southern blotting, and DNA sequencing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the erm(B) gene in Lactobacillus crispatus CHCC3692 as the erythromycin resistance-encoding gene, which can be removed via heat shock treatment, leading to erythromycin sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Southern blotting, DNA sequencing, and heat shock experiments were used to characterize the erm(B) gene and its excision.

full_output.paper_title: Predominance of vanA Genotype among Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcus Isolates from Poultry and Swine in Costa Rica.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the vanA gene as the predominant determinant of vancomycin resistance among Enterococcus isolates from poultry and swine in Costa Rica, highlighting its widespread presence and association with high-level resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR analysis and MIC determination were used to identify vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus isolates and determine their resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: PCR typing of genetic determinants for metallo-beta-lactamases and integrases carried by gram-negative bacteria isolated in Japan, with focus on the class 3 integron.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes metallo-beta-lactamase genes (blaIMP-1, blaIMP-2, and blaVIM-2) in various gram-negative bacteria isolated in Japan, highlighting their prevalence and association with integrons.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize metallo-beta-lactamase genes and integrases in gram-negative bacterial isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the changes in gene cassettes of class 1 integrons among E. coli isolates from urine specimens in Korea over the past two decades, highlighting the prevalence of aminoglycoside and trimethoprim resistance genes and the shift in gene cassette composition over time.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and Southern hybridization were used to analyze the presence and characteristics of class 1 integrons and their gene cassettes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of an RIP (Ribosome-Inactivating Protein)-like protein from tobacco with dual enzymatic activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolates and characterizes TRIP, a ribosome-inactivating protein-like protein from tobacco with dual enzymatic activity, including N-glycosidase and SOD-like activity.
full_output.methodology: Protein purification, enzymatic activity assays, and sequence analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 14 out of 75 E. coli isolates resistant to at least one antimicrobial agent, with 64% resistant to tetracycline and 57% resistant to streptomycin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing of E. coli isolates from apple cider and production environments.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a point mutation in the folA gene (Ile94→Leu) as the mechanism of trimethoprim resistance in E. coli mutators.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of the folA gene and determination of trimethoprim MICs.

full_output.paper_title: Orally administered targeted recombinant Beta-lactamase prevents ampicillin-induced selective pressure on the gut microbiota: a novel approach to reducing antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that orally administered targeted recombinant Beta-lactamase effectively neutralizes ampicillin in the gut, preventing its selective pressure on the gut microbiota and the emergence of ampicillin-resistant bacteria, including those carrying TEM genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used a beagle dog model to evaluate the effects of orally administered targeted recombinant Beta-lactamase on ampicillin levels and gut microbiota, employing high-performance liquid chromatography, TGGE, and PCR analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of garenoxacin in treatment of experimental endocarditis due to Staphylococcus aureus or viridans group streptococci.

mutations_found.validated_by: experimental validation through MIC testing and mutation analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a ciprofloxacin-resistant MRSA isolate (P8-4) with a grlA mutation (Ser80→Phe) that confers resistance to ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro susceptibility testing, time-kill studies, and in vivo experiments in a rat model of endocarditis to evaluate the efficacy of garenoxacin and to identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro inhibition of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis beta-ketoacyl-acyl carrier protein reductase MabA by isoniazid.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MabA as a target of isoniazid in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, showing that isoniazid inhibits MabA activity by forming a covalent adduct with NADP+, leading to resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used biochemical assays, HPLC, mass spectrometry, and crystallography to analyze the interaction between isoniazid and MabA.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of multiple-antimicrobial-resistant salmonella serovars isolated from retail meats.

blaTEM-1.mechanism: confers resistance to penicillins and some cephalosporins

aadA2.mechanism: confers resistance to streptomycin and spectinomycin

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella isolates from retail meats, including bla CMY-2, bla TEM-1, aadA1, aadA2, aacC2, aph (3')-IIa, aac (3)-IVa, sulI, sulII, tetA, and tetB. These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, sulfonamides, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study compares antibiotic resistance patterns and PFGE profiles of historical and contemporary isolates of multi-drug-resistant Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Newport, highlighting differences in resistance to cephalosporins, florfenicol, and other antibiotics between the two periods.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing via disk diffusion and PFGE analysis using Xba I restriction enzyme.

full_output.paper_title: Adaptive resistance to biocides in Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli O157 and cross-resistance to antimicrobial agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified adaptive resistance to biocides and cross-resistance to antimicrobial agents in Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli O157, highlighting the potential for biocides to contribute to the development of microbial resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study involved passaging bacterial strains in media with increasing concentrations of biocides or antibiotics to achieve adaptive resistance, followed by determination of cross-resistance through zone of inhibition assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IS6110 insertion in the promoter region of the phoP gene in a multidrug-resistant M. bovis B strain, which leads to increased phoP transcription and potentially contributes to the virulence and transmission of the strain.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, RFLP analysis, LM-PCR, and sequencing to analyze the IS6110 insertion and its effect on phoP gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of Inoculum and β-Lactamase Activity in AmpC- and Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase (ESBL)-Producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae Clinical Isolates Tested by Using NCCLS ESBL Methodology

blaSHV-5.evidence_note: The paper describes blaSHV-5 as a gene encoding a beta-lactamase that confers resistance to cefotaxime, ceftazidime, and cefepime through hydrolysis. The gene was tested in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various beta-lactamase genes, including blaTEM-1, blaTEM-3, blaTEM-6, blaTEM-10, blaTEM-12, blaTEM-26, blaTEM-28, blaTEM-43, blaSHV-1, blaSHV-5, blaSHV-18, blaCTX-M-10, blaFOX-5, and blaACT-1, which confer resistance to extended-spectrum cephalosporins and other beta-lactam antibiotics in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing, hydrolysis studies, and analysis of beta-lactamase activity.

full_output.paper_title: Utility of NCCLS guidelines for identifying extended-spectrum beta-lactamases in non-Escherichia coli and non-Klebsiella spp. of Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of NCCLS guidelines for detecting extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs) in non-E. coli and non-Klebsiella spp. of Enterobacteriaceae. It found that only a small percentage of isolates showed a CA effect, and only a few isolates had ESBL genes such as bla TEM and bla SHV.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and isoelectric focusing were used to identify ESBLs.

full_output.paper_title: Intrinsic mechanism decreases susceptibility of Escherichia coli O157:H7 to multiple antibiotics.

mar.validation_method: complementation experiments with a functional marR

full_output.key_findings: Chloramphenicol-resistant mutants of Escherichia coli O157:H7 showed increased resistance to tetracycline, nalidixic acid, and ciprofloxacin. Mutation in the mar operon was linked to decreased susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Complementation experiments with a functional marR restored antibiotic susceptibility in mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Levofloxacin treatment failure in Haemophilus influenzae pneumonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports four mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining regions of DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV genes in a levofloxacin-resistant Haemophilus influenzae strain, leading to cross-resistance to multiple fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing of QRDRs and susceptibility testing by microdilution methods.
full_output.sample_size: Three clinical isolates and four additional H. influenzae biotype II isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis in HIV-infected persons, Peru.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR)-TB among HIV-infected individuals in Lima and Callao, Peru, emphasizing the need for improved infection control and targeted interventions.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed drug susceptibility test results from HIV-infected and HIV-negative TB patients to determine the prevalence of MDR-TB.
full_output.sample_size: 81 HIV-seropositive patients and 965 patients with unknown or negative HIV status

full_output.paper_title: A Mutant Form of the Neisseria gonorrhoeae Pilus Secretin Protein PilQ Allows Increased Entry of Heme and Antimicrobial Compounds.
full_output.key_findings: A point mutation in the pilQ gene (pilQ1) leads to increased entry of heme, Triton X-100, and antibiotics in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, demonstrating that PilQ forms a channel for the entry of these compounds.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, sensitivity testing, and genetic manipulation.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro selection and characterization of resistance to macrolides and related antibiotics in Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in 23S rRNA, ribosomal protein L4, and ribosomal protein L22 that confer resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, streptogramins, and ketolides in Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro selection of resistant mutants through serial passages in subinhibitory concentrations of antibiotics, followed by PCR amplification and DNA sequencing to identify mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Reemergence of macrolide resistance in pharyngeal isolates of group a streptococci in southwestern Pennsylvania.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the reemergence of macrolide resistance in pharyngeal isolates of group A streptococci, with the M phenotype (mef(A)) and MLS B phenotype (erm(A)) being the primary resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing, PCR, and molecular typing were used to determine resistance mechanisms and genetic relatedness of isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanism of action of NB2001 and NB2030, novel antibacterial agents activated by beta-lactamases.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes NB2001 and NB2030, novel antibacterial agents that are activated by beta-lactamases, releasing triclosan through hydrolysis of the beta-lactam ring. These compounds show enhanced activity against beta-lactamase-positive strains.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the mechanism of action of NB2001 and NB2030 through enzyme kinetics, PBP binding assays, enoyl reductase inhibition, and cell morphology analyses.

full_output.methodology: In vitro characterization of the reverse tetracycline repressor (revTetR) using EMSA, CD spectroscopy, fluorescence measurements, and SPR.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of streptomycin, sulfadiazine, and tetracycline resistance genes (strA, sul2, and tetB) in E. coli isolates from calves, highlighting the role of these genes in antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening and molecular characterization of SSuT isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed invasive Haemophilus influenzae infections after widespread vaccination against H. influenzae type b, reporting resistance to ampicillin, cotrimoxazole, tetracycline, and chloramphenicol, with higher resistance in capsulated strains.
full_output.methodology: Microbiological identification, susceptibility testing, molecular epidemiology studies, and analysis of antibiotic consumption.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Multiresistant Streptococcus pneumoniae with Both erm(B)- and mef(A)-Mediated Macrolide Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of erm(B) and mef(A) genes in multiresistant Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates, contributing to macrolide resistance. Additionally, the study reports the presence of the mel gene, which is involved in macrolide and streptogramin resistance, and the tet(M) gene, which mediates tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and molecular epidemiological techniques including MLST, PFGE, and serotyping were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of Salmonella enterica serotype typhi infections in Korea for recent 9 years: trends of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the emergence of ciprofloxacin-resistant Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi strains in Korea, along with multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains resistant to ampicillin, chloramphenicol, and SXT-TMP.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of culture-proven cases and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using disk diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the in vitro activity of AC98-6446, a novel semisynthetic glycopeptide derivative, against various gram-positive clinical isolates, including those resistant to other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution and time-kill assays to determine the antimicrobial activity of AC98-6446 against gram-positive bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro and in vivo activities of antimicrobials against Nocardia brasiliensis.

linezolid.validation_method: disk diffusion and in vivo experiments

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro and in vivo activities of various antimicrobials against Nocardia brasiliensis, identifying linezolid, amikacin, and amoxicillin-clavulanic acid as effective treatments.
full_output.methodology: Disk diffusion, broth microdilution, and in vivo experiments in BALB/c mice were used to assess antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Novel chromosomally encoded multidrug efflux transporter MdeA in Staphylococcus aureus.

mdeA.validation_method: overexpression in S. aureus and measurement of MICs

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes MdeA, a novel chromosomally encoded multidrug efflux transporter in Staphylococcus aureus, which confers resistance to quaternary ammonium compounds and antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Overexpression of MdeA in S. aureus and measurement of MICs for various antimicrobial agents.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies murE as a critical gene in the expression of beta-lactam resistance in Staphylococcus aureus, showing that reduced murE function leads to decreased methicillin resistance due to impaired peptidoglycan synthesis.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, transcriptional studies, and cell wall precursor analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Laboratory detection of Haemophilus influenzae with decreased susceptibility to nalidixic acid, ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin due to GyrA and ParC mutations.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified GyrA and ParC mutations associated with decreased susceptibility to nalidixic acid, ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin in Haemophilus influenzae.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of quinolone resistance-determining regions (QRDRs) of gyrA and parC, along with susceptibility testing using microdilution and disk diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of three new enterococcal species, Enterococcus sp. nov. CDC PNS-E1, Enterococcus sp. nov. CDC PNS-E2, and Enterococcus sp. nov. CDC PNS-E3, isolated from human clinical specimens.
