full_output.methodology: Construction of deletion mutants, OM permeability assays, and β-lactamase leakage assays were used to evaluate the impact of PmrAB, pmrC, and cptA on outer membrane integrity.

full_output.key_findings: The study compares biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from mechanically ventilated patients and cystic fibrosis patients, highlighting differences in biofilm-forming ability and resistance patterns.
full_output.methodology: The study used biofilm growth assays, planktonic and biofilm antibiotic susceptibility testing, and RAPD analysis to assess clonality and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: DFMO suppresses the growth of Helicobacter pylori and alters its virulence factors
full_output.key_findings: DFMO suppresses the growth of H. pylori and reduces the expression and translocation of the virulence factor CagA, potentially making it a useful adjunctive treatment for H. pylori infections.
full_output.methodology: Experiments involving growth curves, ATP measurement, and Western blot analysis were conducted to assess the effects of DFMO on H. pylori.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of the transcriptional regulator NcrB in the nickel resistance determinant of Leptospirillum ferriphilum UBK03.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NcrB as a transcriptional regulator that binds to an inverted repeat sequence in the promoter pncrA, regulating the expression of the nickel resistance determinant in Leptospirillum ferriphilum UBK03.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular cloning, promoter-lacZ fusion assays, EMSA, and bacterial one-hybrid analysis to characterize the function of NcrB.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal structure of an integron gene cassette-associated protein from Vibrio cholerae identifies a cationic drug-binding module.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Vch_cass2 as a gene encoding a cationic drug-binding effector domain, suggesting a role in antimicrobial resistance through ligand binding.
full_output.methodology: Structural and functional analysis of the Cass2 protein, including crystallography and fluorescence assays.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of extended-spectrum beta lactamases among Salmonella enterica Typhimurium isolates from pediatric patients with diarrhea in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a high prevalence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs) among Salmonella enterica Typhimurium isolates from pediatric patients in China, including the first report of bla CTX-M-55 in Salmonella spp.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize ESBL genes in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis cluster with developing drug resistance, New York, New York, USA, 2003-2009.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified isoniazid resistance in a Mycobacterium tuberculosis cluster, with all resistant isolates carrying the Ser315Thr mutation in the katG gene.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing of the katG and inhA genes was performed to confirm isoniazid resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium novocastrense-associated pulmonary and wound infections.
full_output.key_findings: Mycobacterium novocastrense was identified in two clinical cases, showing resistance to rifampin and susceptibility to several antimycobacterial agents.
full_output.methodology: Molecular identification through PCR and sequencing of hsp65, 16S rDNA, and rpoB genes, along with susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that transgenic expression of the harpin HrpZ Psph from Pseudomonas syringae pv. phaseolicola enhances resistance to Beet necrotic yellow vein virus (BNYVV) in Nicotiana benthamiana and sugar beet. The SP/HrpZ Psph protein conferred high-level resistance, reducing virus titer and delaying symptom development.
full_output.methodology: Transgenic plants were generated using Agrobacterium-mediated transformation, and resistance was assessed through visual symptom scoring and DAS-ELISA. Protein expression and processing were confirmed via immunoblot analysis.

full_output.methodology: The study used the alamarBlue assay and quantitative suspension test (EN 14348) to determine the minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of biocides against M. smegmatis and its isogenic porin mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of altered function alleles that affect Bacillus subtilis PerR metal ion selectivity.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the role of the agr gene regulatory system in the pathogenesis of community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA), showing that agr influences the expression of methicillin resistance genes mecA and mecR1, contributing to the virulence and resistance of CA-MRSA strain USA300.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide transcriptional profiling and qRT-PCR were used to analyze the impact of the agr system on gene expression in CA-MRSA strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 70 novel substrates of the Dot/Icm system in Legionella pneumophila, highlighting the diverse features recognized by this protein transporter.
full_output.methodology: The study used a β-lactamase reporter system to identify Dot/Icm-dependent translocation of hypothetical proteins in L. pneumophila.

full_output.paper_title: Co-administration of a plasmid DNA encoding IL-15 improves long-term protection of a genetic vaccine against Trypanosoma cruzi.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that co-administration of a plasmid encoding IL-15 with a TS DNA vaccine enhances long-term protection against Trypanosoma cruzi by improving T cell responses and memory T cell expansion.
full_output.methodology: The study involved plasmid DNA vaccination of mice, ELISPOT assays, and cytokine measurements to evaluate immune responses and protection against T. cruzi.

full_output.paper_title: Initial mutations direct alternative pathways of protein evolution.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific mutations in the TEM-1 β-lactamase gene that lead to altered resistance profiles against cefotaxime, highlighting the role of epistasis in shaping evolutionary pathways.
full_output.methodology: In vitro evolution experiments with TEM-1 β-lactamase, mutant construction, and MIC testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 72 novel non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) in Legionella pneumophila, including a second copy of 6S RNA (6S2 RNA) and a family of 20 ncRNAs preferentially expressed during the intracellular life cycle. These ncRNAs are implicated in regulating virulence and adaptation during infection.
full_output.methodology: The study uses strand-specific RNA-seq to analyze the transcriptome of L. pneumophila during different growth phases and intracellular infection, identifying differentially expressed genes and ncRNAs.

full_output.paper_title: Nationwide surveillance of bacterial respiratory pathogens conducted by the Japanese Society of Chemotherapy in 2008: general view of the pathogens' antibacterial susceptibility.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in various bacterial respiratory pathogens in Japan, highlighting high rates of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), penicillin-resistant S. pneumoniae, and beta-lactamase-producing strains in H. influenzae and M. catarrhalis.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed on 987 bacterial strains using standardized methods according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Expression of the ompATb operon accelerates ammonia secretion and adaptation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to acidic environments.
full_output.key_findings: The ompATb operon is required for rapid ammonia secretion and adaptation of M. tuberculosis to acidic environments, but it does not function as a porin.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, uptake experiments, and pH monitoring were used to assess the role of ompATb.

full_output.paper_title: Gene-trap mutagenesis identifies mammalian genes contributing to intoxication by Clostridium perfringens ε-toxin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies HAVCR1 as a critical host factor contributing to ε-toxin-induced cytotoxicity through its role in toxin binding and cellular sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Gene-trap mutagenesis, RNA interference, immunoblotting, and toxin binding assays.

full_output.paper_title: Genome sequence of Helicobacter suis supports its role in gastric pathology.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various genes in Helicobacter suis that are homologous to genes in Helicobacter pylori, including those involved in acid acclimation, chemotaxis, adhesion, oxidative stress resistance, and type IV secretion systems. These genes suggest H. suis's potential role in gastric pathology.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and functional annotation of H. suis strains HS1 T and HS5 using cross-mapping and ab initio methods.

full_output.paper_title: Roles of the spiA gene from Salmonella enteritidis in biofilm formation and virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the spiA gene is involved in biofilm formation and virulence of Salmonella enteritidis. The spiA mutant exhibited reduced biofilm formation, decreased curli production, and was attenuated in a mouse model.
full_output.methodology: The study constructed a spiA mutant using allelic exchange and analyzed its biofilm formation, curli production, and virulence in a mouse model.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic variations define divergence of water/wildlife-associated Campylobacter jejuni niche specialists from common clonal complexes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genomic variations in water/wildlife-associated Campylobacter jejuni strains, highlighting deletions and divergences in regions associated with host-bacterial interactions, including the cdtABC cluster and peb3 gene, which are linked to colonization and virulence.
full_output.methodology: Comparative genomic hybridization, genome sequencing, and PCR assays were used to analyze genomic variations and gene deletions in Campylobacter jejuni isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanisms of resistance to bacteriocins targeting the mannose phosphotransferase system.

manR.notes: Mutations in manR were found in L. monocytogenes strain L1040-L, which exhibited reduced Man-PTS expression and resistance to class IIa bacteriocins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two mechanisms of resistance to Man-PTS-targeting bacteriocins: downregulation of Man-PTS gene expression and potential cell surface changes. Mutations in the regulatory gene manR were associated with reduced Man-PTS expression and resistance.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing, RT-PCR, and growth analysis were used to investigate Man-PTS gene expression and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: various L. monocytogenes isolates and L. lactis mutants

full_output.paper_title: Insights into physiological and genetic mupirocin susceptibility in bifidobacteria.

full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, cloning, MIC assay, and structural analysis of the IleS protein.

full_output.paper_title: Serine protease PrtA from Streptococcus pneumoniae plays a role in the killing of S. pneumoniae by apolactoferrin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PrtA as a serine protease essential for the cleavage of apolactoferrin, releasing bactericidal peptides that kill Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Mutant construction, recombinant protein expression, and protease activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Quorum sensing inhibitors increase the susceptibility of bacterial biofilms to antibiotics in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that quorum sensing inhibitors (QSIs) such as baicalin hydrate (BH), cinnamaldehyde (CA), and hamamelitannin (HAM) can increase the susceptibility of bacterial biofilms to antibiotics, enhancing the effectiveness of antibiotic treatment against biofilms formed by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Burkholderia cenocepacia, Burkholderia multivorans, and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo biofilm models, including C. elegans and G. mellonella, to evaluate the effect of QSIs in combination with antibiotics on biofilm susceptibility and host survival.

full_output.paper_title: Decrease in penicillin susceptibility due to heat shock protein ClpL in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: ClpL, a heat shock protein, modulates cell wall biosynthesis and decreases penicillin susceptibility in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, MIC determination, Western blotting, TEM, and co-immunoprecipitation.

full_output.paper_title: Off-target gene regulation mediated by transcriptional repressors of antimicrobial efflux pump genes in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

full_output.key_findings: The study documents a decline in invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) in Malawi following the scale-up of antiretroviral therapy (ART) and highlights the stability of antibiotic resistance rates, including multidrug resistance, over a 10-year period.
full_output.methodology: Surveillance of pneumococcal isolates from blood and cerebrospinal fluid cultures, along with antibiotic susceptibility testing using disc diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: Global hypomethylation in PPP tolerant cell lines
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes such as ALDH1A3, ANXA1, MAPK, BCL2, and SOCS3 that are dysregulated in PPP tolerant cell lines and contribute to PPP resistance through their expression levels.
full_output.methodology: The study uses siRNA treatment and expression profiling to validate the role of dysregulated genes in PPP resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of ciprofloxacin resistance and its relationship to extended-spectrum β-lactamase production in Proteus mirabilis bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a close association between ciprofloxacin resistance and extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) production in Proteus mirabilis bacteremia.
full_output.methodology: Clinical and microbiological analysis of P. mirabilis bacteremia cases.

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus anthracis protease InhA increases blood-brain barrier permeability and contributes to cerebral hemorrhages.

inhA.mechanism: degrades ZO-1, a tight junction protein, leading to increased permeability of the blood-brain barrier
inhA.validation_method: Western blot, TEER measurement, FITC-dextran permeability assay, immunofluorescence microscopy

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies InhA, a metalloprotease from Bacillus anthracis, as a key factor in increasing blood-brain barrier permeability by degrading ZO-1, a critical tight junction protein. This leads to BBB disruption and contributes to cerebral hemorrhages associated with anthrax meningitis.
full_output.methodology: The study uses in vitro models of the blood-brain barrier, including TEER measurements, FITC-dextran permeability assays, and Western blot analysis, along with in vivo mouse models to assess BBB permeability and histopathological changes.
full_output.sample_size: n=5 for InhA-injected groups; n=3 for control group

full_output.paper_title: Influence of antimicrobial feed additives on broiler commensal posthatch gut microbiota development and performance.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of antimicrobial feed additives on broiler gut microbiota development and found that certain operational taxonomic units (OTUs) were significantly altered by the presence of avilamycin, flavophospholipol, and zinc bacitracin, indicating changes in the gut microbial community composition.
full_output.methodology: The study used T-RFLP and Lac-PCR DGGE to analyze gut microbiota composition and identified OTUs associated with different dietary treatments.

full_output.paper_title: An antirepressor, SrpR, is involved in transcriptional regulation of the SrpABC solvent tolerance efflux pump of Pseudomonas putida S12.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SrpS as a repressor and SrpR as an antirepressor involved in the transcriptional regulation of the SrpABC efflux pump in Pseudomonas putida S12.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized β-galactosidase assays, RT-PCR, EMSAs, and GST pulldown assays to investigate the regulatory mechanisms of SrpS and SrpR.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and in vitro antibacterial activity of 7-(3-amino-6,7-dihydro-2-methyl-2H-pyrazolo[4,3-c] pyridin-5(4H)-yl)fluoroquinolone derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of novel fluoroquinolone derivatives, with compound 8f showing significantly higher potency against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae compared to existing drugs.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and tested for antibacterial activity using agar-dilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Structural studies of the mechanism for biosensing antibiotics in a fluorescein-labeled β-lactamase.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structural mechanism of a fluorescein-labeled β-lactamase (PenP-E166Cf) for biosensing β-lactam antibiotics, demonstrating that the enzyme's fluorescence increases upon binding and acylation of antibiotics like cefotaxime.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, fluorescence spectroscopy, and mutagenesis were used to analyze the biosensing mechanism of the enzyme.

full_output.paper_title: Deletion of mtrC in Haemophilus ducreyi increases sensitivity to human antimicrobial peptides and activates the CpxRA regulon.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mtrC as a gene involved in resistance to LL-37 and human β-defensins in Haemophilus ducreyi, with deletion of mtrC increasing sensitivity to these antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, and antimicrobial susceptibility assays.

gidB.notes: Mutations in gidB confer low-level streptomycin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the gidB gene, which encodes a 16S rRNA methyltransferase, confer low-level streptomycin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The study demonstrates that a gidB knockout mutant exhibits increased streptomycin MIC, and clinical isolates with gidB mutations show varied resistance levels spanning the recommended streptomycin breakpoint concentration.
full_output.methodology: Construction of an isogenic Δ gidB mutant, complementation experiments, and drug susceptibility testing using broth microdilution and agar-based methods.
full_output.sample_size: 18 gidB mutation-containing isolates and 14 gidB mutation-free isolates

full_output.paper_title: Funnel-like Hexameric Assembly of the Periplasmic Adapter Protein in the Tripartite Multidrug Efflux Pump in Gram-negative Bacteria
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the hexameric assembly of the periplasmic adapter protein AcrA in the tripartite multidrug efflux pump of Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting its role in substrate specificity and interaction with TolC.
full_output.methodology: Genetic complementation, in vitro binding assays, electron microscopy, and mutational analysis were used to investigate the structure and function of AcrA.

full_output.paper_title: The genome of Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, the causative agent of swine erysipelas, reveals new insights into the evolution of firmicutes and the organism's intracellular adaptations.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the genome of Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, revealing insights into its intracellular adaptations and evolutionary relationships. It identifies genes involved in capsule synthesis, virulence factors, and antioxidant defenses, but no AMR genes or mutations are explicitly mentioned.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and comparative genomics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of genes and genomic islands correlated with high pathogenicity in Streptococcus suis using whole genome tiling microarrays.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes and genomic islands associated with high pathogenicity in Streptococcus suis, highlighting the role of specific regions of difference (RDs) in virulence. full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, Western blot analysis, and mouse infection models to investigate the role of FopC in immune evasion and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Functional analysis of ycfR and ycfQ in Escherichia coli O157:H7 linked to outbreaks of illness associated with fresh produce.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ycfR as a gene involved in chlorine resistance in E. coli O157:H7 strain Sakai, while ycfQ acts as a repressor of ycfR. Deletion of ycfR in Sakai increases chlorine sensitivity, whereas in TW14359 and EDL933, it does not affect chlorine resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Enterotoxins, colonization factors, serotypes and antimicrobial resistance of enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) strains isolated from hospitalized children with diarrhea in Bolivia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high antimicrobial resistance to ampicillin among ETEC strains from Bolivia, with 67% of the strains showing resistance to one or more antimicrobial agents. The most common toxin profile was LT (70%), followed by LT/STh (23%) and STh (7%).
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic methods including ELISA, dot blot, slide agglutination, disc diffusion, and multiplex PCR were used to analyze ETEC strains for toxins, colonization factors, serotypes, and antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.methodology: The paper reviews the use of various photosensitizers, including phenothiazinium dyes, cationic porphyrins, phthalocyanines, bacteriochlorins, fullerenes, and their conjugates, for antimicrobial PDT.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution and characterization of ampicillin- and tetracycline-resistant Escherichia coli from feedlot cattle fed subtherapeutic antimicrobials.

full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR was used to detect tetracycline and ampicillin resistance genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A strategy for antagonizing quorum sensing.

full_output.methodology: Structural biology, mutagenesis, and biochemical assays were used to investigate the mechanism of quorum-sensing antagonism.

full_output.methodology: Functional assays, competition binding experiments, and mutagenesis studies were used to analyze nisin's mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Dissemination of multiple drug resistance genes by class 1 integrons in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from four countries: a comparative study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple drug resistance genes associated with class 1 integrons in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from four countries, highlighting the dissemination of resistance mechanisms such as bla IMP4, qacG2, aacA4, catB3, aadA1, aadA2, dfrA12, dfrA14, dfrA17, aadA5, qnrB2, bla CTX-M-2, and bla CTX-M-15.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and plasmid typing were used to analyze the genetic context of class 1 integrons and identify resistance genes in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Horizontal Transfer of the OXA-24 Carbapenemase Gene via Outer Membrane Vesicles: a New Mechanism of Dissemination of Carbapenem Resistance Genes in Acinetobacter baumannii.

blaOXA-24.genetic_context: plasmid-borne bla OXA-24 gene (plasmids pMMA2 and pMMCU3, respectively)
blaOXA-24.evidence_note: The study demonstrates that A. baumannii releases outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) during in vitro growth, which harbor the bla OXA-24 gene and can transfer it to carbapenem-susceptible A. baumannii strains, resulting in full resistance to carbapenems.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from Acinetobacter baumannii can transfer the blaOXA-24 carbapenemase gene, leading to carbapenem resistance in recipient strains.
full_output.methodology: Transformation experiments, MIC testing, and dot blot analysis were used to validate the transfer and functionality of the blaOXA-24 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Activities of colistin- and minocycline-based combinations against extensive drug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from intensive care unit patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that colistin-based combinations with meropenem, rifampicin, or minocycline exhibit synergistic bactericidal activity against XDR-AB strains, while individual drugs like colistin at 0.5×MIC or minocycline, meropenem, and rifampicin alone lack significant bactericidal effects.
full_output.methodology: In vitro time-kill studies and susceptibility testing were performed on 14 XDR-AB isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the sensitivity of phenotypic methods for detecting ESBL and AmpC beta-lactamases in Enterobacteriaceae strains, confirming the presence of blaTEM, blaSHV, and blaCTX-M genes through molecular biology techniques.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and phenotypic testing methods including Etest, DDST, and microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: The analysis of para-cresol production and tolerance in Clostridium difficile 027 and 012 strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the hpdBCA operon as crucial for para-cresol production in Clostridium difficile strains 630 and R20291. Mutants in this operon failed to produce para-cresol, confirming its role in the conversion of p-hydroxyphenylacetate to para-cresol.
full_output.methodology: Gene inactivation mutants, NMR spectroscopy, and zNose™ gas chromatography were used to analyze para-cresol production and tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Heterogeneous vancomycin-intermediate susceptibility in a community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus epidemic clone, in a case of Infective Endocarditis in Argentina.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first case of h-VISA phenotype in a community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) strain in Argentina, highlighting the emergence of low-level vancomycin resistance in an epidemic CA-MRSA clone.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization, molecular typing, and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: A central interdomain protein joint in elongation factor G regulates antibiotic sensitivity, GTP hydrolysis, and ribosome translocation.

mutations_found.validated_by: fluorescence spectroscopy and GTP hydrolysis assays

EF-G.notes: The paper describes the mutation F95A in EF-G and its effects on GTP hydrolysis and resistance to fusidic acid.
EF-G.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the F95A mutation confers resistance to fusidic acid.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the F95A mutation in elongation factor G (EF-G) as a cause of fusidic acid resistance, demonstrating that this mutation leads to spontaneous GTP hydrolysis and impaired ribosome translocation.
full_output.methodology: The study uses fluorescence spectroscopy, GTP hydrolysis assays, and ribosome translocation experiments to characterize the functional impact of mutations in EF-G.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiologic analysis of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates from bacteremia and nasal colonization at 10 intensive care units: multicenter prospective study in Korea.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the molecular epidemiology of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates from bacteremia and nasal colonization in Korean ICUs, highlighting the prevalence of specific PFGE types and their association with antibiotic resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: The study employed molecular typing techniques including PFGE, MLST, and spa typing, along with antibiotic susceptibility testing to analyze MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In-vitro activity of polymyxin B, rifampicin, tigecycline alone and in combination against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in Singapore.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA-23-like and bla OXA-51-like carbapenemase genes in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates, which confer resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: MIC testing and clonal relationship analysis were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Adaptation and antibiotic tolerance of anaerobic Burkholderia pseudomallei.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that anaerobic Burkholderia pseudomallei is highly tolerant to conventional antibiotics used for melioidosis treatment but extremely sensitive to nitroimidazole antibiotics like metronidazole and tinidazole. It also identifies that a small subpopulation of B. pseudomallei can survive for at least one year under anaerobic conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study used microarray analysis, anaerobic culture models, and antibiotic susceptibility testing to investigate the response of B. pseudomallei to hypoxia and its antibiotic resistance profile.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a cryptic plasmid pSM429 and its application for heterologous expression in psychrophilic Pseudoalteromonas.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the cryptic plasmid pSM429 from Pseudoalteromonas sp. BSi20429 and develops a shuttle vector pWD for heterologous expression. The erythromycin resistance gene ermC was successfully expressed in Pseudoalteromonas sp. SM20429, demonstrating the utility of the system for cold-adapted protein production.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid isolation, sequencing, vector construction, electroporation, and antibiotic resistance testing.

full_output.paper_title: Sortase independent and dependent systems for acquisition of haem and haemoglobin in Listeria monocytogenes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Lmo2185 and HupD as critical components in the acquisition of haem and haemoglobin in Listeria monocytogenes, highlighting their roles as hemophores and iron porphyrin binders.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, protein purification, binding and transport experiments, and growth assays.

full_output.paper_title: Multiplex fluorescence melting curve analysis for mutation detection with dual-labeled, self-quenched probes.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in the rpoB gene were detected in Mycobacterium tuberculosis samples.

HBV.notes: Mutations in the HBV gene were detected in serum samples.

HBB.notes: Mutations in the HBB gene were detected in clinical samples.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a multiplex fluorescence melting curve analysis (FMCA) method using dual-labeled, self-quenched probes for detecting mutations in the rpoB gene of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, HBV, and HBB gene. The method allows for the detection of various mutations associated with resistance to rifampin, lamivudine, adefovir, and beta-thalassemia.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized FMCA with dual-labeled, self-quenched probes for mutation detection in clinical samples, validated through DNA sequencing of PCR amplicons.
full_output.sample_size: 311 M. tuberculosis samples, 165 HBV samples, 94 HBB samples

full_output.key_findings: The study presents the crystal structures of Burkholderia cenocepacia dihydropteroate synthase (DHPS) in both apo-form and complexed with the product 7,8-dihydropteroate, providing insights into the enzyme's active site and interactions with substrates and inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology techniques including protein expression, purification, crystallization, and X-ray crystallography were employed to determine the structures of DHPS.

full_output.paper_title: Implication of the NorB efflux pump in the adaptation of Staphylococcus aureus to growth at acid pH and in resistance to moxifloxacin.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the NorB efflux pump contributes to resistance to moxifloxacin in Staphylococcus aureus, particularly under acidic pH conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study used gene expression analysis, Western blotting, and susceptibility testing to investigate the role of the NorB efflux pump in acid pH adaptation and moxifloxacin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Trends towards lower antimicrobial susceptibility and characterization of acquired resistance among clinical isolates of Brachyspira hyodysenteriae in Spain.

23S rRNA.notes: The G2032A mutation is associated with increased resistance to pleuromutilins.

L3.notes: Mutations at amino acid positions 148 and 149 of ribosomal protein L3 are associated with reduced susceptibility to pleuromutilins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the 23S rRNA gene and ribosomal protein L3 that contribute to resistance to pleuromutilins in Brachyspira hyodysenteriae isolates in Spain.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of 23S rRNA and L3 genes, along with MIC testing, was used to identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a phenotypic method for detection of fecal carriage of OXA-48-producing enterobacteriaceae after incidental detection from clinical specimen.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the incidental isolation of an OXA-48-producing Escherichia coli strain and highlights the importance of developing a phenotypic method for detecting fecal carriage of such strains, as conventional methods may fail.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and phenotypic testing using Etest strips.

full_output.paper_title: Global network analysis of drug tolerance, mode of action and virulence in methicillin-resistant S. aureus.

vraR.encodes: regulator protein of the vancomycin-resistance associated two-component system (VraSR)
vraR.mechanism: regulates expression of genes induced by vancomycin, many of which function in cell wall biosynthesis
vraR.validation_method: quantitative PCR confirmed upregulation of vraR by ranalexin

tcaA.mechanism: member of the cell wall stress stimulon known to be induced by exposure to antibiotics in a VraRS dependent fashion
tcaA.validation_method: microarray analysis detected tcaA upregulation by ranalexin

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several novel virulence factors in MRSA-252, including SAR0287 and SAR0288, which are downregulated by ranalexin. It also highlights the role of the VraRS two-component system in cell wall stress response and cationic antimicrobial peptide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome and proteome profiling combined with network analysis were used to study the effects of ranalexin on MRSA-252.

full_output.paper_title: Fusidic acid resistance among clinical isolates of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in a Taiwanese hospital.

fusC.encodes: ribosomal translocase and translation elongation factor EF-G

fusB.encodes: inducible protein that protects an in vitro translation system against the inhibitory action of fusidic acid
fusB.validation_method: PCR with FusB-specific primers and sequence analysis

fusA.encodes: ribosomal translocase and translation elongation factor EF-G
fusA.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that mutations in fusA were found in 10 strains, with specific amino acid substitutions in EF-G (fusA gene) detected.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified fusC as the most common fusidic acid resistance determinant in MRSA isolates, with 25 out of 34 isolates harboring this gene. Additionally, one isolate was found to harbor both fusB and fusC. Mutations in the fusA gene, including H457Y, G556S, and R659L, were also associated with fusidic acid resistance.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize fusidic acid resistance determinants in MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Cloning, purification, and functional characterization of Carocin S2, a ribonuclease bacteriocin produced by Pectobacterium carotovorum.
full_output.key_findings: Carocin S2, a ribonuclease bacteriocin produced by Pectobacterium carotovorum, was characterized. It consists of two components: CaroS2K, a 85-kDa killing protein with ribonuclease activity, and CaroS2I, a 10-kDa immunity protein that inhibits CaroS2K's activity.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, expression in E. coli, purification, and biochemical assays were used to characterize Carocin S2.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance to organic hydroperoxides requires ohr and ohrR genes in Sinorhizobium meliloti.

ohr.validation_method: disk diffusion assay and growth inhibition

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ohr and ohrR genes in Sinorhizobium meliloti that are crucial for resistance to organic hydroperoxides. Ohr is essential for surviving organic peroxide stress, while OhrR acts as a transcriptional repressor regulating ohr expression.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, disk diffusion assays, gel mobility shift assays, and transcriptional fusion analyses were used to characterize the role of ohr and ohrR in organic hydroperoxide resistance.

full_output.paper_title: PNA-FISH as a new diagnostic method for the determination of clarithromycin resistance of Helicobacter pylori.

23S rRNA.notes: Mutations in the 23S rRNA gene are associated with clarithromycin resistance in H. pylori.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes a novel PNA-FISH method for detecting clarithromycin resistance in H. pylori by targeting specific point mutations in the 23S rRNA gene. The method shows high sensitivity and specificity and can be applied to gastric biopsy samples.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PNA-FISH, E-test, and sequencing to detect and validate clarithromycin resistance mutations in H. pylori.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified new noncovalent inhibitors of penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) from penicillin-resistant bacteria, including compounds 1 and 9, which showed promising inhibitory activities against PBP2a and PBP2x 5204, as well as good in vitro antibacterial activities against various Gram-positive bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening of a compound library, computational similarity searches, enzymatic inhibition assays, and antibacterial activity testing.

full_output.paper_title: The structure of a Burkholderia pseudomallei immunophilin-inhibitor complex reveals new approaches to antimicrobial development.

BpML1.validation_method: structural analysis and enzymatic activity assays

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes BpML1, a Burkholderia pseudomallei immunophilin, revealing its structure and function, highlighting its role in protein-protein interactions and potential as a target for antimicrobial development.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography and NMR spectroscopy were used to determine the structure of BpML1, along with enzymatic activity assays to evaluate its PPIase activity and inhibitor binding.

full_output.paper_title: Spontaneous phthiocerol dimycocerosate-deficient variants of Mycobacterium tuberculosis are susceptible to gamma interferon-mediated immunity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a spontaneous point mutation in the ppsD gene (G44C) responsible for PDIM deficiency and virulence attenuation in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome resequencing, complementation, and reversion experiments were conducted to validate the role of the ppsD (G44C) mutation in PDIM production and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Moraxella catarrhalis outer membrane vesicles carry β-lactamase and promote survival of Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae by inactivating amoxicillin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that Moraxella catarrhalis outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) carry β-lactamase, which inactivates amoxicillin, thereby promoting the survival of amoxicillin-susceptible bacteria such as Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular biology techniques, including PCR, Western blotting, flow cytometry, and transmission electron microscopy, to characterize the presence and functionality of β-lactamase in M. catarrhalis OMVs.

full_output.paper_title: Is Neisseria gonorrhoeae Initiating a Future Era of Untreatable Gonorrhea?: Detailed Characterization of the First Strain with High-Level Resistance to Ceftriaxone
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a unique penA mosaic allele (penA H041) responsible for high-level ceftriaxone resistance in the first strain of Neisseria gonorrhoeae with this resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study performed genetic and phenotypic characterization, including transformation assays, to confirm the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Inactivation of tesA reduces cell wall lipid production and increases drug susceptibility in mycobacteria.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: abolishes its ability to support PDIM and PGL production

tesA.notes: The S92A mutation in tesAmm abolishes its ability to support PDIM and PGL production.
tesA.evidence_note: The S92A mutation in tesAmm abolishes its ability to support PDIM and PGL production.

full_output.key_findings: Inactivation of tesA in Mycobacterium marinum leads to a drastic reduction in PDIM and PGL production and increases antibiotic susceptibility. A S92A mutation in tesAmm eliminates its ability to support PDIM and PGL production.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, site-directed mutagenesis, LC-MS analysis, and antibiotic susceptibility assays.

full_output.paper_title: Most multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from hospitals in eastern France belong to a few clonal types.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several beta-lactamase genes, including blaPER-1, blaOXA-28, and blaOXA-19, which contribute to multidrug resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from hospitals in eastern France.
full_output.methodology: The study used pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE), multilocus sequence typing (MLST), and PCR-based approaches to characterize resistance mechanisms in multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Resolution of gene regulatory conflicts caused by combinations of antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates how gene regulatory conflicts arise and are resolved in bacterial responses to antibiotic combinations, revealing that most gene expression responses to drug combinations can be explained by growth rate changes and conflict resolution mechanisms such as prioritization or averaging.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized an E. coli promoter-GFP library to study transcriptional responses to antibiotic combinations, employing Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to identify dominant response patterns.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of BAL30072 against Burkholderia pseudomallei.

PenA.notes: PenA is a chromosomally-encoded β-lactamase that weakly hydrolyzes BAL30072.

amrRAB-oprA.notes: Deletion of amrRAB-oprA did not affect BAL30072 susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: BAL30072 shows superior in vitro activity against Burkholderia pseudomallei compared to ceftazidime, meropenem, and imipenem, with rapid bactericidal effects. Resistance mechanisms such as PenA β-lactamase and efflux did not significantly impact BAL30072 activity.
full_output.methodology: MIC testing, time-kill curves, and analysis of mutant strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the REBA MTB-MDR assay for detecting mutations in rpoB, katG, inhA promoter region, and the oxyR-ahpC intergenic region associated with resistance to rifampicin and isoniazid in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Reverse blot hybridization assay combined with PCR amplification and DNA sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Structural analysis of a putative aminoglycoside N-acetyltransferase from Bacillus anthracis.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the structural properties of BA2930, a putative aminoglycoside N-acetyltransferase from Bacillus anthracis, but no resistance phenotype was observed in the experiments.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, site-directed mutagenesis, and biochemical assays were used to study the function of BA2930.

full_output.paper_title: Selection pressure required for long-term persistence of blaCMY-2-positive IncA/C plasmids.

blaCMY-2.validation_method: experimental validation via plasmid transfer and resistance testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaCMY-2 as a gene that confers resistance to expanded-spectrum cephalosporins and examines its persistence in bacterial populations under different selection pressures.
full_output.methodology: The study used filter mating experiments, competition studies, and long-term passage experiments to analyze the persistence and resistance properties of blaCMY-2 plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: Natural and synthetic cathelicidin peptides with anti-microbial and anti-biofilm activity against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several synthetic and natural cathelicidin peptides, including LL-37, NA-CATH, and NA-CATH:ATRA1-ATRA1, which exhibit anti-microbial and anti-biofilm activity against Staphylococcus aureus. These peptides show varying degrees of effectiveness in inhibiting bacterial growth and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Anti-microbial assays, biofilm inhibition experiments, and circular dichroism spectroscopy were used to evaluate the peptides' activities.

full_output.paper_title: Differential effects of thiopeptide and orthosomycin antibiotics on translational GTPases.

rplP.notes: Mutations in rplP confer resistance to Evn and Avn.

rpsL.notes: Mutations in rpsL confer resistance to Evn and Avn.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in rplP and rpsL that confer resistance to evernimicin (Evn).
full_output.methodology: The study uses biochemical and structural analyses to determine the effects of antibiotics on translational GTPases and identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid diagnosis of extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis by use of a reverse line blot hybridization assay.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a reverse line blot hybridization (RLBH) assay for rapid detection of resistance to isoniazid, rifampin, fluoroquinolones, and second-line aminoglycosides in extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) isolates. Key mutations identified include katG S315T, rpoB S531L, and gyrA A90V, D94G, D94A, and D94N, as well as rrs A1401G and G1484T.
full_output.methodology: Reverse line blot hybridization assay combined with PCR and sequencing for detecting mutations in genes associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: New Topoisomerase I mutations are associated with resistance to camptothecin.

TOP1.notes: Mutations in core subdomain III and linker domain of TOP1 contribute to resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Three new TOP1 mutations (p.R621H, p.L617I, and p.E710G) were identified in SN38-resistant HCT116 clones, which reduce the formation of TOP1-DNA cleavage complexes and DNA double-strand breaks upon SN38 treatment.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing, HRM analysis, ICE bioassay, and DNA combing were used to characterize TOP1 mutations and their effects on SN38 resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and functional analyses reveal that Staphylococcus aureus antibiotic resistance factor HmrA is a zinc-dependent endopeptidase.
full_output.key_findings: HmrA is a zinc-dependent endopeptidase that enhances resistance to β-lactam antibiotics in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Structural and functional analyses, including cloning, protein expression, purification, enzymatic activity assays, and in vivo growth and killing assays.

full_output.paper_title: Gene expression profiling and molecular characterization of antimony resistance in Leishmania amazonensis.

MRPA.validation_method: quantitative real-time RT-PCR and southern blot analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identified MRPA overexpression as a key mechanism of antimony resistance in Leishmania amazonensis through gene amplification and increased expression.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression profiling using DNA microarrays and quantitative real-time RT-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Practical approach for reliable detection of AmpC beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae

ampC.mechanism: chromosomal ampC gene overexpression due to promoter mutations
ampC.validation_method: multiplex PCR and ampC promoter sequence analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ampC gene overexpression due to promoter mutations in Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Salmonella enterica as a mechanism for AmpC beta-lactamase production, highlighting the importance of molecular analysis for accurate detection.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, ampC promoter sequence analysis, and phenotypic screening tests were used to detect and characterize AmpC beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of two molecular assays for rapid detection of mycobacterium tuberculosis resistance to fluoroquinolones in high-tuberculosis and -multidrug-resistance Settings.

gyrA.notes: Most common mutation in FQ-resistant strains.

gyrB.notes: Novel mutation found in a sensitive strain.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA and gyrB genes associated with fluoroquinolone resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with the most common mutation being D94G in gyrA and a novel mutation in gyrB.
full_output.methodology: Pyrosequencing and conventional sequencing of the quinolone resistance determining region (QRDR) of gyrA and gyrB genes, along with phenotypic drug susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Enteric pathogens associated with childhood diarrhea in Tripoli-Libya.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various enteric pathogens associated with childhood diarrhea in Tripoli, Libya, including Salmonella species with resistance to multiple antimicrobials, notably ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed stool samples from children with diarrhea using culture, enzyme-immunoassay, and polymerase chain reaction methods to detect bacterial, viral, and parasitic pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of SCCmec elements in methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various SCCmec types in methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MR-CoNS) isolates, highlighting the genetic diversity of SCCmec elements and the need for improved classification schemes.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, sequencing, and analysis of ccr and mec gene complexes were used to determine SCCmec types in MR-CoNS isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic comparison of multi-drug resistant invasive and colonizing Acinetobacter baumannii isolated from diverse human body sites reveals genomic plasticity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Acinetobacter baumannii, including blaOXA-69, which confers resistance to carbapenems, and AdeT, an RND-type efflux pump involved in aminoglycoside resistance. AmpC cephalosporinase was also found to contribute to resistance against cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR screening, and genomic comparisons were used to identify AMR genes and their resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Variable antibiotic susceptibility patterns among Streptomyces species causing actinomycetoma in man and animals.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial susceptibility of 18 Streptomyces strains isolated from actinomycetoma cases in humans and animals in Sudan. It found that all strains were resistant to amphotericin B, penicillin, and sulfamethoxazole, while showing varying levels of susceptibility to other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) agar dilution method on 18 Streptomyces strains.

full_output.paper_title: Low fitness cost of the multidrug resistance gene cfr.

cfr.validation_method: MIC testing and analysis of the modification status of A2503 in 23S rRNA

full_output.key_findings: The cfr gene encodes an rRNA methyltransferase that methylates the 23S rRNA residue A2503, conferring resistance to multiple classes of ribosomal antibiotics, including linezolid, phenicols, lincosamides, pleuromutilins, streptogramins A, macrolides, and oxazolidinones. The study found that the fitness cost of cfr expression in Staphylococcus aureus is minimal.
full_output.methodology: Construction of plasmids, MIC testing, primer extension analysis, and growth competition experiments.

mutations_found.validated_by: ATP-dependent DNA supercoiling assay, quinolone-inhibited supercoiling assay, and DNA cleavage assay

gyrb.notes: The E540V mutation in GyrB was identified as a cause of quinolone resistance in M. tuberculosis.
gyrb.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the E540V mutation in GyrB confers resistance to multiple quinolones, including ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, sparfloxacin, sitafloxacin, nalidixic acid, and enoxacin. The mutation was observed in Mycobacterium tuberculosis and was validated through ATP-dependent DNA supercoiling assay, quinolone-inhibited supercoiling assay, and DNA cleavage assay.

full_output.key_findings: The E540V amino acid substitution in GyrB of Mycobacterium tuberculosis was shown to contribute to quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro DNA supercoiling and cleavage assays to evaluate the impact of the E540V substitution in GyrB on quinolone resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Etiology and antimicrobial susceptibility of udder pathogens from cases of subclinical mastitis in dairy cows in Sweden.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci (CNS) as the most frequent pathogens causing subclinical mastitis in dairy cows in Sweden. Resistance to antimicrobials was rare, with only 4% of S. aureus isolates and 35% of CNS isolates showing resistance to penicillin G.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting milk samples from dairy cows and performing bacteriological analyses and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using microdilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: High frequency of integrons related to drug-resistance in clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii.

aacA4.validation_method: PCR, restriction enzyme digestion, DNA sequencing

catB3.validation_method: PCR, restriction enzyme digestion, DNA sequencing

dfrA1.validation_method: PCR, restriction enzyme digestion, DNA sequencing

blam-1.validation_method: PCR, restriction enzyme digestion, DNA sequencing

aadA1.validation_method: PCR, restriction enzyme digestion, DNA sequencing

sat2.validation_method: PCR, restriction enzyme digestion, DNA sequencing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several drug-resistance genes within class 1 integrons in Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates, including aacA4, catB3, dfrA1, blam-1, orfX, aadA1, and sat2, which contribute to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, restriction enzyme digestion, and DNA sequencing were used to identify and characterize integrons and their gene cassettes in clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Spread of extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis in KwaZulu-Natal province, South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the spread of extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) in KwaZulu-Natal province, South Africa, highlighting the high prevalence of XDR-TB in the Umzinyati district, particularly in the Msinga sub-district, and the increasing number of hospitals reporting XDR-TB cases.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study analyzing the culture and drug susceptibility database of the provincial tuberculosis laboratory in KwaZulu-Natal Province.

full_output.paper_title: Coevolution of ABC transporters and two-component regulatory systems as resistance modules against antimicrobial peptides in Firmicutes Bacteria.

bceAB.validation_method: experimental validation through mutant studies and gene expression analysis

vraFG.validation_method: experimental validation through mutant studies and gene expression analysis

nsaRS.validation_method: experimental validation through mutant studies and gene expression analysis

grars.validation_method: experimental validation through mutant studies and gene expression analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes BceAB-like ABC transporters and BceRS-like two-component regulatory systems as resistance modules against antimicrobial peptides in Firmicutes bacteria, highlighting their coevolution and functional interdependence.
full_output.methodology: The research involved phylogenetic analysis, sequence alignment, and comparative genomics to investigate the coevolution and functional relationships between ABC transporters and two-component systems in Firmicutes bacteria.

blaSPM-1.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the standard strain of P. aeruginosa (SPM-1, P1088) was used as a positive control.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified metallo-beta-lactamase-producing P. aeruginosa strains and found that 5% of the isolates were positive for MBL, although no specific subtypes (bla-IMP, bla-VIM, bla-SPM) were detected by PCR.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, MBL detection via phenotypic test and PCR, and molecular typing via PFGE.

mdr1.validation_method: Western blot, real-time PCR, luciferase reporter assay

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that STAT3 activation leads to the upregulation of mdr1, resulting in adriamycin resistance in leukemia cells. Inhibition of STAT3 reduces mdr1 expression and restores drug sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Western blot, real-time PCR, luciferase reporter assay, flow cytometry, and CCK-8 assay.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic diversity and antimicrobial resistance of Escherichia coli from human and animal sources uncovers multiple resistances from human sources.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates from different sources, including blaTEM, aadA1, tetA, tetB, tetC, intI1, intI2, and sul1, indicating the presence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates.
geographic_location: Middle Santa Ana River watershed, southern California, USA

full_output.paper_title: Self-resistance and cell wall composition in the glycopeptide producer Amycolatopsis balhimycina.

vanY_b.mechanism: cleavage of the terminal d-Ala from peptidoglycan precursors

ompK26.mechanism: compensates for the absence of OmpK35/36 and allows carbapenem resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OmpK26, a novel porin that compensates for the loss of OmpK35/36 and contributes to carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Comparative analysis of outer membrane proteins, insertion-duplication mutagenesis, and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) inner-core phosphates are required for complete LPS synthesis and transport to the outer membrane in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies waaP, wapP, wapQ, and PA5006 as essential genes for LPS synthesis and transport in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1. Depletion of these genes leads to the accumulation of truncated LPS species and affects OM integrity, highlighting their critical role in maintaining the structural and functional properties of the outer membrane.
full_output.methodology: The study uses an arabinose-inducible promoter system to regulate gene expression, analyzes LPS structure via SDS-PAGE and ESI-MS, and examines the effects of gene depletion on cell morphology and antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Selection of resistant bacteria at very low antibiotic concentrations.

rpsL.notes: Mutations in rpsL confer resistance to streptomycin
rpsL.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that rpsL (K42R) confers streptomycin resistance.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA confer resistance to ciprofloxacin

acrR.notes: Inactivation of acrR confers resistance to ciprofloxacin
acrR.evidence_note: The paper states that ΔacrR mutations confer ciprofloxacin resistance and that this was validated by competition experiments and MIC measurements.

marR.notes: Inactivation of marR confers resistance to ciprofloxacin
marR.evidence_note: The paper states that "Δ marR" confers resistance to ciprofloxacin.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that resistant bacteria can be selected at extremely low antibiotic concentrations, even below the minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) of susceptible bacteria. Mutations in rpsL, gyrA, acrR, and marR were identified as conferring resistance to streptomycin, ciprofloxacin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Competition experiments between isogenic pairs of susceptible and resistant strains, MIC measurements, and growth rate analysis were used to identify resistance mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: 20 lineages of S. typhimurium LT2 and 20 lineages of E. coli MG1655

full_output.paper_title: Expression of the lantibiotic mersacidin in Bacillus amyloliquefaciens FZB42.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that Bacillus amyloliquefaciens FZB42 is immune to mersacidin due to the presence of the mrsFGE and mrsK2R2 genes, which confer resistance. Additionally, the researchers successfully transferred the mersacidin biosynthetic gene cluster to B. amyloliquefaciens FZB42, enabling the production of active mersacidin.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, PCR, MIC determination, and HPLC purification were used to validate the presence and functionality of the mersacidin resistance genes and to confirm mersacidin production.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of a globally dominant IncHI1 plasmid type associated with multiple drug resistant typhoid.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of a globally dominant IncHI1 plasmid type (PST6) associated with multiple drug-resistant typhoid. Key resistance genes include blaTEM-1, cat, dfrA7, sul1, sul2, strAB, tetA, tetD, and betU, which contribute to resistance against ampicillin, chloramphenicol, trimethoprim, sulfamethoxazole, streptomycin, tetracycline, and high salt environments.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, SNP typing, plasmid transfer experiments, and growth assays were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms and evolutionary dynamics of IncHI1 plasmids in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that Staphylococcus aureus sortase A (SrtA) is highly resistant to oxidative inhibition by reactive oxygen species (ROS), particularly hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl). This resistance is attributed to the high reduction potential of the catalytic cysteine residue, Cys184, which is protected by the unique active site architecture of SrtA.
full_output.methodology: The study used biochemical assays, including HPLC-based inhibition kinetics, LC/MS analysis, and electrochemical measurements to investigate the resistance of SrtA to oxidative stress.

full_output.key_findings: The study found high rates of antimicrobial resistance in Helicobacter pylori isolates from Alaska Native persons, including metronidazole (42%), clarithromycin (30%), and levofloxacin (19%) resistance.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing of H. pylori isolates to various antibiotics was performed using agar dilution and Etest methods.

full_output.paper_title: Urine antibiotic activity in patients presenting to hospitals in Laos: implications for worsening antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that a significant proportion of patients in Laos had taken antibiotics before hospital consultation, highlighting potential issues with antibiotic misuse and its impact on resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study used urine samples to detect antibiotic activity through bacterial lawn inhibition assays with Bacillus stearothermophilus, Escherichia coli, and Streptococcus pyogenes.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of copolymers of 4-vinyl-N-hexylpyridinium bromide and dimethyl(2-methacryloyloxyethyl) phosphonate that exhibit antimicrobial activity against S. mutans while maintaining biocompatibility with human gingival fibroblasts.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of copolymers, surface analysis techniques, and biocompatibility and antimicrobial testing using cell cultures and bacterial adhesion assays.

full_output.paper_title: Salicylate Functions as an Efflux Pump Inducer and Promotes the Emergence of Fluoroquinolone-Resistant Campylobacter jejuni Mutants.

cmeABC.validation_method: transcriptional fusion assays, real-time qRT-PCR, immunoblotting assays

full_output.key_findings: Salicylate induces the expression of the CmeABC efflux pump in Campylobacter jejuni, leading to decreased susceptibility to fluoroquinolones and increased emergence of fluoroquinolone-resistant mutants.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional fusion assays, real-time qRT-PCR, immunoblotting, and EMSA were used to analyze the effect of salicylate on CmeABC expression and function.

full_output.paper_title: Association of antibiotic resistance in agricultural Escherichia coli isolates with attachment to quartz.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that antibiotic resistance in agricultural Escherichia coli isolates is associated with attachment to quartz, although no specific AMR genes were identified as directly conferring resistance. The presence of attachment factors such as EcpA, type I pili, Ag43, and P pili was detected, but none were significantly related to attachment.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of attachment factor genes and antibiotic resistance assays.

full_output.paper_title: EmmdR, a new member of the MATE family of multidrug transporters, extrudes quinolones from Enterobacter cloacae.

emmdR.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + drug susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies EmmdR, a novel MATE family multidrug transporter in Enterobacter cloacae, which confers resistance to quinolones, disinfectants, and other antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, gene expression, gene deletion, and physiological characterization were used to validate EmmdR's role in multidrug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: The mosaicism of plasmids revealed by atypical genes detection and analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies plasmid atypical genes (PAGs) and explores their distribution, function, and origin, highlighting the role of plasmids in horizontal gene transfer and the spread of genetic traits such as antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Computational analysis combining GC content and δ* measurements to identify atypical genes in plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: A gene optimization strategy that enhances production of fully functional P-glycoprotein in Pichia pastoris.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the optimization of the mdr3 gene encoding P-glycoprotein, leading to enhanced production of a fully functional protein in Pichia pastoris.
full_output.methodology: Gene optimization based on codon usage in Pichia pastoris, cloning, expression, and functional analysis in S. cerevisiae and P. pastoris.

full_output.paper_title: Ongoing phenotypic and genomic changes in experimental coevolution of RNA bacteriophage Qβ and Escherichia coli.

A2.encodes: A2 protein, multifunctional protein involved in host cell lysis, adsorption, RNA binding, protection of 3' terminus, penetration, and blockage of cell wall biosynthesis
A2.notes: Mutations in A2 gene are responsible for increased release efficiency of phage.

traQ.notes: Mutation in traQ led to decreased propilin insertion and partial resistance

full_output.paper_title: Identification of functional toxin/immunity genes linked to contact-dependent growth inhibition (CDI) and rearrangement hotspot (Rhs) systems.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies functional toxin/immunity gene pairs in CDI and Rhs systems, showing that orphan cdiA-CT/cdiI modules and rhs-CT/rhsI modules are capable of mediating contact-dependent growth inhibition and are functionally active.
full_output.methodology: Protein binding assays, tRNase activity assays, plasmid-based expression, and growth inhibition experiments.

blaCTX-M-15.evidence_note: The paper mentions that CTX-M-15 was the most common ESBL type among all species and that ESBLs were characterized by direct sequencing of PCR products.

blaCTX-M-1.evidence_note: The paper mentions that blaCTX-M-1 was identified in E. coli and other isolates, and that ESBLs were characterized by PCR and direct sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including CTX-M-15, SHV-2a, SHV-12, CTX-M-1, and CTX-M-3, which confer resistance to third-generation cephalosporins such as ceftazidime and ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: PCR and direct sequencing were used to characterize ESBLs, along with antibiotic susceptibility testing and molecular epidemiology techniques.

full_output.key_findings: The study discusses the emergence of secondary Buruli ulcer skin lesions after completion of chemotherapy, suggesting possible immune-mediated reactions or new infection foci.
full_output.methodology: Histopathological and immunohistochemical analysis of tissue specimens from patients with secondary skin lesions after Buruli ulcer treatment.

full_output.paper_title: A multi-center randomized trial to assess the efficacy of gatifloxacin versus ciprofloxacin for the treatment of shigellosis in Vietnamese children.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that gatifloxacin and ciprofloxacin were similarly effective in treating acute shigellosis in Vietnamese children, with no significant difference in treatment failure rates. Nalidixic acid-resistant Shigella strains were prevalent, but both antibiotics cleared the bacteria effectively.
full_output.methodology: Randomized, open-label, controlled trial comparing gatifloxacin and ciprofloxacin for the treatment of shigellosis in children.

full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the pharmacokinetics of oral ciprofloxacin in children with severe malnutrition, determining optimal dosing regimens to achieve therapeutic AUC/MIC ratios against various Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Population pharmacokinetic analysis and Monte Carlo simulations were used to evaluate ciprofloxacin dosing regimens in malnourished children.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid detection of isoniazid, rifampin, and ofloxacin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates using high-resolution melting analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a high-resolution melting analysis (HRMA) assay to detect resistance to isoniazid, rifampin, and ofloxacin in Mycobacterium tuberculosis by identifying mutations in the katG, mabA-inhA promoter, rpoB, and gyrA genes.
full_output.methodology: HRMA combined with sequencing was used to identify mutations associated with drug resistance in M. tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The structure-activity relationship of urea derivatives as anti-tuberculosis agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies urea derivatives as potential anti-tuberculosis agents targeting epoxide hydrolase enzymes (EphB and EphE) in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Compounds with a 1-adamantyl-3-phenyl urea core exhibited potent activity against M. tuberculosis and inhibited EphB and EphE enzymes.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and evaluation of urea derivatives for anti-tubercular activity, enzyme inhibition assays, and structure-activity relationship analysis.

full_output.paper_title: The broadly conserved regulator PhoP links pathogen virulence and membrane potential in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: PhoP is required for E. coli virulence during acute urinary tract infection. Deletion of phoP leads to decreased resistance to polymyxin B and acid stress, and increased motility. PhoP regulates genes involved in LPS modification, acid resistance, and membrane potential.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, gene deletion mutants, complementation experiments, and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanisms of fluoroquinolone resistance in Escherichia coli isolates from food-producing animals.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: mutations in GyrA lead to resistance

gyrA.evidence_note: The paper states that all isolates harbored GyrA amino acid substitutions at positions 83 and 87, and specifically mentions Ser83 -> Leu.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple mechanisms contributing to fluoroquinolone resistance in E. coli isolates from food-producing animals, including mutations in target genes such as gyrA, parC, gyrB, and parE, as well as upregulation of the AcrAB-TolC efflux pump and decreased expression of the OmpF porin.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing, qRT-PCR, and ethidium bromide accumulation assays were used to analyze mutations and gene expression in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolates from animals presenting at a university veterinary hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in multidrug-resistant E. coli isolates from animals, including bla TEM, bla CTX-M-2, bla CMY-2, strA-strB, aadA, aphA1, aadB, cat, floR, sul1, sul2, tet(A), and tet(B). full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and conjugation assays were used to identify and validate AMR genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolates from Irish cattle farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in multidrug-resistant E. coli isolates from Irish cattle farms, including strA-strB, aphA1, aadA, aadB, blaTEM, sul2, tet(A), and tet(B). These genes were associated with resistance to streptomycin, neomycin, kanamycin, spectinomycin, ampicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, sulfonamides, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and conjugation assays were used to detect and characterize AMR genes and plasmids in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Nasal carriage of multi-drug resistant Staphylococcus aureus in healthy inhabitants of Amassoma in Niger delta region of Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of nasal carriage of multi-drug resistant Staphylococcus aureus in healthy inhabitants of Amassoma, Nigeria, with 52.5% of isolates showing resistance to three or more antibiotics, including 27.5% methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: Nasal specimens were cultured and analyzed for S. aureus using standard microbiological protocols, with antibiotic susceptibility tested via disc diffusion and agar dilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Hessian fly-associated bacteria: transmission, essentiality, and composition.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various bacteria associated with Hessian flies and their transmission, highlighting the essential role of these bacteria in the survival of the insect on wheat. It also shows that eliminating these bacteria with antibiotics significantly reduces larval survival.
full_output.methodology: The study uses PCR, FISH, culturing techniques, and qPCR to analyze bacterial communities associated with Hessian flies and their impact on insect survival.
full_output.sample_size: Various stages of Hessian flies and wheat plants

full_output.paper_title: Magnesium limitation is an environmental trigger of the Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm lifestyle.

rsmZ.validation_method: promoter lux fusion and gene expression analysis

full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis using promoter lux fusion, gene expression profiling, and biochemical assays.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genomics of multidrug resistance-encoding IncA/C plasmids from commensal and pathogenic Escherichia coli from multiple animal sources.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes multidrug resistance-encoding IncA/C plasmids from various animal sources, identifying genes such as floR, tetA, strAB, sul2, and blaCMY-2 that confer resistance to chloramphenicol, tetracycline, streptomycin/spectinomycin, sulfisoxazole, and ampicillin, respectively.

full_output.paper_title: The role of RamA on the development of ciprofloxacin resistance in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium.

full_output.paper_title: Real time enzyme inhibition assays provide insights into differences in binding of neuraminidase inhibitors to wild type and mutant influenza viruses.

full_output.paper_title: Recombination in IS26 and Tn2 in the evolution of multiresistance regions carrying blaCTX-M-15 on conjugative IncF plasmids from Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaCTX-M-15 as a dominant extended-spectrum beta-lactamase gene in Escherichia coli, carried on conjugative IncF plasmids. It highlights the role of IS26 and Tn2 in the evolution of multiresistance regions.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid analysis, S1 nuclease digestion, PFGE, PCR, and DNA sequencing were used to characterize the multiresistance regions.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenems: past, present, and future.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the history, chemistry, biology, and resistance mechanisms of carbapenems, highlighting their role as last-line antibiotics and the emerging threats posed by resistance mechanisms such as β-lactamases, efflux pumps, and porin loss.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature and studies on carbapenems.

full_output.paper_title: Dynamics of mutator and antibiotic-resistant populations in a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model of Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm treatment.
