E1.evidence_note: The paper describes the mutation E1.T101M as conferring resistance to 8B10-dependent neutralization, as supported by PRNT and binding assays.

mutations_found.validated_by: viral fitness assays and cell-to-cell transmission experiments

E2.notes: Mutations in E2 protein associated with resistance to 5F10 and 8B10 neutralizing antibodies and enhanced cell-to-cell transmission.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies key amino acid substitutions in the E1 and E2 glycoproteins of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) that confer resistance to neutralizing antibodies 5F10 and 8B10. Specifically, E2.V216E and E1.T101M abolish the binding of 5F10 and 8B10, respectively, while E2.R82G enhances CHIKV cell-to-cell transmission.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized plaque reduction neutralization tests (PRNT), sequencing, and binding assays to analyze CHIKV mutants and their resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Thiadiazolidinones: a new class of alanine racemase inhibitors with antimicrobial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies L2-401, a novel thiadiazolidinone inhibitor of alanine racemase (Alr) from Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating its ability to irreversibly inhibit Alr and exhibit selective antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria and fungi.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, enzyme inhibition assays, MIC determination, and structural analysis were used to evaluate the activity and mechanism of L2-401.

full_output.paper_title: Helicobacter pylori antibiotic resistance in Brazil: clarithromycin is still a good option
full_output.key_findings: The study found that clarithromycin resistance in H. pylori was relatively low (8%) in an urban Brazilian population, suggesting that it remains a viable option for first-line therapy. Resistance to metronidazole was high (51%), while no resistance was observed to amoxicillin, tetracycline, or furazolidone.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the E-test and agar dilution method for various antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance to topoisomerase cleavage complex induced lethality in Escherichia coli via titration of transcription regulators PurR and FNR.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that titration of the transcription regulators FNR and PurR by plasmid clones can confer resistance to cell killing mediated by mutant topoisomerase I cleavage complex and norfloxacin. Chromosomal mutations in fnr and purR were found to increase resistance to topoisomerase I cleavage complex and norfloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used plasmid clones, chromosomal mutations, and cell viability assays to investigate the role of FNR and PurR in resistance to topoisomerase I cleavage complex and norfloxacin.

full_output.paper_title: Inactivation of a class A and a class C β-lactamase by 6β-(hydroxymethyl)penicillanic acid sulfone.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the effectiveness of 6β-HM-sulfone as an inhibitor of the class A β-lactamase TEM-1 and the class C β-lactamase PDC-3, showing significant inactivation of these enzymes and enhancing the efficacy of ampicillin against resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used inhibition assays, kinetic studies, and mass spectrometry to evaluate the effects of 6β-HM-sulfone on β-lactamases TEM-1 and PDC-3.

full_output.paper_title: Surface-localized spermidine protects the Pseudomonas aeruginosa outer membrane from antibiotic treatment and oxidative stress.
full_output.key_findings: PA4774 is involved in spermidine synthesis and plays a role in protecting the outer membrane of Pseudomonas aeruginosa from polymyxin B and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, complementation, and NPN uptake assays were used to investigate the role of PA4774 in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of nasal and blood culture isolates of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus from patients in United States Hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates from nasal and blood cultures, identifying spa types and SCC mec types, and highlights the increasing prevalence of USA300 isolates in blood cultures compared to USA100 isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used spa typing, SCC mec typing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to characterize MRSA isolates from 299 nasal and 194 blood cultures.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of unique modification of flagellar rod protein FlgG by Campylobacter jejuni lipid A phosphoethanolamine transferase, linking bacterial locomotion and antimicrobial peptide resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies EptC as a phosphoethanolamine transferase that modifies FlgG at Thr 75, which is crucial for bacterial motility. Additionally, EptC-mediated phosphoethanolamine modification of lipid A provides resistance to antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.methodology: Mass spectrometry, site-directed mutagenesis, and motility assays were used to characterize the modification of FlgG and its effects on bacterial motility and antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: A report on the first case of vancomycin-intermediate Staphylococcus aureus (VISA) in Hawai'i.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reports the first case of vancomycin-intermediate Staphylococcus aureus (VISA) in Hawai'i, highlighting the emergence of VISA strains with reduced susceptibility to vancomycin, emphasizing the need for accurate detection methods and appropriate antibiotic therapy.
full_output.methodology: Clinical case report with antimicrobial susceptibility testing and molecular analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of community-acquired extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli (ESBLEC) in Honolulu, highlighting the presence of blaCTX-M genes responsible for resistance to cephalosporins and aztreonam.
full_output.methodology: Double disk diffusion and MIC analysis were used to confirm the presence of ESBLEC.

full_output.paper_title: AcrB trimer stability and efflux activity, insight from mutagenesis studies.

AcrB.notes: Mutation of P223 to Gly drastically reduced AcrB activity.
AcrB.evidence_note: The paper states that the P223G mutation drastically reduced the activity of AcrB, indicating that this mutation affects the function of the efflux pump.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the role of AcrB trimer stability and efflux activity, showing that mutation of P223 to Gly reduces AcrB activity and disrupts trimer stability.
full_output.methodology: Mutagenesis studies, MIC testing, Western blot analysis, CD spectroscopy, disulfide trapping, and BN-PAGE analysis.

full_output.paper_title: The epidemiology of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in Germany.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the epidemiology of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in Germany, highlighting the prevalence of MRSA in hospitals, homes for the elderly, and care homes, as well as the emergence of community-associated (CA-MRSA) and livestock-associated (LA-MRSA) strains. It discusses the importance of MRSA surveillance and prevention strategies.
full_output.methodology: The paper is a review based on a selective PubMed search and publications from national reference institutions up to 2010.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of novel MDR-Mycobacterium tuberculosis inhibitor by new FRIGATE computational screen.

ag85c.validation_method: NMR binding assay and antibacterial activity testing
ag85c.evidence_note: The paper describes Ag85C as a target for inhibitors, but does not explicitly state that it is an acquired AMR gene. It is involved in cell wall biosynthesis and is a target for small molecule inhibitors.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the identification of a novel small molecule inhibitor, compound 1, targeting the catalytic site of Ag85C, a critical enzyme in Mycobacterium tuberculosis cell wall biosynthesis. Compound 1 exhibited potent antibacterial activity against both Msmeg and MDR-Mtb.
full_output.methodology: Computational docking using FRIGATE, NMR binding assays, and antibacterial activity testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a real-time PCR antibiogram method for rapid susceptibility testing of septicemia, which detects antimicrobial resistance by monitoring pathogenic load through the 16S rRNA gene in blood samples exposed to different antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The method involves real-time PCR to monitor bacterial load after antibiotic exposure, with validation through culture and sequencing.
full_output.sample_size: Three strains of E. coli, two of which were antimicrobial resistant, were spiked into whole blood.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of sub-inhibitory antibiotics on fibronectin-mediated host cell adhesion and invasion by Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Sub-inhibitory concentrations of oxacillin, moxifloxacin, and linezolid increased fibronectin-binding protein (fnbA and fnbB) expression and adhesion of Staphylococcus aureus to fibronectin, while rifampin decreased fibronectin binding without affecting fnbA/B transcription.
full_output.methodology: Examination of fnbA and fnbB mRNA levels via qRT-PCR, fibronectin adhesion assays, and bacterial adhesion/invasion assays in human osteoblasts.

full_output.paper_title: Bisubstrate analogue inhibitors of 6-hydroxymethyl-7,8-dihydropterin pyrophosphokinase: New design with improved properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design and characterization of new bisubstrate analogue inhibitors of 6-hydroxymethyl-7,8-dihydropterin pyrophosphokinase (HPPK), focusing on improving binding affinity and stability. Compounds 17, 18, and 19 were synthesized and evaluated for their inhibitory activity against HPPK.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of new inhibitors, determination of their binding affinities (Kd) and inhibitory potencies (IC50), and structural analysis of their complexes with HPPK using crystallography.

full_output.paper_title: Real-time PCR and high-resolution melt analysis for rapid detection of Mycobacterium leprae drug resistance mutations and strain types.

folP1.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the folP1 gene encodes dihydropteroate synthase and that mutations in folP1, such as CCC->CTC at position 55, confer resistance to dapsone. The paper also states that these mutations were detected in clinical strains and validated by sequencing.

rpoB.notes: Detected in clinical strains
rpoB.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that mutations in rpoB confer resistance to rifampin and provides the specific nucleotide changes (GAT->TAT, CAC->TAC, TCG->TTG) and their corresponding protein changes (D441Y, H451Y, S456L). The mutations were observed in clinical strains of Mycobacterium leprae and validated by sequencing.

gyrA.notes: Detected in clinical strains
gyrA.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the gyrA mutation (A91V) was identified in clinical strains and validated by sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed real-time PCR-high-resolution melt (PCR-HRM) assays for detecting drug resistance mutations in Mycobacterium leprae, focusing on folP1, rpoB, and gyrA genes associated with dapsone, rifampin, and fluoroquinolone resistance, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR-HRM analysis was used to detect mutations in drug resistance-determining regions (DRDRs) of folP1, rpoB, and gyrA genes in M. leprae clinical strains.
full_output.sample_size: 121 clinical strains from the Philippines and 25 from Nepal

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and characterization of Staphylococcus aureus, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, isolated from bulk tank milk from Minnesota dairy farms.

mutations_found.nucleotide_change: different regions of the open reading frame (ORF) of the mecA gene
mutations_found.position_in_molecule: open reading frame (ORF) of the mecA gene

mecA.notes: The mecA gene was detected in the two MRSA isolates, and it conferred resistance to beta-lactams.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified two methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates from bulk tank milk, which showed resistance to beta-lactams, lincosamides, and other antibiotic classes. The mecA gene was responsible for methicillin resistance in these isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to identify and characterize S. aureus isolates, including MRSA, from bulk tank milk samples.
full_output.sample_size: 150 bulk tank milk samples from 50 farms

full_output.paper_title: Methylation and in vivo expression of the surface-exposed Leptospira interrogans outer-membrane protein OmpL32.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes OmpL32, a surface-exposed outer-membrane protein of Leptospira interrogans, which undergoes differential glutamic acid methylation under various environmental conditions.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis, immunofluorescence, and biochemical techniques were used to characterize OmpL32 and its methylation patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Brucella abortus choloylglycine hydrolase affects cell envelope composition and host cell internalization.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the role of Brucella abortus choloylglycine hydrolase (CGH) in deconjugating bile salts and resisting their antimicrobial action, leading to alterations in cell envelope composition and host cell internalization.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic deletion mutants, proteomic analysis, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of CGH in Brucella abortus.

full_output.paper_title: Development of derivatives of 3, 3'-diindolylmethane as potent Leishmania donovani bi-subunit topoisomerase IB poisons.

LdTOP1L.encodes: large subunit of DNA topoisomerase I

mutations_found.effect_on_function: resistance to DIM up to 50 µM concentration
mutations_found.validated_by: experimental validation through cloning and testing of mutant enzyme

LdTOP1L.notes: Mutation in the large subunit of LdTOP1LS

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a point mutation F270L in the large subunit of LdTOP1LS responsible for resistance to DIM and characterizes three DIM derivatives (DPDIM, DMDIM, DMODIM) that inhibit the growth of DIM-resistant parasites and stabilize topoisomerase I-DNA cleavable complexes.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular cloning, plasmid relaxation assays, plasmid cleavage assays, and molecular docking to characterize the effects of DIM derivatives on Leishmania donovani topoisomerase I.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm Formation and Antimicrobial Resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies changes in gene expression and protein production in biofilm-forming Streptococcus pneumoniae, highlighting the down-regulation of capsule production and the up-regulation of adhesins like PsrP and CbpA, which contribute to the hyper-adhesive phenotype. However, no specific AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, qRT-PCR, ELISA, and immunoblotting were used to analyze gene expression and protein production in biofilm-forming S. pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the conformational dynamics of the EmrE transporter, showing that it exchanges between inward- and outward-facing states in an antiparallel asymmetric dimer configuration, which is crucial for its function in exporting polyaromatic cation substrates.
full_output.methodology: The study uses NMR spectroscopy, FRET, and cross-linking experiments to investigate the conformational dynamics and topology of EmrE.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes a suicidal mutant selection system in Staphylococcus carnosus based on the inactive precursor of the lantibiotic gallidermin, which enables the efficient identification of plasmid-free mutants.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic engineering and mutagenesis techniques to develop a selection system based on the activation of gallidermin by the protease GdmP.

full_output.paper_title: Drug resistance to paclitaxel is not only associated with ABCB1 mRNA expression but also with drug accumulation in intracellular compartments in human lung cancer cell lines.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that resistance to paclitaxel in lung cancer cell lines is not solely linked to ABCB1 mRNA expression but also involves the intracellular accumulation of the drug in lysosomal and extra-lysosomal compartments. No mutations in the β-tubulin gene were identified as a factor in resistance.
full_output.methodology: Real-time RT-PCR, cytotoxicity assays, and live cell imaging were used to analyze gene expression, drug accumulation, and cellular responses to paclitaxel.
full_output.sample_size: Three human lung cancer cell lines (RERF-LC-KJ, A549, and II18) were used.

full_output.paper_title: Endemic Acinetobacter baumannii in a New York hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a novel Class I integron sequence in a prevalent strain of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, which was associated with carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and molecular epidemiology techniques were used to analyze the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Battacin (Octapeptin B5), a new cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic from Paenibacillus tianmuensis active against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies battacin (Octapeptin B5), a new cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic produced by Paenibacillus tianmuensis, which shows potent activity against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation, purification, and structural elucidation of battacin, along with in vitro and in vivo evaluations of its antimicrobial activity and mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Neisseria gonorrhoeae With High-Level Resistance to Azithromycin: Case Report of the First Isolate Identified in the United States.
full_output.key_findings: The first Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolate in the United States with high-level resistance to azithromycin was identified. The isolate exhibited a mutation in the 23S rRNA gene (A2059G) associated with macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization of the isolate, including sequencing of the 23S rRNA gene and PCR for resistance-associated mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Dissemination of the Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase in the health care settings: tracking the trails of an elusive offender.

blaKPC.validation_method: tracking the trail of dissemination of the bla KPC gene
blaKPC.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The article discusses the dissemination of the Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC) and highlights the role of the blaKPC gene in the spread of carbapenem resistance, primarily through plasmid transfer and clonal spread.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of previous studies on KPC dissemination.

full_output.paper_title: High proportion of fluoroquinolone-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates with novel gyrase polymorphisms and a gyrA region associated with fluoroquinolone susceptibility.

gyrA.notes: These mutations were identified in fluoroquinolone-resistant isolates and are associated with reduced susceptibility to fluoroquinolones.

gyrB.notes: This mutation was identified in a fluoroquinolone-resistant isolate and is associated with reduced susceptibility to fluoroquinolones.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified novel gyrase polymorphisms in fluoroquinolone-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates, including mutations in the QRDR of gyrA (Met81Thr, Leu109Pro, Gln113Leu) and a mutation in the QRDR of gyrB (Asn538Ile). These mutations are associated with reduced susceptibility to fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sequencing the complete gyrA and gyrB genes of M. tuberculosis isolates and correlating genetic variations with phenotypic fluoroquinolone resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of ST772-MRSA-V, a PVL-positive and multiantibiotic-resistant MRSA strain in Ireland, highlighting its potential for hospital and community transmission.
full_output.methodology: DNA microarray analysis, spa typing, and antimicrobial resistance profiling were used to characterize the MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) carriage in a dermatology unit.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized MRSA carriage in a dermatology unit, identifying the mecA gene as a key determinant of methicillin resistance in MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular typing techniques were used to identify MRSA isolates and their resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Class 2 integrons dissemination among multidrug resistance (MDR) clones of Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals the widespread dissemination of class 2 integrons among multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from Argentina and Uruguay, highlighting the presence of the typical Tn7::In2-7 array in most isolates and the persistence of unique clones contributing to the high frequency of class 2 integrons.
full_output.methodology: Molecular surveillance, PCR, sequencing, and clonal analysis were used to investigate class 2 integrons in A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin resistance among methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates from intensive care units of tertiary care hospitals in Hyderabad.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vancomycin resistance among methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates, with six out of seven vancomycin-resistant S. aureus (VRSA) isolates carrying the vanA gene.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, MIC determination, and PCR amplification for vanA gene detection.

full_output.key_findings: The study compares the antimicrobial efficacy of doripenem and imipenem against ciprofloxacin-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa, focusing on their ability to prevent the enrichment of resistant subpopulations.
full_output.methodology: The study uses an in vitro dynamic model to simulate pharmacokinetic profiles and assess antimicrobial effects, including time-kill curves and mutant prevention concentrations.
full_output.sample_size: Three clinical isolates of ciprofloxacin-resistant P. aeruginosa

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of antimicrobial resistance among clinical isolates of Bacteroides fragilis group in Canada in 2010-2011: CANWARD surveillance study.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports high rates of resistance among Bacteroides fragilis group isolates in Canada, with particular resistance to clindamycin, moxifloxacin, and cefoxitin. Multidrug-resistant isolates were prevalent, especially among B. ovatus and B. thetaiotaomicron.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using broth microdilution methods according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time of flight mass spectrometry-based functional assay for rapid detection of resistance against β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes a MALDI-TOF MS-based assay for detecting β-lactam resistance by analyzing the hydrolysis of β-lactam antibiotics by β-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: The study uses MALDI-TOF MS to detect the hydrolysis of β-lactam antibiotics by β-lactamases in various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence of diversity among epidemiologically related carbapenemase-producing Acinetobacter baumannii strains belonging to international clonal lineage II.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaOXA-23 and blaOXA-58 as carbapenem resistance genes in Acinetobacter baumannii strains belonging to international clonal lineage II, highlighting their prevalence and genetic context.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MLVA-8, Southern blot hybridization, and sequencing to analyze genetic diversity and resistance mechanisms in A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of the role of Bacillus subtilis σ(M) in β-lactam resistance reveals an essential role for c-di-AMP in peptidoglycan homeostasis.

gdpP.mechanism: Inactivation of gdpP restores cefuroxime resistance in a sigM mutant
gdpP.validation_method: Tn7 mutagenesis and suppression of cefuroxime sensitivity

rsiX.mechanism: rsiX::Tn7 insertion increases β-lactam resistance by upregulating σ X

disA.validation_method: genetic manipulation and disk diffusion assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies gdpP, rsiX, and clpP as critical genes involved in cefuroxime resistance in Bacillus subtilis, highlighting the role of c-di-AMP and regulatory pathways in β-lactam resistance.
full_output.methodology: Tn7 mutagenesis, genetic analysis, and resistance assays were used to identify and characterize genes involved in cefuroxime resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Clonally related Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates with decreased susceptibility to the extended-spectrum cephalosporin cefotaxime in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

mutations_found.nucleotide_change: A deletion in the promoter region of mtrR
mutations_found.protein_change: overexpression of the MtrCDE efflux pump

full_output.paper_title: Helicobacter pylori versus the host: remodeling of the bacterial outer membrane is required for survival in the gastric mucosa.

jhp1487.validation_method: in vitro assay using radiolabeled Kdo2-[4′-32P]lipid A, TLC, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies jhp1487 as the gene encoding the lipid A 4′-phosphatase LpxF in H. pylori, which is crucial for resistance to cationic antimicrobial peptides and for host colonization.
full_output.methodology: In vitro enzyme assays, TLC, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and MIC testing were used to validate the function of jhp1487.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic expression analysis reveals strategies of Burkholderia cenocepacia to adapt to cystic fibrosis patients' airways and antimicrobial therapy.

mdtABC.encodes: Multidrug efflux transporter of the Resistance Nodulation Family

bpeA.encodes: Subunit of the drug efflux transporter RND4

BCAM2188.encodes: Component of a putative macrolide-specific efflux transporter

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several efflux pump genes (mdtABC, bpeA, BCAM0201, BCAM2188, BCAM0791) that are up-regulated in the more antibiotic-resistant B. cenocepacia isolate IST4113, contributing to its increased resistance to various antimicrobial classes.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis using DNA microarrays and qRT-PCR to compare gene expression between two B. cenocepacia isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Two clonal variants of B. cenocepacia

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium abscessus glycopeptidolipid prevents respiratory epithelial TLR2 signaling as measured by HβD2 gene expression and IL-8 release.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mmpL4b gene as crucial for GPL biosynthesis in Mycobacterium abscessus. Deletion of mmpL4b results in loss of GPL expression, allowing the bacterium to stimulate TLR2 signaling in respiratory epithelial cells.
full_output.methodology: The study uses gene deletion mutants, real-time PCR, and ELISA to assess the impact of mmpL4b deletion on TLR2 signaling and immune response in respiratory epithelial cells.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activity of doripenem against Gram-negative pathogens: results from INVITA-A-DORI Brazilian study.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of doripenem against Gram-negative pathogens, showing it to be as active as meropenem and more active than imipenem against E. coli and K. pneumoniae. It also showed potent activity against Acinetobacter spp. and P. aeruginosa, retaining some activity against imipenem-resistant P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the CLSI microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of bla (CTX M) extended spectrum beta lactamase gene in enterobacteriaceae from critical care patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected the blaCTX-M gene in 45.7% of Enterobacteriaceae isolates from critical care patients, highlighting the prevalence of CTX-M extended-spectrum beta-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic confirmation via double disc synergy test, minimum inhibitory concentration, and multiplex PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Rising prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in urinary tract infections during pregnancy: necessity for exploring newer treatment options.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in urinary tract infections during pregnancy, with significant resistance to β-lactam antibiotics, fluoroquinolones, and aminoglycosides. ESBL-producing E. coli and K. pneumoniae were prevalent, and MRSA was detected in Staphylococcus species. Carbapenems and glycopeptides remained effective.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of clinical multiresistant isolates of Acinetobacter sp. from hospitals in Porto Alegre, State of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-23 and blaOXA-51 genes as significant contributors to carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter sp. isolates from hospitals in Porto Alegre, Brazil.
full_output.methodology: PCR, phenotypic testing, and ERIC-PCR for molecular typing.

full_output.paper_title: Hemin Binding Protein C Is Found in Outer Membrane Vesicles and Protects Bartonella henselae against Toxic Concentrations of Hemin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies HbpC as a hemin-binding protein in Bartonella henselae that contributes to resistance against toxic hemin concentrations. Constitutive expression of hbpC increases hemin binding and protects B. henselae from hemin toxicity.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, RT-PCR, Western blot, hemin binding assays, and OMV isolation.

full_output.paper_title: Myxobacterium-produced antibiotic TA (myxovirescin) inhibits type II signal peptidase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified lspA as the molecular target of antibiotic TA, showing that overexpression of lspA confers resistance to TA in E. coli. Additionally, mutations in lpp were found to confer TA resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screens, mutant isolation, and biochemical assays were used to determine the molecular target of TA.

full_output.paper_title: Changing trends in antimicrobial resistance and serotypes of Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates in Asian countries: an Asian Network for Surveillance of Resistant Pathogens (ANSORP) study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of erythromycin resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates from Asian countries, primarily mediated by the erm(B) and mef(A) genes. full_output.methodology: The study conducted PCR analysis to detect erm(B) and mef(A) genes in erythromycin-resistant S. pneumoniae isolates and analyzed antimicrobial susceptibility patterns.

full_output.paper_title: blaKPC and rmtB on a single plasmid in Enterobacter amnigenus and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from the same patient.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the identification of blaKPC-2 and rmtB genes on a single plasmid in Enterobacter amnigenus and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from the same patient, highlighting the coexistence of carbapenem and aminoglycoside resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, plasmid analysis, PFGE, and MLST were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms and molecular epidemiology of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Active and passive immunization protects against lethal, extreme drug resistant-Acinetobacter baumannii infection.

Vaccination with recombinant OmpA (rOmpA) significantly improves survival and reduces bacterial burden in diabetic mice infected with XDR A. baumannii.

full_output.methodology: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and DNA sequencing were used to detect the presence of blaNDM and blaVIM genes.

full_output.paper_title: Resident Cats in Small Animal Veterinary Hospitals Carry Multi-Drug Resistant Enterococci and are Likely Involved in Cross-Contamination of the Hospital Environment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanB-mediated vancomycin resistance in Enterococcus faecalis isolates from resident cats in small animal veterinary hospitals, highlighting the potential role of these cats in the cross-contamination of hospital environments with multidrug-resistant enterococci.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR amplification, and conjugation assays were used to characterize resistance mechanisms in enterococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a novel gene product that promotes survival of Mycobacterium smegmatis in macrophages.

aphA3.mechanism: confers resistance to kanamycin and gentamicin by modifying the antibiotic

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MSMEG_5817 as a gene involved in the intracellular survival of Mycobacterium smegmatis within macrophages. Disruption of MSMEG_5817 leads to reduced intracellular survival, and complementation restores survival to wild-type levels.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, Southern hybridization, and complementation experiments were used to investigate the role of MSMEG_5817 in macrophage survival.

full_output.paper_title: A stress-inducible quorum-sensing peptide mediates the formation of persister cells with noninherited multidrug tolerance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rnhB, scrR, and fruA as genes involved in persister formation in Streptococcus mutans, highlighting the role of stress-inducible quorum-sensing peptides in mediating multidrug tolerance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, persistence assays, and molecular biology techniques were used to identify and characterize genes involved in persister formation.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of biocides used in the modern food industry to control salmonella enterica, and links between biocide tolerance and resistance to clinically relevant antimicrobial compounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the tolerance of Salmonella enterica strains to various biocides and found that while some isolates developed tolerance to specific biocidal agents, there was no significant correlation between biocide tolerance and resistance to clinically relevant antimicrobial compounds.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted biocide susceptibility testing, antibiotic susceptibility profiling, and biofilm formation assays on a collection of Salmonella strains.

full_output.paper_title: Feminizing Wolbachia: a transcriptomics approach with insights on the immune response genes in Armadillidium vulgare.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several immune-related genes in Armadillidium vulgare, including genes involved in pathogen recognition, immune response, and stress response, but none of these genes were found to confer antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis using EST libraries and RT-qPCR to compare gene expression between Wolbachia-infected and uninfected A. vulgare.

rpoB.notes: Synonymous mutation in rpoB gene

katG.notes: Mutation in katG gene

full_output.paper_title: Resistance to DDT and pyrethroids and increased kdr mutation frequency in An. gambiae after the implementation of permethrin-treated nets in Senegal.

kdr.notes: The L1014F mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene is associated with resistance to DDT and pyrethroids.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that An. gambiae mosquitoes in Dielmo, Senegal, developed resistance to DDT and pyrethroids, with a significant increase in the frequency of the L1014F kdr mutation after the implementation of permethrin-treated nets.
full_output.methodology: The study used WHO bioassay susceptibility tests, PCR for kdr mutation detection, and statistical analysis to evaluate resistance and mutation frequencies.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of the peptidoglycan hydrolase complement of Lactobacillus casei and characterization of the major γ-D-glutamyl-L-lysyl-endopeptidase.

LCABL_02770.mechanism: hydrolysis of peptidoglycan bonds inside the stem peptide between D-iGln and L-Lys

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes Lc-p75, a major γ-D-glutamyl-L-lysyl-endopeptidase in Lactobacillus casei BL23, which plays a critical role in daughter cell separation and peptidoglycan remodeling.
full_output.methodology: In silico analysis, proteomic approaches, biochemical assays, and genetic studies were used to identify and characterize Lc-p75.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of antibiotics on Shiga toxin 2 production and bacteriophage induction by epidemic Escherichia coli O104:H4 strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of various antibiotics on Shiga toxin 2 (Stx2) production and bacteriophage induction in the E. coli O104:H4 strain. Ciprofloxacin was found to significantly increase Stx2 production and phage induction, while chloramphenicol, meropenem, azithromycin, rifaximin, and tigecycline decreased these effects.
full_output.methodology: The study used subinhibitory concentrations of antibiotics to assess their effects on Stx2 production and phage induction in E. coli O104:H4 isolates through plaque assays, real-time PCR, and Vero cell assays.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and transcriptomic analysis of Streptomyces erythraea Px and NRRL 2338 for improved erythromycin production

mutations_found.position_in_molecule: chromosomal region spanning the pepQ-efp-nusB and bldD genes
chromosomal region spanning the pepQ-efp-nusB and bldD genes

gatA.encodes: Asp-tRNA Asn/Glu-tRNA Gln amidotransferase A subunit

SACE_5919.notes: Frameshift mutation inactivating a paralogous gene

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in nusB and efp genes in Streptomyces erythraea Px strain, which are involved in transcription antitermination and protein synthesis, respectively. These mutations may contribute to the improved erythromycin production by altering the transcriptional and translational machinery.
full_output.methodology: Genomic and transcriptomic analysis, including DNA microarray experiments and sequencing, were performed to compare S. erythraea Px and NRRL 2338 strains.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, characterization, and antimicrobial activity of silver carbene complexes derived from 4,5,6,7-tetrachlorobenzimidazole against antibiotic resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and antimicrobial activity of silver carbene complexes (SCCs) derived from 4,5,6,7-tetrachlorobenzimidazole against antibiotic-resistant bacteria, showing effectiveness against various strains including MRSA and silver-resistant E. coli.
full_output.methodology: The paper describes the synthesis, characterization, and in vitro antimicrobial testing of silver carbene complexes using broth microdilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Differential expression of iron acquisition genes by Brucella melitensis and Brucella canis during macrophage infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies differences in iron acquisition gene expression between Brucella melitensis and Brucella canis during macrophage infection, highlighting distinct strategies for intracellular survival.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis of Brucella species during macrophage infection using microarrays and real-time PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidinedione derivatives as antibacterial agents.
full_output.key_findings: Two thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidinedione derivatives, compounds 1 and 2, exhibited potent antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Gram-positive bacteria, including MRSA, VISA, VRSA, and VRE. Compound 2 showed selective antibacterial activity with low cytotoxicity and minimal hemolytic activity.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidinedione derivatives and evaluation of their antibacterial, cytotoxic, and hemolytic activities.

full_output.paper_title: Dissecting phosphite-induced priming in Arabidopsis infected with Hyaloperonospora arabidopsidis.

mutations_found.validated_by: gene expression, protein accumulation, and phosphorylation analysis

MPK4.notes: MPK4 is negatively regulated by Phi, leading to priming of SA-dependent defenses.

full_output.key_findings: Phi primes SA-dependent defenses in Arabidopsis against Hpa by down-regulating MPK4, a negative regulator of SAR.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression, protein accumulation, and phosphorylation analysis were used to determine the role of MPK4 in Phi-induced priming.

full_output.paper_title: Generation of a novel nucleic acid-based reporter system to detect phenotypic susceptibility to antibiotics in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a novel phage-based reporter system (SGM) that generates a synthetic nucleic acid marker (SML) to detect antibiotic susceptibility in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The system effectively reported resistance to rifampin and ethambutol within 16 hours of drug exposure.
full_output.methodology: The researchers constructed a recombinant mycobacteriophage (phSP6-ProPol) carrying a synthetic genetic module (SGM) that produces a surrogate marker RNA (SML) upon successful phage infection. The SML was detected via RT-PCR to assess bacterial viability and antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and in vitro evaluation of novel lipophilic monophosphorylated gemcitabine derivatives and their nanoparticles.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on synthesizing novel lipophilic monophosphorylated gemcitabine derivatives and their nanoparticles to overcome gemcitabine resistance mechanisms in cancer cells. These derivatives showed increased cytotoxicity compared to gemcitabine HCl in cells with deficiencies in dCK, hENT1, or overexpression of RRM1 or RRM2.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis of gemcitabine derivatives, preparation of nanoparticles, in vitro cytotoxicity assays, and evaluation of resistance mechanisms in cancer cell lines.

full_output.paper_title: Dynamics of ampicillin-resistant Enterococcus faecium clones colonizing hospitalized patients: data from a prospective observational study.

MT159.validation_method: MLVA typing and isolation from rectal swabs

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MT159 as the predominant ampicillin-resistant Enterococcus faecium clone in hospitalized patients, showing its persistence and association with invasive infections.
full_output.methodology: Prospective observational study with MLVA typing and rectal swab analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 5 up-regulated and 19 down-regulated proteins in C. burnetii under tetracycline stress conditions, suggesting potential mechanisms of tetracycline resistance, although no specific AMR genes or mutations were experimentally validated.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative proteome profiling using COFRADIC and LC-MS/MS analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Reversal of the ΔdegP phenotypes by a novel rpoE allele of Escherichia coli.

mutations_found.validated_by: PCR analysis, sequencing, and Western blot analysis of sigma E levels

full_output.key_findings: A novel rpoE allele, rpoE3, was identified that partially reverses the growth and envelope vesiculation phenotypes of a ΔdegP strain by increasing sigma E levels without reducing major outer membrane protein levels.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, PCR, sequencing, Western blot analysis, and growth curve analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Small-molecule inhibitors of bacterial AddAB and RecBCD helicase-nuclease DNA repair enzymes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several small-molecule inhibitors targeting the RecBCD and AddAB helicase-nuclease enzymes, which play crucial roles in DNA repair and recombination in bacteria. These inhibitors show potent activity in both purified enzyme and cell-based assays.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, direct enzyme assays, and cell-based assays were used to identify and characterize the inhibitors.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a range of vectors for allelic replacement in Staphylococcus aureus, incorporating a pyrFE/FOA-based counterselection system. These vectors enable efficient generation of mutants by utilizing a stringent counterselection method based on 5-fluoroorotic acid (FOA) resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study developed vectors for allelic replacement in S. aureus, employing a pyrFE/FOA-based counterselection system. The vectors were constructed with various antibiotic resistance genes and conditional replication origins to facilitate genetic manipulations.

full_output.paper_title: NDM-1 in the Indian environment: hitherto the problem is not disquieting.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the presence of blaNDM-1 in environmental and stool samples in Aligarh, India, and found no evidence of NDM-1-producing bacteria.
full_output.methodology: PCR analysis for detection of blaNDM-1 in environmental and clinical samples.
full_output.sample_size: 90 environmental samples, 40 stool samples from healthy volunteers, 150 stool samples from children

full_output.paper_title: Development of a single-gene, signature-tag-based approach in combination with alanine mutagenesis to identify listeriolysin O residues critical for the in vivo survival of Listeria monocytogenes.
Peptidoglycan-modifying enzyme Pgp1 is required for helical cell shape and pathogenicity traits in Campylobacter jejuni.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pgp1 as a novel peptidoglycan DL-carboxypeptidase involved in maintaining the helical shape of Campylobacter jejuni, which affects pathogenicity traits such as chick colonization, biofilm formation, and IL-8 secretion.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, peptidoglycan analysis, and biochemical assays were used to characterize the function of pgp1.

full_output.paper_title: ZntR-mediated transcription of zntA responds to nanomolar intracellular free zinc.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the roles of ZntA and ZitB in zinc detoxification in E. coli, showing that ZntA is crucial for sustaining low intracellular free zinc levels, while ZitB acts as a first-line defense against zinc influx.
full_output.methodology: Used RT-PCR and intracellular zinc measurements to assess gene expression and zinc concentrations in E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: Increased levels of multiresistant bacteria and resistance genes after wastewater treatment and their dissemination into lake geneva, Switzerland.

sul1.mechanism: gene encoding a dihydropteroate synthase variant that confers resistance to sulfonamides

sul2.mechanism: gene encoding a dihydropteroate synthase variant that confers resistance to sulfonamides

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of sulfonamide resistance genes sul1 and sul2 in wastewater and lake samples, indicating the spread of multidrug-resistant bacteria after wastewater treatment.
full_output.methodology: Culture-based methods, PCR, plasmid analysis, and real-time qPCR were used to detect and quantify resistance genes and multidrug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple samples collected from wastewater, lake water, and sediments near Lausanne.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors, molecular epidemiology and outcomes of ertapenem-resistant, carbapenem-susceptible Enterobacteriaceae: a case-case-control study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified SHV, TEM, CTX-M, and AmpC beta-lactamases as the primary resistance mechanisms in ertapenem-resistant, carbapenem-susceptible Enterobacteriaceae (ERE). These genes were found to confer resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to identify resistance genes in ERE isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 29 ERE cases, 29 ESE cases, and 87 controls

full_output.paper_title: Efficient production of polymyxin in the surrogate host Bacillus subtilis by introducing a foreign ectB gene and disrupting the abrB gene.

ectB.validation_method: introduction of ectB gene into BSK3S leading to polymyxin production without exogenous Dab

spo0A.notes: Spo0A is required for polymyxin production

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that introducing the ectB gene and disrupting the abrB gene in Bacillus subtilis enables efficient production of polymyxin without exogenous Dab. Spo0A is essential for polymyxin production, while abrB disruption enhances it.
full_output.methodology: Gene introduction, mutagenesis, and antimicrobial activity assays were used to validate the findings.

full_output.paper_title: The PhoP/PhoQ system and its role in Serratia marcescens pathogenesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mgtE1 as a PhoP-regulated gene in Serratia marcescens, which is involved in magnesium homeostasis and responds to environmental signals such as low Mg2+, acidic pH, and polymyxin B.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional fusion, β-galactosidase activity assays, and genetic manipulation of the phoPQ operon.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates PCR assays for distinguishing true nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae (NTHi) from Haemophilus haemolyticus (Hh). The hpd#3 real-time PCR assay was found to be the most effective for differentiation.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR assays targeting various genes, including hpd, omp P2, omp P6, lgtC, 16S rRNA, fucK, and iga, along with sequence analysis of 16S rRNA and recA genes to evaluate the effectiveness of different assays in distinguishing NTHi from Hh.

full_output.paper_title: tkt1, located on a novel pathogenicity island, is prevalent in avian and human extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli.

tkt1.validation_method: Phenotype Microarray assay and complementation assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies tkt1 as a gene associated with avian and human extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli (ExPEC), located on a novel genomic island. Functional analysis showed that Tkt1 is involved in peptide nitrogen metabolism and does not confer antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Phenotype Microarray assay, and complementation assay were used to analyze the function and prevalence of tkt1.
full_output.sample_size: 96 APEC strains, 48 avian fecal E. coli strains, 94 UPEC strains, and 89 NMEC strains

full_output.paper_title: Aeromonas hydrophila subsp. dhakensis isolated from feces, water and fish in Mediterranean Spain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Aeromonas hydrophila subsp. dhakensis as an emerging pathogen in Mediterranean Spain, highlighting its resistance to several antibiotics including ticarcillin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, cefoxitin, and imipenem.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized 16S rRNA gene sequencing, biochemical testing, and antimicrobial susceptibility assays to characterize the isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Eight Aeromonas hydrophila-like arabinose-negative isolates, along with reference strains of A. hydrophila subsp. dhakensis and A. aquariorum.

full_output.paper_title: Novel plasmids and resistance phenotypes in Yersinia pestis: unique plasmid inventory of strain Java 9 mediates high levels of arsenic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel transposon, Tn2503, which mediates high levels of arsenic resistance in Yersinia pestis strain Java 9. This transposon is integrated into all four indigenous plasmids of the strain and is responsible for the observed arsenic resistance phenotype.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, conjugation experiments, and PCR were used to characterize the arsenic resistance mechanism in Y. pestis strain Java 9.

full_output.paper_title: Computational analysis of structure-based interactions and ligand properties can predict efflux effects on antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a computational model to predict efflux effects on antibiotics, focusing on the AcrA-AcrB-TolC efflux pump system and its impact on beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Computational modeling, 3D-QSAR analysis, and experimental validation of efflux pump functionality.

full_output.paper_title: Related bifunctional restriction endonuclease-methyltransferase triplets: TspDTI, Tth111II/TthHB27I and TsoI with distinct specificities.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the tspDTIRM gene, which encodes a bifunctional restriction endonuclease and methyltransferase (TspDTI) from Thermus sp. The gene was cloned, expressed, and analyzed for its enzymatic properties, revealing unique characteristics such as its large molecular size, specific DNA recognition, and dual functionality in DNA cleavage and methylation.
full_output.methodology: The tspDTIRM gene was cloned, expressed in E. coli, and purified. Biochemical assays were performed to analyze the enzymatic properties of TspDTI, including its restriction and methylation activities.

full_output.paper_title: Prospective screening of novel antibacterial inhibitors of dihydrofolate reductase for mutational resistance.

dfrA.notes: mutations in the gene encoding dihydrofolate reductase (dfrA) that confer resistance to trimethoprim

full_output.paper_title: Transferable plasmid-mediated resistance to linezolid due to cfr in a human clinical isolate of Enterococcus faecalis.

cfr.mechanism: methylation of A2503 in the 23S rRNA

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first characterization of a transferable cfr-carrying plasmid in a human clinical isolate of Enterococcus faecalis, which confers resistance to linezolid.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, conjugation experiments, and susceptibility testing were used to characterize the cfr gene and its resistance mechanism.

full_output.paper_title: Alanyl-phosphatidylglycerol and Lysyl-phosphatidylglycerol Are Translocated by the Same MprF Flippases and Have Similar Capacities To Protect against the Antibiotic Daptomycin in Staphylococcus aureus.

mprF.validation_method: expression in S. aureus mprF deletion mutant and analysis of aminoacyl phospholipid content

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that MprF proteins from Staphylococcus aureus and Clostridium perfringens can synthesize and translocate both lysyl-phosphatidylglycerol (Lys-PG) and alanyl-phosphatidylglycerol (Ala-PG), which protect against daptomycin. The Lys-PG flippase domains of MprF can also translocate Ala-PG, indicating relaxed substrate specificity.
full_output.methodology: Expression of MprF proteins in S. aureus mprF deletion mutants, analysis of aminoacyl phospholipid content, and determination of daptomycin susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Globally dispersed mobile drug-resistance genes in gram-negative bacterial isolates from patients with bloodstream infections in a US urban general hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various mobile drug-resistance genes, including integron gene cassettes such as dfrA17-aadA5, aadA1, aadA2, aadA5, aadB, dfrA12, dfrA15, dfrA16, dfrA17, dfrA7, and beta-lactamase genes like bla CTX-M and bla TEM-1, which are responsible for resistance to aminoglycosides, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and beta-lactams in Gram-negative bacterial isolates from bloodstream infections.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Dysfunction of organic anion transporting polypeptide 1a1 alters intestinal bacteria and bile acid metabolism in mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Oatp1a1-null mice exhibited altered bile acid metabolism and intestinal bacteria composition, leading to changes in bile acid profiles and microbial populations in the intestines.
full_output.methodology: The study used Oatp1a1-null mice to investigate the role of the organic anion transporting polypeptide 1a1 in bile acid metabolism and intestinal bacteria composition, employing techniques such as UPLC-MS/MS for bile acid quantification and 16S rDNA-based assays for bacterial quantification.

full_output.paper_title: Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli O104:H4: a new challenge for microbiology.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the resistance genes TEM-1 and CTX-M-15 in the E. coli O104:H4 strain, which conferred resistance to penicillins and cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and analysis of the E. coli O104:H4 strain.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular basis of Yersinia enterocolitica temperature-dependent resistance to antimicrobial peptides.

pmrF.validation_method: mutant analysis and lipid A characterization

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pmrF and pagP as genes involved in lipid A modifications that contribute to temperature-dependent resistance to antimicrobial peptides in Yersinia enterocolitica.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, lipid A characterization, and susceptibility assays.

full_output.paper_title: SMU.152 acts as an immunity protein for mutacin IV.
full_output.key_findings: SMU.152 acts as an immunity protein for mutacin IV, providing protection against its antibacterial effects when overexpressed in sensitive host strains.
full_output.methodology: Cloning and overexpression of SMU.152 in sensitive host strains to assess its immunity function against mutacin IV.

full_output.paper_title: The Spx regulator modulates stress responses and virulence in Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Spx as a crucial regulator of stress responses and virulence in Enterococcus faecalis, demonstrating that its inactivation leads to heightened sensitivity to oxidative stress and reduced virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Necrotrophism is a quorum-sensing-regulated lifestyle in Bacillus thuringiensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the krsABC genes as essential for the production of kurstakin, a lipopeptide that supports Bt's necrotrophic lifestyle by enabling survival, swarming, and biofilm formation in insect cadavers.

full_output.paper_title: Xer recombinase and genome integrity in Helicobacter pylori, a pathogen without topoisomerase IV.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies xerH as the sole xer recombinase gene in H. pylori, essential for difH site-specific recombination. xerH inactivation leads to increased DNA content, defective chromosome segregation, and heightened susceptibility to UV and ciprofloxacin.

full_output.paper_title: Re-evaluation of the significance of penicillin binding protein 3 in the susceptibility of Listeria monocytogenes to β-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa overrides the virulence inducing effect of opioids when it senses an abundance of phosphate.

full_output.paper_title: Fungal biofilm resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance, toxinotype, and genotypic profiling of Clostridium difficile isolates of swine origin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes tetM and tetW, and erythromycin resistance gene ermB in Clostridium difficile isolates from swine. These genes were found to confer resistance to their respective antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, and toxin gene detection were used to analyze antimicrobial resistance and toxin profiles in C. difficile isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Role of the Porphyromonas gingivalis extracytoplasmic function sigma factor, SigH.

sigH.notes: SigH is a positive regulator of gene expression required for survival of the bacterium in the presence of oxygen and oxidative stress, hemin uptake, and virulence.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SigH as a critical extracytoplasmic function sigma factor in Porphyromonas gingivalis, essential for adaptation to oxygen, oxidative stress protection, hemin uptake, and virulence. The SigH-deficient mutant strain V2948 exhibits reduced growth in the presence of oxygen, increased susceptibility to oxidative and thiol stress, and impaired hemin uptake and survival in the presence of host cells.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, RNA sequencing, and PCR analysis were used to investigate the role of SigH in P. gingivalis.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and antibacterial evaluation of New N-acylhydrazone derivatives from dehydroabietic acid.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and antibacterial evaluation of new N-acylhydrazone derivatives from dehydroabietic acid. Several compounds exhibited significant antibacterial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, with compound 4p showing potent activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus subtilis.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and evaluated for antibacterial activity using a microdilution method against four bacterial strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-9, and bla TEM-52 genes as the primary extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes in ESBL-producing E. coli isolates from cattle. These genes conferred resistance to cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA array, and sequencing were used to detect and characterize ESBL genes and virulence factors in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A systems biology approach to drug targets in Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies candidate metabolic drug targets for biofilm-associated Pseudomonas aeruginosa using a systems biology approach, focusing on genes essential in different environmental conditions and their roles in metabolic pathways.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a genome-scale metabolic reconstruction of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (iMO1056) combined with flux balance analysis to simulate gene deletions and identify essential genes under various growth conditions.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that a synthetic TM4 peptide can inhibit the drug efflux function of the small multidrug resistance protein Hsmr by disrupting its dimerization, reducing the efflux rate of ethidium bromide.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of peptide synthesis, antimicrobial assays, CD spectroscopy, SDS-PAGE, and ethidium bromide efflux assays to investigate the effect of TM4 peptides on Hsmr-mediated drug efflux.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a β-lactamase-based reporter system to investigate ESX-dependent protein translocation in mycobacteria, demonstrating that BlaTEM fusion proteins can be used to monitor translocation efficiency.
full_output.methodology: Construction of reporter vectors, ampicillin susceptibility testing, and Western blot analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antilisterial activity of nisin-like bacteriocin-producing Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis isolated from traditional Sardinian dairy products.
full_output.key_findings: None of the strains tested was found to produce biogenic amines or to possess haemolytic activity. All strains were sensitive to clinically important antibiotics such as ampicillin, tetracycline, and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was carried out by disc diffusion method according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) guidelines.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that the strA gene, which confers resistance to streptomycin, was present below the PCR detection limit in all soils examined. However, it was successfully amplified from seeded microcosms constructed from all soils studied.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to examine the diversity of strA and atpD genes in soil samples.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple soil sites across various locations.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular analysis and risk factors for Escherichia coli producing extended-spectrum β-lactamase bloodstream infection in hematological malignancies.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified CTX-M-15 as the predominant ESBL in E. coli bloodstream infections among hematological malignancy patients, highlighting its role in resistance to cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and molecular typing techniques were used to characterize ESBL-producing E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic and functional characterization of cyclic lipopeptide white-line-inducing principle (WLIP) production by rice rhizosphere isolate Pseudomonas putida RW10S2.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the genes involved in the biosynthesis of the cyclic lipopeptide WLIP by Pseudomonas putida RW10S2, including wlpA, wlpB, wlpC, and wlpR, which are crucial for WLIP production and its associated phenotypes such as antagonism against Xanthomonas and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Genetic characterization, phenotypic analysis, and biochemical assays were used to identify and validate the roles of the wlp genes in WLIP biosynthesis and regulation.

full_output.paper_title: MexT functions as a redox-responsive regulator modulating disulfide stress resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: MexT functions as a redox-responsive regulator modulating disulfide stress resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Disruption of mexT results in increased susceptibility to diamide, and the MexEF-OprN efflux system is implicated in MexT-associated disulfide stress resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, disk diffusion, broth microdilution, and redox titration experiments were conducted to analyze the role of MexT and the MexEF-OprN efflux system in disulfide stress resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Clostridium difficile MazF toxin exhibits selective, not global, mRNA cleavage.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a unique MazEF TA system in Clostridium difficile strain 630, with MazF-cd exhibiting selective mRNA cleavage at UACAU sequences, and MazE-cd acting as its cognate antitoxin.
full_output.methodology: Protein expression, in vitro cleavage assays, primer extension analysis, and bioinformatics.

full_output.paper_title: Bioassay-guided discovery of antibacterial agents: in vitro screening of Peperomia vulcanica, Peperomia fernandopoioana and Scleria striatinux.
full_output.key_findings: Okundoperoxide, a compound isolated from Scleria striatinux, exhibited antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, showing efficacy comparable to standard antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Disc diffusion and microdilution methods were used to assess antibacterial activity and determine MICs.

full_output.paper_title: Modulation of symbiont lipid A signaling by host alkaline phosphatases in the squid-vibrio symbiosis
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two alkaline phosphatases, EsAP1 and EsAP2, from the squid Euprymna scolopes, which dephosphorylate lipid A from the symbiotic bacterium Vibrio fischeri, thereby modulating its immunostimulatory properties.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic activity assays, PCR, and sequence analysis were used to characterize the alkaline phosphatases.

full_output.paper_title: Regulation of RNase Activity and RNA Stability in Pathogenic Bacteria

mazEF.mechanism: mediates plasmid stability and contributes to vancomycin resistance
mazEF.validation_method: expression in clinical isolates and demonstration of endoribonucleolytic activity

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several toxin-antitoxin systems, including mazEF, axe-txe, relBE, and epsilon-zeta, which contribute to plasmid stability and multidrug resistance in vancomycin-resistant enterococci. The vanA gene cluster was found to be localized on the same plasmid as mazEF, highlighting its clinical significance.
full_output.methodology: Functional characterization of toxin-antitoxin systems in clinical isolates and plasmid analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Benznidazole-resistance in Trypanosoma cruzi is a readily acquired trait that can arise independently in a single population.

Three distinct missense mutations in TcNTR were found in resistant clones, resulting in inactive proteins that cannot activate benznidazole.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular cloning, sequencing, biochemical analysis, and transfection experiments to characterize TcNTR mutations and their impact on benznidazole resistance.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of tigecycline against clinical isolates of carbapenem resistant Acinetobacter baumannii complex in Pretoria, South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of tigecycline against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii complex isolates, finding that 75.8% were fully susceptible to tigecycline, while 7.6% were fully resistant.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the VITEK-2 system, and carbapenemase production was detected via the modified Hodge test.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of N-acylhydrazones 4a-e and 1,3,4-oxadiazole compounds 5a-e for their anti-staphylococcal activity against various strains of Staphylococcus aureus, showing effective antibacterial activity with MIC values between 4 μg/mL and 32 μg/mL.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of compounds, spectral analysis (IR, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR), and determination of antibacterial activity via microdilution assay.

full_output.paper_title: Methionine sulfoxide reductase A (MsrA) deficient Mycoplasma genitalium shows decreased interactions with host cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the absence of MsrA in Mycoplasma genitalium leads to decreased cytotoxicity, increased phagocytosis, reduced differentiation of THP-1 cells, and lower induction of TNF-α, highlighting MsrA's role in virulence and host cell interactions.
full_output.methodology: The study compared wild-type and msrA mutant strains of M. genitalium using cytotoxicity assays, phagocytosis experiments, and cytokine measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Lysozyme resistance in Streptococcus suis is highly variable and multifactorial.

mutations_found.validated_by: isogenic mutant construction and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies oatA, SSU0475, and SSU0519 as genes involved in lysozyme resistance in Streptococcus suis, with experimental validation through mutant construction and MIC testing.
full_output.methodology: Mutant construction, MIC testing, whole genome sequencing, and PCR analysis were used to validate the role of genes in lysozyme resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Different functions of MdtB and MdtC subunits in the heterotrimeric efflux transporter MdtB(2)C complex of Escherichia coli.

mdtB.notes: Mutation in mdtB reduces cloxacillin efflux activity.

mdtC.notes: Multiple mutations in mdtC reduce cloxacillin efflux activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific mutations in the mdtB and mdtC genes that affect cloxacillin efflux activity in E. coli, highlighting the distinct roles of these subunits in the MdtB(2)C efflux complex.
full_output.methodology: Cysteine scanning mutagenesis and efflux activity measurements were performed to analyze the impact of mutations on cloxacillin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Syntheses and biological studies of novel spiropiperazinyl oxazolidinone antibacterial agents using a spirocyclic diene derived acylnitroso Diels-Alder reaction.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and biological evaluation of novel oxazolidinone derivatives with a spiropiperazinyl substituent at the 4'-position of the phenyl ring. Compounds 8a and 12 showed in vitro antibacterial activities comparable to linezolid against Gram-positive bacteria, including drug-resistant strains such as MRSA and VRE. Compound 12 exhibited better MIC values against MSSA and MRSA compared to compound 8a.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis and in vitro antibacterial activity testing against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, identification & characterization of Proteus penneri--a missed rare pathogen.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies eight isolates of Proteus penneri, which were multidrug-resistant (MDR) and exhibited resistance to various antibiotics, including beta-lactams, quinolones, and others. The paper highlights the importance of additional biochemical tests for accurate identification of P. penneri.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical tests, antibiotic sensitivity testing, and beta-lactamase screening were conducted on clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Implication of proteins containing tetratricopeptide repeats in conditional virulence phenotypes of Legionella pneumophila.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LpnE and EnhC, tetratricopeptide repeat-containing proteins, as critical for reversing virulence defects in Legionella pneumophila through water stress treatment, implicating their role in T4SS function.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, immunofluorescence assays, and translocation assays were used to analyze the role of LpnE and EnhC in virulence phenotypes.

full_output.paper_title: The carbon monoxide releasing molecule CORM-2 attenuates Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: CORM-2 attenuates Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm formation and prevents maturation of biofilms, showing additive effects with tobramycin. It effectively reduces biofilm formation in most clinical isolates but is less effective against robust biofilm-forming strains.
full_output.methodology: Experiments involving CORM-2 treatment, biofilm formation assays, and microbial viability assessments were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: The Ruegeria pomeroyi acuI gene has a role in DMSP catabolism and resembles yhdH of E. coli and other bacteria in conferring resistance to acrylate.
full_output.key_findings: The acuI gene from Ruegeria pomeroyi and its homologs in other bacteria confer resistance to acrylate, as demonstrated by complementation of acrylate-sensitive mutants. The E. coli yhdH gene also plays a role in acrylate resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, mutant phenotyping, cloning, and complementation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Etiologic profile and antimicrobial susceptibility of community-acquired urinary tract infection in two Cameroonian towns.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of uropathogens and their antibiotic susceptibility patterns in two Cameroonian towns, highlighting regional variations and low susceptibility to several antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed urine samples using culture and disk diffusion techniques to determine bacterial isolates and their susceptibility to various antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacodynamic evaluation of the activity of antibiotics against hemin- and menadione-dependent small-colony variants of Staphylococcus aureus in models of extracellular (broth) and intracellular (THP-1 monocytes) infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the activity of antibiotics against hemin- and menadione-dependent small-colony variants (SCVs) of Staphylococcus aureus, highlighting differences in intracellular and extracellular susceptibility and the impact of nutrient supplementation on growth and antibiotic effectiveness.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetically engineered mutants of S. aureus and tested antibiotic activity in both extracellular broth and intracellular THP-1 monocyte models.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing pathogens: results of a surveillance study in two hospitals in Ujjain, India.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing pathogens, particularly in Gram-negative bacteria such as E. coli and K. pneumoniae. It also highlighted the high prevalence of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) among S. aureus isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved prospective collection of bacterial isolates from patients in two hospitals in Ujjain, India, followed by antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Francisella tularensis tmRNA system mutants are vulnerable to stress, avirulent in mice, and provide effective immune protection.

full_output.paper_title: The effects of daily chlorhexidine bathing on cutaneous bacterial isolates: a pilot study.

full_output.paper_title: Differential epigenetic compatibility of qnr antibiotic resistance determinants with the chromosome of Escherichia coli.

full_output.paper_title: PDE5 inhibitors, sildenafil and vardenafil, reverse multidrug resistance by inhibiting the efflux function of multidrug resistance protein 7 (ATP-binding Cassette C10) transporter.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the tox gene encoding diphtheria toxin in Corynebacterium ulcerans 0102, which is located on a prophage distinct from that of C. diphtheriae NCTC 13129.

full_output.paper_title: An outbreak of Mycoplasma pneumoniae caused by a macrolide-resistant isolate in a nursery school in China.

full_output.paper_title: Combination antimicrobial susceptibility testing of multidrug-resistant Stenotrophomonas maltophilia from cystic fibrosis patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial susceptibility of multidrug-resistant Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates from cystic fibrosis patients, highlighting the limited susceptibility of these isolates to various antibiotics and the potential for synergistic combinations.
full_output.methodology: The study used Etest methodology for MIC and combination testing of 80 S. maltophilia isolates.

full_output.paper_title: NXL104 irreversibly inhibits the β-lactamase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Increasing prevalence of ESBL production among Irish clinical Enterobacteriaceae from 2004 to 2008: an observational study.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae in Ireland, including in community and long-stay facility settings, with a focus on E. coli and K. pneumoniae.
