full_output.key_findings: A mutation in the F1Fo-ATPase gamma subunit (S284*) confers high-level resistance to isometamidium and ethidium bromide in Trypanosoma brucei.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, drug sensitivity assays, and sequencing were used to characterize the mutation.

full_output.paper_title: IAP antagonists Birinapant and AT-406 efficiently synergise with either TRAIL, BRAF, or BCL-2 inhibitors to sensitise BRAFV600E colorectal tumour cells to apoptosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the overexpression of XIAP, DR4, DR5, and BCL-2 in colorectal adenocarcinoma cell lines, highlighting their roles in resistance to apoptosis. SMAC-mimetics Birinapant and AT-406 showed effectiveness in reducing cell viability and inducing apoptosis when combined with TRAIL, BRAF inhibitors, or BCL-2 inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: The study used cell viability assays, Western blotting, Real Time PCR, and confocal microscopy to evaluate the effects of SMAC-mimetics on colorectal adenocarcinoma cells.

full_output.paper_title: Copper Resistance of the Emerging Pathogen Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several putative copper resistance genes in Acinetobacter baumannii, including ActP2/CopA1, CopA/CueO, CueR, CzcA, CzcB, CzcC, CzcD, PcoA, CopB, CopC, CopR/CusR, CopS/CusS, and ActP1/CopA2, which are involved in copper detoxification and efflux mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, qRT-PCR, and copper sensitivity assays were used to identify and characterize copper resistance genes in Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and Virulence-Modulating Effects of Clove Essential Oil on the Foodborne Pathogen Campylobacter jejuni.

gyrA.notes: Mutation in gyrA gene associated with ciprofloxacin resistance in Campylobacter jejuni.

full_output.key_findings: Clove essential oil exhibits antibacterial effects on Campylobacter jejuni, reducing motility and altering the expression of virulence-associated genes such as PEB1, PEB4, and HtrA.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized proteomic, transcriptomic, and morphological analyses to investigate the effects of clove essential oil on C. jejuni.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance suppression by high-intensity, short-duration aminoglycoside exposure against hypermutable and non-hypermutable Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effect of high-intensity, short-duration aminoglycoside exposure on resistance suppression in hypermutable and non-hypermutable Pseudomonas aeruginosa. It found that shorter exposure durations (1 and 4 hours) resulted in more effective resistance suppression compared to longer durations (10 and 24 hours).
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro time-kill experiments and mechanism-based pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling to assess bacterial killing and resistance emergence under different tobramycin concentration-time profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Proteomic and genomic analysis reveals novel Campylobacter jejuni outer membrane proteins and potential heterogeneity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 47 outer membrane proteins of Campylobacter jejuni strain 81-176 using proteomic analysis, including several previously characterised OM proteins such as adhesins CadF and FlpA, the MapA antigen, porins PorA and Omp50, ABC transporter components PEB1, CjaA, and CjaC, and the multidrug efflux pump component CmeC. It also reports on the sequence heterogeneity and conservation of these proteins among different Campylobacter strains.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis using LC–ESI-MS/MS and bioinformatics tools to identify and characterise outer membrane proteins of Campylobacter jejuni.

full_output.key_findings: The study compared the antimicrobial activity and toxicity of major lipopeptide components of polymyxin B and colistin, revealing no substantial differences in MICs between the components and commercial products against various Gram-negative isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth micro-dilution to determine MICs, in vivo mouse models for efficacy, and FACS analysis for assessing apoptosis in HK-2 cells.

full_output.paper_title: miR-625-3p regulates oxaliplatin resistance by targeting MAP2K6-p38 signalling in human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells.

MAP2K6.validation_method: cloning in HCT116 and SW620 cells, western blotting, luciferase reporter assay

full_output.key_findings: miR-625-3p promotes oxaliplatin resistance in CRC cells by targeting MAP2K6, which is a direct and functional target of miR-625-3p.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, western blotting, luciferase reporter assay, phosphoproteomics, siRNA, and inhibitor treatments.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the in vitro antibacterial activity of the solvent fractions of the leaves of Rhamnus prinoides L'Herit (Rhamnaceae) against pathogenic bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The methanol and chloroform fractions of Rhamnus prinoides leaves exhibited antibacterial activity against several pathogenic bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Salmonella typhi. The aqueous fraction showed no antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: Agar well diffusion and microbroth dilution methods were used to assess antibacterial activity and determine MIC and MBC values.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of serogroup 20 S.pneumoniae isolates from Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all 16 serogroup 20 pneumococcal isolates were resistant to tetracycline and 31% were non-susceptible to trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. Additionally, 31% of the isolates showed non-susceptibility to penicillin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using broth microdilution, and genetic characterization of the cps locus was performed through sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of DprE1-Mediated Benzothiazinone Resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

dprE1.notes: Mutations at position 387 of DprE1 confer resistance to benzothiazinones.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies five mutations (C387G, C387A, C387S, C387N, and C387T) in the DprE1 gene that confer resistance to benzothiazinones in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, MIC determination, enzymatic activity assays, and structural modeling were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: NUDT15 Hydrolyzes 6-Thio-DeoxyGTP to Mediate the Anticancer Efficacy of 6-Thioguanine.

NUDT15.validation_method: enzymatic activity assays, crystallography, protein stability assays

NUDT15 R139C.validation_method: protein stability assays, clonogenic survival assays

mutations_found.validated_by: protein stability assays, clonogenic survival assays

NUDT15.notes: The R139C mutation leads to reduced protein stability and increased sensitivity to thiopurine treatment.
NUDT15.evidence_note: The paper describes the R139C mutation in NUDT15 and its effect on protein stability and thiopurine sensitivity.

full_output.key_findings: NUDT15 hydrolyzes 6-thio-dGTP and 6-thio-GTP, and the R139C mutation in NUDT15 leads to protein instability and increased sensitivity to thiopurine treatment.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic activity assays, crystallography, protein stability assays, clonogenic survival assays, and Western blotting.

full_output.paper_title: Fluorescence-based assay for polyprenyl phosphate-GlcNAc-1-phosphate transferase (WecA) and identification of novel antimycobacterial WecA inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of a fluorescence-based assay for WecA, an essential enzyme for Mycobacterium tuberculosis cell wall biosynthesis, and identifies UT-01320 as a novel WecA inhibitor that effectively kills both replicating and non-replicating Mtb.
full_output.methodology: The study developed a fluorescence-based WecA assay using UDP-Glucosamine-C6-FITC and decaprenyl phosphate, and screened compound libraries to identify WecA inhibitors. UT-01320 was identified as a potent WecA inhibitor with activity against both replicating and non-replicating Mtb.

full_output.paper_title: Chlamydia Serine Protease Inhibitor, targeting HtrA, as a New Treatment for Koala Chlamydia infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies JO146 as a potent inhibitor of the HtrA serine protease, effectively reducing infectious progeny of Chlamydia in koala isolates. It demonstrates that JO146 is not cytotoxic to koala cells and shows promise as a new treatment for koala chlamydiosis.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and ex vivo experiments were conducted to evaluate the efficacy of JO146 against Chlamydia isolates from koalas, including susceptibility testing and cytotoxicity assays.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple koala isolates from Queensland and New South Wales, Australia

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing of multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Myanmar.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various mutations in genes associated with resistance to multiple antibiotics in multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Myanmar, including mutations in rpoB, katG, inhA, embB, rpsL, pncA, rrs, gyrA, thyA, folC, gidB, and ethA.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing was used to analyze the genetic basis of drug resistance in 14 multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Unraveling the essential role of CysK in CDI toxin activation.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that CysK stabilizes the CdiA-CT EC536 toxin, enabling its nuclease activity by organizing the active site for substrate recognition and catalysis. It also identifies key residues (Asp155, His178, Glu181) in the nuclease domain crucial for tRNase activity.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology, site-directed mutagenesis, and biochemical assays were employed to investigate the role of CysK in activating the CdiA-CT EC536 toxin.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-Resistant Shigella Infections in Patients with Diarrhea, Cambodia, 2014-2015.

gyrA.notes: Common mutation in gyrA at position 83
gyrA.evidence_note: The paper states that 'the most common mechanism of quinolone resistance in the Shigella spp. was mutation of gyr A, typically at codon 83 or 87' and 'all isolates in our study had the common mutation in gyr A at position 83 (Ser83→Leu); 1 isolate had another common mutation at position 87 (Asp87→Gly)'.

parC.notes: Detected in S. sonnei isolate

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in gyrA and parC genes contributing to fluoroquinolone resistance, as well as the mphA gene associated with azithromycin resistance in Shigella isolates. Additionally, various beta-lactamase genes, including TEM-1, OXA-1, CTX-M-27, and CTX-M-55, were found to confer resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to characterize resistance genes, while antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli Hybrid Pathotype O80:H2 as a New Therapeutic Challenge.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various virulence genes in EHEC O80:H2 strains, including stx2, eae, ehxA, sitA, cia, iss, iucC, iroN, hlyF, etsC, cvaA, and ompTp, which contribute to the pathogenicity and extraintestinal virulence of the strain.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization, PCR, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to analyze the virulence genes and resistance profiles of EHEC O80:H2 strains.

full_output.paper_title: Drug-resistant tuberculosis in Central Mozambique: the role of a rapid genotypic susceptibility testing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several mutations in genes associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including rpoB, katG, inhA, rrs, gyrA, and embB, which confer resistance to rifampicin, isoniazid, second-line injectable drugs, fluoroquinolones, and ethambutol.
full_output.methodology: Genotype MTBDRplus and MTBDRsl tests were used to detect mutations in specific genes associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Novel Genomic Islands in Liverpool Epidemic Strain of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Using Segmentation and Clustering.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 20 genomic islands (GIs) in the Liverpool epidemic strain of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (LESB58), including 12 novel GIs. These GIs were found to contain various genes associated with virulence and antibiotic resistance, contributing to the hyper-virulence and multidrug resistance of the strain.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of computational methods, including GEMINI, to analyze the genome of P. aeruginosa LESB58 and identify genomic islands. Comparative genomics and phylogenetic analysis were also employed to validate the findings.

full_output.paper_title: Surveillance of Antibiotic Resistance among Hospital- and Community-Acquired Toxigenic Clostridium difficile Isolates over 5-Year Period in Kuwait.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that vancomycin resistance was not encountered among hospital-acquired and community-acquired C. difficile isolates, but metronidazole resistance was observed in 2.9% of hospital-acquired isolates. High resistance rates were noted for ampicillin, clindamycin, levofloxacin, and imipenem among both types of isolates, with rifampicin resistance emerging in hospital-acquired isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the E test method for 15 antimicrobial agents against 111 hospital-acquired and 35 community-acquired C. difficile isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Malaria in urban, semi-urban and rural areas of southern of Gabon: comparison of the Pfmdr 1 and Pfcrt genotypes from symptomatic children.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in Pfmdr1 (N86Y) and Pfcrt (K76T) associated with resistance to amodiaquine, chloroquine, and reduced susceptibility to artemether-lumefantrine in Plasmodium falciparum isolates from Gabon.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping of Pfmdr1 and Pfcrt genes using PCR-RFLP and sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that host-induced gene silencing (HIGS) using RNAi can protect wheat from Fusarium head blight (FHB) by targeting essential genes of the fungus Fusarium culmorum, such as Fc Gls1, Fc Fmk1, and Fc Fgl1, leading to reduced disease symptoms and fungal biomass.
full_output.methodology: The study uses RNA interference (RNAi) through BSMV-mediated VIGS and transgenic wheat lines to silence target genes in Fusarium culmorum, assessing the impact on FHB disease symptoms and fungal transcript levels.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic Detection of rpoB and katG Gene Mutations Associated with Rifampicin and Isoniazid Resistance in Mycobacterium Tuberculosis Isolates: A Local Scenario (Kelantan).

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates, including mef, ermB, tetM, and cat for macrolide, tetracycline, and chloramphenicol resistance, as well as mutations in rplD, 23S rRNA, folP, folA, parC, gyrA, and rpoB for various antibiotic resistances.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and broth dilution testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of Brazilian Clostridium difficile strains determined by agar dilution and disk diffusion.
full_output.key_findings: The study determined the antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of 50 Brazilian Clostridium difficile strains using agar dilution and disk diffusion methods. All strains were susceptible to metronidazole, with low MIC 90 values for most antibiotics tested. Resistance to moxifloxacin was observed in 8% of the strains.
full_output.methodology: Agar dilution and disk diffusion methods were used to assess antimicrobial susceptibility of C. difficile strains.

full_output.paper_title: The Global Regulon sarA Regulates β-Lactam Antibiotic Resistance in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus In Vitro and in Endovascular Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the global regulator sarA regulates β-lactam antibiotic resistance in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) by influencing the expression of mecA and PBP2a, thereby reducing oxacillin resistance and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial strain analysis, oxacillin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) determination, population analyses, PBP2a production measurement, biofilm formation assays, transcription analyses, and an experimental endocarditis model in rabbits.

full_output.paper_title: A tanshinone I derivative enhances the activities of antibiotics against Staphylococcus aureus in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that 16-aldehyde tanshinone I (ALT) enhances the antibacterial effects of antibiotics like streptomycin (STR) and ampicillin (AMP) against Staphylococcus aureus by damaging the bacterial cell membrane, increasing antibiotic accumulation within the cells.
full_output.methodology: The study involved synthesizing ALT, evaluating its antibacterial activity through MIC assays, checkerboard assays, time-kill analyses, biofilm inhibition assays, and in vivo experiments in a murine infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Asymmetric Collagen/chitosan Membrane Containing Minocycline-loaded Chitosan Nanoparticles for Guided Bone Regeneration.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed an asymmetric collagen/chitosan membrane containing minocycline-loaded chitosan nanoparticles, demonstrating antibacterial activity against Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum, while promoting bone regeneration.
full_output.methodology: The membrane was characterized using SEM, TEM, and in vitro assays to assess biocompatibility, antibacterial activity, and bone regeneration capacity.

full_output.paper_title: Novel cationic peptide TP359 down-regulates the expression of outer membrane biogenesis genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa: a potential TP359 anti-microbial mechanism.

oprI.mechanism: up-regulation of gene expression under bacteriostatic conditions

full_output.key_findings: TP359 exhibits bactericidal activity against P. aeruginosa by down-regulating the expression of outer membrane biogenesis genes, particularly oprF, leading to membrane destabilization and cell death.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and electron microscopy were used to assess the impact of TP359 on gene expression and cellular morphology.

full_output.paper_title: Activity of Tedizolid in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Experimental Foreign Body-Associated Osteomyelitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of tedizolid, with and without rifampin, against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in a rat model of foreign body-associated osteomyelitis. Tedizolid showed activity against MRSA, but the emergence of rifampin resistance was noted in animals receiving tedizolid plus rifampin.
full_output.methodology: The study used a rat model of MRSA foreign body-associated osteomyelitis to evaluate the antibacterial activity of tedizolid, with and without rifampin, compared to rifampin and vancomycin.

full_output.paper_title: Lipid composition in a strain of Bacillus subtilis, a producer of iturin A lipopeptides that are active against uropathogenic bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified iturin A lipopeptides produced by Bacillus subtilis I′1a as having strong antibacterial activity against uropathogenic bacteria, including inhibition of biofilm formation and disruption of pre-formed biofilms.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity testing, LC-MS/MS, MALDI-TOF/TOF, and fatty acid analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Disease-Homologous Mutation in the Cation Diffusion Facilitator Protein MamM Causes Single-Domain Structural Loss and Signifies Its Importance.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: severe structural changes in its CTD resulting in abnormal reduced function
mutations_found.validated_by: in silico, in vitro, and in vivo studies

MamM.notes: The M250P mutation in MamM is a disease-homologous mutation that affects the structural integrity and function of the CTD.

full_output.key_findings: The M250P mutation in the cation diffusion facilitator protein MamM causes structural loss in its C-terminal domain, leading to impaired function. This mutation is analogous to the disease-causing ZnT-10 L349P mutation in humans.
full_output.methodology: The study used in silico modeling, in vitro biophysical techniques, and in vivo functional assays to characterize the effects of the M250P mutation in MamM.

full_output.paper_title: The ABC transporter YejABEF is required for resistance to antimicrobial peptides and the virulence of Brucella melitensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the YejABEF ABC transporter is crucial for Brucella melitensis resistance to antimicrobial peptides and virulence, particularly highlighting the key role of YejE in polymyxin B resistance and intracellular survival.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion mutants, polymyxin B sensitivity assays, and intracellular infection experiments were conducted to assess the role of the yej operon in antimicrobial peptide resistance and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: ZpdN, a Plasmid-Encoded Sigma Factor Homolog, Induces pBS32-Dependent Cell Death in Bacillus subtilis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies zpdN, a plasmid-encoded sigma factor homolog, as essential for pBS32-dependent cell death in Bacillus subtilis. Artificial expression of zpdN leads to pBS32 hyperreplication and cell lysis.
full_output.methodology: The study uses genetic manipulation, fluorescence microscopy, and qPCR to investigate the role of zpdN in pBS32-mediated cell death.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudouridine in the Anticodon of Escherichia coli tRNATyr(QΨA) Is Catalyzed by the Dual Specificity Enzyme RluF.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies RluF as the enzyme responsible for catalyzing pseudouridine modification at position 35 in the anticodon of E. coli tRNATyr(QΨA).
full_output.methodology: The study uses LC-MS/MS, CMCT derivatization, and mutagenesis to identify and validate RluF as the pseudouridine synthase for tRNATyr.

full_output.paper_title: Cathepsin B modulates lysosomal biogenesis and host defense against Francisella novicida infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that cathepsin B negatively regulates host defense against Francisella novicida infection by inhibiting lysosomal biogenesis and autophagy.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetically modified mice, macrophage cultures, and various biochemical and imaging techniques to analyze the role of cathepsin B in host defense mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Salmonella enterica Serovar Aberdeen Negative for H2S Production in China.

phsA.notes: The mutation leads to the inability to produce H2S.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a nonsense mutation in the phsA gene of non-H2S-producing Salmonella enterica serovar Aberdeen isolates, which leads to the inability to produce hydrogen sulfide.
full_output.methodology: Sequence analysis of the phs operon and molecular typing techniques including MLST, PFGE, and CRISPR analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Determinants of host susceptibility to murine respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease identify a role for the innate immunity scavenger receptor MARCO gene in human infants.

Marco.notes: The rs1318645 SNP in the MARCO promoter reduces gene expression and is associated with increased RSV disease severity in humans.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the MARCO gene as a susceptibility gene for RSV disease severity in humans, with a promoter SNP (rs1318645) causing reduced gene expression and increased disease risk.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide association studies, promoter sequencing, functional assays, and human population studies.

full_output.paper_title: Fine mapping QTL for resistance to VNN disease using a high-density linkage map in Asian seabass.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a candidate gene, Pcdhac2, associated with resistance to VNN disease in Asian seabass, along with a 6 bp insertion-deletion variant linked to disease resistance.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput sequencing, QTL mapping, and association studies were used to identify genetic variants associated with VNN disease resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Nasal carriage of resistant Staphylococcus aureus in a medical student community.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of mecA, ermA, and ermC genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from medical students, indicating resistance to oxacillin, cephoxitin, erythromycin, and clindamycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR and disk-diffusion testing were used to detect AMR genes and phenotypes.

full_output.paper_title: Protection of Historical Wood against Microbial Degradation-Selection and Application of Microbiocides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified effective microbiocides for protecting historical wood from microbial degradation, focusing on compounds like didecyldimethylammonium chloride (DDAC) and N-(3-aminopropyl)-N-dodecylpropane-1,3-diamine (APDA).
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of various compounds against microorganisms isolated from historical wood using disc-diffusion assays and determined the minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs).

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Phosphate Uptake System Component PstA2 Is Not Required for Gene Regulation or Virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that PstA2 is not required for gene regulation or virulence in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. However, deletion of pstA2 enhances resistance to acidic pH, indicating a role in stress resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic deletion mutants, transcriptome analysis, and survival assays in mice to investigate the roles of PstA2 in M. tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: The Structure of the Antibiotic Deactivating, N-hydroxylating Rifampicin Monooxygenase.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structure and function of the rifampicin monooxygenase (RIFMO) from Nocardia farcinica, which deactivates rifampicin by N-hydroxylation, leading to reduced antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography, small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and enzymatic assays were used to characterize RIFMO.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SerpinB2 as a gene whose down-regulation is associated with gefitinib resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells, and shows that its up-regulation can enhance gefitinib sensitivity and reduce invasiveness.
full_output.methodology: The study used cDNA microarray analysis, Western blot, real-time PCR, and functional assays to investigate the role of SerpinB2 in gefitinib resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Disruption of the carA gene in Pseudomonas syringae results in reduced fitness and alters motility.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that disruption of the carA gene in Pseudomonas syringae leads to reduced fitness, altered motility, and increased biofilm formation. CarA is involved in the metabolism of arginine and uracil, and its disruption affects the bacterium's ability to grow and survive in planta.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation, growth assays, and transcriptional analyses to investigate the role of carA in Pseudomonas syringae.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal Structures of SgcE6 and SgcC, the Two-Component Monooxygenase That Catalyzes Hydroxylation of a Carrier Protein-Tethered Substrate during the Biosynthesis of the Enediyne Antitumor Antibiotic C-1027 in Streptomyces globisporus.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the crystal structures of SgcE6 and SgcC, two components of a monooxygenase system involved in the biosynthesis of the enediyne antitumor antibiotic C-1027 in Streptomyces globisporus. SgcE6 is identified as a flavin reductase, while SgcC is a flavin-dependent monooxygenase.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology techniques including X-ray crystallography and biochemical analysis were employed to determine the structures and functions of SgcE6 and SgcC.

full_output.paper_title: Mp1p Is a Virulence Factor in Talaromyces (Penicillium) marneffei.
full_output.key_findings: Mp1p is a key virulence factor of T. marneffei, mediating virulence by improving the survival of T. marneffei in macrophages.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, knockdown, complementation, and animal challenge experiments were conducted to assess the role of Mp1p in virulence.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple mouse groups and fungal strains were used.

full_output.paper_title: Regulation of Organic Hydroperoxide Stress Response by Two OhrR Homologs in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

ospR.validation_method: mutant construction and analysis of gene expression and survival after treatment with organic hydroperoxides

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies gpx and ospR as genes involved in the response to organic hydroperoxides in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, demonstrating their role in resistance through experimental validation.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR, mutant construction, and survival assays after treatment with oxidants.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the roles of cytochrome P450, Gne epimerase, and CetB in Campylobacter jejuni 81-176, focusing on their functions in cellular processes and potential resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: A Survival Strategy for Pseudomonas aeruginosa That Uses Exopolysaccharides To Sequester and Store Iron To Stimulate Psl-Dependent Biofilm Formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Psl as an exopolysaccharide that binds and stores iron, enhancing biofilm formation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Iron increases Psl production by repressing AmrZ and reducing rhamnolipid synthesis.

full_output.paper_title: De novo ALK kinase domain mutations are uncommon in kinase inhibitor-naïve ALK rearranged lung cancers.

full_output.methodology: Analysis of preclinical models, tumor databases, and clinical response to crizotinib.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Novel IncHI2 Plasmid Carrying Tandem Copies of blaCTX-M-2 in a fosA6-Harboring Escherichia coli Sequence Type 410 Strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a novel IncHI2 plasmid carrying tandem copies of blaCTX-M-2 in a fosA6-harboring Escherichia coli ST410 strain, highlighting the genetic context and dissemination potential of this resistance gene.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid sequencing, replicon typing, and comparative genomic analysis were performed to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Characteristics, Treatment Outcomes, and Resistance Mutations Associated with Macrolide-Resistant Mycobacterium avium Complex Lung Disease.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa as major pathogens causing breakthrough Gram-negative bacteremia during carbapenem therapy, highlighting risk factors such as prolonged hospital stay, hematologic malignancy, and previous colonization by causative microorganisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic failure mediated by a resistant subpopulation in Enterobacter cloacae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PhoQ as a critical factor in the development of a colistin-resistant subpopulation in Enterobacter cloacae, which contributes to antibiotic treatment failure.

full_output.paper_title: Shigella flexneri suppresses NF-κB activation by inhibiting linear ubiquitin chain ligation.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance determinants in quinolone-resistant Escherichia coli isolated from patients with bacteremia in a university hospital in Taiwan, 2001-2015.

aac(6')-Ib-cr.evidence_note: The gene aac(6')-Ib-cr was found in 14 isolates and was associated with plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance.

gyrA.notes: mutations in gyrA and parC were found in PMQR-harboring isolates

parC.notes: mutations in gyrA and parC were found in PMQR-harboring isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) genes, including qnrB2, qnrB4, qnrS1, oqxAB, and aac(6')-Ib-cr, in quinolone-resistant Escherichia coli isolates from Taiwan. Additionally, chromosomal mutations in gyrA and parC were found to contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, direct sequencing, conjugation experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to identify and characterize AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Competing for Iron: Duplication and Amplification of the isd Locus in Staphylococcus lugdunensis HKU09-01 Provides a Competitive Advantage to Overcome Nutritional Limitation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the isd locus duplication and amplification in Staphylococcus lugdunensis HKU09-01, which enhances hemoglobin binding and provides a competitive advantage under iron-limiting conditions.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, Southern blotting, qPCR, and competitive growth experiments were used to characterize the isd locus duplication and its impact on hemoglobin binding and bacterial fitness.

full_output.paper_title: A toxin antitoxin system promotes the maintenance of the IncA/C-mobilizable Salmonella Genomic Island 1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the sgiAT toxin-antitoxin system encoded by the Salmonella Genomic Island 1 (SGI1), which plays a critical role in the stable maintenance of SGI1 in the host chromosome, particularly in the presence of an IncA/C plasmid.
full_output.methodology: Functional characterization of the sgiAT system using plasmid vectors, transformation efficiency assays, PSK assays, and qPCR-based stability tests in E. coli and Salmonella strains.

full_output.paper_title: Gene expression profiling at birth characterizing the preterm infant with early onset infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies differentially expressed genes in preterm infants with early onset infection (EOI), highlighting altered immune responses involving neutrophil and T cell activation, as well as suppressed natural killer (NK) cell function.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide gene expression analysis using CodeLink human microarrays on umbilical arterial blood samples from preterm infants with and without EOI.

full_output.paper_title: The oncometabolite R-2-hydroxyglutarate activates NF-κB-dependent tumor-promoting stromal niche for acute myeloid leukemia cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that R-2HG, produced by IDH-mutated AML cells, activates NF-κB in bone marrow stromal cells, leading to increased expression of cytokines and adhesion molecules that promote AML cell proliferation and chemoresistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used cell culture, molecular biology techniques, and biochemical assays to investigate the effects of R-2HG on NF-κB activation and downstream gene expression in stromal cells.

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus as a potential diagnostic marker for yellow tongue coating.
full_output.key_findings: Bacillus was strongly associated with yellow tongue coating (YTC) in patients with chronic erosive gastritis (CEG) and was not observed in white tongue coating (WTC) samples. Treatment with Ban Xia Xie Xin decoction reduced or eliminated Bacillus in YTC samples.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA sequencing and bacterial culturing were used to analyze the tongue coating microbiota.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Basis for Lytic Bacteriophage Resistance in Enterococci.

PIP EF.notes: mutations in PIP EF lead to phage resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PIP EF as a crucial protein for phage infection in Enterococcus faecalis, and mutations in PIP EF lead to phage resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, genetic manipulation, phage susceptibility assays, and bioinformatics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: A High-Coverage Yersinia pestis Genome from a Sixth-Century Justinianic Plague Victim.

nrdE.notes: nrdE gene is associated with plague virulence

fadJ.encodes: multifunctional fatty acid oxidation complex subunit alpha
fadJ.notes: fadJ gene is associated with plague virulence

pcp.notes: pcp gene is associated with plague virulence

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 30 unique substitutions and structural differences in the Yersinia pestis genome from a sixth-century Justinianic Plague victim, including nonsynonymous substitutions in the nrdE, fadJ, and pcp genes, which are suggested as plague virulence determinants.
full_output.methodology: High-coverage genome sequencing and SNP calling were used to analyze the Yersinia pestis genome from an ancient specimen.

full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the conformational dynamics and structural mechanisms of the d-Ala:d-Lac ligase VanA, which is crucial for vancomycin resistance. It explores the conformational landscape of VanA using enhanced sampling techniques and identifies key structural features and movements involved in the enzyme's function.
full_output.methodology: The research employed molecular dynamics simulations, temperature-accelerated molecular dynamics (TAMD), and graph-based analyses to explore the conformational dynamics and structural changes of VanA.

full_output.paper_title: Novel m4C modification in type I restriction-modification systems.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes ten Type I restriction-modification systems that modify both m4C and m6A, revealing unique mechanisms involving two distinct methyltransferase subunits (M1 and M2) with specific roles in modifying adenine and cytosine, respectively.
full_output.methodology: SMRT sequencing, restriction assays, and genetic manipulation in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: An updated view of plasmid conjugation and mobilization in Staphylococcus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three distinct families of conjugative plasmids in Staphylococcus aureus, namely pSK41/pGO1, pWBG749, and pWBG4, which play a significant role in the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance. Additionally, it highlights the relaxase-in trans mechanism of mobilization, which allows non-conjugative plasmids to be mobilized by conjugative plasmids.
full_output.methodology: Sequence analysis and bioinformatic comparisons of plasmid sequences.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus and Lipopolysaccharide Modulate Gene Expressions of Drug Transporters in Mouse Mammary Epithelial Cells Correlation to Inflammatory Biomarkers.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that Mdr1 gene expression was up-regulated in HC11 cells after treatment with S. aureus and LPS, suggesting a potential role in drug transporter regulation during inflammation.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis using RT-qPCR in HC11 cells treated with S. aureus and LPS.

full_output.paper_title: High minimum inhibitory concentration of imipenem as a predictor of fatal outcome in patients with carbapenem non-susceptible Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies carbapenemase genes (KPC-2, KPC-3, VIM-1, and IMP-8) in carbapenem non-susceptible Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates and highlights the association of high imipenem MIC with increased mortality.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective study analyzing clinical and microbiological data, PCR detection of carbapenemase genes, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Genome Sequence of Avian Escherichia coli Strain IHIT25637, an Extraintestinal Pathogenic E. coli Strain of ST131 Encoding Colistin Resistance Determinant MCR-1.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the genome sequence of an avian ExPEC strain IHIT25637 carrying the plasmid-mediated colistin resistance gene mcr-1, which confers resistance to colistin and polymyxin B.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify the mcr-1 gene and its resistance profile.

full_output.paper_title: Three Yersinia enterocolitica AmpD Homologs Participate in the Multi-Step Regulation of Chromosomal Cephalosporinase, AmpC.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three AmpD homologs (AmpD1, AmpD2, and AmpD3) in Yersinia enterocolitica that participate in the multi-step regulation of chromosomal cephalosporinase, AmpC. These homologs act as negative regulators of ampC expression at different levels, contributing to the regulation of β-lactamase activity and resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, β-lactamase activity assays, and MIC testing to investigate the role of AmpD homologs in regulating ampC expression and β-lactam resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic considerations in the treatment of critically Ill patients infected with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic considerations for treating critically ill patients with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), highlighting the need for optimized antibiotic regimens due to limited treatment options.
full_output.methodology: Review of pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic data for various antibiotics used in the treatment of CRE infections.

full_output.paper_title: Ser/Thr Phosphorylation Regulates the Fatty Acyl-AMP Ligase Activity of FadD32, an Essential Enzyme in Mycolic Acid Biosynthesis.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: Phosphorylation of Thr-552 negatively regulates FadD32 activity
mutations_found.validated_by: mass spectrometry and enzymatic activity assays

full_output.key_findings: FadD32, an essential enzyme in mycolic acid biosynthesis, is phosphorylated at Thr-552, which significantly reduces its fatty acyl-AMP ligase activity and mycolic acid condensation activity.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical assays, mass spectrometry, and enzymatic activity measurements were used to characterize FadD32 phosphorylation and its effects on enzyme activity.

full_output.paper_title: Macrolide resistance mechanisms and virulence factors in erythromycin-resistant Campylobacter species isolated from chicken and swine feces and carcasses.

23S rRNA.notes: mutation in the 23S rRNA gene was primarily responsible for macrolide resistance

L4.notes: amino acid substitutions in the L4 ribosomal protein may play a role in the mechanism of resistance

L22.notes: amino acid substitutions in the L22 ribosomal protein may play a role in the mechanism of resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the 23S rRNA gene, particularly A2075G, as the primary mechanism of macrolide resistance in Campylobacter isolates. Additionally, various amino acid substitutions in the L4 and L22 ribosomal proteins were observed, suggesting their potential role in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study used sequencing to analyze mutations in the 23S rRNA gene and ribosomal proteins L4 and L22 in erythromycin-resistant Campylobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The Intervening Sequence of Coxiella burnetii: Characterization and Evolution.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the IVS of Coxiella burnetii, focusing on the S23p ORF, which encodes a hypothetical ribosomal S23p protein. The research shows that the IVS is excised by RNase III and that the S23p ORF is subject to reductive evolution with variations in sequences upstream and within the ORF across different strains.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro assays, RACE analyses, IVTT, and growth assays to analyze the IVS and S23p ORF in Coxiella burnetii.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into the regulation of small RNA expression: SarA represses the expression of two sRNAs in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: SarA represses the expression of two small RNAs, srn_3610_sprC and srn_9340, in Staphylococcus aureus. The study identifies the specific binding sites of SarA on the promoters of these sRNAs and confirms their regulation in vivo.
full_output.methodology: Northern blotting, EMSA, DNase I footprinting, ChIP assays, and reporter gene experiments were used to investigate the regulation of srn_3610_sprC and srn_9340 by SarA.

full_output.paper_title: A Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis Predicted Serine Protease Is Associated with Acid Stress and Intraphagosomal Survival.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MAP0403, a predicted serine protease, as a key component of the acid stress response network in Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis. MAP0403 is upregulated during phagosome acidification and contributes to bacterial survival under acid stress conditions.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, qRT-PCR, and bacterial survival assays in M. smegmatis.

full_output.paper_title: Differential Regulation of the Surface-Exposed and Secreted SslE Lipoprotein in Extraintestinal Pathogenic Escherichia coli.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Fis and TypA as positive regulators of sslE transcription in extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli, highlighting their role in the differential regulation of SslE expression.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screens, transposon mutagenesis, qRT-PCR, and western blot analysis were used to investigate the regulation of sslE.

full_output.paper_title: The SAV1322 gene from Staphylococcus aureus: genomic and proteomic approaches to identification and characterization of gene function.

sav1322.notes: The sav1322 deletion mutant showed lower MICs for gentamicin, tetracyclines, and glycopeptides.

full_output.key_findings: Deletion of the SAV1322 locus in Staphylococcus aureus leads to reduced growth under temperature stress, increased oxidative stress tolerance, and lower MICs for several antibiotics including gentamicin, tetracycline, and glycopeptides.
full_output.methodology: Generation of a sav1322 knockout mutant, complementation strain, and analysis of growth, oxidative stress response, microarray, proteomic, and antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: VapCs of Mycobacterium tuberculosis cleave RNAs essential for translation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that VapC4, VapC11, VapC28, and VapC37 from Mycobacterium tuberculosis cleave specific tRNAs in M. smegmatis and M. tuberculosis, highlighting their role in translational inhibition.
full_output.methodology: CRAC analysis, in vitro cleavage assays, and Northern blotting were used to identify and validate the RNA targets of VapC toxins.

It also characterizes other carbapenemases, including IMP-15, IMP-51, and NDM-1, in these isolates.

protein purification and membrane leakage assay

full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, membrane-permeabilizing activity assays, and virulence testing in macrophages and zebrafish embryos.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro antimicrobial activities of animal-used quinoxaline 1,4-di-N-oxides against mycobacteria, mycoplasma and fungi.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activities of quinoxaline 1,4-di-N-oxides (QdNOs) against mycobacteria, mycoplasma, and fungi. QdNOs showed activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Mycoplasma gallisepticum, and several fungal species, but none of the QdNOs or their metabolites exhibited antiviral activity against the tested viruses.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted in vitro antimicrobial susceptibility tests, including microdilution alamar blue assay, antifungal assays, antimycoplasma assays, and combination susceptibility tests.

full_output.paper_title: A Putative Bacterial ABC Transporter Circumvents the Essentiality of Signal Peptidase.

full_output.key_findings: Resistance to compound 103 in S. aureus is primarily due to mutations in the transcriptional repressor gene cro/cI, leading to overexpression of a putative ABC transporter. The ABC transporter ATPase gene SAUSA300_0352 is crucial for this resistance mechanism.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid complementation, qRT-PCR, and genetic experiments were used to validate the resistance mechanism.

full_output.paper_title: Point mutations in the major outer membrane protein drive hypervirulence of a rapidly expanding clone of Campylobacter jejuni.
full_output.key_findings: Point mutations in the major outer membrane protein (porA) of Campylobacter jejuni clone SA are responsible for hypervirulence and abortion induction in guinea pigs.
full_output.methodology: Directed genome evolution, defined mutagenesis, and animal infection experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic and complete reversal of the multidrug resistance of mitoxantrone hydrochloride by three-in-one multifunctional lipid-sodium glycocholate nanocarriers based on simultaneous BCRP and Bcl-2 inhibition.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents three-in-one multifunctional lipid-sodium glycocholate nanocarriers (TMLGNs) that synergistically reverse multidrug resistance (MDR) by simultaneously inhibiting BCRP and Bcl-2, demonstrating enhanced cytotoxicity and MDR reversal in cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized nanocarrier formulation, in vitro cytotoxicity assays, and pharmacokinetic studies to evaluate the effectiveness of TMLGNs in reversing MDR.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility, antibacterial activity and characterisation of Enterococcus faecium strains isolated from breast milk.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Enterococcus faecium strains isolated from human breast milk and evaluated their antibiotic susceptibility and antibacterial activity. Some strains showed resistance to several antibiotics, while others were sensitive to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic tests, including ribotyping, were used to identify the strains. Antibiotic susceptibility was determined using the Kirby-Bauer Disk Diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Targeted Disruption of Chlamydia trachomatis Invasion by in Trans Expression of Dominant Negative Tarp Effectors.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that mutant Tarp effectors, particularly those lacking the phosphorylation domain, significantly reduce the ability of Chlamydia trachomatis to invade host cells. The TarpΔphos mutant showed the greatest inhibition of chlamydial entry, suggesting a critical role for Tarp in pathogen entry.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic engineering, pyrene actin polymerization assays, and invasion assays to characterize the role of Tarp in Chlamydia trachomatis invasion.

full_output.paper_title: Francisella tularensis IglG Belongs to a Novel Family of PAAR-Like T6SS Proteins and Harbors a Unique N-terminal Extension Required for Virulence.
full_output.key_findings: IglG is a PAAR-like protein with a unique N-terminal extension required for virulence in Francisella novicida and Francisella tularensis. It binds metal ions and is essential for T6SS-dependent secretion and intracellular replication.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics, gene deletion, complementation, secretion assays, metal binding experiments, and virulence studies in mice.

full_output.methodology: Genomic and transcriptomic analysis combined with functional studies in human T-cells.

full_output.paper_title: Screen of Non-annotated Small Secreted Proteins of Pseudomonas syringae Reveals a Virulence Factor That Inhibits Tomato Immune Proteases.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Cip1, a small secreted protein from Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000, which acts as a protease inhibitor targeting immune proteases C14, Pip1, and Rcr3 in tomato, contributing to bacterial virulence.
full_output.methodology: Genome mining, protein expression, protease inhibition assays, and mutant analysis were used to characterize Cip1.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a pathway-specific activator of milbemycin biosynthesis and improved milbemycin production by its overexpression in Streptomyces bingchenggensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes MilR, a LAL family transcriptional regulator, as a pathway-specific activator of milbemycin biosynthesis in Streptomyces bingchenggensis. Overexpression of milR significantly increases milbemycin A3/A4 production.
full_output.methodology: Gene disruption, complementation, transcriptional analysis, site-directed mutagenesis, and overexpression experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of new antibiotic cocktails against contaminating bacteria found in allograft tissues.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the effectiveness of new antibiotic cocktails against contaminating bacteria in allograft tissues, identifying cocktails C and D as more effective than the current cocktail Z at 4°C and 22°C.
full_output.methodology: The study assessed the bactericidal activity of antibiotic cocktails against a panel of bacterial strains using MIC and MBC measurements, and evaluated their efficacy at different temperatures.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial type B RNase P: functional characterization of the L5.1-L15.1 tertiary contact and antisense inhibition.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the L5.1-L15.1 tertiary contact in B. subtilis type B RNase P RNA and shows that its disruption severely impairs enzyme function, demonstrating its critical role in maintaining the active conformation of the RNA.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, in vitro enzymatic assays, in vivo complementation, and antisense oligonucleotide inhibition experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of Unusual Biaryl Polyketides by Activation of a Silent Streptomyces venezuelae Biosynthetic Gene Cluster.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a cryptic polyketide biosynthetic gene cluster (vem) in Streptomyces venezuelae, which produces an unusual biaryl metabolite called venemycin and its halogenated derivatives. The cluster includes genes involved in the biosynthesis of 3,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid and the assembly of venemycin by type I modular PKSs. The study also shows that the expression of the vem cluster can be activated by deleting the bldM gene, leading to the production of venemycin and its derivatives.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, bioinformatics, structural characterization via NMR, and heterologous expression in Streptomyces coelicolor.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Evolutionary Pathways toward Two Successful Community-Associated but Multidrug-Resistant ST59 Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Lineages in Taiwan: Dynamic Modes of Mobile Genetic Element Salvages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes including ermB, aph(3')-IIIa, aadE, aacA-aphD, and cat, which confer resistance to erythromycin, clindamycin, kanamycin, streptomycin, gentamicin, and chloramphenicol in ST59 MRSA strains in Taiwan.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and MLVA analysis were used to characterize AMR genes and mobile genetic elements in ST59 MRSA strains.

full_output.paper_title: Yersinia pestis Caf1 Protein: Effect of Sequence Polymorphism on Intrinsic Disorder Propensity, Serological Cross-Reactivity and Cross-Protectivity of Isoforms.

mutations_found.origin: Yersinia pestis subsp. microtus biovar caucasica

caf1.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations in the caf1 gene of Yersinia pestis subsp. microtus biovar caucasica, specifically Ala48→Ser48 and Phe117→Val117, which are validated by sequencing and immunological assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes three Caf1 isoforms (NT1, NT2, NT3) of Yersinia pestis, highlighting differences in serological cross-reactivity and cross-protection. The NT1 isoform provided the highest level of protection against Y. pestis strains carrying NT2 or NT3 alleles.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of caf1 genes, immunological assays, and animal experiments to evaluate cross-reactivity and cross-protection.

full_output.paper_title: Sustained Release of Antibacterial Lipopeptides from Biodegradable Polymers against Oral Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes four ultra-short lipopeptides (C16-KGGK, C16-K K K, C16-KA A K, and C16-KL L K) that exhibit antibacterial activity against various oral pathogens, demonstrating their effectiveness in disrupting bacterial membranes and inhibiting biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Microdilution assay, turbidometric assay, live/dead staining, and flow cytometry were used to assess the antibacterial and anti-biofilm effects of the lipopeptides.

full_output.paper_title: Lytic transglycosylases LtgA and LtgD perform distinct roles in remodeling, recycling and releasing peptidoglycan in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the roles of LtgA and LtgD, lytic transglycosylases, in the remodeling, recycling, and release of peptidoglycan fragments in Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Both enzymes exhibit lytic transglycosylase activity, creating 1,6-anhydromuramyl bonds, and have distinct substrate specificities and cellular localizations.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized recombinant protein production, enzymatic assays, subcellular fractionation, and microscopic techniques to analyze the functions and localizations of LtgA and LtgD.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility pattern and analysis of plasmid profiles of Pseudomonas aeruginosa from human, animal and plant sources.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of resistance to ceftazidime and carbenicillin among Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from various sources, along with the detection of ESBL-producing strains and plasmid profiles indicating multiple resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, ESBL detection via DDST, and plasmid isolation and profiling were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of Season, Demographic and Environmental Factors on Salmonella Occurrence in Raccoons (Procyon lotor) from Swine Farms and Conservation Areas in Southern Ontario.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Salmonella was detected in 26% of raccoon fecal samples, 6% of soil samples, 30% of manure pit samples, and 23% of dumpster samples. Antimicrobial resistance was detected in 5% of raccoon fecal, 8% of soil, 10% of manure pit, and 0% of dumpster samples. The most common resistance was to ampicillin, tetracycline, and streptomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting fecal, soil, manure pit, and dumpster samples from raccoons in swine farms and conservation areas. Salmonella was isolated and tested for antimicrobial resistance using the NARMS CMVA2GNF plate.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico analysis using various bioinformatics tools.

full_output.paper_title: Draft Genome Sequence of Enterococcus faecalis Strain F165 Isolated from a Urinary Tract Infection.

full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, annotation, and comparative analysis of resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Complete Genome Sequences of Three Important Methicillin-Resistant Clinical Isolates of Staphylococcus pseudintermedius.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing using multiple platforms followed by de novo assembly and annotation.

full_output.paper_title: Suppressor Mutations Linking gpsB with the First Committed Step of Peptidoglycan Biosynthesis in Listeria monocytogenes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies suppressor mutations in clpC and murZ that restore growth of the L. monocytogenes ΔgpsB mutant, implicating these genes in the regulation of peptidoglycan biosynthesis.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, growth analysis, and Western blotting were used to validate the roles of clpC and murZ in suppressing the ΔgpsB phenotype.

full_output.paper_title: EssD, a Nuclease Effector of the Staphylococcus aureus ESS Pathway.

essD.notes: The L546P mutation in EssD abolishes its nuclease activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies EssD as a nuclease effector of the Staphylococcus aureus ESS pathway, which is involved in modulating host immune responses during infection. A mutation in EssD (L546P) inhibits its nuclease activity.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, protein purification, and functional assays were used to characterize EssD and its mutation.

full_output.paper_title: Combined Systems Approaches Reveal a Multistage Mode of Action of a Marine Antimicrobial Peptide against Pathogenic Escherichia coli and Its Protective Effect against Bacterial Peritonitis and Endotoxemia.
full_output.key_findings: The marine antimicrobial peptide N4 exhibits potent antibacterial activity against various pathogens, including Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, and protects mice from lethal challenges with E. coli and LPS. N4 disrupts bacterial membranes, inhibits DNA and RNA synthesis, and induces apoptosis-like cell death in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of cytological, transcriptomic, and biochemical approaches to investigate the mechanism of action of N4 against E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating Polymyxin B-Based Combinations against Carbapenem-Resistant Escherichia coli in Time-Kill Studies and in a Hollow-Fiber Infection Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of polymyxin B-based combinations against carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli (CREC) using time-kill studies and a hollow-fiber infection model. It found that polymyxin B combined with tigecycline was rapidly bactericidal and effectively suppressed the emergence of polymyxin B resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used time-kill studies and a hollow-fiber infection model to assess the activity of polymyxin B-based combinations against CREC strains.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of AmpC Derepression on Fitness and Virulence: the Mechanism or the Pathway?
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that high-level ampC overexpression, especially in an amidase-deficient background, significantly impairs the fitness and virulence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The findings highlight the importance of the pathway involved in ampC derepression rather than the mere overexpression of ampC itself.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, plasmid-based overexpression, and various microbiological assays including growth rate, motility, and virulence tests.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic and phenotypic heterogeneity in Streptococcus mutans isolated from diabetic patients in Rome, Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study found no antimicrobial resistance in Streptococcus mutans isolates from diabetic patients, highlighting the absence of resistant strains despite the potential risks associated with diabetes.
full_output.methodology: The study involved antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR screening, serotyping, and macrorestriction analysis to assess the genotypic and phenotypic characteristics of S. mutans isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanisms of Increased Resistance to Chlorhexidine and Cross-Resistance to Colistin following Exposure of Klebsiella pneumoniae Clinical Isolates to Chlorhexidine.

full_output.paper_title: Competitive Growth Enhances Conditional Growth Mutant Sensitivity to Antibiotics and Exposes a Two-Component System as an Emerging Antibacterial Target in Burkholderia cenocepacia.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the two-component system esaSR as a critical factor in antibiotic resistance in Burkholderia cenocepacia, with esaR playing an essential role in maintaining cell membrane integrity and efflux activity.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized a conditional growth mutant library, Illumina sequencing, and efflux activity assays to analyze antibiotic resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology and Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Clostridium difficile Isolates from a University Teaching Hospital in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the antimicrobial resistance profiles of 116 Clostridium difficile isolates, identifying high levels of resistance to ciprofloxacin, erythromycin, clindamycin, and levofloxacin, with notable differences in resistance rates among various molecular types.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing methods including MLST, PCR ribotyping, and MLVA were used alongside antimicrobial susceptibility testing via agar dilution.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of KPC Carbapenemase in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolated From Clinical Samples Using Modified Hodge Test and Boronic Acid Phenotypic Methods and Their Comparison With the Polymerase Chain Reaction.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 13 Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates (12%) positive for the blaKPC gene, indicating KPC carbapenemase production. The boronic acid phenotypic method showed higher sensitivity than the Modified Hodge Test for detecting KPC-producing strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic methods (Modified Hodge Test and boronic acid) were used to detect KPC carbapenemase in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Halogenated Pyrazine-Based Chalcones as Potential Antimicrobial Drugs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified novel halogenated pyrazine-based chalcones with antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus sp., particularly 15a and 15b showing significant inhibition.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and biological evaluation of halogenated pyrazine-based chalcones using microdilution broth methods for antifungal, antibacterial, and antimycobacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Human Lysozyme Synergistically Enhances Bactericidal Dynamics and Lowers the Resistant Mutant Prevention Concentration for Metronidazole to Helicobacter pylori by Increasing Cell Permeability.
full_output.key_findings: Human lysozyme (hLYS) enhances the bactericidal dynamics of metronidazole (MNZ) against Helicobacter pylori by increasing cell permeability, thereby reducing the resistant mutant prevention concentration (MPC) and improving the effectiveness of MNZ.
full_output.methodology: Experiments involving cell survival assays, permeabilization assays, and bactericidal kinetics were conducted to evaluate the effects of hLYS on H. pylori.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel Putrescine Exporter SapBCDF of Escherichia coli
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SapBCDF as a novel putrescine exporter in Escherichia coli, demonstrating its role in exporting putrescine from the cell to the extracellular environment.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, measurement of putrescine concentrations in culture supernatants, and complementation experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies clavanin-MO, a synthetic peptide with potent antimicrobial and immunomodulatory properties, effective against multidrug-resistant bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluates the antimicrobial activity of clavanin-MO against various bacterial strains, including multidrug-resistant isolates, and investigates its immunomodulatory effects in vitro and in vivo.

full_output.paper_title: Diverse drug-resistant subpopulations of Mycobacterium tuberculosis are sustained in continuous culture.

full_output.methodology: Sequencing of the katG gene and analysis of bacterial growth in chemostat cultures.

full_output.paper_title: The antifungal caspofungin increases fluoroquinolone activity against Staphylococcus aureus biofilms by inhibiting N-acetylglucosamine transferase.
full_output.key_findings: Caspofungin inhibits the activity of IcaA, a membrane-located N-acetylglucosamine transferase, thereby reducing the synthesis of poly-beta(1-6)-N-acetylglucosamine, a major component of S. aureus biofilm matrix, leading to increased fluoroquinolone penetration and efficacy against biofilms.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo experiments, including enzyme activity assays, biofilm formation studies, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Significance of nucleic acid testing in diagnosis and treatment of post-neurosurgical meningitis caused by multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii: a case report.

full_output.key_findings: The case report highlights the importance of molecular techniques in diagnosing post-neurosurgical meningitis caused by multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, identifying the presence of VEB, NDM-1, IMP, and OXA-58 genes.
full_output.methodology: Polymerase chain reaction-based assays were used to identify the causative pathogen and detect resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Genome Dynamics and Molecular Infection Epidemiology of Multidrug-Resistant Helicobacter pullorum Isolates Obtained from Broiler and Free-Range Chickens in India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple multidrug-resistant Helicobacter pullorum isolates from broiler and free-range chickens in India, highlighting the presence of resistance genes such as tufA, dna gyrA, cmeB, and aph(3')-Ib.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted to identify AMR genes and mutations in H. pullorum isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Autochthonous Aquatic Vibrio cholerae in Haiti.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in environmental isolates of Vibrio cholerae non-O1/non-O139 in Haiti, including strA, strB, sul1, sul2, ermA, ermB, and mefA, which confer resistance to streptomycin, sulfonamide, and erythromycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance-associated genes and disk diffusion susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and antimicrobial susceptibility of one antibiotic-sensitive and one multidrug-resistant Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii strain isolated from patients with granulomatous mastitis.

full_output.paper_title: Comparing culture and molecular methods for the identification of microorganisms involved in necrotizing soft tissue infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study compared culture and molecular methods for identifying microorganisms in necrotizing soft tissue infections (NSTIs), highlighting the ability of molecular methods to detect additional microorganisms not identified by culture. It identified S. pyogenes, Acinetobacter baumannii, Streptococcus pneumoniae, fungi, mycoplasma, and Fusobacterium necrophorum as causative agents.
full_output.methodology: The study used culture, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), 16S rRNA gene sequencing, Ibis T5000 biosensor, and 454 pyrosequencing to identify microorganisms in tissue samples from NSTI patients.

full_output.key_findings: PBP3 is essential for the growth of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and its deletion leads to significant growth defects and increased susceptibility to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout experiments, conditional deletion, growth assays, and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Relationship between antibiotic resistance genes and metals in residential soil samples from Western Australia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic resistance genes in residential soil samples from Western Australia, including beta-lactamase genes (bla TEM, bla CTX, bla OXA, bla SHV), tetracycline resistance genes (tet M, tet W), and sulfonamide resistance genes (sul 1, sul 2, sul 3). These genes were detected through quantitative PCR and showed associations with metal concentrations in the soil.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR was used to detect and quantify antibiotic resistance genes in soil samples.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Complete Antimicrobial Characterization of CEOBACTER, an Ag-Based Nanocomposite.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the synthesis and comprehensive antimicrobial characterization of CEOBACTER, an Ag-based nanocomposite. It demonstrates that CEOBACTER effectively eliminates bacterial growth with a minimal bactericidal concentration of 3 μg/ml, bactericidal action time of 2 hours, and re-use capacity of at least five times against E. coli cultures. The bactericidal mechanism is attributed to the release of Ag ions.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of CEOBACTER via a sol-gel process, followed by physico-chemical characterization using XRD, SEM, STEM, ICP-AES, and XPS. Antimicrobial properties were assessed through MIC, MBC, and LD50 determinations, as well as re-use capacity and ion-mediated bactericidal effect experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Inactivation of MSMEG_0412 gene drastically affects surface related properties of Mycobacterium smegmatis.
full_output.key_findings: The inactivation of the msmeg_0412 gene drastically affected the surface properties of Mycobacterium smegmatis, leading to enhanced drug susceptibility and deficiencies in GPLs production.
full_output.methodology: Construction of a null mutant strain, complementation analysis, and biochemical assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a high-throughput antimicrobial susceptibility assay (HIGA) to identify effective drugs and drug combinations against multidrug-resistant bacteria. It identified several drug combinations, including colistin–auranofin–ceftazidime and colistin–auranofin–rifabutin, that showed strong activity against multiple MDR strains.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a high-throughput screening assay (HIGA) combined with drug combination strategies to identify effective antimicrobial agents against MDR bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Use of molecular typing to investigate bacterial translocation from the intestinal tract of chlorpyrifos-exposed rats.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains in chlorpyrifos-exposed rats, demonstrating resistance to methicillin, oxacillin, and cefoxitin.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing (ERIC2-PCR and RAPD-PCR) and disk diffusion method were used to analyze bacterial translocation and antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus resistance to topical antimicrobials in atopic dermatitis.

full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of bacitracin resistance (100%) among Staphylococcus aureus isolates from atopic dermatitis patients in southern Brazil, along with low prevalence of mupirocin and fusidic acid resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Mycobacterium avium subsp. hominissuis secreted proteins using an in vitro system mimicking the phagosomal environment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified MAV_1356, a hypothetical protein in Mycobacterium avium subsp. hominissuis, which interacts with host proteins Annexin A1 and Protein S100-A8. This protein was found to be secreted into the macrophage cytosol and is part of the secretome induced by a metal mixture mimicking the phagosomal environment.
full_output.methodology: In vitro system mimicking phagosomal environment, beta-lactamase reporter system, pull-down assay, and mass spectrometry.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial Load in Daily Urine Samples of Patients Infected with Mycoplasma genitalium, Mutation Analysis, and Response to Treatment.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antibacterial activity of G1 (Furvina) and its conversion products, highlighting their reactivity with thiol groups and the resulting antimicrobial effects.
full_output.methodology: The study used colorimetric measurements, NMR spectroscopy, HPLC-HRMS analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to evaluate the stability, reactivity, and antibacterial effects of G1 and its conversion products.

full_output.paper_title: Surveillance of Dihydropteroate Synthase Genes in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia by LAMP: Implications for Infection Control and Initial Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed LAMP assays for the detection of sul1 and sul2 genes in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, which are responsible for sulfamethoxazole resistance. The LAMP assays showed high sensitivity and specificity, and the study found that sul1 and sul2 were prevalent in sulfamethoxazole-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used LAMP assays and PCR to detect sul1 and sul2 genes in clinical isolates of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the BD MAX Staph SR Assay for detecting Staphylococcus aureus and methicillin resistance in blood cultures, identifying mecA as a key gene for methicillin resistance.
