full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus species, including S. aureus, S. intermedius group, and coagulase-negative staphylococci, with multidrug resistance phenotypes. The mecA gene was found in all methicillin-resistant staphylococci, conferring resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of mecA gene, SCCmec typing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing by disk diffusion and oxacillin MIC determination.

full_output.paper_title: Genomics and Virulence of Klebsiella pneumoniae Kpnu95 ST1412 Harboring a Novel Incf Plasmid Encoding Blactx-M-15 and Qnrs1 Causing Community Urinary Tract Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the bla CTX-M-15 and qnrS1 genes on a novel IncFIB(K) plasmid pKpnU95 in a multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae ST1412 strain causing community urinary tract infections. The plasmid contributes to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) phenotype and quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, plasmid curing, reconstitution, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to characterize the AMR genes and their impact on resistance and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Volatiles and Antifungal-Antibacterial-Antiviral Activity of South African Salvia spp. Essential Oils Cultivated in Uniform Conditions.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial and antiviral activities of essential oils from South African Salvia species, identifying S. dentata EO as effective against certain fungi and the H1N1 virus.
full_output.methodology: Chemical analysis of essential oils and antimicrobial/antiviral testing using microdilution and Kirby-Bauer assays.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses ribosome protection proteins (RPPs) as significant contributors to antibiotic resistance, particularly against tetracyclines, fusidic acid, and various other antibiotics targeting the ribosome. Key RPPs include TetM, TetO, FusB, VgaA, LsaA, MsrE, MsrA, optrA, and poxtA, which confer resistance through mechanisms involving direct interaction with the ribosome and displacement of antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews experimental studies and structural analyses of ribosome protection proteins and their roles in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Potent Antimicrobial and Antibiofilm Activities of Feleucin-K3 Analogs Modified by α-(4-Pentenyl)-Ala against Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Feleucin-K3 analogs, K65 and K70, which show potent antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities against multidrug-resistant bacteria, including MRSA. These analogs exhibit improved stability, low hemolytic activity, and reduced resistance development compared to traditional antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and evaluation of Feleucin-K3 analogs, assessing their antimicrobial activity, stability, hemolytic activity, and antibiofilm effects through various in vitro and in vivo experiments.

full_output.paper_title: New O-Aryl-Carbamoyl-Oxymino-Fluorene Derivatives with MI-Crobicidal and Antibiofilm Activity Enhanced by Combination with Iron Oxide Nanoparticles.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the synthesis and evaluation of new O-aryl-carbamoyl-oxymino-fluorene derivatives and their enhanced antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity when combined with iron oxide nanoparticles. The compounds showed improved activity against bacterial and fungal strains, particularly against Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, spectral analysis (NMR, IR), and microbiological assays (MIC, MBEC) were used to evaluate the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of the compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Environmental Spread of Antibiotic Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The review discusses the environmental spread of antibiotic resistance, focusing on the mechanisms of ARG transmission and the hotspots of antibiotic contamination leading to the emergence of ARGs. It highlights the role of environmental factors such as agricultural practices, wastewater, and biocides in selecting and spreading antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The paper is a review article analyzing existing literature on the environmental spread of antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Human Papillomaviruses, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis and Mycoplasma genitalium among Female Sex Workers in Burkina Faso: Prevalence, Coinfections and Drug Resistance Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes, including bla QNR B, bla GES, bla SHV, bla CTX-M, and bla QNR S, in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, and Mycoplasma genitalium among female sex workers in Burkina Faso.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and classical PCR were used to detect HPV and antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Baicalein Ameliorates Streptococcus suis-Induced Infection In Vitro and In Vivo.

SLY.validation_method: co-incubation with purified protein and baicalein

full_output.key_findings: Baicalein inhibits the hemolytic activity of SLY, a virulence factor of Streptococcus suis, reducing inflammation and improving survival in infected mice.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial tests, hemolysis assays, circular dichroism analysis, and in vivo mouse models were used to evaluate the effects of baicalein on SLY and S. suis infection.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Analysis of a Novel Phage Infecting the Turkey Pathogen Escherichia coli APEC O78 and Its Endolysin Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a novel endolysin, LysO78, from the phage vB_EcoM_APEC, which exhibits broad-spectrum bacteriolytic activity against various Gram-negative bacteria, including E. coli APEC O78. Site-directed mutagenesis confirmed that E54 and E64 are critical catalytic residues for its lytic activity.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, genome sequencing, bioinformatics analysis, site-directed mutagenesis, and lytic activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Novel (+)-Neoisopulegol-Based O-Benzyl Derivatives as Antimicrobial Agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the synthesis and evaluation of novel (+)-neoisopulegol-based O-benzyl derivatives as antimicrobial agents, showing potent activity against various bacterial and fungal strains.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of O-benzyl derivatives and assessment of their antimicrobial activity against selected microorganisms.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of an Endolysin Targeting Clostridioides difficile That Affects Spore Outgrowth.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a cell wall hydrolase (CWH) from the C. difficile phage phiMMP01, demonstrating that the truncated form CWH 351-656 exhibits enhanced lytic activity against C. difficile strains and inhibits spore outgrowth.
full_output.methodology: The study involved cloning, expression, and purification of CWH and its subdomains, followed by lytic activity assays and structural modeling.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Mastitis and Antibiotic Resistance of Bacterial Isolates from CMT Positive Milk Samples Obtained from Dairy Cows, Camels, and Goats in Two Pastoral Districts in Southern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in bacterial isolates from milk samples, particularly in E. coli and S. aureus, with resistance to multiple antibiotics including penicillin, spectinomycin, ceftriaxone, clindamycin, and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method on Mueller-Hinton agar plates.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and sequencing were used to identify mutations in genes associated with tigecycline and colistin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Presence of plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) genes in non-typhoidal Salmonella strains with reduced susceptibility to fluoroquinolones isolated from human salmonellosis in Gyeonggi-do, South Korea from 2016 to 2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified PMQR genes such as qnrA, qnrB, qnrS, and aac(6')-Ib-cr in non-typhoidal Salmonella strains with reduced susceptibility to fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility tests, PCR amplification, and Sanger sequencing were used to detect PMQR genes and analyze QRDR regions.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis and phylogenetic position of the complex IncC plasmid found in the Spanish monophasic clone of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various AMR genes in the IncC plasmid pUO-STmRV1, including blaTEM-1, cmlA1, aac(3)-IV, aadA1, aadA2, sul1, sul2, sul3, tet(A), dfrA12, arsR2, arsH, merRTPCADE, and silESRCBAP, which confer resistance to antibiotics and heavy metals.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, in silico PCR typing, and MIC testing were used to analyze the plasmid and its resistance characteristics.

full_output.paper_title: The higBA-Type Toxin-Antitoxin System in IncC Plasmids Is a Mobilizable Ciprofloxacin-Inducible System.

A G64V mutation in the higB gene abolishes the toxicity and mRNA cleavage activity of the HigB toxin.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, overexpression, growth inhibition assays, qRT-PCR, and mutagenesis were used to characterize the higBA system.

full_output.paper_title: Secondary Infections in Hospitalized COVID-19 Patients: Indian Experience.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies high levels of carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii (92.6%) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (72.8%) among hospitalized COVID-19 patients in India, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug-resistant organisms.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of secondary infections in hospitalized COVID-19 patients from ten ICMR AMR network hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: Landscape of Multidrug-Resistant Gram-Negative Infections in Egypt: Survey and Literature Review.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative infections in Egypt, with significant resistance to carbapenems and extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs). Key resistance genes identified include blaNDM, blaKPC, blaVIM, blaIMP, blaOXA-48, blaCTX-M, blaSHV, and blaTEM.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and online survey of medical centers in Egypt.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Extensively-Drug Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Sequence Type 2 Co-Harboring bla (NDM) and bla (OXA) From Clinical Origin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of bla OXA-23, bla NDM-1, and bla OXA-51 genes in extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates, highlighting the co-harborance of these resistance genes in clinical settings.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance genes and phenotypes in the isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of FLASH, a chemiluminescent protease probe for detecting and monitoring drug susceptibility of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). FLASH is sensitive to fmol of recombinant Hip1 enzyme in vitro and can detect as few as thousands of Mtb cells in culture or in human sputum samples within minutes. FLASH can be used to measure antibiotic killing of Mtb in culture with greatly accelerated timelines compared to traditional protocols.
full_output.methodology: The study developed a chemiluminescent substrate probe for Mtb Hip1, tested its sensitivity and selectivity, and evaluated its ability to detect live Mtb and assess antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and biological evaluation of thiazolidinedione derivatives with high ligand efficiency to P. aeruginosa PhzS.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the synthesis and evaluation of thiazolidinedione derivatives as inhibitors of P. aeruginosa PhzS, a key enzyme in pyocyanin biosynthesis. Several compounds showed high affinity and ligand efficiency, with some demonstrating competitive inhibition of PhzS.
full_output.methodology: The study involved chemical synthesis of thiazolidinedione derivatives, their evaluation using thermal shift assays (TSA), and determination of their inhibitory effects on PhzS.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in domain V of Mycoplasma pneumoniae 23S rRNA and clinical characteristics of pediatric M. pneumoniae pneumonia in Nanjing, China.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the A2063G mutation in domain V of 23S rRNA in 92.39% of Mycoplasma pneumoniae strains, along with several novel mutations. However, these mutations were not associated with clinical characteristics of pediatric M. pneumoniae pneumonia.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of 23S rRNA domain V in Mycoplasma pneumoniae strains from pediatric patients with pneumonia.

full_output.paper_title: Responses to chemical cross-talk between the Mycobacterium ulcerans toxin, mycolactone, and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Mycolactone reduces S. aureus hemolytic activity and suppresses hla promoter activity without affecting S. aureus growth.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of aerobic bacterial pathogens associated with early embryonic death in pregnant New Zealand female Rabbits in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in bacterial pathogens associated with early embryonic death in rabbits, including iss, stx1, invA, stn, avrA, ompF, hly, hlg, tetA(A), aad1, blaTEM, and qac. These genes were detected through PCR and were linked to resistance against various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial sensitivity testing were used to identify AMR genes and resistance profiles in bacterial isolates from rabbit samples.

full_output.paper_title: Significance of the coexistence of non-codon 315 katG, inhA, and oxyR-ahpC intergenic gene mutations among isoniazid-resistant and multidrug-resistant isolates of Mycobacterium tuberculosis: a report of novel mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel mutations in the katG, inhA, and oxyR-ahpC genes associated with isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, highlighting the significance of these mutations in the development of multidrug-resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: Sanger DNA sequencing analysis was used to identify mutations in the katG, inhA, and oxyR-ahpC genes in isoniazid-resistant and multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Industrialization as a source of heavy metals and antibiotics which can enhance the antibiotic resistance in wastewater, sewage sludge and river water.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in wastewater, sewage sludge, and river water samples from two wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) in Poland, highlighting the impact of industrialization on the spread of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR was used to analyze the copy numbers of ARGs, integrase genes, and the 16S rRNA gene in environmental samples.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of multidrug resistant Enterobacterales strains isolated from liver and kidney transplant recipients in Spain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-G1 and bla OXA-48 as the primary resistance genes in multidrug-resistant Enterobacterales strains isolated from liver and kidney transplant recipients in Spain.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization of resistance genes through PCR and sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: A high-throughput screening assay based on automated microscopy for monitoring antibiotic susceptibility of Mycobacterium tuberculosis phenotypes.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed an automated live-cell imaging assay to monitor the growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis phenotypes and assess their susceptibility to antibiotics, revealing differences in susceptibility between planktonic and cording phenotypes.
full_output.methodology: Automated live-cell imaging and analysis of aggregate sizes to determine antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Klebsiella spp. cause severe and fatal disease in Mozambican children: antimicrobial resistance profile and molecular characterization.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-15 as the most prevalent ESBL gene in Klebsiella isolates from postmortem blood, along with genes associated with hypermucoviscosity (rmpA, wzi-K1) and invasiveness (traT).
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, multiplex PCR, and Sanger sequencing were used to identify AMR genes and virulence factors.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial, antifungal and antioxidant activities of whole plant chemical constituents of Rumex abyssinicus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several compounds from Rumex abyssinicus with antibacterial, antifungal, and antioxidant activities, but no AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: The paper focused on isolating and evaluating the antimicrobial and antioxidant properties of compounds from Rumex abyssinicus using various biochemical and microbiological assays.

full_output.paper_title: Safety and Efficacy of a Phage, kpssk3, in an in vivo Model of Carbapenem-Resistant Hypermucoviscous Klebsiella pneumoniae Bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the bla GIM gene in the CR-HMKP isolate NY03, which confers resistance to ceftazidime/avibactam. Phage kpssk3 showed high efficacy in treating CR-HMKP bacteremia in a mouse model with no significant toxicity.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, phage therapy in a mouse model, 16S rDNA sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: The Spatiotemporal Dynamics and Microevolution Events That Favored the Success of the Highly Clonal Multidrug-Resistant Monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium Circulating in Europe.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various AMR genes in the highly clonal multidrug-resistant monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium ST34, including beta-lactamases, sulfonamide resistance genes, tetracycline resistance genes, phenicol resistance genes, and polymyxin resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic screening and analysis of 298 Salmonella Typhimurium and S. 1,4,[5],12:i:- genomes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular survey of aminoglycoside-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolated from tertiary hospitals in Qazvin, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several aminoglycoside resistance genes, including aph(3')-VI, aac(6')-Ib, aac(3)-II, aph(3')-Ia, and armA, in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from Qazvin, Iran. These genes were associated with high levels of resistance to aminoglycosides such as gentamicin, tobramycin, and amikacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and sequencing to detect aminoglycoside resistance genes in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic surveillance of Neisseria gonorrhoeae in the Philippines, 2013-2014.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from the Philippines, including bla TEM for penicillin resistance, tetM for tetracycline resistance, and various mutations in gyrA, parC, mtrR, rpsJ, penA, ponA, and porB that contribute to resistance against penicillin, ciprofloxacin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in N. gonorrhoeae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: β-Lactam-Induced Cell Envelope Adaptations, Not Solely Enhanced Daptomycin Binding, Underlie Daptomycin-β-Lactam Synergy in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that β-lactam-induced cell envelope adaptations, rather than solely enhanced daptomycin binding, underlie daptomycin-β-lactam synergy in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. These adaptations include decreased surface charge, reduced membrane fluidity, and increased anionic phospholipid content, particularly cardiolipin.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized a qPCR assay targeting the fiu gene to measure Klebsiella colonization density in rectal swabs, validated through in silico analysis and experimental testing.

full_output.paper_title: The Burkholderia pseudomallei hmqA-G Locus Mediates Competitive Fitness against Environmental Gram-Positive Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the hmqA-G locus in Burkholderia pseudomallei as responsible for producing antimicrobial compounds that inhibit environmental Gram-positive bacteria. Mutations in hmqA, hmqD, and hmqF abolish this antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, complementation studies, and LC-MS analysis were used to characterize the role of the hmqA-G locus in antimicrobial activity.
full_output.sample_size: Approximately 8,000 Bp82 transposon mutants were screened.

full_output.paper_title: Cefdinir and β-Lactamase Inhibitor Independent Efficacy Against Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

katG.notes: associated with isoniazid resistance

rpoB.notes: associated with rifampin resistance

gyrA.notes: associated with fluoroquinolone resistance

full_output.key_findings: Cefdinir showed efficacy against both drug-susceptible and multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis without the need for a β-lactamase inhibitor. The study identified several mutations in Mtb strains associated with resistance to various anti-TB drugs.
full_output.methodology: The study used minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) experiments, dose-response studies, and a hollow fiber model of tuberculosis to evaluate cefdinir's efficacy and resistance profiles.
full_output.sample_size: 20 clinical isolates (8 drug susceptible and 12 MDR-TB)

full_output.paper_title: A New PqsR Inverse Agonist Potentiates Tobramycin Efficacy to Eradicate Pseudomonas aeruginosa Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a new QSI (Quorum Sensing Inhibitor) called QSI 4, which enhances the efficacy of tobramycin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms by targeting the PqsR regulator.
full_output.methodology: The research involved medicinal chemistry-driven optimization, biological profiling, and in vivo pharmacokinetic studies to develop and characterize QSI 4.

full_output.paper_title: Subtypes, resistance and virulence platforms in extended-drug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Romanian isolates.

blaOXA-24.evidence_note: The paper states that all isolates harbored the intrinsic bla OXA-51-like gene, 66.66% of A. baumannii revealed bla OXA-24 and 33.33% of A. baumannii isolates carried bla OXA-23.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes including bla OXA-23, bla OXA-24, bla OXA-51, and various aminoglycoside, sulfonamide, tetracycline, and macrolide resistance genes in XDR A. baumannii isolates from Romania.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing, PCR, WGS, PFGE, and MLST were used to characterize the AMR genes and resistance profiles of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Yeast-Host Interactions: Anadenanthera colubrina Modulates Virulence Factors of C. albicans and Inflammatory Response In Vitro.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effects of Anadenanthera colubrina extract on virulence factors of Candida albicans and its regulation on immune response. The extract showed antifungal activity with MIC <15.62 μg/ml against Candida strains, reduced biofilm and proteolytic activity, and modulated host immune response by decreasing IL-6 and IL-8 cytokine secretion.
full_output.methodology: Antifungal activity was assessed using broth microdilution method, biofilm assays, enzyme secretion assays, cytotoxicity tests, and real-time PCR for gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Novel tigecycline resistance mechanisms in Acinetobacter baumannii mediated by mutations in adeS, rpoB and rrf.

adeS.notes: Two types of mutations were observed in adeS: one resulting in a substitution in amino acid number 51 (E51K) and an insertion by the insertion sequence (IS) element IS Aba1.

rrf.notes: One SNP was observed in rrf (H33P)

rpoB.notes: One SNP was observed in rpoB (G136D)

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in adeS, rrf, and rpoB contribute to tigecycline resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii through various mechanisms, including altered ribosome recycling and efflux pump regulation.
full_output.methodology: Construction of mutant strains, MIC testing, Raman spectrometry, Western blot, and polysome profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and molecular characterization of pyrazinamide resistance among multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates in Ningbo, China.

pncA.mechanism: mutated pncA gene leads to reduced pyrazinamide susceptibility

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the pncA gene as the primary mechanism of pyrazinamide resistance among multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates in Ningbo, China.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing of the pncA gene was used to detect mutations associated with pyrazinamide resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Developing a model to predict individualised treatment for gonorrhoea: a modelling study.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a model to predict individual susceptibility to antibiotics for gonorrhoea treatment, aiming to reduce reliance on ceftriaxone. It found that cefixime and azithromycin had lower resistance prevalence compared to ciprofloxacin and penicillin, suggesting potential for their use in targeted treatment strategies.
full_output.methodology: The study used GRASP surveillance data to analyze antibiotic resistance prevalence in different patient subgroups and developed an Excel-based model to predict individualized treatment recommendations.

full_output.paper_title: Community-acquired bacteremia among HIV-infected and HIV-exposed uninfected children hospitalized with fever in Mozambique.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that community-acquired bacteremia was common in HIV-infected and HIV-exposed uninfected children in Mozambique, with high rates of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing organisms.
full_output.methodology: Observational study with blood culture and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

mutations_found.position_in_molecule: extracellular surface of the beta-barrel domain

tolC.notes: Mutations in the tolC gene conferred resistance to colicin E1 and TLS phage without affecting antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the tolC gene that confer resistance to colicin E1 and TLS phage without affecting antibiotic resistance, indicating that TolC is a highly evolvable target under negative selection.
full_output.methodology: Deep mutational scanning and fitness assays were used to analyze the effects of mutations in the tolC gene under various selection pressures.

full_output.paper_title: Adaptive Resistance Mutations at Suprainhibitory Concentrations Independent of SOS Mutagenesis.

rpoB.mechanism: Single nucleotide mutations in the rpoB gene confer resistance to rifampicin (RIF)

rpoB.notes: Single point mutation in the rpoB gene located in the rifampicin resistance determining region (RRDR) was identified in resistant clones.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies single nucleotide mutations in the rpoB gene as the primary mechanism of rifampicin resistance in Bartonella species, demonstrating that these mutations arise during antibiotic exposure rather than from pre-existing variants.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of resistant colonies, MIC testing, and experimental cultivation under various antibiotic concentrations.

full_output.paper_title: The Role of Whole Genome Sequencing in the Surveillance of Antimicrobial Resistant Enterococcus spp.: A Scoping Review.
full_output.key_findings: The scoping review highlights the significance of whole genome sequencing (WGS) in understanding antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Enterococcus spp., particularly focusing on the prevalence of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) and the identification of AMR genes such as vanA, vanB, and optrA.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a scoping review approach, analyzing 72 articles that focused on the use of WGS in the surveillance of AMR in Enterococcus spp.

full_output.paper_title: Nationwide Surveillance and Molecular Characterization of Critically Drug-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria: Results of the Research University Network Thailand Study.

blaOXA-48-like.role_in_paper: The paper discusses the prevalence and molecular characteristics of blaOXA-48-like genes in carbapenem-resistant isolates of E. coli and K. pneumoniae.
blaOXA-48-like.genetic_context: The paper mentions that blaOXA-48-like was the most prevalent carbapenemase gene in CR-E. coli and CR-K. pneumoniae isolates.
blaOXA-48-like.source: The paper discusses the prevalence and molecular characteristics of blaOXA-48-like genes in carbapenem-resistant isolates of E. coli and K. pneumoniae.
blaOXA-48-like.evidence_note: The paper states that blaOXA-48-like was the most prevalent carbapenemase gene in CR-E. coli and CR-K. pneumoniae isolates.

blaOXA-23-like.evidence_note: The paper states that bla OXA-23-like was the most prevalent carbapenemase gene in both MDR-A. baumannii and XDR-A. baumannii isolates.

blaVIM.evidence_note: bla VIM was detected in MDR- P. aeruginosa and XDR- P. aeruginosa

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M, bla NDM, bla OXA-48-like, bla OXA-23-like, bla IMP, and bla VIM as the primary resistance genes in critically drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria in Thailand.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization of bla genes through PCR and sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the pncA gene that confer resistance to pyrazinamide in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, highlighting the importance of detecting heteroresistance using methods like WGS.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, Bactec MGIT 960, and Wayne’s test were used to detect pyrazinamide heteroresistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic profiling of antibiotic resistance and virulence removal: Activated sludge vs. algal wastewater treatment system.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares the effectiveness of activated sludge (CAS) and algal wastewater treatment (A-WWT) systems in reducing antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and virulence genes (VGs). The A-WWT system was found to be more effective in reducing ARGs and VGs compared to the CAS system.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic shotgun sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to detect and analyze ARGs and VGs in wastewater samples from both treatment systems.
full_output.sample_size: Primary effluent (P), algal system effluent (A), and activated sludge system effluent (S)

full_output.paper_title: Accumulation of Succinyl Coenzyme A Perturbs the Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) Succinylome and Is Associated with Increased Susceptibility to Beta-Lactam Antibiotics.

relA.notes: mutations in relA and relQ are associated with high-level β-lactam resistance

relQ.notes: mutations in relA and relQ are associated with high-level β-lactam resistance

sucA.notes: mutations in sucA reverse the β-lactam susceptibility of the sucC mutant

sucB.notes: mutations in sucB reverse the β-lactam susceptibility of the sucC mutant

sucC.notes: sucC is a regulatory gene whose mutation affects β-lactam resistance

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the TCA cycle genes sucC and sucD increase susceptibility to β-lactam antibiotics in MRSA. The accumulation of succinyl-CoA in the sucC mutant leads to increased lysine succinylation, which impairs autolytic activity and increases β-lactam susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, complementation, and biochemical analyses were used to characterize the role of TCA cycle genes in β-lactam resistance.

full_output.paper_title: CroS(R391), an ortholog of the λ Cro repressor, plays a major role in suppressing polV(R391)-dependent mutagenesis.
full_output.key_findings: CroS R391 acts as a transcriptional repressor of the rumAB operon, reducing polV R391-dependent mutagenesis. Deletion of croS R391 leads to increased mutagenesis, highlighting its role in controlling mutagenesis in R391.
full_output.methodology: Mutagenesis assays, western blot analysis, and plasmid construction were used to investigate the role of CroS R391 in regulating rumAB and polV R391 activity.

full_output.paper_title: Mosaic Ends Tagmentation (METa) Assembly for Highly Efficient Construction of Functional Metagenomic Libraries.

full_output.key_findings: The study discovered novel nourseothricin resistance genes, including a potential new mode of resistance involving ribosome methylation. It also identified tetracycline and colistin resistance genes in a goose fecal microbiome library.
full_output.methodology: Functional metagenomic library preparation using METa assembly, subcloning, and resistance testing in E. coli.
full_output.sample_size: 5 μg soil metagenomic DNA, 300 ng goose fecal metagenomic DNA

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility profile of bacterial isolates from febrile children under 5 years of age in Nanoro, Burkina Faso.
full_output.key_findings: High resistance rates to common antibiotics were observed in bacterial isolates from febrile children in Nanoro, Burkina Faso. Escherichia coli isolates showed high resistance to trimethoprim-sulphamethoxazole, ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, ceftriaxone, and gentamycin. Salmonella isolates were highly resistant to ampicillin and trimethoprim-sulphamethoxazole. Multi-drug resistance was prevalent among the isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer method and E-test.

full_output.paper_title: Characterisation of mobile colistin resistance genes (mcr-3 and mcr-5) in river and storm water in regions of the Western Cape of South Africa.

mcr-3.37.evidence_note: The mcr-3.37 gene was cloned and expressed in E. coli, and the recombinant E. coli showed increased colistin MIC, confirming that mcr-3.37 confers colistin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified novel mcr-3 variants (mcr-3.33, mcr-3.34, mcr-3.35, mcr-3.36, mcr-3.37) and mcr-5.1 in water samples from the Western Cape of South Africa, demonstrating their ability to confer colistin resistance through cloning and BMD testing.
full_output.methodology: PCR, cloning, BMD testing, and Sanger sequencing were used to identify and validate mcr genes.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple water samples from rivers and storm water sources.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Analysis of Enterococcus spp. Isolated From a Wastewater Treatment Plant and Its Associated Waters in Umgungundlovu District, South Africa.

mef(A).evidence_note: The paper mentions that the E. durans isolate (E115) had the mef(A) gene as part of a resistance island.

tet(M).evidence_note: The tet(M) resistance gene was consistently found associated with a conjugative transposon protein (TcpC).

tet(L).evidence_note: The tet(M) resistance gene was consistently found associated with a conjugative transposon protein (TcpC).

tet(S).genetic_context: the genetic environment of the tetracycline resistance gene tet(S) was associated with the insertion sequence IS6

dfrG.evidence_note: The dfrG gene was identified in the plasmid pAD1 of E. faecalis strain 133170041-3.

aph(3')-IIIa.evidence_note: The genetic context of the tet(M) gene was found in 9/10 (90%) of isolates that harboured the tet(M) gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic resistance genes in Enterococcus spp. isolated from a wastewater treatment plant in South Africa, including genes conferring resistance to tetracycline, macrolides, aminoglycosides, and trimethoprim.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the antibiotic resistome, mobilome, and virulome of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance of Escherichia coli from Broilers, Pigs, and Cattle in the Greater Kumasi Metropolis, Ghana.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the bla CTX-M gene in Escherichia coli isolates from broilers and cattle, which confers resistance to various cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion and PCR for ESBL gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-Resistant and Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified OXA-48, MBL, and KPC carbapenemases in multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae isolates from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, highlighting the importance of detecting these resistance mechanisms for appropriate antimicrobial therapy.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic characterization of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae using disk diffusion and modified carbapenem inactivation test.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from combat casualties, highlighting reduced susceptibility to carbapenems, fluoroquinolones, and other antimicrobials, with amikacin and colistin retaining some efficacy.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, pulsed-field gel electrophoresis, and whole genome sequencing were used to analyze P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in bdcA and valS Correlate with Quinolone Resistance in Wastewater Escherichia coli.

gyrA.notes: known mutation

parC.notes: known mutation

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in bdcA and valS that correlate with quinolone resistance in wastewater E. coli, along with known mutations in gyrA and parC.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide association study (GWAS) combined with whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Advances in Bacteriophage Therapy against Relevant MultiDrug-Resistant Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: This review highlights the potential of phage therapy as an alternative to antibiotics for treating multidrug-resistant pathogens such as Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. It discusses various case reports and in vivo studies demonstrating the effectiveness of phage therapy in reducing bacterial loads and managing infections.
full_output.methodology: The review summarizes recent studies on phage therapy, including in vivo experiments and clinical case reports, focusing on the efficacy of phage cocktails and their combination with antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Antimicrobial Laser-Induced Photodynamic Therapy Based on Ethylcellulose/Chitosan Nanocomposite with 5,10,15,20-Tetrakis(m-Hydroxyphenyl)porphyrin.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed an ethylcellulose/chitosan nanocomposite loaded with 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(m-hydroxyphenyl)porphyrin (m THPP) for antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT). The nanocomposite effectively reduced the viability of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, and Candida albicans under laser irradiation.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial efficacy of m THPP-loaded nanocomposites using laser irradiation and assessed the photodynamic inactivation of microbial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Metallacarborane Derivatives Effective against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Yersinia enterocolitica.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies metallacarborane derivatives as effective against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Yersinia enterocolitica, demonstrating unique antibacterial properties and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized compound screening, IC50 determination, and SEM analysis to evaluate the antibacterial efficacy and resistance mechanisms of metallacarborane derivatives.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Fosfomycin Resistant E. coli from a Pigeon Farm in China.

fosA3.genetic_context: A comparative genomic analysis indicated that fosA3 was present in three genomic contexts including types Ⅰ, Ⅲ and Ⅴ, with Ⅰ being the most prevalent, which originated from faeces, ceca and sewage.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of fosA3-positive E. coli isolates in a pigeon farm in China, highlighting the role of horizontal and clonal transfer in the spread of fosfomycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, MLST, PFGE, and whole-genome sequencing were used to analyze fosfomycin-resistant E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of Novel Chemical Series of OXA-48 β-Lactamase Inhibitors by High-Throughput Screening.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel chemical series of OXA-48 β-lactamase inhibitors, highlighting the 4-ideneamino-4H-1,2,4-triazole (SC_2) and pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyridine (SC_7) cores as potential inhibitors. The most potent compound, ID2, inhibits OXA-48 via a reversible and competitive mechanism.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening of a proprietary compound collection against OXA-48, followed by biochemical and X-ray studies to determine the mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of the Anti-Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Activity of (+)-Tanikolide- and (+)-Malyngolide-Based Analogues Prepared by Asymmetric Synthesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two malyngolide-based analogues, (4S,6S)-4-methylmalyngolide and (4R,6S)-4-methylmalyngolide, which showed anti-methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus activity with MIC values of 12.5 µg/mL and 50 µg/mL, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and antibacterial activity testing of malyngolide analogues.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of a Library of Thioxanthones and Their Potential as Efflux Pump Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several thioxanthone derivatives with potential as efflux pump inhibitors, showing activity against bacterial strains and modulating P-gp expression and activity in mammalian cells.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of thioxanthone derivatives, in vitro antibacterial activity testing, efflux pump inhibition assays, and P-gp expression/activity evaluations.

full_output.paper_title: The Synergistic Activity and Optimizing Doses of Tigecycline in Combination with Aminoglycosides against Clinical Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA-48 and bla NDM genes as the primary carbapenemase determinants in clinical carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, with bla OXA-48 being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution, checkerboard technique, and multiplex PCR were used to assess antimicrobial susceptibility and identify resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence and Spread of Cephalosporinases in Wildlife: A Review.
full_output.key_findings: The review identifies CTX-M-1, CTX-M-14, CTX-M-15, and CMY-2 as the most prevalent cephalosporinases in wildlife, emphasizing their global spread and association with high-risk clones of E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Systematic literature review of publications on cephalosporinases in wildlife.
full_output.sample_size: 1980 publications analyzed, 149 included in the final review

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistant and Biofilm-Associated Escherichia coli Isolates from Diarrheic and Healthy Dogs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in E. coli isolates from healthy and diarrheic dogs, including blaTEM-1, qnrB, qnrS, aac(6')-Ib-cr, tetA, tetB, dfrA, sul1, sul2, int1, and tn3. These genes confer resistance to various antibiotics such as ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, trimethoprim, and sulfonamide.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and MIC testing for antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular and Anti-Microbial Resistance (AMR) Profiling of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) from Hospital and Long-Term Care Facilities (LTCF) Environment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the exfoliative toxin eta gene in all MRSA isolates and characterized the prevalence of various SCCmec types, including SCCmec III and IV, along with enterotoxin genes such as entB and entC. High levels of multidrug resistance were observed, particularly in isolates from hospital environments.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection, ERIC-PCR, SCCmec typing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to characterize MRSA isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 71.17% of bacterial isolates from juvenile green turtle rearing seawater were resistant to at least one antibiotic, with high resistance rates to beta-lactam antibiotics (ampicillin, penicillin, cefazolin) and low resistance to aminoglycosides (gentamicin, tobramycin, kanamycin, amikacin, streptomycin).
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the disc diffusion method on 111 bacterial isolates from seawater samples collected over three periods.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Determinants in Genomes and Plasmids from Acinetobacter baumannii Clinical Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes and mutations in Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates, including aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, beta-lactamases, sulfonamide resistance genes, and efflux pumps, along with mutations in gyrA, parC, lpxD, pmrA, and pmrB that contribute to resistance against various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, susceptibility testing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in A. baumannii isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Five A. baumannii clinical isolates and one reference strain.

full_output.paper_title: Low Glucose Mediated Fluconazole Tolerance in Cryptococcus neoformans.

AFR1.validation_method: qPCR and efflux pump activity assay

AFR2.validation_method: qPCR and efflux pump activity assay

full_output.key_findings: Low glucose conditions enhance fluconazole resistance in Cryptococcus neoformans by increasing the expression of efflux pump genes AFR1 and AFR2, leading to increased efflux pump activity.
full_output.methodology: qPCR, efflux pump activity assay, and MIC determination.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of High-Level Aminoglycoside-Resistant Enterococcus faecalis Isolated from Bulk Tank Milk in Korea.

ant(6)-Ia.mechanism: adds an adenosine group to aminoglycosides

full_output.key_findings: High-level aminoglycoside-resistant Enterococcus faecalis isolates from Korean bulk tank milk were found to carry aac(6')Ie-aph(2")-la, ant(6)-Ia, ermB, tetM, and tetL genes, which confer resistance to aminoglycosides, macrolides, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of antimicrobial resistance genes in E. faecalis isolates from bulk tank milk.

full_output.paper_title: Dynamics of Diversity and Abundance of Sulfonamide Resistant Bacteria in a Silt Loam Soil Fertilized by Compost.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the abundance and diversity of sulfonamide resistance genes (sul1 and sul2) in soil fertilized with compost, showing that compost increases the abundance of these genes, particularly in the presence of sulfadiazine.
full_output.methodology: qPCR and high throughput sequencing of sul1, sul2, and 16S rRNA genes.

full_output.paper_title: Prevotella melaninogenica, a Sentinel Species of Antibiotic Resistance in Cystic Fibrosis Respiratory Niche?
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 96% of P. melaninogenica isolates were beta-lactamase producers, with 34% resistant to clindamycin and 24% to moxifloxacin. Multidrug-resistant isolates were also detected.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the agar diffusion method and E-test strips.

full_output.paper_title: High Levels of Antibiotic Resistance Patterns in Two Referral Hospitals during the Post-Ebola Era in Free-Town, Sierra Leone: 2017-2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports high levels of antibiotic resistance in bacterial isolates from two referral hospitals in Sierra Leone, with resistance rates exceeding 90% for many antibiotics, including penicillin, ampicillin, gentamycin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method on bacterial isolates from various clinical samples.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and Genotypic Properties of Fluoroquinolone-Resistant, qnr-Carrying Escherichia coli Isolated from the German Food Chain in 2017.
