full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes and mutations in Australian E. coli ST131 isolates, including bla CTX-M-15 and bla CTX-M-27 for beta-lactam resistance, aadA5, strA, strB, mphA, dfrA17, sul1, qacEΔ1, and chrA for resistance to aminoglycosides, macrolides, trimethoprim, sulfonamides, quaternary ammonium compounds, and chromate. Fluoroquinolone resistance mutations in gyrA and parC were also found.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and antibiogram of Escherichia coli O157: H7 from diarrhoeic calves in urban and peri-urban dairy farms of Hawassa town.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that E. coli O157:H7 isolates from diarrhoeic calves in Hawassa town were highly sensitive to gentamycin, ceftriaxone, trimethoprim-sulphamethoxazole, and ciprofloxacin, but resistant to tetracycline, kanamycin, and amoxicillin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting faecal samples from diarrhoeic calves, isolating E. coli O157:H7, and performing antibiotic susceptibility testing using the disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Prediction and Analysis in silico of Genomic Islands in Aeromonas hydrophila.

Mph(A) family.evidence_note: The Mph(A) family is listed in the traits encoded in predicted genomic islands (GIs) of strains AL06-06, ZYAH75, MX16A, and WCHAH045096, and is associated with resistance to macrolides.

APH(3″)-I.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the gene is part of the predicted genomic islands in A. hydrophila strains and is associated with aminoglycoside resistance.

AAC(6′)-Ib/AAC(6′)-II.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the gene is part of the predicted GIs and is associated with resistance to aminoglycosides.

CmlA family.evidence_note: The paper mentions 'chloramphenicol resistance, MFS efflux pump - CmlA family' in the context of resistance genes in genomic islands.

FloR family.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the FloR family is associated with chloramphenicol/florfenicol resistance in the context of genomic islands.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic resistance genes in Aeromonas hydrophila genomic islands, including genes conferring resistance to aminoglycosides, chloramphenicol, sulfonamides, tetracyclines, macrolides, beta-lactams, and mercury.
full_output.methodology: In silico analysis of genomic islands in Aeromonas hydrophila genomes.

full_output.key_findings: The study found low carbapenem resistance (3%) among Acinetobacter strains and low 30-day mortality (16%) in patients with Acinetobacter bacteraemia in South Sweden.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study analyzing blood cultures and susceptibility testing of Acinetobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Meropenem-Resistant Pandoraea Pneumonia in a Critically Ill Patient With COVID-19.
full_output.key_findings: The case presents a critically ill patient with COVID-19 who developed ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia caused by Pandoraea species, which showed resistance to meropenem and other carbapenems but remained susceptible to imipenem, amikacin, ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and minocycline.
full_output.methodology: Clinical case report with susceptibility testing using broth microdilution and interpretation according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates to cefixime and cefpodoxime among bacterial isolates from infected chronic wounds, with complete susceptibility to cefoperazone+sulbactam except for 7.1% resistance in Proteus spp.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial culture, identification, and broth microdilution susceptibility testing were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Alterations of fecal antibiotic resistome in COVID-19 patients after empirical antibiotic exposure.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several antibiotic resistance genes, including OXA_209, major facilitator superfamily transporter, EmrB_QacA family major facilitator transporter, mexF, and mexD, which are associated with increased resistance in the fecal microbiota of COVID-19 patients exposed to empirical antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of fecal samples from COVID-19 patients and healthy controls to identify antibiotic resistance genes and their abundance.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Salmonella Typhi Isolated From a Referral Hospital of Kathmandu, Nepal.

gyrA.notes: The gyrA ser83 mutation was found in 95.65% of S. Typhi isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 95.65% of S. Typhi isolates carried the gyrA ser83 mutation, which is associated with reduced susceptibility to fluoroquinolones. Additionally, there was an increase in azithromycin MIC values among S. Typhi isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, MIC determination, and PCR-RFLP analysis were used to identify resistance mechanisms in S. Typhi isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteria Are New Targets for Inhibitors of Human Farnesyltransferase.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial effects of farnesyltransferase inhibitors (FTIs) lonafarnib and tipifarnib against various Gram-positive bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus, methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), Staphylococcus epidermidis, and Streptococcus pneumoniae. Both FTIs exhibited bactericidal effects on these bacteria, while no effect was observed on Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized agar well diffusion assays, time kill assays, and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) determinations to assess the antibacterial efficacy of lonafarnib and tipifarnib against a panel of bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-Genome Epidemiology and Characterization of Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus ST398 From Retail Pork and Bulk Tank Milk in Shandong, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in MSSA ST398 isolates from retail pork and bulk tank milk in Shandong, China, including DHA-1, blaZ, aac(6')-Ie-aph(2'')-Ia, tetL, and tetK, which confer resistance to penicillin, gentamicin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes in MSSA ST398 isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance in patients with suspected urinary tract infections in primary care in Assam, India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several ESBL genes, including bla CTX-M-15, bla SHV-148, bla PER-1, and bla TEM, as well as the carbapenemase gene bla NDM-1, in E. coli isolates from patients with UTIs in Assam, India. These genes contribute to multidrug resistance and highlight the need for improved diagnostic and treatment strategies.
full_output.methodology: PCR, phenotypic testing, and sequence analysis were used to characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of colistin heteroresistance in carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and association with clinical outcomes in patients: an observational study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that colistin heteroresistance was present in up to 26% of carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) isolates, depending on the definition used. However, no significant association was found between colistin heteroresistance and 90-day mortality.
full_output.methodology: The study used a modified population analysis profile (mPAP) technique to detect colistin heteroresistance in CRPA isolates and compared it with the reference PAP method. Clinical outcomes were analyzed using logistic regression.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effects of an antimicrobial feed additive composed of essential oils, medium-chain fatty acids, and a toxin-adsorbing mineral on diarrhea and gut microbiome in weanling pigs infected with E. coli. full_output.methodology: The study involved feeding weanling pigs a diet supplemented with 0.25% or 0.50% of the antimicrobial blend and analyzing fecal and ileal microbiota using 16S rRNA sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of novel rapid diagnostic of blood culture identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing by Accelerate Pheno system and BioFire FilmArray Blood Culture Identification and BioFire FilmArray Blood Culture Identification 2 panels.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a monoclonal antibody (B39) that targets the O-antigen of Klebsiella pneumoniae O1 and O2 strains, demonstrating protective efficacy in a murine pneumonia model.

full_output.paper_title: Astaxanthin-Mediated Bacterial Lethality: Evidence from Oxidative Stress Contribution and Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antibacterial mechanism of astaxanthin, highlighting its ability to induce oxidative stress and disrupt bacterial viability through increased superoxide anion levels and decreased glutathione concentration. It also suggests that astaxanthin interacts with topoisomerases IV ParC and ParE, potentially affecting DNA replication.
full_output.methodology: Computational molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations, along with in vitro antioxidant and antimicrobial assays.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-Locus Sequence Typing and Drug Resistance Analysis of Swine Origin Escherichia coli in Shandong of China and Its Potential Risk on Public Health.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in swine and human-origin E. coli, including blaTEM, cmlA, flor, tetC, tetW, qacEΔ1-sulI, and aac(6′)-Ib, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as beta-lactams, chloramphenicol, tetracycline, and quinolones.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect AMR genes in E. coli isolates from swine and human sources.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains Causing Intestinal Colonization and Extraintestinal Infections: Clinical, Virulence, and Molecular Epidemiological Characteristics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC-2 as the predominant carbapenemase gene in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) strains, with high prevalence in both intestinal colonization and extraintestinal infection groups.

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the mechanisms of antibiotic heteroresistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae, focusing on colistin, carbapenems, tetracyclines, and aminoglycosides. full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the presence and distribution of ClpK in Klebsiella species, identifies its structural features, and reports the successful expression and purification of ClpK, demonstrating its ATPase activity.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics analysis, molecular dynamics simulation, protein expression, purification, and biophysical characterization.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Polyketide Metabolites from Penicillium bissettii and P. glabrum.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified polyketide metabolites from Penicillium bissettii and P. glabrum, including penicillic acid (1), citromycetin (2), penialdin A (3), penialdin F (4), and myxotrichin B (5). Among these, penicillic acid (1) and penialdin F (4) showed antimicrobial activity against Methicillin-resistant S. aureus, with penialdin F (4) exhibiting the strongest activity.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and structural elucidation of polyketide metabolites from Penicillium species, followed by antimicrobial activity testing against various bacterial and fungal strains.

full_output.paper_title: Urinary Tract Infections in Kidney Transplant Recipients-Is There a Need for Antibiotic Stewardship?

full_output.paper_title: Structural basis for the context-specific action of the classic peptidyl transferase inhibitor chloramphenicol.
full_output.key_findings: The study elucidates the structural basis for the context-specific action of chloramphenicol (CHL), demonstrating that the penultimate residue of the nascent peptide influences CHL binding and ribosome stalling. Specific interactions between CHL and the penultimate amino acid residue (such as threonine, alanine, or serine) enhance CHL's affinity for the ribosome, leading to effective ribosome stalling. Conversely, bulky residues like phenylalanine hinder CHL binding, reducing its effectiveness.
full_output.methodology: High-resolution crystallography and biochemical assays were used to analyze the structural interactions between CHL, peptidyl-tRNA analogs, and the ribosome.

waaL.notes: The waaL gene encodes an O-antigen ligase. Mutants with an inactivated waaL gene cannot complete the lipopolysaccharide (LPS) biosynthesis pathway, and thus, they lack the surface-exposed portion of O-antigen molecules.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three novel lytic phages (MLP1, MLP2, and MLP3) that effectively infect and kill multidrug-resistant E. coli strains, including UPEC and InPEC. The phages recognize different regions of the lipopolysaccharide (LPS) molecule, with MLP1 and MLP3 targeting the O-antigen and MLP2 targeting the LPS outer core. Mutations in genes involved in LPS biosynthesis, such as waaL, rfaG, rfaI, rfaH, c2564, c2559, and c3693, were found to confer resistance to phage infection.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, EOP assays, LPS profiling, and whole-genome sequencing of phage-resistant mutants were used to identify phage receptors and analyze resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Potentiating the Anti-Tuberculosis Efficacy of Peptide Nucleic Acids through Combinations with Permeabilizing Drugs.

Ethambutol significantly improves the effectiveness of anti-inhA PNA by increasing membrane permeability.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized broth microdilution assays, disc diffusion assays, and NPN permeability assays to assess the efficacy of anti-inhA PNA and permeabilizing drugs against mycobacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Real time monitoring of Staphylococcus aureus biofilm sensitivity towards antibiotics with isothermal microcalorimetry.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a real-time isothermal microcalorimetry method to assess the sensitivity of Staphylococcus aureus biofilms to antibiotics. It found that biofilms can survive exposure to maximum serum concentrations of various antibiotics, with rifampicin showing the best initial efficacy but resistance developing in some strains. Combination therapies with rifampicin and other antibiotics were more effective in preventing resistance.
full_output.methodology: Isothermal microcalorimetry was used to monitor biofilm sensitivity to antibiotics in real-time, alongside traditional susceptibility testing methods like VITEK 2 and broth microdilution.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of meropenem/vaborbactam (M/V) plus aztreonam (ATM) for treating bloodstream infections caused by ceftazidime/avibactam-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CAZ/AVI-R-Kp) when carbapenemase gene typing was unavailable. full_output.paper_title: Lagoon, Anaerobic Digestion, and Composting of Animal Manure Treatments Impact on Tetracycline Resistance Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the impact of various manure treatment methods on tetracycline resistance genes (tet genes) and found that lagoons, anaerobic digesters, and composting have varying degrees of effectiveness in reducing these genes. full_output.sample_size: Multiple farms and lagoon systems studied.

full_output.paper_title: ICU-Associated Gram-Negative Bloodstream Infection: Risk Factors Affecting the Outcome Following the Emergence of Colistin-Resistant Isolates in a Regional Greek Hospital.

full_output.paper_title: Combination of Amphiphilic Cyclic Peptide [R(4)W(4)] and Levofloxacin against Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antibacterial activity of the cyclic peptide [R 4 W 4 ] and its combination with levofloxacin against multidrug-resistant bacteria. full_output.paper_title: Mechanisms of Action of Carbapenem Resistance.

full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of existing studies on carbapenem resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Evaluation of Various Honey Types against Carbapenemase-Producing Gram-Negative Clinical Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antibacterial activity of various Greek honeys against carbapenemase-producing Gram-negative clinical isolates, highlighting the effectiveness of certain honeys in inhibiting bacterial growth.

full_output.paper_title: Human Serum Proteins and Susceptibility of Acinetobacter baumannii to Cefiderocol: Role of Iron Transport.

full_output.paper_title: An In Vivo Model of Separate M. tuberculosis Phagocytosis by Neutrophils and Macrophages: Gene Expression Profiles in the Parasite and Disease Development in the Mouse Host.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of ALDH1A1 Gene Knockout on Drug Resistance in Paclitaxel and Topotecan Resistant Human Ovarian Cancer Cell Lines in 2D and 3D Model.

full_output.paper_title: 4-Arylthiosemicarbazide Derivatives as Toxoplasmic Aromatic Amino Acid Hydroxylase Inhibitors and Anti-inflammatory Agents.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of Plant Antimicrobial Peptides against Selected Pathogenic Bacterial Species Using a Peptide-Protein Docking Approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the binding interactions of selected antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) with specific bacterial proteins using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. Napin and snakin-1 showed strong interactions with penicillin-binding protein 1a of Acinetobacter baumannii, glucose-1-phosphate thymidylyltransferase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, streptomycin 3''-adenylyltransferase of Salmonella enterica, oxygen-insensitive NADPH nitroreductase of Helicobacter pylori, and penicillin-binding protein 2a of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the interactions between selected antimicrobial peptides and bacterial receptor proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Large-Scale Samples Based Rapid Detection of Ciprofloxacin Resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae Using Machine Learning Methods.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed machine learning models to rapidly detect ciprofloxacin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CIRKP) using MALDI-TOF MS data, achieving high accuracy with AUC values up to 0.89.
full_output.methodology: The study used machine learning models (SVM, XGB, LR, RF) combined with MALDI-TOF MS data and non-spectrometric features to predict ciprofloxacin resistance in K. pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Prolonged Outbreak of Carbapenem and Colistin-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae at a Large Tertiary Hospital in Brazil.

mgrB.notes: mutations in mgrB gene are associated with colistin resistance
mgrB.evidence_note: The paper states that alterations in the mgrB gene, including insertion sequence IS 903B, premature stop codon (Q30*), and thymine deletion at position 104 (104delT), were detected in 87.5% of the isolates and are associated with colistin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: An Update on African Trypanocide Pharmaceutics and Resistance.

TbAAT6.mechanism: deletion or mutation leads to eflornithine resistance
TbAAT6.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

TeDR40.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses various trypanocidal drugs and their resistance mechanisms, highlighting the role of specific transporters and genes such as TbAAT6, P2, and TeDR40 in mediating resistance to eflornithine, melarsoprol, and diminazene aceturate, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Review of literature and discussion of resistance mechanisms in African trypanosomes.

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed 34 cases of pediatric pneumococcal meningitis post-PCV13 introduction in Japan, identifying penicillin-resistant S. pneumoniae strains (26.5%) and highlighting the increase in non-PCV13 serotypes. All strains were susceptible to vancomycin and linezolid, while daptomycin showed favorable MIC values.
full_output.methodology: Clinical and bacteriological analysis of S. pneumoniae strains from pediatric pneumococcal meningitis cases, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing and serotyping.

full_output.paper_title: 50S subunit recognition and modification by the Mycobacterium tuberculosis ribosomal RNA methyltransferase TlyA.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TlyA as a ribosomal RNA methyltransferase that modifies 23S rRNA nucleotide C2144 by 2′-O-methylation, which is crucial for optimal activity of the antitubercular drug capreomycin.
full_output.methodology: Structural and functional analyses using cryo-electron microscopy, mutagenesis, and enzymatic activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance including Extended Spectrum Beta Lactamases (ESBL) among E. coli isolated from kenyan children at hospital discharge.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates from Kenyan children at hospital discharge, with notable resistance to ampicillin, gentamicin, ceftriaxone, and the presence of ESBL. Risk factors for ESBL-producing E. coli included antibiotic use during hospitalization, prior hospitalization, and open defecation.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing via disc diffusion and statistical analysis of risk factors.

full_output.paper_title: Oryza-Specific Orphan Protein Triggers Enhanced Resistance to Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae in Rice.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Xio1, an Oryza-specific orphan gene, which when overexpressed in rice, leads to enhanced resistance against Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae. However, this overexpression also causes severe growth retardation and premature death in transgenic plants.
full_output.methodology: Transgenic rice plants were generated to overexpress Xio1, and their resistance to Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae was assessed through lesion length measurements and bacterial colony counts.

full_output.paper_title: The prevalence of virulence determinants in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolated from different infections in hospitalized patients in Poland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several virulence genes in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates, including eno, ebps, fib, fnbB, bbp, cna, map/eap, splA, splE, sspA, etB, etD, sea, seb, sec, sed, see, and tst. These genes were associated with adhesion, proteolysis, and toxin production, highlighting their roles in MRSA pathogenesis.
full_output.methodology: PCR and spa typing were used to analyze the presence of virulence genes in MRSA isolates from various clinical sources.

full_output.paper_title: Nepetin reduces virulence factors expression by targeting ClpP against MRSA-induced pneumonia infection.
full_output.key_findings: Nepetin was identified as a ClpP inhibitor that reduces the virulence of MRSA by inhibiting the expression of virulence factors such as α-toxin and PVL.
full_output.methodology: The study used biochemical assays, molecular docking, and in vivo experiments to demonstrate the inhibitory effect of nepetin on ClpP and its impact on MRSA virulence.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that a high-fat/low-fiber diet increased mortality in a murine model of antibiotic-induced Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). The diet led to higher levels of C. difficile toxin TcdA, altered bile acid profiles, and reduced levels of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and secondary bile acids, which are protective against CDI.
full_output.methodology: The study used a murine model of antibiotic-induced CDI, analyzing the effects of different diets on C. difficile infection outcomes, bile acid levels, and gut microbiome composition through various biochemical and microbiological techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Structural basis to repurpose boron-based proteasome inhibitors Bortezomib and Ixazomib as β-lactamase inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Bortezomib and Ixazomib as inhibitors of the serine β-lactamase CTX-M-14, demonstrating their ability to mimic the deacylation transition state and inhibit β-lactam hydrolysis.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography and inhibition assays were used to analyze the interaction between Bortezomib/Ixazomib and CTX-M-14.

full_output.paper_title: Ultrafast and Cost-Effectiveness Pathogen Identification and Resistance Gene Detection in a Clinical Setting Using Nanopore Flongle Sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the effectiveness of Oxford Nanopore Technology's Flongle sequencing for rapid bacterial identification and detection of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in clinical settings. It identifies several beta-lactamase genes (TEM-1B, CTX-M-2, CTX-M-14, CTX-M-35, SHV-187) and other resistance genes (fosA, oqxA) in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing using Flongle and comparison with Illumina and MinION data for validation.
full_output.sample_size: 4 clinical isolates of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, and 2 blood samples.

full_output.paper_title: Increased Drug Resistance and Biofilm Formation Ability in ST34-Type Salmonella Typhimurium Exhibiting Multicellular Behavior in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in ST34-type Salmonella Typhimurium strains, including BlaCTXM, BlaTEM, Bloxa, BlaNDM-5, flo, sulI, sulII, TetA, TetB, and mcr-1, which contribute to resistance against various antibiotics such as ampicillin, florfenicol, sulfamethoxazole, tetracycline, imipenem, and polymyxin B.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of antibiotic resistance genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: TonB-Dependent Receptors Affect the Spontaneous Oxytetracycline Resistance Evolution in Aeromonas Hydrophila

tonB.encodes: outer membrane receptor involved in iron acquisition
tonB.resistance_mechanism_class: efflux pump or outer membrane permeability
tonB.validation_method: experimental analysis of spontaneous resistance evolution

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies tonB and fepA as TonB-dependent receptors affecting spontaneous oxytetracycline resistance evolution in Aeromonas hydrophila.
full_output.methodology: Experimental analysis of spontaneous resistance evolution in Aeromonas hydrophila.

full_output.paper_title: First Report of a Methicillin-Resistant, High-Level Mupirocin-Resistant Staphylococcus argenteus.

mupA.evidence_note: The paper states that the mupA gene was found on a plasmid in the isolate and that it conferred mupirocin resistance.

blaZ.evidence_note: The paper states that the second plasmid (20,644 bp) carried the resistance determinants for penicillin (blaZ).

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first methicillin-resistant, high-level mupirocin-resistant Staphylococcus argenteus isolate, which harbors the mupA gene on a plasmid and the blaZ gene on another plasmid.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR detection, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Synthetic Biology Tool Development Advances Predictable Gene Expression in the Metabolically Versatile Soil Bacterium Rhodopseudomonas palustris.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on developing synthetic biology tools for Rhodopseudomonas palustris, particularly addressing challenges related to antibiotic resistance and gene expression. It identified the need for higher antibiotic concentrations for selection and characterized the sensitivity of R. palustris to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study involved constructing plasmids, testing antibiotic sensitivity, and using fluorescent reporters to characterize gene expression in R. palustris.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several natural product compounds that act as colistin adjuvants, enhancing the antibiotic's efficacy against multidrug-resistant bacteria. These adjuvants do not themselves confer resistance but enhance colistin's activity by mechanisms that may involve increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic whole-cell screening of a natural product library combined with antibiotic susceptibility testing and mechanistic studies including MALDI-TOF analysis, RT-qPCR, and ROS measurement.

full_output.paper_title: Chemical-genetic interaction mapping links carbon metabolism and cell wall structure to tuberculosis drug efficacy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes involved in carbon metabolism and cell wall biosynthesis that influence rifampicin efficacy in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, highlighting the role of metabolic states and cell wall structure in drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput hypomorph mutant analysis and growth inhibition assays were used to evaluate the impact of gene depletion on antibiotic efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Convergence of virulence and resistance in international clones of WHO critical priority enterobacterales isolated from Marine Bivalves.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various CTX-M-type and CMY-type beta-lactamase genes in multidrug-resistant Enterobacterales isolated from marine bivalves, highlighting the presence of resistance and virulence genes in marine environments.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, in vitro experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted to investigate the virulence and resistance profiles of the isolated bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: CRISPR-Cas System: An Adaptive Immune System's Association with Antibiotic Resistance in Salmonella enterica Serovar Enteritidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies antibiotic resistance genes gyrA, blaTEM-1, and tetB in Salmonella enteritidis isolates from poultry, highlighting their association with antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing to identify resistance genes and assess resistance profiles in Salmonella enteritidis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phytochemical Profiling of the Leaf Extract of Ximenia americana var. caffra and Its Antioxidant, Antibacterial, and Antiaging Activities In Vitro and in Caenorhabditis elegans: A Cosmeceutical and Dermatological Approach.
full_output.key_findings: The leaf extract of Ximenia americana var. caffra contains various secondary metabolites with antioxidant, antibacterial, and antiaging activities. It inhibits enzymes involved in skin aging and reduces oxidative stress in Caenorhabditis elegans.
full_output.methodology: The study used HPLC-PDA-ESI-MS/MS for phytochemical profiling, enzyme inhibition assays, and in vivo experiments with C. elegans to evaluate antioxidant and antiaging effects.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characteristics of Antimicrobial Resistance and Virulence in Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains Isolated from Goose Farms in Hainan, China.

blaNDM-5.genetic_context: blaNDM-5 was present in all 33 CRKP isolates and was carried on IncX3 plasmids in 32 of the 33 isolates.
blaNDM-5.evidence_note: The paper states that all 33 CRKP isolates possessed blaNDM-5 and that the gene was carried on IncX3 plasmids in 32 of the 33 isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla NDM-5 as a prevalent carbapenem resistance gene in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from goose farms in Hainan, China. Additionally, other resistance genes such as bla CTX-M, aadA, oqxAB, tet, and mcr-1 were also detected, highlighting the complex resistance profiles of these isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and plasmid analysis were used to characterize the resistance and virulence features of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characteristic, Antibiotic Resistance, and Detection of Highly Immunoreactive Proteins of Group B Streptococcus Strains Isolated From Urinary Tract Infections in Polish Adults.

ermB.evidence_note: The ermB gene was detected in every strain with cMLS B phenotype.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified ermB and mefA/E genes as contributors to macrolide resistance in Group B Streptococcus (GBS) strains isolated from urinary tract infections in Polish adults. The ermB gene was present in all cMLS B phenotype strains, while mefA/E was found in three M phenotype strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR, disk diffusion, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis were used to analyze antibiotic resistance and genetic characteristics of GBS strains.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance Profile of Common Bacteria Isolated from Blood Stream, Lower Respiratory Tract and Urinary Infections in Intensive Care Unit in Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance among common bacteria isolated from ICU patients in Saudi Arabia, including Klebsiella pneumoniae, Coagulase-negative staphylococci, Escherichia coli, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Staphylococcus aureus. Notably, resistance to aztreonam, ampicillin, co-amoxiclav, cotrimoxazole, and cephalosporin group antibiotics was prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical isolates and antibiotic susceptibility testing using standardized methods.

full_output.paper_title: Silver Resistance in Gram-Negative Pathogens: Endogenous Mechanisms and Genetic Determinants

ompK36.evidence_note: The paper states that a single mutation in cusS gene and loss of major porins conferred silver resistance in the five K. pneumoniae strains.

cusS.notes: Mutation in cusS leads to silver resistance in K. pneumoniae.

ompK35.notes: Mutations in ompK35 lead to silver resistance in K. pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies silS and silR as key genes involved in silver resistance in Gram-negative bacteria, along with mutations in cusS and ompK35 contributing to endogenous silver resistance. Additionally, various beta-lactamase and other resistance genes were found in sil-positive strains.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and phenotypic testing were performed to characterize silver resistance mechanisms and associated genes.

full_output.paper_title: Gene expression analysis of resistant and susceptible rice cultivars to sheath blight after inoculation with Rhizoctonia solani.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes involved in rice resistance to sheath blight, including OsPR1b, OsPAL1, OsPAL6, and OsWRKY30, which show altered expression patterns in resistant versus susceptible rice cultivars upon R. solani infection.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq and qRT-PCR were used to analyze gene expression changes in rice cultivars after R. solani infection.
full_output.sample_size: Two rice cultivars: Shennong 9819 (resistant) and Koshihikari (susceptible)

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a two-component regulatory system involved in antimicrobial peptide resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TCS01 and BceAB as a two-component regulatory system and ABC transporter involved in antimicrobial peptide resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Deletion mutant strains, qPCR, Western blot, and EMSA were used to investigate the roles of TCS01 and BceAB in antimicrobial peptide resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Exposure Aggravates Bacteroides-Linked Uremic Toxicity in the Gut-Kidney Axis.

Bacteroides acidifaciens.mechanism: production of indole metabolites linked to uremic toxicity
Bacteroides acidifaciens.validation_method: functional assessment of dysbiotic microbiota and in vitro indole production test

full_output.key_findings: Bacteroides acidifaciens was identified as a key producer of indole metabolites, contributing to uremic toxicity in a gut-kidney axis model. Its presence exacerbated cisplatin-induced renal injury and increased levels of indoxyl sulfate, a uremic toxin.
full_output.methodology: Clinical transcriptome analysis, mouse model of renal injury, 16S rRNA sequencing, and in vitro indole production assays.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a Novel Antimicrobial Peptide From the Ancient Marine Arthropod Chinese Horseshoe Crab, Tachypleus tridentatus.
full_output.key_findings: A novel antimicrobial peptide, Tatritin, was identified and characterized in the hemolymph of Chinese horseshoe crab, Tachypleus tridentatus, infected with Gram-negative bacteria. Tatritin exhibited broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against various bacteria and fungi.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis, qRT-PCR, peptide synthesis, and antimicrobial activity assays were used to characterize Tatritin.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular mechanisms underlying the emergence of polygenetic antifungal drug resistance in msh2 mismatch repair mutants of Cryptococcus.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that mutations in the MSH2 gene, which is involved in DNA mismatch repair, lead to an elevated mutation rate and contribute to the emergence of antifungal resistance in Cryptococcus neoformans. Resistance is due to small contributions from mutations in many genes rather than a single gene.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, and flow cytometry were used to analyze the genetic changes and resistance mechanisms in msh2 mutants.
full_output.sample_size: 27 independently isolated fluconazole- or amphotericin B-resistant strains

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a d-stereospecific peptidase produced by Bacillus anthracis that hydrolyzes gramicidin A, suggesting a mechanism of intrinsic resistance against non-ribosomal peptide antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Peptidase activity was analyzed using fluorogenic peptide substrates, protease inhibitors, and MALDI-TOF analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies VapC2 and VapC21 toxins from Mycobacterium tuberculosis that specifically cleave and inactivate initiator tRNA fMet, leading to translation inhibition and cell death. These toxins are part of toxin-antitoxin (TA) systems and could serve as targets for developing novel antitubercular agents.
full_output.methodology: The study used RNA-seq, in vitro cleavage assays, and protein expression analyses to characterize the function of VapC2 and VapC21 toxins.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Putative Vaccine and Drug Targets against the Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus by Reverse Vaccinology and Subtractive Genomics Approaches.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several potential vaccine candidates and drug targets against MRSA, including PrsA, EssA, PBP1, and PBP2, which are highlighted for their antigenic properties and potential as therapeutic targets.
full_output.methodology: Reverse vaccinology and subtractive genomics approaches were used to identify potential vaccine and drug targets.

full_output.paper_title: The Healing Capability of Clove Flower Extract (CFE) in Streptozotocin-Induced (STZ-Induced) Diabetic Rat Wounds Infected with Multidrug Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Proteus mirabilis LC587231 as a multidrug-resistant strain resistant to cefepime, and demonstrated the antibacterial efficacy of clove flower extract (CFE) against this strain.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility tests, GC-MS phytochemical screening, and wound healing experiments in diabetic rat models.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Effect of Lithocholic Acid with Gentamicin against Gram-Positive Bacteria but Not against Gram-Negative Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Lithocholic acid (LCA) enhances the bactericidal effect of gentamicin (Genta) against Gram-positive bacteria, including Listeria monocytogenes, Staphylococcus aureus, and Streptococcus suis, but not against Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Checkerboard microdilution, BacLight LIVE/DEAD staining, scanning electron microscopy, and biofilm inhibition assays were used to evaluate the synergistic effects of LCA with Genta.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptional Regulation of RIP2 Gene by NFIB Is Associated with Cellular Immune and Inflammatory Response to APEC Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NFIB as a transcription factor that binds to the promoter region of the RIP2 gene, enhancing its expression and contributing to APEC-induced immune and inflammatory responses in chicken HD11 cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used gene overexpression, RNA interference, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, dual luciferase reporter assay, CHIP-PCR, and flow cytometry to investigate the role of RIP2 and NFIB in APEC infection.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterisation of second-line drug resistance among drug resistant tuberculosis patients tested in Uganda: a two and a half-year's review.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several mutations associated with second-line drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including gyrA D94G and A90V mutations for fluoroquinolone resistance, and rrs A1401G for injectable agent resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Line Probe Assay Genotype MTBDRsl Version 2.0 to characterize mutations in M. tuberculosis isolates from patients with rifampicin and/or isoniazid resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of a Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia coli Co-Carrying a New mcr-1.33 Variant and bla (NDM-5) Genes Recovered from a Urinary Tract Infection.

bla(NDM-5).genetic_context: an insertion sequence IS Aba125 exists upstream of bla NDM-5 as a truncated fragment harboring IS 5 and IS 3000 . The bla NDM-5 gene is downstream of the ble MBL , trpF, tat and IS 26 elements

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first multidrug-resistant ST101 E. coli strain in China carrying a new mcr-1.33 variant and bla NDM-5 genes, highlighting the emergence of plasmid-mediated resistance to colistin and carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed to characterize the resistance mechanisms in the E. coli isolate.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo efficacy of WCK 6777 (ertapenem/zidebactam) against carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae in the neutropenic murine pneumonia model.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vivo efficacy of WCK 6777 (ertapenem/zidebactam) against carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae, demonstrating potent activity against isolates with WCK 6777 MICs up to 8 mg/L.
full_output.methodology: The study used a neutropenic murine pneumonia model to assess the efficacy of WCK 6777 against carbapenemase-producing K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanistic insights into tRNA cleavage by a contact-dependent growth inhibitor protein and translation factors.

full_output.paper_title: Population structure of blaKPC-harbouring IncN plasmids at a New York City medical centre and evidence for multi-species horizontal transmission.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes blaKPC-harbouring IncN plasmids and identifies their role in carbapenem resistance among various Enterobacterales species, highlighting horizontal transmission.
full_output.methodology: Short- and long-read sequencing, hybrid assembly, and comparative genomic analysis were used to analyze plasmid structures and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: In Vivo Antibacterial Efficacy of Antimicrobial Peptides Modified Metallic Implants─Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial efficacy of antimicrobial peptide (AMP)-modified metallic implants in preventing bacterial infections in vivo, showing that AMP-coated implants significantly reduced bacterial counts compared to controls.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of in vivo studies assessing the antibacterial effects of AMP-modified implants.

full_output.paper_title: Stone Age Yersinia pestis genomes shed light on the early evolution, diversity, and ecology of plague.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genetic variations in ancient Yersinia pestis genomes, including deletions and pseudogenizations, which suggest reduced virulence and flea transmission efficiency in the LNBA− lineage.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of ancient Y. pestis samples using next-generation sequencing and phylogenetic comparisons.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial and parasite co-infection in Mexican golden trout (Oncorhynchus chrysogaster) by Aeromonas bestiarum, Aeromonas sobria, Plesiomonas shigelloides and Ichthyobodo necator.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first case of co-infection by Aeromonas bestiarum, Aeromonas sobria, Plesiomonas shigelloides, and Ichthyobodo necator in a Mexican golden trout. All bacterial isolates were resistant to amoxicillin-clavulanic acid and cefazoline, with P. shigelloides showing resistance to third-generation β-lactams.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial sensitivity tests were conducted using disk diffusion methods according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: The regulation of hsacirc_004413 promotes proliferation and drug resistance of gastric cancer cells by acting as a competing endogenous RNA for miR-145-5p.

hsacirc_004413.validation_method: knockdown experiments showing increased sensitivity to 5-Fu

full_output.key_findings: hsacirc_004413 promotes drug resistance in gastric cancer cells by acting as a competing endogenous RNA for miR-145-5p, leading to reduced sensitivity to 5-Fu.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing, qPCR, CCK-8 assay, and antisense RNA transfection.

full_output.paper_title: A facile and general method for synthesis of antibiotic-free protein-based hydrogel: Wound dressing for the eradication of drug-resistant bacteria and biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel antibiotic-free protein hydrogel (B-Hydrogel) synthesized using tetrakis (hydroxymethyl) phosphonium sulfate (THPS) and bovine serum albumin (BSA). This hydrogel exhibits potent antibacterial activity against drug-resistant bacteria such as MRSA and SA, as well as effective anti-biofilm properties. The hydrogel promotes wound healing in MRSA-infected mice without significant side effects.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and characterization of B-Hydrogel, along with in vitro and in vivo evaluations of its antibacterial and wound-healing properties using techniques such as SEM, TEM, LDH release assays, and animal experiments.

full_output.paper_title: A shotgun metagenomics approach to detect and characterize unauthorized genetically modified microorganisms in microbial fermentation products.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes various AMR genes, including cat, aadD, ble, ermB, and bla, in genetically modified microbes (GMMs) using shotgun metagenomics. These genes were detected through metagenomics sequencing and qPCR, confirming their presence in the GMM strains.

full_output.paper_title: Overcoming Multidrug Resistance (MDR): Design, Biological Evaluation and Molecular Modelling Studies of 2,4-Substituted Quinazoline Derivatives.

full_output.methodology: PCR-based screening for antibiotic resistance genes and molecular typing techniques including MLST and agr typing.

full_output.paper_title: QSAR, Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Simulation Studies of Sigmacidins as Antimicrobials against Streptococci.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified sigmacidins as a class of benzoic acid derivatives that inhibit the bacterial RNA polymerase-σ factor interaction, showing excellent antimicrobial activity against Streptococci. Computational approaches, including QSAR, docking, and MD simulations, were used to understand the structural basis and mechanism of action of these compounds.
full_output.methodology: Computational methods including QSAR, docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were employed to analyze the structure-activity relationship and binding mechanisms of sigmacidins against Streptococci.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Antimicrobial Potential of CAPE and Caffeamide Derivatives against Oral Microbes.

mecA.notes: 36M repressed the expression of mecA in MRSA.

mecI.notes: 36M repressed the expression of mecI in MRSA.

mecR1.notes: 36M repressed the expression of mecR1 in MRSA.

full_output.key_findings: 36M repressed the expression of drug-resistance genes mecA, mecI, and mecR1 in MRSA, suggesting its potential to reduce antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was assessed via agar diffusion, MIC/MBC determination, and biofilm formation assays. Gene expression was analyzed using RT-qPCR.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm and Gene Expression Characteristics of the Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales, Escherichia coli IMP, and Klebsiella pneumoniae NDM-1 Associated with Common Bacterial Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified and characterized several AMR genes, including blaIMP, blaNDM-1, marA, ramA, csgA, mqsR, bssS, fimH, luxS, tnaA, intl, soxS, evgA, entB, and ycfM, which are associated with biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance in E. coli IMP and K. pneumoniae NDM-1.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR and CLSM to analyze gene expression and biofilm formation in E. coli IMP and K. pneumoniae NDM-1 under different growth conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Mutations in Putative Nicotinic Acid Phosphoribosyltransferases of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Their Effect on Protein Thermodynamic Properties.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel mutations in pncB1 and pncB2 of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, focusing on their structural effects and potential implications for protein stability and function.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and structural analysis using computational tools like DynaMut and PSIPRED.

full_output.paper_title: Two Novel Lytic Bacteriophages Infecting Enterococcus spp. Are Promising Candidates for Targeted Antibacterial Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes two novel lytic bacteriophages, SSsP-1 and GVEsP-1, which show promise for targeted antibacterial therapy against Enterococcus spp. The phages exhibited broad and moderate host ranges, respectively, and did not contain known antibiotic-resistance determinants or virulence factors.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, transmission electron microscopy, in vitro efficacy testing, host range determination, DNA isolation, whole-genome sequencing, and bioinformatic analysis were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of a Novel Oligosaccharide from Streptomyces californics against Erwinia carotovora subsp. Carotovora.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a novel oligosaccharide from Streptomyces californics with antibacterial activity against Erwinia carotovora subsp. carotovora. The compound was identified as having a molecular formula of C29H53NO18 and C14H26O9, and it exhibits significant antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of analytical techniques including UV/Vis, FT-IR, 1H- and 13C-NMR, and mass spectrometry to characterize the antibacterial agent. Additionally, the production of the compound was optimized using ANFIS and ANN models.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of Quorum-Sensing Regulator from Pseudomonas aeruginosa Using a Flavone Derivative.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a flavone derivative, E6, as a potent inhibitor of the Pseudomonas aeruginosa las quorum-sensing system by binding to the LasR regulator and preventing its DNA-binding capability.
full_output.methodology: The study used a luciferase reporter assay, fluorescent thermal shift assay, electrophoretic mobility shift assay, and molecular docking to characterize the inhibitory activity of the flavone derivative E6 against the LasR regulator.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Functional Composite Cu(II)-Polyoxometalate/PLA with Antimicrobial Properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of a Cu(II)-polyoxometalate/PLA composite with antimicrobial properties against E. coli, showing significant inhibition zones and reduced colony counts.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of POMs, preparation of PLA composite films, copper ion release studies, and antimicrobial activity evaluation via agar diffusion tests.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Investigation of the Impact of Bacterial-Fungal Interaction on Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: Two carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae isolates (ST101) lost bla-CTX-M-14, bla-OXA-48, tir, strA, and strB genes after co-culture with Scopulariopsis brevicaulis. The other three isolates (ST383 and 147) remained carbapenem-resistant.
full_output.methodology: Genotypic comparison via next-generation sequencing (NGS) and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST).

full_output.paper_title: Regulation of CDK6-PI3K axis on ABCB1-mediated drug resistance

ABCB1.validation_method: knockout of cdk6 gene induced downregulation of ABCB1 expression and reversal of MDR

full_output.key_findings: Knockout of cdk6 gene in KB-C2 cells led to downregulation of ABCB1 expression and reversal of ABCB1-mediated drug resistance, particularly against colchicine and paclitaxel.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR/Cas9 gene knockout, transcriptome sequencing, Western blot, and immunofluorescence analysis.

full_output.paper_title: CinA mediates multidrug tolerance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

cinA.mechanism: mediates drug tolerance via cleavage of NAD-drug adducts

full_output.key_findings: CinA mediates tolerance to isoniazid, ethionamide, delamanid, and pretomanid in Mycobacterium tuberculosis through cleavage of NAD-drug adducts.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screens, mutant construction, complementation studies, and biochemical analyses.

full_output.paper_title: The High Risk of Bivalve Farming in Coastal Areas With Heavy Metal Pollution and Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria: A Chilean Perspective.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the co-occurrence of heavy metal and antibiotic resistance in Vibrio spp., highlighting the potential risks posed by contaminated bivalve farms. It emphasizes the role of heavy metals in selecting for antibiotic resistance and the potential for co-selection of resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The paper is a review article analyzing existing literature on heavy metal and antibiotic resistance in Vibrio spp. in the context of bivalve farming in Chile.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Analysis of Short- and Long-Read Sequencing of Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci for Application to Molecular Epidemiology.

vanC.validation_method: presence in isolates detected by SR-NGS and LR-NGS

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized various AMR genes in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus isolates, including vanA, vanB, vanC, aminoglycoside resistance genes like AAC(6')-Ii, aad(6), ANT(9)-Ia, APH(3')-IIIa, and AAC(6')-Ie-APH(2'')-Ia, tetracycline resistance genes like tetM and tetU, trimethoprim resistance gene dfrG, MLS resistance genes like ErmA, ErmB, msrC, lsaA, and vatD, and the streptothricin resistance gene SAT-4.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing using both short-read and long-read next-generation sequencing technologies was employed to identify AMR genes and mutations in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Heteroresistance Is Associated With in vitro Regrowth During Colistin Treatment in Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that colistin heteroresistance in carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CR-KP) is associated with in vitro regrowth during treatment. Overexpression of phoPQ and pmrD was identified as a key mechanism of colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Population analysis profiling (PAP), time-kill assays, transcriptomic analysis, and qRT-PCR were used to investigate colistin resistance mechanisms and the effectiveness of combination therapies.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance genes aph(3')-III, erm(B), sul2 and tet(W) abundance in animal faeces, meat, production environments and human faeces in Europe.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the abundance of four antimicrobial resistance genes (aph(3')-III, erm(B), sul2, and tet(W)) in various animal and human samples across Europe, highlighting variations in resistance profiles across different species and environments.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR (qPCR) was used to analyze the abundance of antimicrobial resistance genes in a large dataset of samples from animals, meat, production environments, and humans.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic tracking of antibiotic resistance genes through a pre-harvest vegetable production system: an integrated lab-, microcosm- and greenhouse-scale analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a diverse array of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in vegetables, particularly radishes and lettuces, highlighting the potential for agricultural practices to contribute to the spread of ARGs. Key clinically relevant ARGs included blaKPC-15, blaKPC-10, blaCARB, blaCTX-M, blaOXA, blaTEM, blaSHV, blaVIM, blaMCR-4.2, blaMCR-8.1, blaOXA-226, blaOXA-278, blaOXA-296, blaOXA-347, and vanA.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analyses were used to profile and track ARGs across different sample types including amendments, soils, and vegetables.

full_output.paper_title: Penicillin- and Ciprofloxacin-Resistant Invasive Neisseria meningitidis Isolates from Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified penicillin- and ciprofloxacin-resistant Neisseria meningitidis isolates in Japan, highlighting the emergence of invasive lineages with resistance to these antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and core-genome phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the genetic features of the resistant isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Transposable Element Insertions into the Escherichia coli Polysialic Acid Gene Cluster Result in Resistance to the K1F Bacteriophage.
full_output.key_findings: Insertion sequences caused disruptions in the kpsE and neuC genes, leading to resistance against the K1F bacteriophage in Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing, phenotypic analysis, and growth curve experiments were conducted to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: S51 Family Peptidases Provide Resistance to Peptidyl-Nucleotide Antibiotic McC.

mccG.mechanism: hydrolyzes the carboxamide bond in processed McC-like compounds
mccG.validation_method: overexpression in E. coli and resistance assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MccG, a peptidase from Nocardia vaccinii, that provides resistance to peptidyl-nucleotide antibiotics like McC by hydrolyzing the carboxamide bond in processed McC-like compounds.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, protein expression, in vitro hydrolysis assays, and resistance testing in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Acetylation of CspC Controls the Las Quorum-Sensing System through Translational Regulation of rsaL in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: CspC regulates the Las quorum-sensing system by repressing the translation of rsaL, which in turn affects the production of pyocyanin and QS signal molecules.
full_output.methodology: Binding assays, qRT-PCR, Western blot, EMSA, and mutagenesis studies.

full_output.key_findings: The paper analyzes the failure of antibiotic candidates in the clinical pipeline against Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting issues such as toxicity, lack of efficacy, and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Review and analysis of clinical development data, preclinical studies, and toxicology reports of antibiotic candidates.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Potency and Spectrum of the Novel Polymyxin MRX-8 Tested against Clinical Isolates of Gram-Negative Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the in vitro potency and spectrum of the novel polymyxin MRX-8 against clinical isolates of Gram-negative bacteria, showing comparable activity to colistin and polymyxin B against most isolates, except those with acquired or intrinsic resistance to polymyxins.
full_output.methodology: The study assessed the antimicrobial activity of MRX-8, colistin, and polymyxin B against a large set of Gram-negative clinical isolates using MIC testing and comparative analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Cefotaxime Exposure Selects Mutations within the CA-Domain of envZ Which Promote Antibiotic Resistance but Repress Biofilm Formation in Salmonella.

GGCTGG insertion between L406 and A407

envZ.notes: associated with increased cefotaxime MIC and reduced biofilm formation

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the envZ gene, particularly R397H, INFR1, and INFR2, were identified as the primary mechanism of cefotaxime resistance in Salmonella. These mutations alter the ATPase activity of EnvZ, leading to reduced OmpF porin expression and increased cefotaxime resistance, but also repress biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, phenotypic analysis, ATPase activity assay, qRT-PCR, and SEM were used to characterize the mutations and their effects.

full_output.paper_title: Real-Life Use of Ceftolozane/Tazobactam for the Treatment of Bloodstream Infection Due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Neutropenic Hematologic Patients: a Matched Control Study (ZENITH Study).
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of ceftolozane/tazobactam (C/T) in treating bloodstream infections caused by multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in neutropenic hematologic patients, showing improved outcomes compared to other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: A multicenter, matched-cohort study comparing patients treated with C/T to those treated with other antibiotics, analyzing clinical outcomes and resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Extraintestinal Pathogenic Escherichia coli Utilizes Surface-Located Elongation Factor G to Acquire Iron from Holo-Transferrin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies elongation factor G (EFG) as a surface-localized protein in ExPEC that binds holo-transferrin and facilitates iron acquisition, contributing to bacterial survival in macrophages.
full_output.methodology: Binding assays, mutagenesis, and functional studies in E. coli and macrophages.

full_output.paper_title: Metabolic preference assay for rapid diagnosis of bloodstream infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a rapid metabolic preference assay (MPA) and metabolic inhibition assay (MIA) for diagnosing bloodstream infections and determining antimicrobial susceptibility, reducing testing times significantly compared to conventional methods.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized metabolomics and metabolic profiling techniques to identify biomarkers and assess antimicrobial susceptibility through changes in metabolite production and consumption.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of the murine gut resistome following broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the evolution of the murine gut resistome following broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment, highlighting the role of integrons in mediating antimicrobial resistance. Specific genes such as bla, vanA, and mcr were found to confer resistance to beta-lactam, glycopeptide, and polymyxin antibiotics, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Longitudinal fecal sampling, metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), and functional analysis of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs).

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis DosS binds H(2)S through its Fe(3+) heme iron to regulate the DosR dormancy regulon.
full_output.key_findings: Mycobacterium tuberculosis DosS binds H2S through its Fe(3+) heme iron, leading to increased autokinase activity and phosphorylation of DosR, thereby regulating the DosR dormancy regulon.
full_output.methodology: Spectroscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, and kinase assays were used to investigate the interaction of H2S with DosS and its impact on DosR phosphorylation.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of ceftolozane-tazobactam, imipenem-relebactam, and ceftazidime-avibactam against Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from U.S. hospitals, highlighting the effectiveness of these agents against multidrug-resistant and difficult-to-treat resistance isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used CLSI broth microdilution to determine MICs and analyzed the susceptibility of P. aeruginosa isolates to various antimicrobial agents.

full_output.paper_title: Empirical antibiotic choice alters microbiological outcomes: Findings from comparative antibiograms in a trauma intensive care unit.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that escalating empirical antibiotic therapy from piperacillin-tazobactam to imipenem and amikacin led to a reduction in multidrug-resistant (MDR) Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, as well as an increase in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales. The findings emphasize the importance of antibiogram-guided empirical antibiotic selection in managing antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of bacterial and fungal susceptibility data from a trauma ICU over two time periods, comparing organism prevalence and resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic Analysis of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Wastewater Treatment Plants
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in influent and effluent water samples from municipal wastewater treatment plants, including beta-lactamases (blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCTX-M, blaOXA), tetracycline resistance (Tet), sulfonamide resistance (Sul), chloramphenicol resistance (Cat), and multidrug efflux pumps (MDF). These genes were detected through metagenomic analysis and showed varying levels of abundance and distribution between the two water sources.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomics sequencing followed by analysis of the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) to identify and characterize ARGs in influent and effluent water samples.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacodynamic Evaluation of Zoliflodacin Treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae Strains With Amino Acid Substitutions in the Zoliflodacin Target GyrB Using a Dynamic Hollow Fiber Infection Model.

full_output.paper_title: Cefiderocol for the Treatment of Multidrug-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria: A Systematic Review of Currently Available Evidence.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the resistance mechanisms of cefiderocol against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting that mutations in the target gene PBP-3 may contribute to cefiderocol resistance.
full_output.methodology: The paper includes experimental validations and analyses of resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: First study on diversity and antimicrobial-resistant profile of staphylococci in sports animals of Southern Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant staphylococci (MRS) in sports animals, with a high prevalence of mecA and blaZ genes. S. sciuri was the most common species, showing high resistance to penicillins and cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and species identification via VITEK 2.

full_output.paper_title: Plantaricin A, Derived from Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, Reduces the Intrinsic Resistance of Gram-Negative Bacteria to Hydrophobic Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: Plantaricin A (PlnA) and its analog OP4 enhance the permeability of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, thereby reducing intrinsic antibiotic resistance and enhancing the efficacy of hydrophobic antibiotics. Mutations in lpxA, waaC, waaY, and expression of mcr-1 affect the interaction of PlnA with LPS, influencing outer membrane permeability.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic modifications, MIC testing, and biochemical assays to evaluate the impact of PlnA and OP4 on bacterial outer membrane permeability and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Spiropyrimidinetrione DNA Gyrase Inhibitors with Potent and Selective Antituberculosis Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies spiropyrimidinetrione (SPT) compounds as potent and selective DNA gyrase inhibitors with activity against drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). These compounds demonstrate high inhibitory potency against Mtb DNA gyrase and lower Mtb MICs compared to existing antibiotics, with selectivity for Mtb over other bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the synthesis, structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis, and biological assessment of SPT compounds, including their evaluation against Mtb, S. aureus, and E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype distribution and antimicrobial resistance of invasive Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates among Croatian adults during a fifteen-year period (2005-2019).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ermB and mefA genes as contributors to macrolide resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates from Croatian adults.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of invasive pneumococcal isolates with capsular typing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Omadacycline Efficacy against Streptococcus Agalactiae Isolated in China: Correlation between Resistance and Virulence Gene and Biofilm Formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in S. agalactiae isolates from China, including ermB, ermC, OptrA, msrB, mefAE, tetM, tetO, and tetK, which are associated with resistance to various antibiotics. The scpB gene was found to be significantly correlated with biofilm formation in OMC-resistant S. agalactiae.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance and virulence genes, MIC testing, and biofilm formation analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characterization of the WYL BrxR protein and its gene as separable regulatory elements of a BREX phage restriction system.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the BrxR gene as a regulatory element of a BREX phage restriction system in Acinetobacter, showing that it is required for phage restriction but not for host methylation.
full_output.methodology: The study uses whole-genome sequencing, gene deletion, and functional assays to characterize the BREX system and the role of BrxR.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and molecular characterization of Staphylococcus aureus causing bovine mastitis in water buffaloes from the Hazara division of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified low levels of methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from bovine mastitis in the Hazara division of Pakistan. No antiseptic resistance genes (qacA/B, smr) or mupirocin resistance genes (mupA, mupB) were detected in the isolates.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization, PCR amplification, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were performed on S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a phage-derived depolymerase specific for KL47 capsule of Klebsiella pneumoniae and its therapeutic potential in mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a phage-derived capsule depolymerase, P560dep, which specifically targets the KL47 capsule of Klebsiella pneumoniae, demonstrating significant antibiofilm activity and therapeutic potential in mice against carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae infections.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, gene cloning, protein expression and purification, activity assays, and in vivo mouse infection experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Proteomics and metabolomics analysis reveal potential mechanism of extended-spectrum β-lactamase production in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies differentially expressed proteins and metabolites associated with extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) production in E. coli, highlighting the purine metabolism pathway as a potential mechanism.
full_output.methodology: TMT proteomics and untargeted metabolomics analysis were used to compare ESBL-producing and non-ESBL-producing E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial susceptibility in bloodstream infections: results from China Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Trial (CARST) program, 2015–2016
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing resistance rates of gram-negative bacteria, especially P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii, to various antimicrobial agents, with particular emphasis on carbapenem resistance and the limited effectiveness of current treatments.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial susceptibility data from bloodstream infections in China over a 10-year period, focusing on resistance trends and susceptibility profiles of common gram-negative pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Cytotoxic effect of green silver nanoparticles against ampicillin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that green silver nanoparticles (N-SNPs) exhibit strong bactericidal activity against ampicillin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, affecting gene expression related to DNA damage, biofilm formation, and virulence.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar well diffusion assay, qRT-PCR, and TEM to evaluate the antibacterial effects of N-SNPs and AgNO3 against K. pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: PLGA/xylitol nanoparticles enhance antibiofilm activity via penetration into biofilm extracellular polymeric substances.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that PLGA nanoparticles loaded with xylitol enhance antibiofilm activity by penetrating the biofilm extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) and improving the effectiveness of xylitol against bacterial biofilms.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the development and characterization of PLGA/xylitol nanoparticles, including particle size, zeta potential, polydispersity index, morphology, entrapment efficiency, and drug release studies. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated using XTT assays and live/dead viability staining.

full_output.paper_title: An iron-chelating sulfonamide identified from Drosophila-based screening for antipathogenic discovery.

full_output.paper_title: Demonstrating the utility of Escherichia coli asymptomatic bacteriuria isolates' virulence profile towards diagnosis and management-A preliminary analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several virulence genes associated with E. coli isolates from asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB) in pregnant women, including fimH, papC, sfa, iroN, fyuA, hlyA, cnf, sat, usp, kpsMTII, ompT, and chuA. full_output.paper_title: Topical niclosamide (ATx201) reduces Staphylococcus aureus colonization and increases Shannon diversity of the skin microbiome in atopic dermatitis patients in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial.

full_output.paper_title: Unravelling the physiological roles of mazEF toxin-antitoxin system on clinical MRSA strain by CRISPR RNA-guided cytidine deaminase.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa Alters Peptidoglycan Composition under Nutrient Conditions Resembling Cystic Fibrosis Lung Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies unique peptidoglycan (PG) modifications in Pseudomonas aeruginosa under nutrient conditions resembling cystic fibrosis (CF) lung infections, including O-methylation, mDAP deamination, and novel substitutions, which are linked to bacterial virulence and antibiotic resistance.
