full_output.paper_title: High frequency of antimicrobial resistance and virulence gene in Shigella species isolated from pediatric patients in an Iranian Referral Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates to certain antibiotics in Shigella strains, particularly in S. sonnei. The virulence genes sigA, virF, and invE were prevalent, with sigA being significantly more common in S. sonnei.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method, and the presence of virulence genes was detected via PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Sequence-Based Genomic Analysis Reveals Transmission of Antibiotic Resistance and Virulence among Carbapenemase-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several carbapenem resistance genes (KPC-2, OXA-232, NDM-5, IMP-8) and virulence genes (rmpA, rmpA2, iuc1, iuc3, iuc5, iro1) in carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae strains. Four novel plasmids carrying virulence genes were also identified.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in the studied strains.

full_output.paper_title: An Efficient Evaluation System Accelerates α-Helical Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery and Its Application to Global Human Genome Mining.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel screening system, MultiDS, for discovering α-helical antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) from the human genome. It identifies 60 peptides with potent antimicrobial activity against various pathogens, demonstrating the effectiveness of the system in predicting and validating AMPs.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of physicochemical and structural parameters, along with machine learning algorithms, to screen and validate antimicrobial peptides from the human genome.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro Activity of Antivirulence Drugs Targeting the las or pqs Quorum Sensing Against Cystic Fibrosis Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the effectiveness of antivirulence drugs niclosamide and clofoctol against Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from cystic fibrosis patients, focusing on their impact on quorum sensing systems and virulence factors.
full_output.methodology: The study used biosensors and biochemical assays to measure quorum sensing signal molecules and virulence factors in P. aeruginosa isolates treated with niclosamide and clofoctol.

full_output.paper_title: Small Things Matter: The 11.6-kDa TraB Protein is Crucial for Antibiotic Resistance Transfer Among Enterococci.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TraB as a critical component for the conjugative transfer of the pIP501 plasmid in Enterococci, highlighting its essential role in antibiotic resistance gene transfer.
full_output.methodology: Biparental mating assays, subcellular fractionation, and biochemical analyses were used to investigate the role of TraB in pIP501 transfer.

full_output.paper_title: Mutation of TonB-Dependent Receptor Encoding Gene MCR_0492 Potentially Associates with Macrolides Resistance in Moraxella catarrhalis Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies an indel mutation in the MCR_0492 gene, which encodes a TonB-dependent receptor protein, potentially associated with macrolide resistance in Moraxella catarrhalis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: First report of whole-genome analysis of an extensively drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolate with bedaquiline, linezolid and clofazimine resistance from Uganda.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first identification of extensively drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates with resistance to bedaquiline, linezolid, and clofazimine in Uganda, highlighting the importance of adherence to treatment and the need for improved surveillance and diagnostics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance-associated mutations in the clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Drug Resistance and Risk Factors for Acquisition of Gram-Negative Bacteria and Carbapenem-Resistant Organisms Among Liver Transplant Recipients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia as the most common Gram-negative pathogens in liver transplant recipients. Carbapenem-resistant organisms (CRO) were prevalent, with specific resistance profiles noted for various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 136 liver transplant recipients, including microbial culture, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and statistical analysis of risk factors for Gram-negative and CRO infections.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Genomics Identifies Features Associated with Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) Transmission in Hospital Settings.

full_output.methodology: Comparative genomics, phylogenetic analysis, and genome-wide association studies were used to analyze MRSA isolates from multiple hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: The EnvZ/OmpR Two-Component System Regulates the Antimicrobial Activity of TAT-RasGAP(317-326) and the Collateral Sensitivity to Other Antibacterial Agents.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a Host-Targeted Compound to Control Typhoid Fever.

full_output.paper_title: Roles of SmeYZ, SbiAB, and SmeDEF Efflux Systems in Iron Homeostasis of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the roles of SmeYZ, SmeDEF, and SbiAB efflux systems in iron homeostasis and stenobactin secretion in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. Loss of SmeYZ leads to iron starvation and pleiotropic defects, while SmeDEF and SbiAB are upregulated to compensate for stenobactin secretion.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq transcriptome analysis, qRT-PCR, CAS activity assay, iron source utilization assay, and ICP-MS for intracellular iron measurement.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Identification of Two DNA Methyltransferase Genes and Their Functional Characterization in the Anti-Bacterial Immunity of Antheraea pernyi.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two DNA methyltransferase genes, ApDNMT-1 and ApDNMT-2, in the Chinese oak silkworm, A. pernyi, and demonstrates their role in innate immunity against bacterial infections.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bioinformatics analysis, qRT-PCR, and 5-AZA treatment to investigate the function of ApDNMT-1 and ApDNMT-2 in A. pernyi's immune response.

full_output.paper_title: Punicalagin, an Inhibitor of Sortase A, Is a Promising Therapeutic Drug to Combat Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Infections.
full_output.key_findings: Punicalagin was identified as an inhibitor of sortase A (SrtA) in Staphylococcus aureus, which reduces the virulence of the bacteria without affecting its growth. It was shown to inhibit SrtA activity with an IC50 of 4.23 μg/mL and had no antibacterial activity. Additionally, punicalagin reduced the adhesion of S. aureus to fibrinogen, biofilm formation, and the anchoring of surface proteins like SpA.
full_output.methodology: The study used FRET assays, fluorescence quenching, molecular docking, and in vivo experiments in mice to evaluate the effects of punicalagin on SrtA and S. aureus virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative in silico characterization of Klebsiella pneumoniae hypervirulent plasmids and their antimicrobial resistance genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in hypervirulent plasmids of Klebsiella pneumoniae, identifying various beta-lactamases, quinolone resistance genes, aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, chloramphenicol acetyltransferases, tetracycline resistance genes, and macrolide resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study uses bioinformatics tools to analyze the genetic features, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and mobile genetic elements of 79 hypervirulent plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: An Anti-MRSA Phage From Raw Fish Rinse: Stability Evaluation and Production Optimization.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolated a bacteriophage (F2) with broad lytic activity against MRSA strains, demonstrating stability under various environmental conditions and optimizing its production through response surface methodology.
full_output.methodology: Bacteriophages were isolated from environmental samples, screened for lytic activity against MRSA, and their characteristics were evaluated. Production optimization was performed using response surface methodology.

full_output.paper_title: The Activity of Liposomal Linolenic Acid Against Helicobacter pylori In Vitro and Its Impact on Human Fecal Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: LipoLLA showed good anti-H. pylori effects by destroying the outer membrane barrier and causing leakage of bacterial contents. It had little effect on human fecal bacteria in vitro.
full_output.methodology: MIC determination, concentration-bactericidal curves, glucose and AST leakage detection, electron microscopy, and high-throughput sequencing of fecal samples.

full_output.paper_title: Shielding Surfaces from Viruses and Bacteria with a Multiscale Coating.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a multiscale coating with dual functionalities: water-repellent and antimicrobial. The coating incorporates ZIF-8 nanoparticles, which release zinc ions to kill bacteria, ensuring antimicrobial efficacy even after physical damage or prolonged submersion.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) to characterize the coating's structure and performance.

full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis and CRISPRi knockdown experiments were used to identify and validate the essentiality of MAB_3167c.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Characterization, Antimicrobial, Antibiofilm, Antioxidant, Anticancer and Acute Toxicity Properties of N-(2-hydroxyphenyl)-2-phenazinamine From Nocardiopsis exhalans (KP149558).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified N-(2-hydroxyphenyl)-2-phenazinamine (NHP) as a compound with antimicrobial, antibiofilm, antioxidant, anticancer, and low acute toxicity properties. NHP was isolated from the marine actinomycete Nocardiopsis exhalans and showed significant activity against human clinical pathogens such as Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The compound was isolated from Nocardiopsis exhalans using ethyl acetate extraction, purified via column chromatography, and characterized using FTIR, GC-MS, and NMR. Its antimicrobial, antibiofilm, antioxidant, and anticancer activities were evaluated using in vitro assays, and its toxicity was assessed in zebrafish.

full_output.paper_title: Host gut resistome in Gulf War chronic multisymptom illness correlates with persistent inflammation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) associated with the gut resistome in Gulf War chronic multisymptom illness (CMI) models and veterans, including vanXYN, adeS, lra-3, mexD, novA, and afca, which show increased abundance and expression in CMI groups.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome shotgun sequencing, metagenomic assembly, functional gene annotation, and qRT-PCR analysis were used to characterize the gut resistome and its association with inflammation in CMI models and veterans.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation and comparison of antibiotic susceptibility profiles of Streptomyces spp. from clinical specimens revealed common and region-dependent resistance patterns.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified intrinsic resistance to penicillin, tetracycline, chloramphenicol, ciprofloxacin, erythromycin, gentamicin, vancomycin, and linezolid in Streptomyces clinical isolates. High resistance rates were observed for penicillin, ampicillin, amoxicillin, cefazolin, ceftriaxone, erythromycin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, whereas all isolates were susceptible to amikacin, gentamicin, and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Disk diffusion and broth microdilution methods were used to determine antibiotic susceptibility profiles of 84 Streptomyces clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic insights of high-risk clones of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli isolated from community infections and commercial meat in southern Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple ESBL-producing E. coli clones, including CTX-M-2, CTX-M-8, CTX-M-14, CTX-M-15, CTX-M-24, CTX-M-27, and CTX-M-55, along with other resistance genes such as aadA1, strA, strB, dfrA1, dfrA17, sul1, sul2, tet(A), tet(B), mph(A), catB3, floR, cmlA1, and catA1, highlighting the spread of high-risk clones in both human and animal sources in southern Brazil.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the resistome and clonal relationships of ESBL-producing E. coli isolates from human urine, chicken meat, and pork samples.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the role of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) such as cathelicidins and defensins in the treatment of TB and HIV, focusing on their potential as novel therapeutics and the influence of genetic polymorphisms on their efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature on the mechanisms of action and therapeutic potential of AMPs in TB and HIV, along with the impact of genetic variations on their function.

full_output.paper_title: Heavy isotope labeling and mass spectrometry reveal unexpected remodeling of bacterial cell wall expansion in response to drugs.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals the role of YcbB L,D-transpeptidase in bacterial cell wall expansion and resistance to β-lactam antibiotics by inserting multiple glycan strands cross-linked to existing tripeptide-containing acceptors.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized heavy isotope labeling and mass spectrometry to analyze peptidoglycan synthesis and remodeling in response to antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic treatments to mothers during the perinatal period leaving hidden trouble on infants.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that antibiotic treatments during the perinatal period had no significant impact on the microbiota of breast milk but caused disturbances in the gut microbiota of infants. The abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the infant gut microbiota initially declined but increased significantly after a 6-month recovery period.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the gut microbiota of breast milk and fecal samples using 16S rRNA sequencing and high-throughput quantitative PCR (HT-qPCR) to assess the impact of perinatal antibiotic treatments on microbial communities and ARG abundance.
full_output.sample_size: 25 breast milk samples and 30 fecal samples

full_output.paper_title: The Effect of Conjugation of Ciprofloxacin and Moxifloxacin with Fatty Acids on Their Antibacterial and Anticancer Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several MXF-fatty acid conjugates with antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus species, particularly highlighting the effectiveness of 14m, 2m, and 1m against quinolone-susceptible and resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: In vitro antibacterial studies, MIC determination, and molecular docking experiments were conducted to evaluate the activity of the conjugates.

full_output.paper_title: nor 3'-Demethoxyisoguaiacin from Larrea tridentata Is a Potential Alternative against Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria Associated with Bovine Mastitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies nor-3-demethoxyisoguaiacin as a potent antibacterial compound from Larrea tridentata with activity against multidrug-resistant bacteria associated with bovine mastitis.
full_output.methodology: HPLC analysis, MIC testing, and antibacterial activity assessment.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified O25 as the most prevalent O serotype among extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli (ExPEC) isolates causing bloodstream infections, with a particular dominance among multidrug-resistant (MDR) isolates. Other notable O serotypes included O2, O6, O1, O75, O15, O8, O16, O4, O18, O77 group, O153, O9, O101/O162, O86, and O13.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 3217 ExPEC blood culture isolates from four regions using agglutination and whole-genome sequencing for O serotyping, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing via broth microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: Relationship Between Antibiotic Resistance, Biofilm Formation, and Biofilm-Specific Resistance in Escherichia coli Isolates from Ningbo, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in E. coli isolates from Ningbo, China, including aac(3)-II, acc(6')-Ib-cr, ant(2"), and tetA, which conferred resistance to gentamicin, moxifloxacin, ofloxacin, and tetracycline, respectively.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and assess resistance profiles.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Bacillus cereus and Enterobacter cloacae as prevalent bacterial pathogens on hand sanitizer dispensers, with B. cereus showing tolerance to alcohol and resistance to β-lactams and macrolides, while E. cloacae exhibited resistance to multiple antibiotic classes.
full_output.methodology: Culture-dependent cultivation, MALDI-TOF, alcohol killing assays, biofilm eradication assays, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: wecB Gene of Salmonella Gallinarum Plays a Critical Role in Systemic Infection of Fowl Typhoid.
full_output.key_findings: The wecB gene of Salmonella Gallinarum was identified as a critical factor in systemic infection of fowl typhoid. Deletion of wecB resulted in decreased resistance to bile acid and nalidixic acid, reduced virulence in chickens, and induced a protective immune response.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, bacterial growth assays, chicken infection model, and cytokine expression analysis were used to evaluate the role of wecB in S. Gallinarum pathogenesis.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating the Contribution of the Predicted Toxin-Antitoxin System HigBA to Persistence, Biofilm Formation, and Virulence in Burkholderia pseudomallei.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the HigBA toxin-antitoxin system in Burkholderia pseudomallei, demonstrating its role in persistence, biofilm formation, and virulence. The toxin mutant (ΔhigB) showed increased survival under levofloxacin stress, while the antitoxin deletion led to differential responses, suggesting both components contribute to the persister phenotype.
full_output.methodology: Genomic annotation, gene expression analysis, mutant construction, and phenotypic characterization were used to evaluate the HigBA system's role in B. pseudomallei.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of Ceftolozane/Tazobactam Infusion Regimens in a Hollow-Fiber Infection Model against Extensively Drug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolates.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro susceptibility testing, HFIM experiments, and genetic analysis to characterize resistance mechanisms in P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Fecal carriage of vanB antibiotic resistance gene affects adipose tissue function under vancomycin use.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the presence of the vanB gene in the gut microbiota influenced the response to vancomycin treatment, affecting adipose tissue insulin sensitivity and gene expression.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR, hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp, and microbiome analysis to investigate the effects of vanB on metabolic health.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotyping and genotyping studies on extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli isolates from mastitic cows on dairy farms in Egypt.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM and blaSHV genes as the most prevalent extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes in Escherichia coli isolates from mastitic cows in Egypt. These genes confer resistance to several beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to identify and characterize ESBL genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Thymol Increases Sensitivity of Clinical Col-R Gram-Negative Bacteria to Colistin.
full_output.key_findings: Thymol enhances the effectiveness of colistin against colistin-resistant (Col-R) Gram-negative bacteria by increasing outer membrane permeability, leading to synergistic antibacterial and antibiofilm effects.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, checkerboard assays, time-kill assays, biofilm formation inhibition, and scanning electron microscopy were used to evaluate the synergistic effects of thymol and colistin.

full_output.paper_title: A longitudinal investigation of the effects of age, dietary fiber type and level, and injectable antimicrobials on the fecal microbiome and antimicrobial resistance of finisher pigs.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of age, dietary fiber type and level, and injectable antimicrobials on the fecal microbiome and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) of finisher pigs. It found that age had a greater impact on the fecal microbiome composition than diet, and that antimicrobial treatments had minimal effects on bacterial diversity and AMR gene abundance.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA amplicon-based microbiome analysis and culture methods to quantify AMR coliforms and enterococci populations in fecal samples from finisher pigs.

full_output.paper_title: Penicillin-Binding Protein 1 (PBP1) of Staphylococcus aureus Has Multiple Essential Functions in Cell Division.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the essential role of PBP1, its PASTA domains, and transpeptidase activity in cell division and peptidoglycan synthesis in Staphylococcus aureus. Mutants lacking PBP1 or its PASTA domains exhibit severe growth defects and impaired septum formation.
full_output.methodology: Conditional mutants, immunoblot analysis, and microscopic imaging were used to study the role of PBP1 in cell division and peptidoglycan synthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Dysbiosis and Restoration Dynamics of the Gut Microbiome Following Therapeutic Exposure to Florfenicol in Snubnose Pompano (Trachinotus blochii) to Aid in Sustainable Aquaculture Production Strategies.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a transient increase in the relative abundance of kanamycin-resistant bacteria and two multidrug resistance encoding genes (K03327 and K03585) in the treated fish gut during the initial 10 days post-withdrawal of florfenicol (FFC) treatment.
full_output.methodology: Culture-dependent and independent techniques, metagenomic analysis, and statistical analysis were used to assess the impact of FFC on the gut microbiome of snubnose pompano.

full_output.paper_title: A Bacterial Isolate Capable of Quenching Both Diffusible Signal Factor- and N-Acylhomoserine Lactone-Family Quorum Sensing Signals Shows Much Enhanced Biocontrol Potencies.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes three AHL-acylase genes (aigA, aigB, and aigC) in Pseudomonas sp. HS-18, which effectively degrade various AHL signals, thereby reducing virulence factor production and biofilm formation in pathogens like B. cenocepacia and P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, heterologous expression in E. coli, LC-MS analysis, and AHL degradation assays.

full_output.paper_title: Conformational flexibility in carbapenem hydrolysis drives substrate specificity of the class D carbapenemase OXA-24/40.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the class D carbapenemase OXA-24/40 from Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting its ability to hydrolyze various carbapenems with differing efficiencies, and identifies structural features contributing to its substrate specificity and catalytic activity.
full_output.methodology: Steady-state kinetic analysis and X-ray crystallography were used to investigate the activity and structure of OXA-24/40.

full_output.paper_title: An antibacterial compound pyrimidomycin produced by Streptomyces sp. PSAA01 isolated from soil of Eastern Himalayan foothill.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a new antibacterial compound, pyrimidomycin, produced by Streptomyces sp. PSAA01, which exhibits potent activity against Gram-positive bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains, and shows synergy with conventional antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The compound was isolated, purified, and structurally characterized using various analytical techniques, and its antimicrobial activity was evaluated through MIC, MBC, and biofilm assays.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of metal(loid)s and antibiotic resistance in bacteria of human gut microbiota from chronic kidney disease subjects.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic and metal(loid) resistance genes in gut microbiota from chronic kidney disease (CKD) subjects, including genes encoding beta-lactamases, quinolone resistance proteins, macrolide phosphotransferases, and efflux pumps. Additionally, genes conferring resistance to arsenicals and heavy metals were detected.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized qPCR to detect and quantify antibiotic and metal(loid) resistance genes in stool samples from CKD patients and healthy controls.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and Antibiotic Susceptibility of Eggerthella lenta in Bloodstream Infections.
full_output.key_findings: Eggerthella lenta was identified as the causative agent of bloodstream infections in two patients, and it was found to be sensitive to several antibiotics including piperacillin-tazobactam, imipenem, meropenem, metronidazole, clindamycin, and vancomycin, but resistant to amoxicillin, penicillin, cefotaxime, and ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: MALDI-TOF MS, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and agar dilution method for antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Bloodstream Infections in the Intensive Care Unit: a Single-Center Retrospective Bacteriological Analysis Between 2007 and 2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes and mutations in bloodstream infections, including bla genes in Acinetobacter baumannii, ESBL, NDM, KPC, and OXA-48 carbapenemases in Klebsiella pneumoniae, and MBL in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of blood samples and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: A new model of endotracheal tube biofilm identifies combinations of matrix-degrading enzymes and antimicrobials able to eradicate biofilms of pathogens that cause ventilator-associated pneumonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents an in vitro endotracheal tube biofilm model that mimics the in vivo environment, highlighting the challenges in eradicating biofilms of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Candida albicans. It demonstrates that combining matrix-degrading enzymes with antimicrobials improves biofilm eradication.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized an in vitro endotracheal tube biofilm model, employing cryo-scanning electron microscopy and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to analyze biofilm structure and susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Novel N,N-Dimethyl-idarubicin Analogues Are Effective Cytotoxic Agents for ABCB1-Overexpressing, Doxorubicin-Resistant Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies N,N-dimethyl-idarubicin and its trisaccharide derivative as effective cytotoxic agents against ABCB1-overexpressing, doxorubicin-resistant cells, demonstrating histone eviction-mediated cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: Cytotoxicity profiling, flow cytometry, subcellular fractionation, and Western blotting were used to assess the effects of anthracycline variants on cell viability and subcellular localization.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity evaluation of a novel K3-specific phage against Acinetobacter baumannii and evidence for receptor-binding domain transfer across morphologies.
full_output.key_findings: Phage P1068 exhibits antibacterial activity against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB), particularly targeting the K3 capsule type. It shows efficacy in reducing bacterial loads in mouse models and has potential for phage therapy against CRAB infections.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified five tetracycline resistance genes (tet(32), tet(40), tet(W), tet(Q)) and one trimethoprim resistance gene (dfrF) that were significantly more abundant in human microbiomes compared to lemur microbiomes. These genes were found to be highly conserved between human and lemur microbiomes.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery and characterization of a novel LysinB from F2 sub-cluster mycobacteriophage RitSun.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes a novel LysinB from the F2 sub-cluster mycobacteriophage RitSun, which exhibits intrinsic activity against Mycobacterium smegmatis, with high specific activity and anti-biofilm properties.
full_output.methodology: In silico and in vitro analysis, including sequence alignment, purification, and enzymatic activity assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multidrug efflux pumps MexAB-OprM, MexCD-OprJ, MexEF-OprN, and MexXY-OprM as the primary resistance determinants in Pseudomonas aeruginosa AUST-03 isolates. Mutations in regulatory genes mexR, mexT, nalC, and nfxB contribute to the upregulation of these efflux pumps. Additionally, the study detects several antibiotic resistance genes, including crpP, blaOXA-50, blaOXA-1034, blaPDC-3, and blaPDC-374, which are associated with resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance determinants in Pseudomonas aeruginosa AUST-03 isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-mediated azithromycin resistance in non-typhoidal Salmonella recovered from human infections.

mph(A).genetic_context: IS 26 - mph (A)- mrx (A)- mphR (A)-IS 6100 /IS 26 that co-arranged with intI1 harbour multidrug-resistant (MDR) gene cassettes on diverse plasmids

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the plasmid-mediated azithromycin resistance gene mph(A) in 10 non-typhoidal Salmonella isolates, highlighting the spread of this gene on various plasmids and its association with multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, whole-genome sequencing, conjugation experiments, and bioinformatics analysis were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Phenanthrenes from Juncus articulatus with Antibacterial and Biofilm Formation Inhibitory Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolated and identified 20 phenanthrenes from Juncus articulatus, including 10 new compounds. Compounds 12 and 14 showed potent antibacterial activity against both methicillin-susceptible and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus with MIC values of 15.1 and 15.3 μM, respectively. Additionally, these compounds inhibited biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were isolated using various chromatographic techniques and their structures were determined using NMR and HRMS. Antimicrobial activity was assessed using MIC assays against E. coli, P. aeruginosa, MSSA, and MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Pathogenic Staphylococci Causing Mastitis and Skin, Ear and Vaginal Infections in Animals
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes tetK and tetM in staphylococci isolated from animals in Uganda, with tetK being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR for AMR gene detection, and MALDI-TOF MS for species identification.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and virulence gene analysis of Shigella species causing dysentery in Iranian children: Implications for fluroquinolone resistance.

gyrA.notes: Most common mutation in Shigella isolates
gyrA.evidence_note: The paper states that the D87Y mutation in the gyrA gene was the most common in Shigella isolates, occurring in 73 % of cases.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified qnrA, qnrS, and qnrD genes as major contributors to plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance in Shigella isolates, along with specific mutations in gyrA and parC genes associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and disk diffusion methods were used to analyze antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes in Shigella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Extended spectrum and metalo beta lactamase producing gram negative bacterial pathogens from cockroaches collected at hospital, Southern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL) producing Gram-negative bacteria from cockroaches in a hospital setting in Southern Ethiopia. ESBL-producing bacteria included Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli, while MBL-producing bacteria included K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa, E. coli, A. baumannii, Enterobacter spp., and K. oxytoca.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving collection of cockroaches from hospital wards, isolation and identification of bacterial pathogens, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and detection of ESBL and MBL production using disk diffusion and double disc methods.

full_output.paper_title: Standardization of an antimicrobial resistance surveillance network through data management.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the importance of standardized data management in AMR surveillance networks, particularly through the Kor-GLASS system. It characterizes various AMR genes such as TEM, SHV, CTX, CMY, DHA, CIT, KPC, GES, VIM, IMP, NDM, mecA, and SCCmec, which confer resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized antibiotic susceptibility testing (AST) and characterized AMR genes through molecular techniques.
full_output.sample_size: Data from multiple analysis centers in South Korea

full_output.paper_title: Lys-63-specific deubiquitinase BRCC36 enhances the sensitivity of multiple myeloma cells to lenalidomide by inhibiting lysosomal degradation of cereblon.
full_output.key_findings: BRCC36, a Lys-63-specific deubiquitinase, interacts with CRBN and stabilizes it by removing K63-linked polyubiquitin chains, thereby enhancing the antimyeloma effect of lenalidomide. SHIN1, an SHMT2 inhibitor, disrupts the BRISC complex and increases CRBN levels, improving lenalidomide sensitivity in multiple myeloma cells.
full_output.methodology: Proximity labeling (TurboID), quantitative proteomics, immunoblotting, co-immunoprecipitation, siRNA knockdown, plasmid transfection, and CCK-8 assays.

full_output.paper_title: Maternal antibiotic prophylaxis during cesarean section has a limited impact on the infant gut microbiome.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that maternal antibiotic prophylaxis during cesarean section has a limited impact on the infant gut microbiome, with feeding mode being a more significant factor. Subtle differences in bacterial strain levels and antibiotic resistance gene loads were observed, but no significant associations with bacterial composition, metabolic pathways, short-chain fatty acids, or bile acids were found.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted a randomized controlled trial and combined data from multiple cohorts to analyze the impact of maternal antibiotic timing on the infant gut microbiome using metagenomic sequencing and statistical analyses.
full_output.sample_size: 172 samples from 28 infants and 79 infants from 3 cohorts

full_output.paper_title: Zap the clap with DNA: a novel microbicide for preventing Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes DNA-based microbicides that effectively kill Neisseria gonorrhoeae without harming commensal bacteria. The DNA molecule MB-14-1-15 was particularly effective against various clinical isolates, including antibiotic-resistant strains, and remained effective when delivered via personal lubricants.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized DNA killing assays, PCR, cloning, and sequencing to evaluate the efficacy of engineered DNA molecules against Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.sample_size: various clinical isolates from different sources

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of clinical isolation of drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae with overexpression of OqxB efflux pump as the decisive drug resistance factor.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the OqxB efflux pump as a key factor in quinolone resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae, demonstrating that its overexpression leads to increased resistance to quinolones such as levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used qRT-PCR, MIC assays, and gene knockout/complementation experiments to validate the role of OqxB in quinolone resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Adaptive evolution of carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae in the urinary tract of a single patient.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in rmpA and wcaJ, mediated by IS Kpn26, which lead to a mucoid phenotype switch in CR-hvKp, reducing virulence but increasing colonization in the urinary tract.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, and functional assays were used to validate the role of rmpA and wcaJ mutations in the mucoid phenotype switch of CR-hvKp.
full_output.sample_size: 2 clinical Kp strains (Y8 and Y9) from a single patient, 25 hypermucoid clones, and 25 hypomucoid variants from urine samples of Y8-infected mice

full_output.paper_title: First report of detection of mcr-1 and virulence genes in avian pathogenic Escherichia coli in the center of Algeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of the mcr-1 gene in avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) in the center of Algeria, highlighting its association with colistin resistance. The mcr-1 gene was found in 96.3% of colistin-resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and broth microdilution for MIC determination were used to detect mcr-1 and assess colistin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Nef peptide-19 as a promising antimicrobial peptide with significant antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, showing MIC and MBC values of 10 µM and 20 µM, respectively, and inhibiting biofilm formation at 20 µM.
full_output.methodology: In silico and in vitro evaluations, including molecular docking analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the performance of routine methods for fosfomycin and mecillinam susceptibility testing of Enterobacterales urine isolates, highlighting differences in accuracy across species and methods.
full_output.methodology: The study compared VITEK® 2, ETEST®, and disc diffusion methods with agar dilution as the reference method for determining fosfomycin and mecillinam susceptibility in Enterobacterales isolates.

full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, RNAseq analysis, MIC determination, ROS measurement, and in vivo infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB): metabolic adaptation and transcriptional response to human urine (HU).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies differentially expressed genes in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) strains AB5075 and AMA40 upon exposure to human urine (HU), highlighting metabolic adaptations and transcriptional responses.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq and qRT-PCR were used to analyze gene expression changes in CRAB strains exposed to human urine.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcal sRNA IsrR downregulates methylthiotransferase MiaB under iron-deficient conditions.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IsrR as a small regulatory RNA that downregulates the expression of MiaB, a methylthiotransferase involved in tRNA modification, under iron-deficient conditions in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular biology techniques including gene cloning, reporter assays, and fluorescence measurements to investigate the regulatory role of IsrR on MiaB expression.

full_output.paper_title: Three prolonged outbreaks of metallo-β-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa in an Upper Austrian hospital, 2017-2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified three distinct genomic clusters of metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa (MBL-Pa) in an Austrian hospital, linked to prolonged outbreaks. Key resistance genes included blaVIM-2, blaVIM-1, and blaIMP-13, which conferred resistance to carbapenems, cephalosporins, and penicillins.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and core genome multilocus sequence typing (cgMLST) were used to analyze the genetic relatedness of P. aeruginosa isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 62 P. aeruginosa strains (54 clinical and 8 environmental)

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX−M and bla TEM genes in multidrug-resistant ESBL-producing E. coli isolates from dumpsite leachate and surface water, highlighting the environmental spread of these resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, disc diffusion, and phenotypic testing were used to detect ESBL genes and assess antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaNDM-1 and blaKPC-2 as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in K. pneumoniae 0692, which were experimentally validated through PCR and whole-genome sequencing.
full_output.methodology: PCR, whole-genome sequencing, and proteomic analysis were used to identify and validate AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology of string test-positive Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates in Huzhou, China, 2020-2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in string test-positive Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, including SHV, SHV-11, SHV-1, SHV-142, LAP-2, TEM-1D, OXA-1, rmtB, aadA, aac(6')-Ib-cr, aph3-Ia, qnr, GyrA, ParC-80I, OmpK, KPC-2, sul, tet, dfrA, CTX-M, fosA3, and catA1, contributing to resistance against various antibiotics such as β-lactams, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, carbapenems, sulfonamides, tetracyclines, trimethoprim, cephalosporins, fosfomycin, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the AMR genes and mutations in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Rescue of morphological defects in Streptomyces venezuelae by the alkaline volatile compound trimethylamine.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the alkaline volatile compound trimethylamine (TMA) produced by wild-type Streptomyces venezuelae can rescue the morphological defects of the mutant strain MU-1, restoring aerial mycelium and spore formation.
full_output.methodology: Co-incubation experiments, pH measurements, TMA quantification via UHPLC, and scanning electron microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic collaboration between AMPs and non-direct antimicrobial cationic peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AW1 and AW2 as a synergistic pair of peptides, where AW1 exhibits direct antimicrobial activity and AW2 enhances this activity without itself having direct antimicrobial properties. Together, they disrupt bacterial membranes, inhibit biofilm formation, and reduce resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of in vitro antimicrobial assays, membrane disruption experiments, transcriptomic analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the synergistic effects of AW1 and AW2.

full_output.paper_title: Burden of multidrug-resistant bacteria among HIV-positive individuals in Ethiopia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: This study found a high burden of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria among HIV-positive individuals in Ethiopia, with a pooled prevalence of 58.02%. The highest MDR prevalence was observed in the Oromia region, patients with multiple infections, and studies identifying both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 22 studies involving 5636 HIV-positive individuals.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic efficacy of compound organic acids administration on methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus-induced arthritis in broilers.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that compound organic acids, including cinnamic acid, significantly inhibited the growth of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA85) and reduced its antibiotic resistance. These compounds also enhanced the sensitivity of MRSA85 to oxacillin and showed potential as novel antibacterial agents.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of in vitro MIC testing, FICI analysis, and in vivo animal experiments to evaluate the antibacterial effects of compound organic acids against MRSA85.

full_output.paper_title: BWC0977, a broad-spectrum antibacterial clinical candidate to treat multidrug resistant infections.
full_output.key_findings: BWC0977 is a novel bacterial topoisomerase inhibitor with broad-spectrum activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens, including those resistant to fluoroquinolones, carbapenems, and colistin. It exhibits high efficacy in preclinical models and is well-tolerated in human volunteers.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo studies, including MIC testing, resistance frequency analysis, and PK/PD modeling, were conducted to evaluate BWC0977's antibacterial activity and safety.

full_output.paper_title: Global burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance 1990-2021: a systematic analysis with forecasts to 2050.
full_output.key_findings: This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the global burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance (AMR) from 1990 to 2021, highlighting the significant increase in AMR-related deaths and the projected rise in the future. It identifies key pathogens and drug resistance patterns, emphasizing the need for improved infection prevention, antibiotic stewardship, and new drug development.
full_output.methodology: The study used a systematic analysis of multiple data sources, including death records, hospital data, microbiology data, and literature studies, to estimate the burden of AMR. Statistical modeling was employed to project future trends under different scenarios.

full_output.paper_title: Modular, inducible, and titratable expression systems for Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study develops modular vectors and a novel IPTG-inducible promoter, P_abstBR, for gene expression in Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii. P_abstBR shows reduced leakiness and is titratable at both population and single-cell levels.
full_output.methodology: Vector construction, promoter engineering, and fluorescence-based expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: The genetic relationship between human and pet isolates: a core genome multilocus sequence analysis of multidrug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed multidrug-resistant bacteria from humans and pets using whole-genome sequencing and core genome multilocus sequence typing, identifying genetic relationships and potential transmission events between human and pet isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and core genome multilocus sequence typing were used to analyze genetic relationships among multidrug-resistant bacteria from humans and pets.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the use of a crude beta-lactamase enzyme from Bacillus cereus to effectively destroy penicillin residues in milk, reducing them to undetectable levels.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic degradation of penicillin in milk using beta-lactamase enzyme followed by assessment of penicillin levels and effects on dairy fermentation processes.

full_output.paper_title: Enhancing the antibacterial efficacy of vancomycin analogues: targeting metallo-β-lactamases and cell wall biosynthesis.
full_output.key_findings: VanNHdipi, a vancomycin analogue, shows enhanced antibacterial activity against vancomycin-resistant bacteria and effectively inactivates metallo-beta-lactamases (MBLs) such as NDM-1, VIM-1, VIM-27, IMP-1, and L1, restoring susceptibility to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized microbiological assays, biochemical analyses, proteomics, and computational studies to evaluate the mechanism of action and efficacy of VanNHdipi.

full_output.paper_title: Hyaluronic Acid-Modified Micelles of Azithromycin and Quercetin Against Infections Caused by Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that HA-AZI/Qe-M micelles exhibit potent antibacterial activity against MRSA, effectively inhibiting bacterial growth, biofilm formation, and intracellular infection. The micelles show improved targeting and therapeutic efficacy compared to conventional drug formulations.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of in vitro and in vivo experiments, including TEM, DLS, FTIR, MIC determination, live/dead staining, biofilm inhibition assays, and animal infection models to evaluate the effectiveness of HA-AZI/Qe-M micelles against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria and resistance-genes in drinking water source in north Shoa zone, Amhara region, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M- gp 8/25, bla CTX-M- gp 9, and bla CTX-M- gp 1 as the predominant ESβL genes in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from drinking water sources in the North Shoa zone, Amhara region, Ethiopia.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolates were subjected to antimicrobial susceptibility testing and molecular detection of resistance genes via multiplex PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of Secondary Amine and Molecular Weight on the Biological Activities of Cationic Amphipathic Antimicrobial Macromolecules.
full_output.key_findings: The study develops novel cationic amphipathic macromolecules with secondary amine piperidine derivatives as cationic moieties, showing strong antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant bacteria, particularly low molecular weight D2 dendrons with synergistic effects with rifampicin.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of cationic amphipathic macromolecules, determination of minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), bactericidal efficacy, membrane permeability, and synergy with rifampicin.

full_output.paper_title: Role of DNA Double-Strand Break Formation in Gyrase Inhibitor-Mediated Killing of Nonreplicating Persistent Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Caseum.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the importance of DNA double-strand break (DSB) formation in the bactericidal activity of fluoroquinolones (FQ) against nonreplicating persistent Mycobacterium tuberculosis in caseum. Unlike other gyrase inhibitors, FQ were uniquely able to induce DSBs, which correlated with their effectiveness in killing nonreplicating MTB.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the in vitro potency of various gyrase inhibitors against M. tuberculosis using DNA supercoiling and cleavage assays, along with MIC and MBC measurements in replicating and nonreplicating cultures.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of a bla(NDM-1)-positive strain in Israel predating the earliest observations from India.

Mutations in gyrA (C257T) and 23S rRNA (A2075G) were associated with fluoroquinolone and macrolide resistance, respectively. The tetO gene conferred tetracycline resistance, while blaOXA was linked to ampicillin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Florfenicol-resistant Brevundimonas sanguinis sp. nov., a novel bacterium isolated from patient blood in South Korea.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of lytic bacteriophage vB_KpnP_23: A promising antimicrobial candidate against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: Phage vB_KpnP_23 was isolated from hospital sewage and characterized as a lytic phage with potent activity against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP). It lacks virulence and resistance genes, making it suitable for therapeutic use. The phage exhibited a broad lytic range against multiple CRKP strains and showed synergistic effects with antibiotics like meropenem, amikacin, and levofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, transmission electron microscopy, genomic sequencing, and activity assays were performed to characterize vB_KpnP_23.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of antimicrobial resistance and genetic diversity of Acinetobacter baumannii in a tertiary care hospital in Haikou City.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from a tertiary care hospital in Haikou City, with significant resistance to several antibiotics, including gentamicin, ticarcillin/clavulanate, and others. Genetic diversity was observed through RAPD-PCR analysis, revealing distinct genetic types and clusters among the isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RAPD-PCR for genetic diversity analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via VITEK-32 to determine resistance patterns in 513 A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic Lineages and Diseases Associated with Moraxella catarrhalis Isolates Recovered from Bulgarian Patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that all M. catarrhalis strains were resistant to penicillin, aminopenicillins, and first-generation cephalosporins due to the presence of BRO-1 and BRO-2 beta-lactamases. The strains exhibited high susceptibility to other antibiotics, with only a small percentage showing resistance to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, serotyping, MLST analysis, and PCR for detection of beta-lactamase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Acidocin A and Acidocin 8912 Belong to a Distinct Subfamily of Class II Bacteriocins with a Broad Spectrum of Antimicrobial Activity.
full_output.key_findings: Acidocin A, acidocin 8912, and acidocin 8912A are antimicrobial peptides with broad-spectrum activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, as well as fungi. Acidocin A exhibits the highest antifungal activity, while acidocin 8912 and acidocin 8912A demonstrate lower but still significant antibacterial and antifungal effects.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial and antifungal activity assays, CD spectroscopy, and membrane permeability tests were conducted to characterize the peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance in the Terrestrial Environment of Agricultural Landscapes in Norway.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in 59.5% of the 644 environmental samples collected from agricultural landscapes in Norway. Key ARGs detected included strA, strB, sul2, aph(3")-Ib, and aph(6)-Id, which confer resistance to streptomycin, sulfonamides, and aminoglycosides. The research highlights the role of livestock manure in increasing ARG loads in agricultural soils.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput quantitative PCR (HT-qPCR) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) were used to detect and characterize ARGs and antimicrobial-resistant E. coli (AREC) in environmental samples from agricultural and control areas in Norway.

full_output.paper_title: Measurable residual disease monitoring in AML with FLT3-ITD treated with intensive chemotherapy plus midostaurin.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the importance of FLT3-ITD measurable residual disease (MRD) monitoring in AML patients treated with intensive chemotherapy and midostaurin. FLT3-ITD MRD negativity after two cycles of chemotherapy was associated with improved outcomes, including lower relapse rates and better overall survival. Additionally, conversion from FLT3-ITD MRD negativity to positivity during follow-up was linked to higher relapse risk and poorer survival.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized next-generation sequencing (NGS) for FLT3-ITD MRD monitoring in a cohort of 157 patients with FLT3-ITD positive AML. Statistical analyses, including Cox proportional hazards models, were employed to assess the prognostic impact of MRD status.

full_output.paper_title: The enhanced antibacterial and antibiofilm properties of titanium dioxide nanoparticles biosynthesized by multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Decubitus ulcer infection and bacteremia due to tazobactam/piperacillin-resistant Veillonella parvula.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales at a New York City hospital over a 10-year period reveals complex plasmid-clone dynamics and evidence for frequent horizontal transfer of bla (KPC).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the complex dynamics of plasmid and clone transmission of bla KPC in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, highlighting the significant role of plasmids in the spread of carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, hybrid assembly, and plasmid clustering analysis were used to investigate the transmission dynamics of bla KPC in CRE isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified secondary bacterial infections in scabies patients, with Staphylococcus aureus, coagulase-negative staphylococci, and Streptococcus pyogenes being the most prevalent. Resistance to tetracycline, erythromycin, and clindamycin was observed in Gram-positive bacteria, while Klebsiella species showed resistance to ampicillin, cefazolin, and ciprofloxacin.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of the conceivable inhibitory activity of pathogenic microorganisms extracted from seaweed using phytochemicals, antioxidants, and in-silico molecular dynamic simulation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several bioactive compounds from seaweed extracts with potential antibacterial and antioxidant properties, focusing on the interaction of these compounds with Beta-ketoacyl [acyl carrier protein] synthase.
full_output.methodology: The study used GC-MS analysis, molecular docking, and antimicrobial assays to evaluate the bioactivity of seaweed extracts.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a rich diversity of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the intestinal microbiota of preterm infants, with beta-lactam, MLS, and tetracycline resistance being the most prevalent. Key ARGs included ermC, ermB, mecA, TEM-4, ANT(4')-Ib, isaA, vgaC, and oqxB, which were associated with various bacterial species and drug classes.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and analysis of meconium and stool samples from preterm infants to detect and characterize ARGs.

full_output.paper_title: R-Loop Toxicity Following Plasmid-Borne Expression of Endogenous Chromosomal Cryptic Antisense Regions
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that engineered expression of endogenous antisense RNAs in E. coli can lead to the formation of R-loops, which can cause genome instability and toxicity. The research also identifies specific chromosomal regions that are prone to R-loop formation and highlights the role of Rho and RNase HI in preventing these toxic structures.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized plasmid-based expression of antisense regions, chloroquine-agarose gel electrophoresis to assess plasmid supercoiling, and whole-genome sequencing to analyze DNA copy number changes and identify prophage escape replication.

full_output.paper_title: Dynamic basis of lipopolysaccharide export by LptB(2)FGC.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the conformational dynamics of the LptB2FGC complex involved in lipopolysaccharide (LPS) export in Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting the role of LptC in regulating the LPS entry gate and facilitating LPS transport.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized pulsed dipolar electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy and laser-induced liquid bead ion desorption mass spectrometry (LILBID-MS) to investigate the structural and dynamic properties of the LptB2FGC complex.

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces pSCRATCH, a CRISPR-based genomic recorder designed to track bacterial persisters during antibiotic treatment. It demonstrates that pSCRATCH can selectively mark growth-arrested bacteria and differentiate between treatment failure due to persistence versus resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized CRISPR technology, bacterial culture, macrophage infection models, and molecular biology techniques such as PCR and qPCR to validate the pSCRATCH system.

full_output.paper_title: A global genome dataset for Salmonella Gallinarum recovered between 1920 and 2024.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a comprehensive genome dataset of 574 Salmonella Gallinarum isolates, highlighting the presence of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genomic elements (MGEs). It identifies 635 ARG records and 5,636 MGE records, emphasizing the role of MGEs in the spread of resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and in silico prediction were used to analyze the genomic characteristics of Salmonella Gallinarum isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Environmental contamination with carbapenem resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in healthcare settings in Fiji: a potential source of infection.

qacJ.validation_method: genomic analysis and previous study confirmation

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CR Ab) isolates from high-touch surfaces in Fijian hospitals, revealing the presence of resistance genes such as bla OXA-23, bla NDM-1, and others, along with mutations in genes like parC and gyrA, contributing to resistance against multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms and genetic relatedness of CR Ab isolates from environmental and clinical sources.

full_output.paper_title: Protein aggregation is a consequence of the dormancy-inducing membrane toxin TisB in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TisB as a membrane toxin that induces protein aggregation in E. coli, contributing to dormancy and antibiotic tolerance. TisB expression leads to ATP depletion and the formation of protein aggregates, which prolong dormancy and affect persister cell survival.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a moderate tisB expression system, RNA sequencing, qRT-PCR, and fluorescence microscopy to investigate TisB's effects on protein aggregation and dormancy.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Pseudomonas aeruginosa from subjects with diffuse panbronchiolitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized 24 Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains from diffuse panbronchiolitis (DPB) patients, revealing significant genomic variability and antibiotic resistance profiles, particularly to erythromycin.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and lipid A structural analysis were employed to examine P. aeruginosa strains from DPB patients.

full_output.paper_title: Structure of a Rhs effector clade domain provides mechanistic insights into type VI secretion system toxin delivery.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the Tse15 Rhs effector from Acinetobacter baumannii, revealing its structure and mechanism of toxin delivery via the type VI secretion system (T6SS). Tse15 consists of an N-terminal clade domain, a central Rhs domain forming a β-cocoon, and a C-terminal toxin domain. The clade domain acts as an internal chaperone facilitating toxin delivery, while the Rhs cage is rarely secreted.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis using cryo-electron microscopy, biochemical assays, and genetic manipulation.

full_output.paper_title: An investigative study on Yersinia enterocolitica in animals, humans and dried milk in New Valley Governorate, Egypt.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro and in vivo activities of scutellarein, a novel polyphosphate kinase 1 inhibitor against Acinetobacter baumannii infection.

It also reports two isolates (one from GC1 and one from GC2) that were susceptible to carbapenems despite being part of globally distributed clones typically associated with resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Chlorhexidine Resistance Among Clinical Isolates of Coagulase-Negative Staphylococcus Species in a Tertiary Care Center, Chennai.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified qacA/B and smr genes as mediators of chlorhexidine resistance in CoNS isolates, with 34.5% of isolates carrying these genes. A significant association was found between the presence of these genes and reduced susceptibility to chlorhexidine.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of multi-drug resistant organisms in the gut flora of healthy rural individuals in northern India.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of multi-drug resistant organisms in the gut flora of healthy rural individuals in northern India, with a significant presence of ESBL and carbapenemase genes such as bla TEM, bla SHV, bla CTXM-1, and OXA-48.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR to detect antimicrobial resistance genes in isolates from stool samples, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing via the Vitek-2 system.

full_output.methodology: PCR assay and agar dilution method for molecular characterization and MIC determination.

full_output.paper_title: Campycins are novel broad-spectrum antibacterials killing Campylobacter jejuni.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two H-fibers from CJIE1 prophages in C. jejuni strains CAMSA2147 and RM1221, which were used to construct campycins 1 and 2. These campycins exhibit broad antibacterial activity against diverse C. jejuni strains by targeting the major outer membrane protein (MOMP).
full_output.methodology: The study involved constructing campycins by replacing the receptor-binding domain of R2-pyocins with H-fibers from CJIE1 prophages, followed by assessing their antibacterial activity through lysis spot assays and determining the receptor using pull-down assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and antioxidant properties of propolis extract and Lepidium sativum mucilage for bio-preservation of raw buffalo meat
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial and antioxidant properties of propolis extract (PE) and Lepidium sativum mucilage (LS) for the bio-preservation of raw buffalo meat. PE showed significant antimicrobial activity against various bacterial species, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, with the lowest MIC observed for B. cereus. The combination of PE with LS demonstrated enhanced antimicrobial effects, reducing microbial load and extending the shelf life of buffalo meat. Additionally, PE exhibited antioxidant properties, contributing to the preservation of meat quality.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the antimicrobial and antioxidant properties of propolis extract and Lepidium sativum mucilage using disc diffusion agar, well diffusion agar, and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) methods. The physical and sensory properties of buffalo meat coated with different combinations of PE and LS were also evaluated.

full_output.paper_title: The epidemiology of gram-negative bacteremia in Lebanon: a study in four hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the rising prevalence of antimicrobial resistance among gram-negative bacteria in Lebanon, with particular emphasis on carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) and multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii. full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 2400 patients with bloodstream infections across four Lebanese hospitals, focusing on resistance patterns of gram-negative bacteria.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of dietary Lactobacillus postbiotics and bacitracin on the modulation of mucosa-associated microbiota and pattern recognition receptors in pigs challenged with enterotoxigenic F18(+) Escherichia coli. full_output.paper_title: A multiantigenic antibacterial nanovaccine utilizing hybrid membrane vesicles for combating Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel nanovaccine (AuNP@HMV@SPs) designed to combat Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections by combining hybrid membrane vesicles (HMVs) with gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) as an adjuvant. full_output.paper_title: New-generation tetracyclines for severe macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children: a retrospective analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of new-generation tetracyclines, doxycycline and minocycline, for treating severe macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MRMP) pneumonia in children. Doxycycline showed higher fever resolution rates compared to minocycline.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 165 children with severe MRMP pneumonia treated with doxycycline or minocycline, with comparisons of clinical outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Recombinant Lactococcus lactis secreting FliC protein nanobodies for resistance against Salmonella enteritidis invasion in the intestinal tract.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies FliC-Nb76, a nanobody that inhibits Salmonella enteritidis motility and adhesion, offering a novel approach for treating antibiotic-resistant infections.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and animal experiments evaluating the inhibitory effects of FliC-Nb76 on Salmonella enteritidis.

full_output.paper_title: β-Cyclodextrin Catalyzed, One-Pot Multicomponent Synthesis and Antimicrobial Potential of N-Aminopolyhydroquinoline Derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the synthesis of N-aminopolyhydroquinoline (N-PHQ) derivatives using β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) as a catalyst. The synthesized compounds exhibited moderate to excellent antimicrobial activity against both bacterial and fungal strains, with specific derivatives showing activity comparable to standard drugs like amoxicillin and fluconazole.
full_output.methodology: The synthesis of N-PHQ derivatives was performed using β-CD as a catalyst in a one-pot multicomponent reaction. The structures of the compounds were confirmed using spectroscopic techniques, and their antimicrobial activity was evaluated using the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) method.

full_output.paper_title: Intranasal B5 promotes mucosal defence against Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae via ameliorating early immunosuppression
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies B5, an antimicrobial peptide, as having protective effects against bacterial infections by ameliorating early immunosuppression.
full_output.methodology: The study involved in vivo experiments using a mouse model to evaluate the protective effects of B5 against bacterial infections.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiofilm PDMS Coating Development and Release Kinetics Analysis of PDA
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the development of PDA spray-coated and incorporated PDMS surfaces as effective antibiofilm coatings, demonstrating reduced biofilm formation by S. epidermidis. It also characterizes the release kinetics of PDA from PDMS surfaces using a fluorescent probe, showing sustained effectiveness over time.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PDMS fabrication techniques, PDA coating methods, contact angle measurements, FTIR spectroscopy, and biofilm analysis via confocal microscopy to evaluate the antibiofilm properties and PDA release kinetics.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing of Streptococcus uberis isolated from cows with mastitis in Thuringia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in S. uberis isolates from Thuringia, including genes conferring resistance to tetracyclines, lincosamides, macrolides, and erythromycin. A plasmid carrying lnuA and ermB was found in some strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze AMR profiles of 84 S. uberis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of bla(OXA-181)-bearing tigecycline-resistant Klebsiella aerogenes in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the isolation of a tigecycline-resistant Klebsiella aerogenes strain carrying the blaOXA-181 gene on an IncX3 plasmid, along with the qnrS1 and tet(A) genes, indicating multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, conjugation assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.methodology: Biochemical studies, cryo-EM structure analysis, in vitro translation assays, whole-genome sequencing, and MIC determination.

full_output.methodology: Genome mining, chemical synthesis, drop-diffusion tests, MIC determination, in vitro toeprinting analysis, and in vivo stop codon readthrough assays.

full_output.paper_title: Suppression of virulence factors of uropathogenic Escherichia coli by Trans-resveratrol and design of nanoemulgel.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the effect of trans-resveratrol (t-RSV) on the expression of virulence factors in clinical isolates of uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC). t-RSV was found to downregulate the phenotypic and genotypic expression of various virulence factors, including adhesins, biofilm formation, serum resistance, cytotoxicity, and hemolysin production. The study also developed a t-RSV-loaded nanoemulgel formulation with favorable physicochemical properties.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR detection of virulence genes, biofilm assays, hemagglutination tests, serum resistance assays, hemolysin production assays, and cytotoxicity assays to evaluate the impact of t-RSV on UPEC virulence factors.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring Medicinal Plants for Antimicrobial Activity and Synergistic Effects With Doxycycline Against Bacterial Species.

full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of plant extracts using broth microdilution, biofilm formation assays, and combination studies with doxycycline.
