full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) associated with mitochondrial damage and apoptosis in EBL cells infected with M. bovis. Key proteins include YWHAZ, PIK3CA, HSP90AB1, RAP1A, TXN, RAF1, MAPK1, PKM, PGK1, and GAPDH, which may be involved in mitochondrial pathway apoptosis induced by M. bovis infection.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis using DDA and DIA mass spectrometry, bioinformatics tools for GO and KEGG analysis, and PPI network analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of Quinazolone Pyridiniums as Potential Broad-Spectrum Antibacterial Agents.
full_output.key_findings: Quinazolone pyridinium 19a exhibits strong antibacterial activity against MRSA and E. coli with low MIC values, demonstrating potential as a broad-spectrum antibacterial agent.
full_output.methodology: In vitro antibacterial activity testing, hemolysis assay, resistance study, bactericidal kinetics, and biofilm inhibition assays.

full_output.paper_title: 6-Bromoindole- and 6-Bromoindazole-Based Inhibitors of Bacterial Cystathionine γ-Lyase Containing 3-Aminothiophene-2-Carboxylate Moiety.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of new inhibitors targeting bacterial cystathionine gamma-lyase (CGL), showing their potential as antibiotic potentiators. Compounds MNS3, MNS4, and MNS5 exhibited significant inhibitory activity against B. subtilis when combined with gentamicin and kanamycin.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of new inhibitors, MIC assays, and hydrogen sulfide production monitoring in B. subtilis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Shelter Dogs: A Metagenomic Study
full_output.key_findings: This study identified a diverse array of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in shelter dogs, highlighting the potential role of these animals in the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples from 58 shelter dogs was used to identify ARGs.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and Whole-Genome Characteristics of Bordetella trematum Isolated from Captive Snakes.

tmexD4.evidence_note: The tmexD4 gene was identified in the genomes of B. trematum isolates PIW211 and PIW212, and it was noted to confer resistance to tetracycline, doxycycline, minocycline, and tigecycline.

adeF.evidence_note: The adeF gene (99.72% identity, 76.91% coverage), coding for the efflux pump targeting fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines

fosA8.evidence_note: The fosA8 gene was identified in the genomes of B. trematum isolates PIW211 and PIW212 through CARD analysis, and it is responsible for fosfomycin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified three AMR genes in Bordetella trematum isolates from captive snakes: tmexD4, adeF, and fosA8, which confer resistance to tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones/tetracyclines, and fosfomycin, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial resistance testing using microbroth dilution.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Susceptibility Patterns and Virulence Profiles of Classical and Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains Isolated from Clinical Samples in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several biofilm-related genes, including mrkD, pgaABCD, fimH, treC, wzc, pilQ, and luxS, in hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae strains, highlighting their role in biofilm formation and potential contribution to increased virulence and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized whole-genome sequencing and genetic analysis to identify biofilm-related genes and antibiotic resistance profiles in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phage vB_KlebPS_265 Active Against Resistant/MDR and Hypermucoid K2 Strains of Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the phage KlebP_265, which shows lytic activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) and hypermucoid K2 strains of Klebsiella pneumoniae. The phage genome was sequenced and analyzed, revealing no genes encoding integrases, toxins, or antibiotic resistance, suggesting potential therapeutic applications.
full_output.methodology: The study involved phage isolation, propagation, morphological analysis, host range testing, and genome sequencing. The genome was annotated and compared to other phages to determine its taxonomic classification.

full_output.paper_title: Two pathogen-inducible UDP-glycosyltransferases, UGT73C3 and UGT73C4, catalyze the glycosylation of pinoresinol to promote plant immunity in Arabidopsis.
full_output.key_findings: UGT73C3 and UGT73C4 promote plant immunity by glycosylating pinoresinol, enhancing resistance to Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000.
full_output.methodology: Gene overexpression, mutant analysis, metabolomics, and enzymatic assays.

full_output.paper_title: Distinct relative abundances in pathogens detected in mechanically ventilated patients with suspected pneumonia in the intensive care unit at King Abdulaziz University Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies carbapenem resistance genes blaOXA-48, blaNDM-1, and blaVIM in pathogens from ventilator-associated pneumonia patients, highlighting their role in resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing and culture-based methods were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in pathogens from ventilator-associated pneumonia patients.

full_output.paper_title: Metatranscriptomic time series insight into antibiotic resistance genes and mobile genetic elements in wastewater systems under antibiotic selective pressure.
full_output.key_findings: The P14171 gene, encoding a class A beta-lactamase, was identified as the primary antibiotic resistance gene responding to ampicillin in activated sludge systems, highlighting its potential health risks and role in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Metatranscriptomic analysis of activated sludge samples under ampicillin exposure to identify resistance genes and their transcriptional responses.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Potentiation of Doxorubicin Cytotoxicity Utilizing Clarithromycin Loaded-PEGylated Liposomes.

P-gp.notes: The study shows that CAM/DOX-PEGylated liposomes reduced P-gp expression, which may contribute to increased doxorubicin sensitivity.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that CAM/DOX-PEGylated liposomes enhance doxorubicin cytotoxicity against MCF-7 cells by reducing P-gp expression, potentially overcoming drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used PEGylated liposomes to deliver doxorubicin and clarithromycin, evaluating their cytotoxicity and P-gp expression via ELISA and MTT assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobials profiling, biofilm formation, and clonal lineage of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolated from cockroaches.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in S. aureus isolates from cockroaches, including ermA, ermB, ermC, msrA, mupA, and icaA, which confer resistance to erythromycin, mupirocin, and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection and sequencing of AMR genes in S. aureus isolates from cockroaches.

full_output.paper_title: Risk assessment and photo-disinfection of antibiotic residues and antibiotic-resistant bacteria in water sources from Ede, Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibiotic residues and antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) in various water sources in Ede, Nigeria, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria such as Bacillus spp. and Staphylococcus. It also assessed the ecological and health risks associated with these residues and proposed a photocatalytic material for water disinfection.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sampling and analysis of water sources, determination of antibiotic residues using HPLC, screening for ARB via disk diffusion, and evaluation of ecological and health risks.

full_output.paper_title: Retrospective Analysis of Antibiotic Resistance Patterns of Uropathogenic Escherichia coli With Focus on Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase at a Tertiary Central Hospital in Saudi Arabia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 31% of E. coli specimens were positive for ESBL. ESBL-producing E. coli exhibited higher resistance rates than non-ESBL-producing E. coli, with specific resistance rates noted for various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 347 urine specimens collected between January 2022 and March 2023.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the specificity and tunability of efflux pumps in bacteria, focusing on how proton gradients and membrane potentials influence their ability to extrude diverse drug molecules. The research reveals that efflux pump specificity is not solely determined by drug affinity but is also significantly affected by the periplasmic pH and transmembrane potential, highlighting the complex interplay between thermodynamic forces and pump functionality.
full_output.methodology: The study employs theoretical models and mathematical formulations to analyze the operation of efflux pumps as a cyclic stochastic process, incorporating structural and kinetic data from experimental studies.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of magnetization on antibacterial, lipid-lowering and antioxidant activities of isoquinoline alkaloids.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that magnetization of isoquinoline alkaloids enhances their antibacterial, lipid-lowering, and antioxidant activities. Specifically, [Ber·H]+[FeCl4]- showed the best antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli, while [Pal·H]+[FeCl4]- exhibited the strongest lipid-lowering activity.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial, lipid-lowering, and antioxidant activities of magnetized isoquinoline alkaloids using MIC, MBC, and DPPH assays.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and dynamics of antimicrobial resistance in pioneer and developing Arctic soils.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in Arctic soils, showing that their abundance increases with soil age. Key ARGs include tetA, tetX, ampC, blaCTX-M, blaNDM-1, pncA, oqxA, and vanB, which confer resistance to tetracycline, beta-lactams, pyrazinamide, quinolones, and glycopeptides.
full_output.methodology: The study uses qPCR and metagenomic sequencing to analyze the abundance and diversity of ARGs and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in Arctic soils across different developmental stages.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple soil samples from different glacier forefields in Svalbard.

full_output.paper_title: Single-cell analysis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with diverse drug resistance using surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific Raman spectral bands associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, highlighting DNA methylation patterns and glutathione-related features as potential biomarkers for resistance detection.
full_output.methodology: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) was used to analyze single M. tuberculosis cells, focusing on spectral features linked to drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Cockroaches as Reservoirs, Vectors, and Potential Sentinels of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria in Ugandan Communities: A Retrospective Analysis.

tetA.validation_method: molecular detection of AMR markers via colony PCR

tetM.validation_method: molecular detection of AMR markers via colony PCR

tetL.validation_method: molecular detection of AMR markers via colony PCR

sul1.validation_method: molecular detection of AMR markers via colony PCR

sul2.validation_method: molecular detection of AMR markers via colony PCR

full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline and sulfonamide resistance genes (tetA, sul1, sul2) in Escherichia coli and tetracycline resistance genes (tetM, tetL) in Enterococcus spp. from cockroaches in Ugandan communities.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection of AMR markers via colony PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Ester derivatives of Dictyostelium differentiation-inducing factors exhibit antibacterial activity, possibly via a prodrug-like function.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial activity of DIF compounds and their ester derivatives, suggesting that ester derivatives may function as prodrugs, with their antibacterial activity possibly restored by bacterial esterases.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of DIF compounds and their ester derivatives against Gram-positive bacteria, including MSSA, MRSA, VSE, and VRE, in the presence or absence of human serum albumin.

full_output.paper_title: Population pharmacokinetics and pulmonary modeling of eravacycline and the determination of microbiological breakpoint and cutoff of PK/PD.
full_output.key_findings: The study determined the population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model of eravacycline and its microbiological breakpoints for four bacteria: Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, and Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.methodology: The study used a three-compartment population PK model, Monte Carlo simulations, and in vitro susceptibility testing to determine PK/PD cutoff values and breakpoints for eravacycline.

full_output.paper_title: Structural analysis of extracellular ATP-independent chaperones of streptococcal species and protein substrate interactions.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the roles of PrsA and SlrA, ATP-independent chaperones in Streptococcus pneumoniae and Streptococcus pyogenes, which are crucial for the maturation and folding of the pneumolysin toxin, a key virulence factor.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography, protein pull-down assays, biophysical analyses, and chaperone-assisted folding assays were employed to investigate the structural and functional properties of PrsA and SlrA.

full_output.paper_title: Role of the Mobile Active Site Flap in IMP Dehydrogenase Inhibitor Binding.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: The Leu413Ala mutation increases the potency of most inhibitors, even those that contacted Leu413 in the crystal structures.

Leu413.notes: The Leu413 residue is a structural determinant of inhibitor potency and interacts with various inhibitors.
Leu413.source: Wang X, Rosenberg MM, Kim Y, Maltseva N, Cuny GD, Joachimiak A, Kuzmič P, Hedstrom L
Leu413.evidence_note: The study shows that Leu413 is a structural determinant of inhibitor potency and that the Leu413Ala mutation increases the potency of most inhibitors.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Leu413 as a critical residue in IMP dehydrogenase that influences inhibitor potency through transient interactions with the active site flap.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and kinetic experiments were used to analyze inhibitor binding and the role of the active site flap in IMP dehydrogenase.

full_output.paper_title: Fusobacterium nucleatum upregulates the immune inhibitory receptor PD-L1 in colorectal cancer cells via the activation of ALPK1.
full_output.key_findings: Fusobacterium nucleatum upregulates PD-L1 in colorectal cancer cells through ALPK1-dependent NF-κB activation, potentially affecting immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
full_output.methodology: ELISA, RT-qPCR, western blot, and RNA-seq to analyze PD-L1 expression and signaling pathways.

full_output.paper_title: Global insights into the genome dynamics of Clostridioides difficile associated with antimicrobial resistance, virulence, and genomic adaptations among clonal lineages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies high-frequency antibiotic resistance genes such as cdeA, cplR, and nimB in Clostridioides difficile, along with blaCDD-1, blaCDD-2, tet(M), and ermB, which are associated with resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of 19,711 C. difficile genomes using Prokka, MLST, and Roary, with resistance genes identified via CARD and ABRicate.

full_output.paper_title: Assessing the threat of Yersinia pestis harboring a multi-resistant IncC plasmid and the efficacy of an antibiotic targeting LpxC.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the IncC plasmid pIP1202 in Yersinia pestis, which confers resistance to multiple antibiotics. The plasmid was found to be stable in both mice and fleas, highlighting the potential threat of multidrug-resistant Y. pestis. The LpxC inhibitor LPC-233 was shown to be effective against pIP1202-positive and negative Y. pestis strains.
full_output.methodology: The study involved transferring the pIP1202 plasmid into Y. pestis strains via conjugation, assessing virulence in mice and fleas, and evaluating the efficacy of LPC-233 in treating plague caused by multidrug-resistant Y. pestis.

full_output.paper_title: Effectiveness of clindamycin-based exposure strategies in experimental mature staphylococcal biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: Clindamycin was ineffective as a first-line treatment for mature staphylococcal biofilms but showed effectiveness when used after initial rifampicin-ciprofloxacin treatment. Repeated clindamycin exposure at concentrations ≥16 mg/L significantly reduced bacterial load in biofilms.
full_output.methodology: In vitro mature biofilm model with clindamycin exposure strategies, MIC testing, and imaging techniques including confocal laser scanning microscopy and atomic force microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmids encode and can mobilize onion pathogenicity in Pantoea agglomerans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies plasmid-borne genes alt and copABCDRS associated with thiosulfinate and copper resistance, respectively, in P. agglomerans strains linked to onion pathogenicity.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and conjugation assays were used to characterize plasmid-mediated pathogenicity and resistance mechanisms in P. agglomerans.

full_output.paper_title: Incidence and resistance rates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa bloodstream infections in Switzerland: a nationwide surveillance study (2010-2022).
full_output.key_findings: The study found an increase in the incidence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa bloodstream infections in Switzerland from 2010 to 2022, along with rising resistance rates for several antibiotics including cefepime, ceftazidime, ciprofloxacin, and piperacillin-tazobactam.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective, nationwide observational study analyzing incidence and antimicrobial resistance of P. aeruginosa bloodstream infections using data from the Swiss Center for Antimicrobial Resistance (ANRESIS).

full_output.paper_title: Chemical composition, antibacterial and antioxidant activities of Piper betle and Anethum graveolens essential oils against Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial and antioxidant activities of Piper betle and Anethum graveolens essential oils against Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) clinical isolates. Both essential oils showed significant antibacterial activity, with Piper betle exhibiting higher efficacy. The chemical composition of the oils was analyzed using GC-MS, revealing key compounds such as eugenol and o-cymene. The study also highlighted the antioxidant potential of the essential oils, particularly Piper betle, which had higher total phenolic and flavonoid content.
full_output.methodology: The study employed GC-MS for chemical composition analysis, DPPH, FRAP, and ABTS assays for antioxidant activity, and broth microdilution for determining the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) of the essential oils against MRSA isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 5 MRSA clinical isolates and 1 MRSA reference strain

full_output.paper_title: Pilin antigenic variants impact gonococcal lifestyle and antibiotic tolerance by modulating interbacterial forces.
full_output.key_findings: Pilin antigenic variants alter the stereochemistry of Type 4 pili, influencing bacterial aggregation and antibiotic tolerance. Variants with altered C-terminal regions show reduced attractive forces and decreased aggregation, affecting survival under antibiotic stress.
full_output.methodology: Cloning of pilE genes from clinical isolates, structural predictions using AlphaFold, laser tweezers experiments, and assessment of bacterial aggregation and antibiotic tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Essential oils modulate virulence phenotypes in a multidrug-resistant pyomelanogenic Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolate.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes in the MDR P. aeruginosa strain U804, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, and efflux pumps, which contribute to its resistance against various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and database screening for AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Azurin a potent anticancer and antimicrobial agent isolated from a novel Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain (105) capable of producing azurin, a blue-copper protein with significant antimicrobial and anticancer properties. Azurin exhibited antimicrobial activity against multiple bacterial strains and anticancer activity against MCF7 breast cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and identification of P. aeruginosa strain 105, genomic DNA extraction, PCR amplification and sequencing of the azurin gene, purification of azurin, and assessment of its antimicrobial and anticancer activities using various biochemical and molecular techniques.

full_output.paper_title: PIF/harbinger transposon-derived protein promotes 7SL expression to enhance pathogen resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ADF-1L, a protein derived from the PIF/harbinger transposon, as a cis-acting factor that regulates the 7SL-23 gene. ADF-1L promotes the expression of 7SL-23, which enhances the host's resistance to pathogens by modulating the 7SL/miR-2187-3p/TRAF6 axis.
full_output.methodology: The study uses chromatin immunoprecipitation, DNA pull-down assays, electrophoresis mobility shift assays, qPCR, and RNA-seq to analyze the regulatory mechanisms of ADF-1L and 7SL-23.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into incompatible plasmids in multidrug-resistant Raoultella superbugs.

strAB.genetic_context: Tn 5393c remnant, the 5’ end was truncated while retaining the Δ tnpR – strAB –IRR structure
strAB.evidence_note: strAB is part of the Tn 5393c transposon, which carries streptomycin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes on plasmids in multidrug-resistant Raoultella isolates, including blaKPC-2, mcr-9.1, tetA(D), and others, highlighting the role of plasmids in the spread of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, and comparative genomics were used to identify AMR genes and their resistance profiles.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy of the combination of amikacin, cefoxitin, and clarithromycin against Mycobacterium abscessus, highlighting the poor effectiveness of this regimen, particularly in the context of macrolide-inducible resistance. It also notes the impact of clarithromycin concentrations on the response to treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a hollow-fiber infection model to assess the antimicrobial activity of the antibiotic combination against M. abscessus, measuring bacterial growth and antibiotic tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, screening, and characterization of heavy metal-resistant bacteria from solid waste dumping sites in Central Gondar, Northwest, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified six heavy metal-resistant bacterial isolates (Agri10−2 Is2, Agri10−3 Is2, Agri10−3 Is1, AL10−1 Is2, AL10−3 Is1, and GA10−2 Is1) that showed resistance to copper, chromium, and lead. These isolates were characterized as Bacillus subtilis, Bacillus species, Bacillus tequilensis, Klebsiella species, and Cronobacter sakazakii.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and screening of heavy metal-resistant bacteria from soil samples, followed by morphological, biochemical, and molecular characterization using 16S rRNA sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: DNA Polymerase IV dinB Favors the Adaptive Fitness of mcr-carrying Bacteria Through a Negative Feedback Regulatory Mechanism.

mcr-1.mechanism: Modifies lipid A in the bacterial outer membrane by attaching phosphoethanolamine to the N-acetylglucosamine head, reducing the negative charge on the bacterial surface and conferring colistin resistance
mcr-1.validation_method: CRISPRi screening, transcriptional and translational analysis, and complementation experiments

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies DNA polymerase IV (dinB) as a crucial regulator that balances mcr-1 expression and bacterial fitness through a negative feedback mechanism. DinB negatively regulates mcr-1 expression, reducing colistin resistance and improving bacterial fitness.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide CRISPRi crRNA library screening, transcriptional and translational analysis, and complementation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Basis and Mechanism of a Unique Haemophore in the Haem-Iron Acquisition by Riemerella anatipestifer.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes RhuH, a unique haemophore in Riemerella anatipestifer, which plays a crucial role in haem acquisition from host hemoglobin. RhuH binds haem with high affinity and is secreted in outer membrane vesicles. Its structure and function are conserved among related Flavobacteriales species.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, protein purification, biochemical assays, structural analysis, and comparative genomics.

full_output.paper_title: Solvent Effect on Antimicrobial Hydrophilic Xerogel Coating of Medicinal Leathers in Simulated Industrial Finishing Process.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the PEI-Ag-SiO2-TiO2 hybrid xerogel composite exhibits significant antimicrobial activity against various pathogens including Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was assessed using the inhibition-zone method on LB-medium agar plates.

full_output.paper_title: Rational Design of Natural Xanthones Against Gram-negative Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies A20 as a potent broad-spectrum antibacterial compound that effectively targets Gram-negative bacteria by penetrating the outer membrane through a self-promoted pathway and disrupting bacterial respiration by interacting with the cofactor heme in the respiratory complex.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized virtual screening, structural optimization, and experimental validation to characterize the antibacterial activity of A20 and its mechanisms of action.

full_output.paper_title: The pivotal role of IncFIB(Mar) plasmid in the emergence and spread of hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two major virulence plasmids, pIUC1-IncFIB(K) 37 and pIUC1-IncFIB(Mar), involved in the emergence and spread of hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (hv-CRKP). These plasmids contribute to hypervirulence and are associated with the spread of hv-CRKP in different regions.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid sequencing, conjugation experiments, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the virulence plasmids and their roles in hv-CRKP emergence.

full_output.paper_title: Fragment optimized chalcone derivatives targeting OmpA protein as a therapeutic approach against multidrug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the use of chalcone derivatives targeting the OmpA protein of Acinetobacter baumannii, aiming to develop new therapeutic agents against multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in silico analysis, molecular docking, and ADMET analysis to evaluate the potential of chalcone derivatives as antibacterial agents.

full_output.paper_title: Optimization and characterization of bioactive secondary metabolites from Streptomyces sp CMSTAAHL-4 isolated from mangrove sediment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Streptomyces sp. CMSTAAHL-4 as a producer of bioactive secondary metabolites with antibacterial, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory properties. The metabolites showed significant activity against various bacterial pathogens, including S. aureus, K. pneumoniae, E. coli, P. aeruginosa, S. typhi, and E. faecalis.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation, molecular characterization, media optimization, and evaluation of secondary metabolites from Streptomyces sp. CMSTAAHL-4 using techniques such as FT-IR, GC-MS, and bioactivity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Amino acid substitutions in PBP3 in Haemophilus influenzae strains, their phenotypic detection and impact on resistance to β-lactams.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies twenty different amino acid substitutions in the ftsI gene of Haemophilus influenzae strains, which are associated with β-lactam resistance. These substitutions include D350N, S357N, M377I, S385T, L389F, S406G, P408S, V418A, A437S, I449V, V461I, G490E, R501C, A502V, A502T, I519L, R517H, N526K, A530S, and T532S. The study highlights the challenges in phenotypic detection of these resistant strains and emphasizes the importance of molecular methods for accurate identification.
full_output.methodology: The study involved susceptibility testing of β-lactam antibiotics and sequencing of the ftsI gene to identify amino acid substitutions in Haemophilus influenzae strains.

full_output.paper_title: Capture of mobile genetic elements following intercellular conjugation promotes the production of ST11-KL64 CR-hvKP.

full_output.methodology: Plasmid analysis, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Double carbapenemases in Klebsiella pneumoniae blood isolates: dissemination in a single medical center via multiple plasmids and a variety of highly efficient clones.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla KPC-2, bla KPC-3, and bla VIM-1 genes as the primary carbapenemase genes responsible for resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae blood isolates. These genes were found on separate plasmids and contributed to extensive drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and plasmid analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and their dissemination mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Role of metabolism, resistance, and/or antagonism as drivers of endomicrobiomes assemblage in Origanum heracleoticum L.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the metabolic capabilities and antibiotic resistance profiles of bacterial endophytes from different plant organs of Origanum heracleoticum, highlighting organ-specific differences in metabolic activity and resistance patterns.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic characterization of bacterial endophytes using Biolog GEN III MicroPlate for carbon source utilization and antibiotic resistance testing.

full_output.paper_title: Who arrived first? Priority effects on Candida albicans and Pseudomonas aeruginosa dual biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the impact of priority effects on the virulence and antimicrobial susceptibility of dual-species biofilms formed by Candida albicans and Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAET1. It shows that the order of inoculation affects biofilm composition, structure, and susceptibility to antimicrobials, with sequential colonization leading to increased virulence and altered susceptibility profiles.
full_output.methodology: The study used clinical isolates of C. albicans and P. aeruginosa PAET1 to form dual-species biofilms under different inoculation orders. Biofilm composition, structure, and susceptibility to antimicrobials were assessed using CFU counts, microscopy, and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular analysis of AmpC-producing Escherichia coli isolated from pediatric patients.

ampC.notes: Mutations in the promoter and attenuator regions of the chromosomal ampC gene contribute to increased AmpC production and resistance to cephalosporins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified plasmid-mediated AmpC genes blaDHA-1 and blaCMY-2, as well as chromosomal ampC mutations in pediatric E. coli isolates, contributing to cephalosporin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of β-lactam antibiotic resistance of Escherichia coli isolated from a neonatal intensive care unit.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several β-lactam resistance genes, including bla KPC-2, bla CTX-M-64, bla CTX-M-65, bla TEM-1, bla OXA-1, and bla DHA-1, in Escherichia coli isolates from a neonatal intensive care unit. These genes were found to confer resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar dilution method for antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR for screening β-lactamase genes, and conjugation experiments to assess horizontal transferability of resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Global biogeography and projection of antimicrobial toxin genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 4400 antimicrobial toxin gene (ATG) clusters from 149 families, highlighting the global distribution and diversity of ATGs across various habitats, with human-associated habitats showing greater diversity and sharing with natural habitats.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of metagenomic data, machine learning, and bioinformatics to identify and characterize ATGs across 10,000 samples.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and resistome analysis of Salmonella enterica isolates from retail markets in Yichun city, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella enterica isolates from retail markets in Yichun city, China, including genes conferring resistance to various antibiotics such as chloramphenicol, tetracycline, trimethoprim, and extended-spectrum beta-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and virulence factors in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome analysis of a ST45-SCCmec IVa (2B)-t116 methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strain isolated from the sputum of a 5-year-old child with pneumonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the mecA and blaZ genes in the ST45-SCCmec IVa (2B)-t116 MRSA strain SA2107, which confer resistance to methicillin and penicillin, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify antibiotic resistance genes and mutations in the MRSA strain SA2107.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the Vibrio anguillarum VaRyhB regulon and role in pathogenesis.

full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis, qRT-PCR, siderophore assays, swimming motility assays, and virulence assays in turbot larvae.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals transmission pattern and drug resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis intra- or inter-hosts.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various drug-resistant mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including mutations in katG, rpoB, embB, fabG1, gyrA, rrs, rpsL, gidB, and thyA, which confer resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, fluoroquinolones, amikacin, kanamycin, streptomycin, and para-aminosalicylic acid.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and molecular drug susceptibility testing were used to identify drug-resistant mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis samples.

full_output.paper_title: Preserving the antimicrobial arsenal: exploring alternatives to carbapenems in ESBL battles within the southeast of Ireland.
full_output.key_findings: Temocillin, mecillinam, cefiderocol, and fosfomycin display excellent activity against ESBL-producing Enterobacterales, offering promising alternatives to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted following EUCAST guidelines using disc diffusion and gradient strip methods.

full_output.paper_title: Class B scavenger receptor resists WSSV replication by recognizing the viral lipid molecule and promoting phagocytosis.

full_output.key_findings: PcSRB, a class B scavenger receptor in Procambarus clarkii, binds to the WSSV lipid molecule CD3,5 and viral envelope proteins, thereby promoting phagocytosis and inhibiting WSSV replication.
full_output.methodology: RNA interference, TEM, ELISA, MST, phagocytosis assay, qRT-PCR

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial peptide DiPGLa-H exhibits the most outstanding anti-infective activity among the PGLa variants based on a systematic comparison.
full_output.key_findings: DiPGLa-H exhibited the most outstanding antibacterial activity among PGLa variants, with high therapeutic index and effective disruption of bacterial membranes.
full_output.methodology: Systematic comparison of PGLa variants, determination of MIC and MBC, and assessment of membrane permeability and antibacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Artificial intelligence using a latent diffusion model enables the generation of diverse and potent antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel pipeline using a latent diffusion model to generate diverse and potent antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). Twenty-five out of forty synthesized peptides exhibited antimicrobial activity, with AMP-24 showing potent activity against Gram-negative bacteria and AMP-29 demonstrating selective antifungal activity against Candida glabrata and Cryptococcus neoformans.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a latent diffusion model combined with molecular dynamics simulations to generate and filter antimicrobial peptides, followed by experimental validation through MIC testing and in vivo evaluations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Bte1 as a T6-dependent effector that targets the PpiD-YfgM chaperone complex in recipient cells, leading to protein misfolding and toxicity. A mutation in the SecE protein (D49G) confers resistance to Bte1 toxicity.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screens, crystallography, proteomics, and in vivo experiments in germ-free mice.

full_output.paper_title: Size Distribution and Pathogenic Potential of Culturable Airborne Clostridium spp. in a Suburb of Toyama City, Japan.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in Clostridium perfringens isolates, including mprF, tetA[P], tetB[P], erm[Q], cfrC, and mef[A]. These genes confer resistance to defensin, tetracycline, erythromycin, linezolid, phenicol, and macrolide antibiotics.

Mutations in the 23S rRNA gene (A2142G, A2143G, A2142C) and gyrA gene (A260T, C261A, T261G, G271A, G271T, A272G) were associated with resistance to these antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR to detect mutations in the 23S rRNA and gyrA genes of H. pylori isolates.

full_output.paper_title: C10-Benzoate Esters of Anhydrotetracycline Inhibit Tetracycline Destructases and Recover Tetracycline Antibacterial Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies C10-benzoate esters of anhydrotetracycline as effective inhibitors of tetracycline destructases (TetX7 and Tet50), restoring tetracycline's antibacterial activity against resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: In vitro assays, NMR analysis, and crystallography were used to evaluate the inhibitory effects of C10-benzoate esters on tetracycline destructases.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify rpoB mutations and their association with rifampicin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antibiotic resistance of Escherichia coli in urban and peri-urban garden ecosystems in Bangladesh.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of blaTEM and tetA genes in E. coli isolates from urban and peri-urban gardens in Bangladesh, contributing to their resistance to ampicillin and tetracycline, respectively.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect AMR genes and resistance profiles in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, characterization and genomic analysis of bacteriophages for biocontrol of vibriosis caused by Vibrio alginolyticus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bacteriophages P122, P125, and P160 with broad host range against Vibrio alginolyticus, exhibiting lytic activity and stability in artificial seawater. Genomic analysis confirmed the absence of antibiotic resistance or virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, host range determination, one-step growth curve, stability testing, TEM, and WGS analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Development of tolerance to bedaquiline by overexpression of trypanosomal acetate: succinate CoA transferase in Mycobacterium smegmatis.
full_output.key_findings: Overexpression of trypanosomal ASCT in M. smegmatis leads to partial restoration of intracellular ATP levels and acquired tolerance to bedaquiline (BDQ) at low concentrations, highlighting the role of ATP in BDQ's mechanism of action.
full_output.methodology: Metabolic engineering and biochemical characterization of ASCT activity in M. smegmatis.

full_output.paper_title: Guanosine enhances the bactericidal effect of ceftiofur sodium on Streptococcus suis by activating bacterial metabolism.
full_output.key_findings: Guanosine enhances the bactericidal effect of ceftiofur sodium on Streptococcus suis by activating bacterial metabolism, improving the sensitivity of multidrug-resistant strains to antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo experiments, MIC assays, checkerboard studies, and gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra-resistant and MTBDRplus-susceptible rifampicin results in people with tuberculosis: utility of FluoroType MTBDR and deep sequencing.

rpoB.notes: Multiple rpoB mutations were detected, including L511P, D516Y, and S531L.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the importance of advanced sequencing techniques like SMOR in detecting rifampicin resistance-associated variants (RAVs) in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, particularly in cases where conventional methods like MTBDR plus fail to detect resistance. It identifies specific rpoB mutations such as L511P, D516Y, and S531L that contribute to rifampicin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized SMOR sequencing, FluoroType MTBDR, and traditional methods like MTBDR plus to analyze rifampicin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mecillinam activity against multidrug-resistant Shigella sonnei and Shigella flexneri.

cysB.notes: No resistance mutations in cysB were detected.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that mecillinam had favorable susceptibility profiles against multidrug-resistant Shigella isolates, with no known clinically relevant mecillinam resistance mutations detected, including the absence of cysB mutations.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic susceptibility testing, whole-genome sequencing, and analysis of genetic resistance markers.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several clinically relevant antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in bovine respiratory disease (BRD) pathogens, including estT, floR, mphE, erm(42), msrE, aadA, ANT(2''-Ia), APH(3''-Ib), APH(3'-Ia), APH(6)-Id, sul2, tet(H), ROB-1, and OXA-2. Additionally, mutations in gyrA and parC were found to confer resistance to fluoroquinolones in Mannheimia haemolytica.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) and identification of mutations through sequence data.

full_output.paper_title: Artesunate, EDTA, and colistin work synergistically against MCR-negative and -positive colistin-resistant Salmonella.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cheA and spvD as critical genes for the bacteriostatic synergistic effects of the AEC combination against colistin-resistant Salmonella, highlighting their role in chemotaxis and virulence.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis, overexpression experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to investigate the mechanisms of the AEC combination against Salmonella.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of risk factors associated with Ancylostoma spp. infection and the benzimidazole F167Y resistance marker polymorphism in dogs from the United States.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the F167Y polymorphism in the beta-tubulin gene of Ancylostoma caninum as a resistance marker for benzimidazole anthelmintics in dogs in the United States.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and statistical analysis of fecal samples from dogs.

full_output.paper_title: The tetracycline resistome is shaped by selection for specific resistance mechanisms by each antibiotic generation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific tetracycline resistance mechanisms (efflux pumps, ribosomal protection proteins, and type 1 tetracycline destructases) that are preferentially selected by different generations of tetracycline antibiotics, highlighting the evolutionary dynamics of resistance.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput barcode sequencing and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to evaluate the relative fitness of tetracycline-resistant E. coli strains expressing various resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: The Hippo pathway promotes platinum-based chemotherapy by inhibiting MTF1-dependent heavy metal response.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MTF1 and its downstream heavy metal response genes MT1A and MT2A as critical players in platinum-based chemotherapy resistance. Loss of MTF1 sensitizes cancer cells to cisplatin, while its reconstitution with MT1A and MT2A rescues cell viability. The Hippo pathway regulates MTF1 activity, and its activation enhances cisplatin sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas9 gene knockout, Western blot, q-PCR, cell viability assays, xenograft tumor models.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of phenotypic and genetic traits of ESBL-producing UPEC strains causing recurrent or single episode UTI in postmenopausal women.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that ESBL-producing UPEC strains causing recurrent UTIs in postmenopausal women exhibited higher intracellular CFU counts and increased ompT expression compared to single episode strains, suggesting a role for these genes in intracellular persistence and virulence.
full_output.methodology: PCR, qRT-PCR, and intracellular CFU assays were used to analyze gene expression and bacterial persistence in bladder epithelial cells.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic-associated changes in Akkermansia muciniphila alter its effects on host metabolic health.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the promoter of a TEM-type β-lactamase gene and in pur genes of Akkermansia muciniphila that confer reduced antibiotic susceptibility and impair the bacterium's ability to mitigate host obesity.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, qPCR, Etest, and mouse models were used to analyze mutations and their effects on antibiotic resistance and host health.

full_output.paper_title: Priestia megaterium cells are primed for surviving lethal doses of antibiotics and chemical stress.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 'primed cells' in Priestia megaterium that are pre-adapted to become persisters before antibiotic stress, contributing to increased antibiotic persistence. These cells exhibit transient epigenetic memory and are not inherently resistant but survive by entering a non-dividing state.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a modified Luria-Delbrück Fluctuation Test to analyze persister dynamics and identify primed cells in P. megaterium.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring New Delhi Metallo Beta Lactamases in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli: genotypic vs. phenotypic insights.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla NDM and bla OXA as the primary carbapenemase genes in CREK isolates, with bla NDM−5 being the most prevalent variant. The RESIST-5 lateral flow assay showed high sensitivity and specificity for detecting bla NDM in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: PCR, WGS, lateral flow assay, and MIC testing were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of Zinc Oxide Nanoparticles Combined with Streptomycin and Moringa Oleifera Leaf Extract Against Multidrug-Resistant Enterococcus faecalis
full_output.key_findings: The study identified biofilm-related genes gelE, sprE, and fsrABC in multidrug-resistant Enterococcus faecalis isolates from feline urinary tract infections. These genes were detected via PCR and correlated with biofilm formation capabilities.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assessment, PCR for gene detection, and nanoparticle characterization.

full_output.paper_title: Selection of Lactobacillus strains from native chicken feces for the fermentation of purple onion (Allium cepa L.) as an antibiotic alternative against Salmonella spp. in chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Lactobacillus strains with potential as probiotics to combat Salmonella in poultry, highlighting their antibacterial activity and compatibility with purple onion extract.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and screening of Lactobacillus strains, assessment of their antibacterial activity, molecular identification, and evaluation of probiotic properties.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic analysis blaTEM gene of Escherichia coli isolated from cave bats in West Nusa Tenggara Province, Indonesia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the blaTEM gene as the ESBL encoding gene in E. coli isolates from cave bats in West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, showing genetic closeness to E. coli strains from Thailand.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of blaTEM gene and phylogenetic analysis using MegaX 11 software.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and molecular identification of bacteria from sheep with eye infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibiotic-resistant bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Pasteurella multocida in sheep with eye infections, highlighting the need for effective antibiotic use and stewardship programs.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial isolation, PCR for molecular identification, and antibiotic susceptibility testing to analyze the resistance profiles of isolated bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Anti-MRSA effects of synergism of recombinant lysostaphin with biosynthesized silver nanoparticles.
full_output.key_findings: Recombinant lysostaphin and biosynthesized silver nanoparticles (SNPs) showed significant antibacterial activity against MRSA, with a synergistic effect when combined.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, expression, and purification of recombinant lysostaphin in E. coli, biosynthesis of SNPs using C. albicans, and antibacterial assays.

full_output.paper_title: β-Lactamase diversity in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the diversity and distribution of β-lactamase alleles in Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting the most common intrinsic and acquired alleles such as bla ADC-73, bla ADC-30, bla OXA-66, and bla OXA-23, which are associated with carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing analysis of 28,330 Acinetobacter baumannii isolates to identify and characterize β-lactamase alleles.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of GABARAP or GABARAPL1 prevents aminoglycoside- induced hearing loss.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies GABARAP and GABARAPL1 as essential for aminoglycoside-induced hearing loss, with GABARAP playing a more prominent role. Genetic depletion of these proteins prevents hair cell death and hearing loss without affecting normal hearing.
full_output.methodology: Genetic approaches, morphological and functional assays, and AAV-mediated RNAi were used to investigate the role of GABARAP and GABARAPL1 in aminoglycoside ototoxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Development and Evaluation of Vancomycin-Loaded Hybrid Nanostructured Lipid Carriers for Enhanced Antimicrobial Activity Against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus
full_output.key_findings: The study developed and evaluated vancomycin-loaded hybrid nanostructured lipid carriers (VCM-HNLCs) for enhanced antimicrobial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). VCM-HNLCs showed improved antibacterial activity, reduced MIC values, and enhanced biofilm eradication compared to bare vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution, flow cytometry, crystal violet assays, and fluorescence microscopy to evaluate the antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of VCM-HNLCs against S. aureus and MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Helicobacter pylori Infection in Colombia: Phylogeny, Resistome, and Virulome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various mutations associated with antimicrobial resistance in Helicobacter pylori genomes from Colombia, including resistance to clarithromycin, tetracycline, levofloxacin, amoxicillin, and metronidazole.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico analysis were used to detect mutations associated with antimicrobial resistance in H. pylori genomes.

full_output.paper_title: Risk assessment of antibiotic residues and resistance profile of E. coli in typical rivers of Sichuan, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibiotic resistance in E. coli isolates from Sichuan's rivers, with tetracycline showing the highest resistance rate. Multidrug-resistant E. coli strains were found, highlighting the ecological risks of antibiotic pollution.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic combination of ceftazidime and avibactam with Aztreonam against MDR Klebsiella pneumoniae in ICU patients.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes associated with antibiotic resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including rpoB, embB, katG, rpsL, gyrA, rrs, rplC, and PPE54, which are linked to resistance against various antibiotics such as rifampicin, ethambutol, isoniazid, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, and linezolid.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a machine learning classifier (MTB++) to predict antibiotic resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates and aligns k-mer features to the MTB reference genome to identify resistance-associated genes.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors for Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales infections: A case-control study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA-48 and bla NDM as the primary resistance genes in CRE isolates, with bla OXA-48 being the most common (49.1%) followed by bla NDM (12.3%). No bla KPC or bla VIM genes were detected.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective case-control study analyzing antimicrobial susceptibility and resistance genes in CRE isolates using RESIST-4 O.K.N.V assay and statistical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic diversity and transmission pattern of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis based on whole-genome sequencing in Wuhan, China.
full_output.key_findings: This study identified various drug resistance mutations in multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) isolates from Wuhan, China, using whole-genome sequencing. Key findings include mutations in rpoB, katG, embB, rpsL, pncA, gyrA, rrs, fabG1, and ahpC genes associated with resistance to rifampicin, isoniazid, ethambutol, streptomycin, pyrazinamide, ofloxacin, amikacin, kanamycin, capreomycin, and ethionamide.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was used to identify resistance-conferring mutations in MDR-TB isolates, followed by bioinformatics analysis to determine the genetic relationships and clustering profiles of the strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that gelatinous zooplankton organic matter (GZ-OM) from jellyfish blooms acts as a hotspot for the proliferation of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in marine microbial communities. Key bacterial players like Vibrio spp. were found to harbor multiple ARGs, including multidrug efflux pumps and tetracycline and quinolone resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study re-analyzed metagenomic datasets from microcosm experiments involving the degradation of GZ-OM from Mnemiopsis leidyi and Aurelia aurita, combined with whole-genome sequencing of a Vibrio isolate to identify ARGs and MGEs.

full_output.paper_title: Roles of efflux pumps and nitroreductases in metronidazole-resistant Trichomonas vaginalis.

full_output.paper_title: Histamine Promotes Pseudomonas aeruginosa Biofilm Formation and Renders P. aeruginosa Biofilms More Resistant to Gentamicin and Azithromycin.

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed microbial isolates and antibiotic susceptibilities in acute-onset postoperative endophthalmitis, finding that most isolates were Gram-positive bacteria, with no significant changes in bacterial trends over two decades. All Gram-positive bacteria were sensitive to Vancomycin, and most Gram-negative bacteria were sensitive to Ceftazidime/Amikacin.

full_output.paper_title: Co-translational protein aggregation and ribosome stalling as a broad-spectrum antibacterial mechanism.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies P33, a synthetic peptide that induces co-translational protein aggregation and ribosome stalling, leading to bactericidal activity against a wide range of pathogenic bacteria, including ESKAPE pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of microscopic techniques, proteomic analyses, and in vivo models to evaluate the antibacterial activity and mechanism of action of P33.

full_output.paper_title: Biotransformation of Thiochroman Derivatives Using Marine-Derived Fungi: Isolation, Characterization, and Antimicrobial Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the biotransformation of thiochroman derivatives using marine-derived fungi, identifying several new compounds and characterizing their stereochemistry. However, no AMR genes or mutations were found to be directly responsible for antimicrobial resistance in this study.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the biotransformation of thiochroman derivatives using marine fungi, structural characterization via NMR, HR ESI-MS, and ECD, and antimicrobial activity testing against bacterial and fungal pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Binary Combinations of Essential Oils: Antibacterial Activity Against Staphylococcus aureus, and Antioxidant and Anti-Inflammatory Properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that Origanum vulgare L. essential oil (O. vulgare L.) exhibited strong antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, with synergistic and additive effects observed when combined with Cistus ladaniferus L. and Juniperus communis L. essential oils. full_output.paper_title: Systemic Activation of Immunity-Related Genes in Arabidopsis Roots Infected with Verticillium longisporum

qnrS1.genetic_context: qnrS1 was found to be the most prevalent TMQR gene both in our isolates (n = 12) and in the RefSeq genomes (n = 21), irrespective of the source (i.e., surface water or wastewater), and was detected on plasmids of diverse replicon types or on the chromosome (Tables S1 and S2).
qnrS1.evidence_note: The genetic contexts of qnrS1 were largely classified into 13 types (types A to M in Fig. 4). Types B, E, and I are found only in the genomes analyzed in this study, and no other hits were found by blastn analysis.

qnrD1.genetic_context: Three genomes sequenced to closure in the present study carried qnrD1 . qnrD1 was first described on a 4270 bp plasmid, p2007057, in a clinical Salmonella enterica strain isolated in China [ 31 ]. qnrD1 has since been detected on multiple plasmids; however, blastn analysis identified that qnrD1 is rare in Enterobacteriaceae and mostly detected on ~ 2.7 kbp plasmids in Morganellaceae. Two of the three genomes carried qnrD1 on a plasmid identical to p2007057 (Fig. 3 ). The remaining genome carried qnrD1 on a 6657 bp plasmid, named pKFu015_4, with no close blastn hits (all hits were below 50% query coverage). The qnrD1 region, including qnrD1 and ORF2, in pKFu015_4, is identical to ~ 2.7 kbp Morganellaceae plasmids such as pRS12-11 ( KF364953 ) and is ~ 95% identical to the corresponding region in p2007057 (and thus pKMi029_6 and pKTa005_7).
qnrD1.evidence_note: The paper mentions that qnrD1 was detected in environmental E. coli isolates and provides information about its genetic context.

aac(6')-Ib-cr.genetic_context: Three genomes sequenced to closure in this study and nine RefSeq genomes carried aac(6′)-Ib-cr . aac(6′)-Ib-cr was detected on the chromosome ( n = 6) or on IncF plasmids ( n = 6) (Fig. 6 ).

qnrB4.genetic_context: Three RefSeq genomes carried qnrB4 on different IncF plasmids. qnrB4 is known to be globally distributed and often associated with the AmpC type β-lactamase gene bla DHA-1 [ 24 ]. In all three plasmids, qnrB4 is linked to bla DHA-1 and also to other AMR genes (Fig. 2 a).
qnrB4.evidence_note: The study analyzed the complete genomes of 53 environmental E. coli isolates containing one or more transferable quinolone resistance determinants, including 20 sequenced in this study and 33 sourced from RefSeq.

qnrB7.genetic_context: Two isolates sequenced to closure in the present study carried qnrB7. qnrB7 was previously reported to be associated with the ESBL gene bla SHV-12 [24]. However, reports of complete plasmid (or chromosome) sequences carrying qnrB7 are scarce; blastn analysis identified only four complete plasmid sequences carrying qnrB7. One of them, the IncX3 plasmid pLHST2018_IncX3 harbored by a clinical Salmonella enterica isolate from India, carried both qnrB7 and bla SHV-12 [28]. In our isolates, qnrB7 was also carried by IncX3 plasmids and associated with bla SHV-12 (Fig. 2 b). The genetic contexts in our isolates and pLHST2018_IncX3 were similar, but a region next to bla SHV-12 was deleted in pLHST2018_IncX3, probably due to intramolecular transposition of IS 26.

qnrB19.genetic_context: qnrB19 is usually mobilized by transposition units (TPU) mediated by IS Ecp1, such as Tn 2012 and Tn 5387, or small ColE1-like plasmids containing fragments of these transposons

oqxAB.genetic_context: Mobile oqxAB genes are commonly found within an IS 26 - oqxA - oqxB - oqxR -IS 26 pseudo-compound transposon, named Tn 6010 [ 46 ]. All four oqxAB genes identified in the present study are situated within Tn 6010 and carried by plasmids of different Inc types (Fig. 7 ).

qepA1.genetic_context: qepA1 was located between a truncated intI1 and IS CR3 on an IncF plasmid

full_output.paper_title: Re-Emergence of Bacteriophages and Their Products as Antibacterial Agents: An Overview.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the potential of bacteriophages (BPhs) and their products as antibacterial agents, focusing on their use in treating multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) bacterial infections. It highlights the effectiveness of BPhs in eradicating biofilms, their synergy with antibiotics, and successful case reports in treating various infections.
full_output.methodology: The review synthesizes findings from various studies on bacteriophages and their enzymatic products, analyzing their roles in antibacterial therapies, including phage-antibiotic synergy and biofilm disruption.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, Antimicrobial Activities, and Model of Action of Indolyl Derivatives Containing Amino-Guanidinium Moieties.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial properties of cannabidiol (CBD) in PMMA denture coatings, demonstrating significant bactericidal effects against Gram-positive bacteria like Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus agalactiae, while showing limited effectiveness against Gram-negative bacteria such as Escherichia coli. CBD coatings significantly reduced biofilm formation on both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized 1H NMR, SEM, and FTIR spectroscopy for coating characterization, and antimicrobial activity was assessed through MIC, zone of inhibition, and bactericidal studies.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Treatment Options for Multidrug Resistant Gram-Negative Pathogens in Bone and Joint Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the challenges of treating multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Gram-negative bacteria (GNB) in bone and joint infections, highlighting the importance of combination therapies and the role of specific antibiotics such as colistin, fosfomycin, tigecycline, and novel β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: The paper is a narrative review analyzing epidemiological trends, experimental data, and clinical experiences with antimicrobial treatments for MDR/XDR GNB in bone and joint infections.

full_output.paper_title: The Role of Stratified Cumulative Antibiograms in the (Choice of Appropriate Antibiotics in Urinary Tract Infection) Management of Urinary Tract Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights significant differences in antibiotic resistance patterns of Escherichia coli isolates from patients with urinary tract infections (UTIs) across different healthcare facilities and patient demographics. It emphasizes the importance of stratified cumulative antibiograms for guiding appropriate antibiotic use.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed data from 383 patients with UTIs from a hospital department and 272 patients from an outpatient medical facility, focusing on E. coli resistance to commonly used antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Anaerobiosis and Mutations Can Reduce Susceptibility of Pseudomonas aeruginosa to Tobramycin Without Reducing the Cellular Concentration of the Antibiotic.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fusA1 mutations as a key factor in reduced tobramycin susceptibility under anaerobic conditions in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, without affecting cellular antibiotic concentration.
full_output.methodology: Experimental evolution, genome sequencing, and LC-MS/MS-based assay for measuring cellular tobramycin concentration.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of NDM-7-Producing Klebsiella quasipneumoniae subs. simillipneumoniae ST138 in a Hospital from the Northern Region of Brazil.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Characterization of Carbapenemase-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST895 Isolates from Canine Origins Through Whole-Genome Sequencing Analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Cefepime-enmetazobactam: first approved cefepime-β- lactamase inhibitor combination for multi-drug resistant Enterobacterales.

full_output.paper_title: Optimizing phage therapy for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacter cloacae bacteremia: insights into dose and timing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three novel lytic phages (ФEBU8, ФECL22, and ФECL30) with broad host ranges against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacter cloacae. These phages demonstrate effective bactericidal activity and stability under various conditions, highlighting their potential for phage therapy.
full_output.methodology: Phages were isolated from sewage, characterized for host range, and tested for stability and lytic activity. In vivo experiments evaluated the efficacy of phage cocktails in a mouse model of bacteremia.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a 6.33% prevalence of MRSA nasal carriage among healthcare workers in critical care units, with the highest prevalence among attendants and housekeeping staff. All MRSA isolates showed 100% resistance to penicillin and 100% susceptibility to linezolid.
full_output.methodology: Nasal swabs were collected and analyzed using standard microbiological methods, including antibiotic susceptibility testing via the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: A noncanonical intrinsic terminator in the HicAB toxin-antitoxin operon promotes the transmission of conjugative antibiotic resistance plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: Biocompatibility and photoinactivation evaluation of zinc hydroxide chloride nanosheets against Streptococcus mutans.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the biocompatibility and photoinactivation effectiveness of zinc hydroxide chloride nanosheets (ZHC-NSs) against Streptococcus mutans. ZHC-NSs showed good biocompatibility at lower concentrations and enhanced antibacterial activity when combined with a 980 nm diode laser, demonstrating potential for use in dental caries prevention.
full_output.methodology: The study used microscopic and spectroscopic techniques for characterization, along with in vitro tests for biocompatibility, acute toxicity, genotoxicity, and cytotoxicity. Antibacterial activity was assessed using colony-forming unit (CFU) counts and FESEM imaging.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a Weighted-Incidence Syndromic Combination Antibiogram (WISCA) to guide empiric antibiotic treatment for ventilator-associated pneumonia in a Mexican tertiary care university hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a WISCA model to optimize empirical antibiotic therapy for ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) by analyzing local microbiological data and resistance profiles. Key findings include the high prevalence of multidrug-resistant organisms such as Acinetobacter baumannii and the effectiveness of specific antibiotic regimens in covering these pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 197 VAP episodes, including microbiological data and susceptibility testing, using a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate antibiotic coverage.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotype and genotype of carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae in a teaching hospital in Shanghai, China.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of antimicrobial peptides from the Ambystoma mexicanum displaying antibacterial and antitumor activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) derived from the skin mucus of the axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum) that exhibit antibacterial activity against MRSA and MSSA, as well as antitumor activity against T-47D mammary carcinoma cells.
full_output.methodology: The study uses mass spectrometric analysis, bioinformatics prediction tools, and in vitro assays to evaluate the antimicrobial and antitumor activities of synthesized AMPs.

full_output.paper_title: In silico screening and molecular dynamics analysis of natural DHPS enzyme inhibitors targeting Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two natural ligands, MSID_000725 and CID_291096, as potential inhibitors of the DHPS enzyme in Acinetobacter baumannii through in silico screening and molecular dynamics simulations.
full_output.methodology: In silico screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA binding free energy analysis were used to evaluate natural ligands as DHPS enzyme inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical outcomes and pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics of intravenous polymyxin B treatment for various site carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacterial infections: a prospective observational multicenter study.
full_output.key_findings: This study evaluated the clinical outcomes and PK/PD of intravenous polymyxin B treatment for various site carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacterial infections. full_output.methodology: Prospective observational multicenter study analyzing clinical outcomes and PK/PD parameters of polymyxin B treatment in patients with carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacterial infections.

full_output.paper_title: In Situ-Gelling Antimicrobial Poly(oligoethylene glycol methacrylate)-Based Hydrogels Integrating Bound Quaternary Ammonium Compounds and Antibiotic Functionalities for Effective Infected Wound Healing.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of in situ-gelling antibacterial hydrogels incorporating quaternary ammonium (QA) groups and the antibiotic ciprofloxacin (CIP) for effective treatment of infected wounds. These hydrogels show broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against both gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of polymer precursors, assessment of antibacterial activity, determination of minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC), and evaluation of in vivo wound healing efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Harnessing Monoterpenes and Monoterpenoids as Weapons against Antimicrobial Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the antimicrobial potential of monoterpenes and monoterpenoids against multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, highlighting their ability to disrupt cell membranes, inhibit biofilm formation, and modulate gene expression related to virulence and resistance.
full_output.methodology: The paper analyzes literature on the efficacy of monoterpenes against AMR, focusing on their mechanisms of action and minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) against various pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of Doxycycline-Sitafloxacin Sequential Therapy for Urogenital Mycoplasma genitalium Infection in Nanjing, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of doxycycline-sitafloxacin sequential therapy for urogenital Mycoplasma genitalium infections in Nanjing, China, and identified several mutations in the 23S rRNA, parC, gyrA, and gyrB genes associated with macrolide and fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sequencing of PCR-amplified genes to detect mutations in 23S rRNA, parC, gyrA, and gyrB genes in Mycoplasma genitalium isolates.

full_output.methodology: Cryo-EM, ATPase activity assays, and bacterial complementation experiments were used to analyze the structure and function of the DppABCDF transporter.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various beta-lactamase genes, vancomycin resistance cassettes, and methicillin resistance cassettes in rectal swab metagenomes, highlighting the dynamic nature of the resistome and the potential for horizontal gene transfer.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in rectal swabs.

full_output.paper_title: Zinc-Doped Antibacterial Coating as a Single Approach to Unlock Multifunctional and Highly Resistant Titanium Implant Surfaces.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed zinc-doped coatings on titanium implants via plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO), demonstrating enhanced antimicrobial efficacy against Streptococcus sanguinis and Escherichia coli, along with improved mechanical and corrosion resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the development and characterization of zinc-doped titanium implant coatings using PEO, followed by extensive testing of their mechanical, electrochemical, and antimicrobial properties.

full_output.paper_title: South African Propolis: Anti-Helicobacter pylori Activity, Chemistry, and Toxicity.
full_output.key_findings: South African propolis exhibited significant anti-Helicobacter pylori activity, with certain compounds like pinocembrin, 3-O-acetylpinobanksin, and pinobanksin showing high antimicrobial effectiveness. The propolis extracts were found to be non-toxic.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial broth microdilution assay, UPLC-MS chemical analysis, and brine shrimp lethality assay for toxicity evaluation.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating the Performance of Two Rapid Immunochromatographic Techniques for Detecting Carbapenemase in Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales Clinical Isolates.
