full_output.key_findings: The study identified a novel bla KPC gene, bla KPC-145, which contains a point mutation (A to G) at nucleotide position 787, resulting in the amino acid substitution of threonine to alanine (T263A). This variant was accurately detected by the K-Set but not by Carba 5.
full_output.methodology: PCR, whole genome sequencing, and immunochromatographic assays were used to detect and characterize carbapenemase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Potassium-Doped MnO(2) Nanoparticles Reprogram Neutrophil Calcium Signaling to Accelerate Healing of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus-Infected Diabetic Wounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes involved in neutrophil responses to MRSA infection, including Cxcl1, Cxcl5, PAD4, H3-cit, and various calcium channel-related genes, which are modulated by K-MnO2 nanoparticles to improve neutrophil function and wound healing.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, immunofluorescence, and in vivo experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Esc peptides and derivatives potentiate the activity of CFTR with gating defects and display antipseudomonal activity in cystic fibrosis-like lung disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Esc peptides and their derivatives as effective potentiators of CFTR with gating defects and demonstrates their antipseudomonal activity in a cystic fibrosis-like lung disease model.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized electrophysiology experiments, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vivo studies on mouse models to evaluate the effects of Esc peptides on CFTR function and antibacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: The efflux pump SugE2 involved in protection of Salmonella 4,[5],12:i:- against quaternary ammonium salts and inhibition of virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SugE1 and SugE2 efflux pumps as essential for Salmonella 4,[5],12:i:- resistance to quaternary ammonium compounds (DDAB). Both genes contribute to resistance, with SugE2 additionally affecting virulence by modulating SPI-1 expression.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, transcriptome analysis, MIC determination, gene deletion, and complementation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Directed Evolution of a Macrolide-Sensing Transcription Factor Biosensor for the Detection of Macrolactone Aglycones via "Effector Walking" and Efflux Pump Deletion.

MphR.notes: Mutations S106F and N94D were identified through directed evolution to broaden the effector specificity of MphR.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the engineering of the MphR transcription factor biosensor to detect macrolide aglycones through directed evolution and efflux pump deletion, resulting in the identification of mutations S106F and N94D that enhance sensitivity to 6-dEB and EB.
full_output.methodology: Directed evolution, site-directed mutagenesis, and fluorescence-based biosensor assays were used to engineer and validate the MphR biosensor.

full_output.paper_title: Baohuoside I targets SaeR as an antivirulence strategy to disrupt MRSA biofilm formation and pathogenicity.

saeR.validation_method: virtual screening, thermal shift assay, EMSA, CETSA, fluorescence quenching, SPR, molecular docking

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic analysis of the faecal microbiota and AMR in roe deer in Western Pomerania.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the faecal microbiome and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in roe deer from Western Pomerania, identifying resistance genes such as MLS23S, A16S, rrsC, rrsH, and rrsA, primarily associated with macrolide, lincosamide, streptogramin, and aminoglycoside resistance.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis of faecal samples from 27 roe deer.

full_output.paper_title: Adoption of an in-silico analysis approach to assess the functional and structural impacts of rpoB-encoded protein mutations on Chlamydia pneumoniae sensitivity to antibiotics.

rpoB.notes: All mutations were identified in previous studies and analyzed in-silico.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified eight mutations in the rpoB gene of Chlamydia pneumoniae that are associated with resistance to rifampin and rifalazil. These mutations affect the structure and function of the beta subunit of RNA polymerase, reducing the effectiveness of these antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: In-silico analysis using bioinformatics tools to predict the functional and structural impacts of rpoB mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Blocking copper transporter protein-dependent drug efflux with albumin-encapsulated Pt(IV) for synergistically enhanced chemo-immunotherapy.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ATP7B as a gene involved in platinum resistance in NSCLC, demonstrating that its high expression correlates with resistance to platinum drugs. It also shows that TM can down-regulate ATP7B expression, enhancing platinum accumulation and inducing oxidative stress in tumor cells.
full_output.methodology: Protein blotting, flow cytometry, and immunofluorescence were used to analyze ATP7B expression and its correlation with platinum resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular and genetic features of a bla(NDM-1) and bla(SHV-12) coharboring hypermucoviscous Klebsiella pneumoniae of serotype K2 and ST65.

blaNDM-1.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and conjugation experiments

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of bla(NDM-1) and bla(SHV-12) genes in a hypermucoviscous Klebsiella pneumoniae strain (KP114) of serotype K2 and ST65, which confers resistance to multiple antibiotics, including carbapenems.

full_output.paper_title: Global molecular epidemiology of the incomplete CirA protein related to cefiderocol resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae: a genome-based study.

cirA.mechanism: incomplete protein leading to reduced susceptibility to cefiderocol
cirA.validation_method: genomic analysis and detection of incomplete CirA variants

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug resistance in group B Streptococcus causing urinary tract infection exposes an erythromycin-driven protective effect against oxidative stress.

erm(B).validation_method: detection of resistance mechanism in strain 807

mef(I).validation_method: detection of resistance mechanism in strain 807

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug resistance in group B Streptococcus (GBS) isolates from urinary tract infections, with high resistance rates to azithromycin, clindamycin, erythromycin, and tetracycline. It also found that erythromycin exposure partially counteracted the growth inhibitory effect of hydrogen peroxide in multidrug-resistant GBS strains.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method and in vitro growth assays to evaluate the effect of erythromycin on GBS resistance to oxidative stress.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of temperature on the activity of efflux pumps in selected species of human opportunistic bacterial pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that elevated temperatures (43°C) and cold temperatures (7°C) significantly affect the activity of efflux pumps in Acinetobacter junii, Bacillus cereus, and Enterobacter cloacae, reducing their ability to expel ethidium bromide and thereby affecting antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized the agar-ethidium bromide cartwheel method to assess efflux pump activity and disc diffusion assays to evaluate meropenem resistance in bacterial isolates under varying temperatures.

full_output.paper_title: Screening for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE)-considering the practical implications of molecular results, the value of culture and deciding criteria for resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes carbapenemase genes (OXA-48, NDM, KPC, IMP, VIM) detected in CPE screening, highlighting their prevalence and correlation with culture results.
full_output.methodology: PCR and culture-based screening for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and phylogenetic analysis of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae ST23 in Ireland.

blaOXA-48.validation_method: Genomic analysis using ABRicate and Kleborate

blaOXA-181.validation_method: Genomic analysis using ABRicate and Kleborate

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes, including bla OXA-48, bla OXA-181, and bla NDM-1, which confer resistance to carbapenems in hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae ST23 isolates in Ireland. Additionally, quinolone efflux pumps oqxA5 and oqxB12, and fosfomycin resistance gene fosA6 were characterized.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis using Kleborate, ABRicate, and Platon, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Aetiology, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns and factors associated with bacteriuria among HIV-infected women attending Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission (PMTCT) clinic at Bukoba Municipality, Tanzania.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of bacteriuria among HIV-infected women, with Escherichia coli being the most common pathogen. High resistance rates were observed against trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, and penicillin, while lower resistance was noted against nitrofurantoin. Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) producers and multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains were prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving urine culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: A plant peptide with dual activity against multidrug-resistant bacterial and fungal pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NCBP1, a plant-derived noncanonical antibacterial peptide with broad-spectrum activity against multidrug-resistant bacteria and fungi. NCBP1 targets bacterial membranes, causing membrane damage and dysfunction, and shows promise as a novel antimicrobial agent.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar diffusion assays, broth microdilution methods, and molecular techniques to evaluate the antibacterial and antifungal activities of NCBP1.

full_output.paper_title: Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam cocktail for the treatment of VIM-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections: good enough to have another?

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in VIM-producing P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors for drug-resistant pathogens in community-acquired pneumonia: systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: This study identified 11 significant risk factors for drug-resistant pathogens (DRPs) in patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), including prior DRP infection/colonisation, tracheostomy, severe respiratory failure requiring early induction of mechanical ventilation, prior use of antibiotics, chronic lung disease, COPD, wound care, neurological disorders, prior hospitalisation, nursing home residence, and low activities of daily living.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of risk factors for DRPs in CAP patients.

full_output.paper_title: Establishment of a Multilocus Sequence Typing Scheme for Pasteurella canis Using Isolates from Infected Humans and Diseased Companion Animals.
full_output.key_findings: The study established a multilocus sequence typing (MLST) scheme for Pasteurella canis using isolates from infected humans and diseased companion animals in Japan and Korea. Seven housekeeping genes (adk, aroA, deoD, gdhA, g6pd, mdh, and pgi) were selected for MLST, and the genetic diversity of the isolates was analyzed.
full_output.methodology: The study used whole-genome sequencing and PCR-based methods to analyze the genetic diversity of P. canis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of the in vitro antimicrobial activity of eravacycline alone and in combination with various antibiotics against MDR Acinetobacter baumanni strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the in vitro antimicrobial activity of eravacycline against MDR Acinetobacter baumannii strains, highlighting its potential to prevent the emergence of resistant mutants and its effectiveness in inhibiting biofilm formation when used alone or in combination with other antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Metronidazole response profiles of Gardnerella species are congruent with phylogenetic and comparative genomic analyses.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified eleven distinct genospecies of Gardnerella vaginalis and found that the aruH gene is diagnostic for strains with high metronidazole resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the Antibiotic and Copper Resistance of Emergent Species of Onion-Pathogenic Burkholderia Through Genome Sequence Analysis and High-Throughput Sequencing of Differentially Enriched Random Transposon Mutants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified genes involved in DNA integration, recombination, and cation transport as important for the survival of B. cenocepacia CCRMBC56 in copper-stressed conditions. It also found that mutations in genes related to the oxidative stress response, cation transport, ABC transporter, and the cell outer membrane are detrimental to the bacteria under copper stress, whereas mutations in genes involved in the TCA cycle, penicillin binding, and FAD binding are beneficial.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and transposon mutagenesis followed by high-throughput sequencing to identify essential genes for copper resistance in B. cenocepacia CCRMBC56.

full_output.paper_title: Susceptibility to Postbiotic Substances-Enterocins of the Strains Enterococcus thailandicus from Beavers (Castor fiber).
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the susceptibility of Enterococcus thailandicus strains from beavers to postbiotic substances called enterocins, which showed high inhibitory activity against the strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA gene sequencing for species identification and tested the susceptibility of E. thailandicus strains to various enterocins using the agar spot method.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Diversity, Virulome, and Resistome of Streptococcus agalactiae in Northeastern Brazil: Are Multi-Host Adapted Strains Rising?

ant(6)-Ia.genetic_context: ant(6)-Ia gene is part of the resistance genes detected in the genome of S. agalactiae isolates
ant(6)-Ia.evidence_note: The ant(6)-Ia gene was detected in the genome of S. agalactiae isolates, indicating its presence and potential role in conferring resistance to aminoglycosides.

tetM.genetic_context: tetM gene is part of the transposon Tn916
tetM.evidence_note: tetM gene was detected in 14 isolates and is associated with tetracycline resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in S. agalactiae isolates from northeastern Brazil, including resistance to tetracycline, macrolides, lincosamides, and chloramphenicol. Key genes include tetM, ermB, mefA, and lnuB.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and analysis of 14 S. agalactiae isolates, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry discriminates drug-susceptible and -resistant strains in Mycobacterium abscessus.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry can discriminate between drug-susceptible and -resistant strains of Mycobacterium abscessus, identifying potential biomarkers at specific mass peaks for amikacin, linezolid, clarithromycin, and cefoxitin.
full_output.methodology: The study used MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry combined with machine learning algorithms to analyze protein profiles of M. abscessus isolates and identify biomarkers for drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of gram-negative bacteria contaminating the hands of patients' visitors at regional referral hospitals in Dar-es-Salaam.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Klebsiella pneumoniae was the most prevalent gram-negative bacterium on the hands of patients' visitors, with high levels of resistance to several antibiotics, including cephalosporins, ampicillin, and ciprofloxacin. The prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria was 36.3% in sample A and 30.9% in sample B.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving bacterial culture, identification using VITEK MS, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: A thiouracil desulfurase protects Clostridioides difficile RNA from 4-thiouracil incorporation, providing a competitive advantage in the gut.

tudS.mechanism: converts 4-thiouracil (4-TU) to uracil, preventing its incorporation into RNA
tudS.validation_method: mutant strain analysis, heterologous expression in E. coli, growth assays

pyrR.mechanism: mutations in pyrR confer resistance to 4-TU by increasing de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis and decreasing s 4 UMP production

upp.notes: mutations in upp confer resistance to 4-TU by preventing its incorporation into RNA

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TudS, a thiouracil desulfurase, as a key enzyme that allows Clostridioides difficile to utilize 4-thiouracil (4-TU) as a pyrimidine source, preventing its incorporation into RNA and providing a competitive advantage in the gut. Mutations in upp and pyrR were found to confer resistance to 4-TU by altering nucleotide metabolism.
full_output.methodology: Genetic selection, mutant strain analysis, heterologous expression, growth assays, HPLC, SLAM-seq, and transcript analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Inosine monophosphate overcomes the coexisting resistance of mcr-1 and bla(NDM-1) in Escherichia coli.

mcr-1.mechanism: confers resistance to colistin by modifying the lipid A component of the outer membrane
mcr-1.evidence_note: The paper states that mcr-1 encodes a phosphoethanolamine transferase that modifies the lipid A component of the outer membrane, thereby conferring resistance to colistin.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that inosine monophosphate (IMP) effectively combats the resistance conferred by mcr-1 and bla(NDM-1) in Escherichia coli, demonstrating potent bactericidal activity and a low risk of resistance development.
full_output.methodology: Metabolomic profiling, time-killing assays, and in vivo mouse infection models were used to evaluate the antibacterial effects of IMP against E. coli strains carrying mcr-1 and bla(NDM-1).

full_output.paper_title: Chlorpromazine inhibits the plasmid-mediated oqxAB multidrug efflux pump in Escherichia coli isolates of Egyptian patients with utis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the oqxA and oqxB genes as plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance determinants in E. coli isolates from Egyptian patients with UTIs. Chlorpromazine was shown to inhibit the efflux pump activity, reducing levofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, conjugation experiments, and MIC determination were used to characterize the oqxA and oqxB genes and their role in quinolone resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of Sub-Inhibitory Concentrations of Quaternary Ammonium Compounds and Heavy Metals on Antibiotic Resistance and Expression of Virulence Factors Among Staphylococcus spp. from Dairy Products.
full_output.key_findings: Sub-inhibitory concentrations of benzalkonium chloride and cadmium chloride induce the overexpression of antibiotic resistance genes such as bla Z, erm B, mec A, tet K, and tet M in Staphylococcus isolates from dairy products, leading to increased antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Real-Time PCR and MIC determination to assess gene expression and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of the Technical Snow Production Process on Bacterial Community Composition, Antibacterial Resistance Genes, and Antibiotic Input-A Dual Effect of the Inevitable.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in water and snow samples from ski resorts, including blaTEM, blaCTX-M, mecA, ereA, ermB, strA, tetK, and sulIII. These genes were associated with resistance to beta-lactams, macrolides, aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, and sulfonamides. The presence of these ARGs highlights the potential environmental impact of technical snow production on antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR tests to detect antibiotic resistance genes in water and snow samples from five ski resorts.

full_output.paper_title: Seeking Correlation Among Porin Permeabilities and Minimum Inhibitory Concentrations Through Machine Learning: A Promising Route to the Essential Molecular Descriptors.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the relationship between antibiotic permeability through the OmpF porin of E. coli and antimicrobial efficacy, utilizing machine learning to correlate permeability coefficients (RPC) with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized liposome swelling assays to measure relative permeability coefficients (RPC) and determined MIC values for 38 antibiotics. Machine learning models were developed to correlate RPC with MIC values.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, Chemical Characterization, and Antimicrobial Activity of Secondary Metabolites from Pseudocyphellaria faveolata.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified physciosporin and methyl virensate as secondary metabolites from Pseudocyphellaria faveolata with antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, showing inhibition of bacterial proliferation and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were isolated using column chromatography and characterized by NMR spectroscopy. Antimicrobial activity was assessed using broth microdilution and crystal violet staining.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating Antibiotic Resistance in Pediatric UTIs: Five-Year Data from a Tertiary Hospital in Turkey.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies high resistance rates to ampicillin and TMP-SMX in pediatric UTI pathogens, with E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Proteus mirabilis showing significant resistance. Amikacin, nitrofurantoin, and carbapenems remained effective against these pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 2753 pediatric UTI cases with positive urine cultures, including antibiotic resistance pattern evaluation.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial-Resistance and Virulence-Associated Genes of Pasteurella multocida and Mannheimia haemolytica Isolated from Polish Dairy Calves with Symptoms of Bovine Respiratory Disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance and virulence-associated genes in Pasteurella multocida and Mannheimia haemolytica isolates from Polish dairy calves with bovine respiratory disease. Key resistance genes included tetH and tetR for tetracycline resistance, and mphE and msrE for macrolide resistance. Virulence genes such as sodA, hgbB, ompH, lkt, gs60, and gcp were also detected.
full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular detection techniques were used to identify antimicrobial resistance and virulence-associated genes in bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology and Antibiotic Resistance Associated with Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli in Shanxi Province, China, from 2021 to 2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in APEC strains, including tetA, bla-TEM, cat1, floR, strA, aphA, sul1, sul2, and mcr1, which conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as tetracycline, beta-lactams, chloramphenicol, florfenicol, streptomycin, kanamycin, sulfamethoxazole, and colistin.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of AMR genes and virulence genes in APEC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanisms of Salmonella typhimurium Resistance to Cannabidiol.

blaTEM-1.validation_method: highly expressed gene in CBD-resistant S. typhimurium strain
blaTEM-1.evidence_note: The paper states that blaTEM-1 is highly expressed in the CBD-resistant S. typhimurium strain and is known to exhibit resistance to penicillin and cephalosporins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM, fimA, fimZ, STM0959, STM0716, and spy genes as key contributors to Salmonella typhimurium resistance to cannabidiol (CBD).
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR analysis was used to evaluate gene expression in CBD-resistant and CBD-susceptible S. typhimurium strains.

full_output.paper_title: Phyllanthus emblica: Phytochemistry, Antimicrobial Potential with Antibiotic Enhancement, and Toxicity Insights.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of Phyllanthus emblica fruit extracts against both antibiotic-susceptible and resistant bacterial pathogens, demonstrating that the extracts exhibit antibacterial activity against S. aureus and MRSA, with some extracts showing notable activity against K. pneumoniae. The extracts also showed additive interactions with conventional antibiotics, suggesting potential for enhancing antibiotic efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study used disc diffusion and broth microdilution assays to assess the antibacterial activity of P. emblica fruit extracts, along with LC-MS analysis for phytochemical profiling and Artemia franciscana nauplii lethality assays for toxicity evaluation.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the global dissemination and evolution of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial pathogens, emphasizing the role of various AMR genes such as blaTEM, sul2, aph(6)-Id, aph(3'')-Ib, mcr-3.16, mcr-3.3, blaCTX-M-15, blaCTX-M-55, mph(A), qnrS1, blaCTX-M-14, blaCTX-M-65, blaKPC-2, blaNDM-1, blaNDM-5, blaOXA-48, and mcr-1 in conferring resistance to different antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and surveillance studies were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in various bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing E. coli from Czech diary calves and their caretakers.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-14, bla CTX-M-1, bla TEM-1b, qnrS1, and mcr-1 as the primary AMR genes in cefotaxime-resistant E. coli isolates from Czech dairy calves and their caretakers.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and disc diffusion tests were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Dynamics of Antimicrobial Susceptibility and Risk Factors Associated with Infections Caused by Colistin-Resistant Bacteria: A Study from the Northern Region of Haryana, India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1 to mcr-5 genes as potential contributors to colistin resistance in Gram-negative bacteria, although none of the colistin-resistant isolates harbored these genes. The study highlights the importance of monitoring colistin resistance and identifying risk factors associated with its development.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized multiplex PCR to screen for mcr-1 to mcr-5 genes in colistin-resistant isolates and broth microdilution to determine colistin MICs.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of OXA232-Producing Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae: Genomic Analysis and Virulence Assessment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the blaOXA-232 gene as a key determinant of carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, specifically in ST231 and ST11 strains. The gene was consistently located on a non-conjugative ColKP3 plasmid and was associated with multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the resistance and virulence profiles of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Green Synthesis of Silver Nanoparticles from Kefir Fractions and Their Antimicrobial Activity
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) from kefir fractions and evaluates their antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant bacteria. WSF-AgNPs showed effective inhibition of A. baumannii and K. pneumoniae at low concentrations, while < 10 kDa-AgNPs exhibited inconsistent antibacterial effects.
full_output.methodology: The study used green synthesis methods, DLS, SEM, FT-IR, and in vitro susceptibility tests to characterize and evaluate the antimicrobial activity of AgNPs.

full_output.paper_title: Conserved marseilleviruses harboring diverse antibiotic resistance genes isolated from the Yangtze river Delta and the Pearl river delta, China.

These genes show structural and functional similarities to bacterial SMR, DHFR, and RPP, suggesting potential roles in viral interactions with antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, protein structure prediction, and in-silico tertiary structure analysis were used to characterize the antibiotic resistance genes in marseilleviruses.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial properties of a nasal solution containing oxymetazoline (NS-OXY) and benzalkonium chloride (BKC) against Rothia dentocariosa, a bacterium associated with dental caries. NS-OXY and BKC showed significant antimicrobial activity, with NS-OXY demonstrating biocompatibility with dental pulp stem cells at certain dilutions.
full_output.methodology: The study used disc diffusion and broth inhibition assays to evaluate the antimicrobial effects of NS-OXY, BKC, and other agents against Rothia dentocariosa. Biomass quantification and biocompatibility assessments were also conducted.

full_output.paper_title: A Snapshot of Antimicrobial Resistance in Semi-Wild Oryx: Baseline Data from Qatar.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes tetA and tetB, as well as bla CTX-M and bla TEM-1 for beta-lactam resistance in E. coli isolates from semi-wild oryx in Qatar. Whole genome sequencing revealed additional resistance mechanisms, including mutations in soxR associated with tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing, PCR analysis, and whole genome sequencing using Oxford Nanopore Technology were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance and Mortality in ICU Patients: A Retrospective Analysis of First Culture Growth Results.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens such as Acinetobacter baumannii, MRSA, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Klebsiella pneumoniae as major contributors to increased ICU mortality and prolonged ICU stays. Carbapenem, cephalosporin, fluoroquinolone, and aminoglycoside resistance were significantly associated with adverse clinical outcomes.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of initial culture growth results from ICU patients, including microbial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing according to CLSI and EUCAST guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: In-depth characterization of Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC)-encoding plasmids points at transposon-related transmission of resistance genes.

blaKPC-3.validation_method: long-read whole genome sequencing and PCR

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a blaKPC-3 gene encoded on an IncF plasmid in K. pneumoniae isolates, highlighting the role of transposons in the transmission of carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Long-read whole genome sequencing, PCR, and bioinformatic analysis were used to characterize the resistance genes and plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: Quantitative performance of humanized plasma and epithelial lining fluid exposures of meropenem, cefiderocol and tobramycin against a challenge set of Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a standardized neutropenic murine pneumonia model.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various AMR genes and mutations in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, focusing on their resistance to meropenem, cefiderocol, and tobramycin. Key findings include the identification of several aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, beta-lactamases, and other resistance mechanisms contributing to multidrug resistance in these isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study employed in vivo efficacy studies in a neutropenic murine pneumonia model, along with MIC testing and genotypic profiling of bacterial isolates.
full_output.sample_size: The study involved multiple isolates from different sources, including the CDC Bank, Paul Ehrlich Institute, and Leibniz Institute.

full_output.paper_title: Immobilization of KR-12 on a Titanium Alloy Surface Using Linking Arms Improves Antimicrobial Activity and Supports Osteoblast Cytocompatibility.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that immobilizing KR-12 on titanium surfaces using HELP linkers enhances antimicrobial activity against multiple bacterial strains, including Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, while maintaining osteoblast cytocompatibility.
full_output.methodology: Surface modification techniques, antimicrobial activity assays, and cell viability assessments were used to evaluate the performance of KR-12 immobilized on titanium surfaces.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-Informed Clustering of Chemical Perturbations Reveals Insights Into Inhibitor Function
full_output.key_findings: The study identified lptA and lpxC as essential genes involved in chemical susceptibility and resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, with lptA knockdown increasing sensitivity to antibiotics like tigecycline and azithromycin, and lpxC knockdown affecting colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR interference screening combined with chemical genomics and MIC assays to evaluate gene function and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro and in silico pharmacological effects of Rosmarinus officinalis leaf methanolic extracts and essential oils.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial, antioxidant, antidiabetic, and anticancer properties of Rosmarinus officinalis leaf essential oil (ROLEO) and methanolic extract (ROLME). ROLEO showed higher antioxidant activity, better antidiabetic potential, and stronger antibacterial effects against Gram-positive bacteria compared to ROLME. Molecular docking identified key compounds in ROLEO that interact with α-amylase, caspase-3, and E. coli gyrase B.
full_output.methodology: The study used GC-MS for chemical profiling, DPPH and ABTS assays for antioxidant activity, MTT assay for cytotoxicity, and molecular docking for evaluating interactions with target proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and genomic characteristics of Campylobacter spp. From Australian meat chickens with A follow up investigation.

full_output.paper_title: Efflux pump modulation by Montelukast and its roles in restoring antibiotic susceptibility in multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

mgrA.encodes: global regulator that regulates efflux pumps in S. aureus
mgrA.mechanism: regulates the expression of efflux pumps such as NorA, NorB, Tet38, and AbcA
mgrA.validation_method: expression and purification of MgrA, EMSA analysis, and interaction studies with Montelukast

norB.validation_method: EtBr accumulation assay, gene expression analysis, and synergy assay with Montelukast

full_output.key_findings: Montelukast was identified as an efflux pump inhibitor that enhances the effectiveness of moxifloxacin against multidrug-resistant S. aureus by modulating MgrA activity and reducing norB expression.
full_output.methodology: Ethidium bromide accumulation assay, gene expression analysis, synergy assays, and molecular interaction studies.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitory effect of paeoniflorin on the LuxS/AI-2 quorum sensing system and the virulence of Glaesserella parasuis.
full_output.key_findings: Paeoniflorin (PF) inhibits the LuxS/AI-2 quorum sensing system and reduces the virulence of Glaesserella parasuis. PF shows synergistic effects with lincomycin against G. parasuis strains, enhancing therapeutic outcomes.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm inhibition assays, AI-2 activity assays, and RT-qPCR were used to assess the effects of PF on G. parasuis.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of pilus islets and association with clonal complex in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolated from children in Suzhou, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 63.6% of S. pneumoniae isolates expressed at least one type of pilus islet (PI), with PI-1 being more prevalent than PI-2. Piliated isolates showed higher resistance to several antibiotics compared to non-piliated isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR assays were used to detect PI-1 and PI-2 genes, and antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the E-test method.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-center evaluation of the Selux next-generation phenotyping system for gram-negative direct-from-positive blood culture antimicrobial susceptibility testing.
full_output.key_findings: The Selux next-generation phenotyping system demonstrated effective antimicrobial susceptibility testing directly from positive blood culture samples for gram-negative bacteria, showing high concordance with reference methods and consistent performance across various laboratory settings.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the Selux system's performance using clinical and seeded samples, comparing results with reference broth microdilution methods.
full_output.sample_size: 162 fresh clinical positive blood culture samples, 307 seeded clinical samples, and 87 seeded challenge samples

full_output.paper_title: Infection model of THP-1 cells, growth dynamics, and antimicrobial susceptibility of clinical Mycobacterium abscessus isolates from cystic fibrosis patients: Results from a multicentre study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified resistance mechanisms in Mycobacterium abscessus isolates from cystic fibrosis patients, including inducible resistance to clarithromycin mediated by erm(41) mutations, acquired resistance to clarithromycin via rrl gene mutations, and amikacin resistance associated with rrs gene mutations.
full_output.methodology: Genotypic and phenotypic susceptibility testing, along with molecular analysis of resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Photodynamic Inactivation of Staphylococcus aureus and Biomolecules by Free and Encapsulated Indium(III) Phthalocyanines in PHB Nanoparticles: The Influence of the Position of the Coumarin Group.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the photodynamic inactivation of methicillin-resistant and methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus using indium(III) phthalocyanines substituted with coumarin groups, both in free and encapsulated forms in polyhydroxybutyrate nanoparticles. The results showed that 4nInOAc demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing bacterial colonies.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized photodynamic therapy with phthalocyanine derivatives, assessing their photodynamic activity through photooxidation of biomolecules and antimicrobial efficacy against S. aureus strains.

full_output.paper_title: Luteolin loaded PEGylated cerosomes: a novel treatment for MRSA skin infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates luteolin-loaded PEGylated cerosomes (F5) as a novel treatment for MRSA skin infections, demonstrating improved antibacterial activity and reduced biofilm formation compared to luteolin suspension.
full_output.methodology: The study involved formulation and evaluation of luteolin-loaded PEGylated cerosomes, in vitro release studies, MIC and MBC determination, biofilm inhibition assays, and in vivo murine skin infection models.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro susceptibility of 313 clinical Clostridioides difficile isolates to metronidazole, vancomycin, fidaxomicin, ridinilazole, and ibezapolstat, finding low resistance rates to metronidazole (2.2%) and vancomycin (1.6%), with 7.35% of isolates showing resistance to fidaxomicin. Ridinilazole and ibezapolstat demonstrated potent activity against the isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using Etest and agar dilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Morphological variability of Escherichia coli colonizing human wounds: a case report.

full_output.paper_title: Unraveling the genomic epidemiology and plasmid-mediated carbapenem resistance of Klebsiella pasteurii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the carbapenem resistance gene blaKPC-2 in a Klebsiella pasteurii strain, K1134, which was resistant to meropenem and imipenem. The gene was found on a plasmid pK1134-KPC belonging to the IncFII pCP020359 group.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR assays, and comparative genomic analysis were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes and plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: Pandemic human-associated extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli lineages of ST38, ST131 and ST141 identified in Viennese dogs.

tet(A).evidence_note: tetracycline resistance gene detected in ESBL E. coli isolates

dfrA14.evidence_note: dfrA14 was identified as a resistance gene in the whole genome sequencing analysis.

qnrS1.evidence_note: qnrS1 was identified as an antimicrobial resistance gene in the whole genome sequencing analysis.

mph(A).evidence_note: The gene mph(A) was identified in the whole genome sequencing of ESBL E. coli isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified ESBL-producing E. coli in Viennese dogs carrying multiple AMR genes, including bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-15, bla TEM-1B, tet(A), dfrA14, qnrS1, mph(A), and aadA5, indicating a high prevalence of multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatic analyses were used to identify AMR genes and determine the genetic characteristics of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Novel mutations in the marR gene (MAB_2648c) modify nitroxoline activity in Mycobacterium abscessus.

marR.notes: Mutations in marR are associated with reduced nitroxoline susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel mutations in the marR gene (MAB_2648c) that modify nitroxoline activity in Mycobacterium abscessus. These mutations, including a 34-bp deletion and a point mutation, are associated with reduced nitroxoline susceptibility. Complementation of the mutants with the wild-type marR gene restored the MIC values to those of the wild-type strain, confirming the role of marR mutations in modifying nitroxoline activity.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, and gene complementation experiments were conducted to identify and validate the mutations in the marR gene.

full_output.paper_title: UBR-1 deficiency leads to ivermectin resistance in Caenorhabditis elegans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies UBR-1 as a key regulator of IVM resistance in C. elegans, demonstrating that its dysfunction leads to altered glutamate metabolism and reduced IVM sensitivity. Ceftriaxone was shown to restore IVM sensitivity by reducing glutamate levels.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic mutants, transgenic lines, and pharmacological interventions to investigate the role of UBR-1 in IVM resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Toward a Bactericidal Oral Drug Combination for the Treatment of Mycobacterium abscessus Lung Disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a triple-drug combination of tebipenem (TBP) with avibactam (TBP-A), moxifloxacin (MXF), and rifabutin (RFB) as highly effective against Mycobacterium abscessus, demonstrating strong bactericidal activity against both replicating and nonreplicating forms of the bacterium. The combination shows potentiation of bactericidal effects, reduces the emergence of resistant mutants, and retains activity in a caseum-like environment.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro and in vivo experiments, including time-concentration kill kinetics, checkerboard analyses, and assessment of bactericidal activity, metabolic responses, and postantibiotic effects.

full_output.paper_title: Factors associated with clinical antimicrobial resistance in China: a nationwide analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various factors associated with clinical antimicrobial resistance in China, highlighting the significant impact of human and veterinary antibiotic usage, environmental pollutants like PM 2.5, and socioeconomic factors on the rise of AMR.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a beta regression model to analyze the relationship between antimicrobial resistance and multiple variables, incorporating data from the China Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance System and other environmental and socioeconomic datasets.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli from Swedish piglets with diarrhoea and associations with potential risk factors.

Trimethoprim-sulphonamide resistance was associated with the proportion of sows receiving post-farrowing antibiotic treatments.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed E. coli isolates from clinical submissions and study samples, performing antimicrobial susceptibility testing and statistical analyses to identify risk factors for antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of bloodstream infections in the emergency department, highlighting the dominance of Gram-negative bacteria such as Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, along with their low resistance rates to carbapenems, piperacillin-tazobactam, and amikacin. It also noted the low resistance rates of Gram-positive bacteria to glycopeptides.

full_output.paper_title: A small regulatory RNA controls antibiotic adaptation in Staphylococcus aureus by modulating efflux pump expression.

full_output.methodology: Fitness competition assays, spot tests, growth curve analysis, northern blotting, and complementation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Potential of saccharomyces cerevisiae fermentation-derived postbiotic technology in mitigating multiple drug-resistant Salmonella enterica serovars in an in vitro broiler cecal model.

The findings suggest that SCFP can enhance microbial diversity and reduce Salmonella abundance, highlighting the importance of niche-specific interactions in intervention strategies.
full_output.methodology: The study used an in vitro poultry cecal model to assess the effect of SCFP on MDR Salmonella serovars, involving enumeration of Salmonella counts and microbiome analysis through 16S rRNA sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptional response study of auto inducer-2 regulatory system in Escherichia coli harboring bla(NDM).

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus at human-animal interfaces on Chongming Island, Shanghai: A One Health perspective.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high levels of antimicrobial resistance in clinical and food animal isolates of E. coli and S. aureus on Chongming Island, with particular emphasis on extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing E. coli and methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) was conducted using minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values, with data analyzed to determine resistance rates and multidrug resistance (MDR) profiles.
full_output.sample_size: 2625 clinical E. coli isolates and 994 clinical S. aureus isolates

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae infections in Chinese children: in vitro activities of ceftazidime-avibactam and aztreonam-avibactam against carbapenemase-producing strains in a two-center study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla NDM-5, bla NDM-1, and bla KPC-2 as the predominant carbapenemase genes in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) isolates from Chinese children. These genes were associated with varying levels of resistance to antibiotics, with NDM-KP showing lower resistance to certain antibiotics compared to KPC-KP.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect carbapenemase genes, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using broth microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa population dynamics in a vancomycin-induced murine model of gastrointestinal carriage.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a murine model of Pseudomonas aeruginosa gastrointestinal carriage using vancomycin pretreatment, demonstrating that the stomach acts as a major barrier to carriage, with most bacteria eliminated within 6 hours. The small intestine and cecum supported high bacterial replication, leading to long-term carriage.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a vancomycin-treated mouse model, barcoded P. aeruginosa libraries, and STAMPR analysis to track bacterial population dynamics during gastrointestinal carriage.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical characteristics and genomic epidemiological survey of tuberculosis in Wuzhou, China, 2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various drug resistance mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Wuzhou, China, including mutations in katG, fabG1, rpoB, embA, embB, pncA, rpsL, rrs, gyrA, inhA, thyA, and others, contributing to resistance against isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, streptomycin, fluoroquinolones, ethionamide, and para-aminosalicylic acid.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing was used to analyze drug resistance profiles and lineage distribution of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Transformation of Gardnerella vaginalis with a Bifidobacterium-Escherichia coli shuttle vector plasmid.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the successful transformation of Gardnerella vaginalis ATCC 49145 with the Bifidobacterium-E. coli shuttle vector pKO403-lacZ'-Sp, which includes a spectinomycin resistance gene (spR) that increased the MIC of spectinomycin from 2 µg/mL to >512 µg/mL.
full_output.methodology: Electroporation and transformation of G. vaginalis with the pKO403-lacZ'-Sp plasmid, followed by MIC testing and plasmid copy number analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Recent emergence of cephalosporin-resistant Salmonella Typhi in India due to the endemic clone acquiring IncFIB(K) plasmid encoding bla (CTX-M-15) gene.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of a new clone of ceftriaxone-resistant Salmonella Typhi in India, which acquired an IncFIB(K) plasmid encoding the bla(CTX-M-15) gene, along with other resistance determinants such as qnrS1, sul2, dfrA14, tet(A), aph(3"), and aph(6').
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Current pattern of antibiotic resistance and molecular characterization of virulence genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae obtained from urinary tract infection (UTIs) patients, Peshawar.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of virulence genes fimH (80%), SAT (65%), papEF (49%), afa (29%), and VAT (16%) in multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from urinary tract infections in Peshawar.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and sequencing to characterize virulence genes in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Guts of healthy humans, livestock, and pets harbor critical-priority and high-risk Escherichia coli clones.

mcr-1.mechanism: modification of lipid A to confer colistin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla CTX-M, bla NDM, and mcr-1 as key resistance genes in Escherichia coli from healthy humans, livestock, and pets, highlighting the widespread presence of critical-priority and high-risk clones.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting E. coli resistance mechanisms against 3GC, CARB, and COL.

full_output.paper_title: The importance of monitoring a new antibiotic: ceftazidime/avibactam usage and resistance experience from England, 2016 to 2020.

blaKPC.validation_method: molecular detection of antimicrobial resistance mechanisms

blaOXA-48-like.validation_method: molecular detection of antimicrobial resistance mechanisms

blaNDM.validation_method: molecular detection of antimicrobial resistance mechanisms

blaIMP.validation_method: molecular detection of antimicrobial resistance mechanisms

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of ceftazidime/avibactam resistance in Enterobacterales in England, with nearly 90% of resistance cases associated with metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL) genes such as bla KPC, bla OXA-48-like, bla NDM, bla VIM, and bla IMP. These genes were experimentally validated as conferring resistance to ceftazidime/avibactam.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed ceftazidime/avibactam resistance data from routine surveillance and reference laboratory testing, including molecular detection of carbapenemase genes and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) determinations.

full_output.paper_title: Teicoplanin Nonribosomal Peptide Synthetase Is Unable to Incorporate Alpha-Ketoacid Building Blocks.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the substrate specificity of the teicoplanin NRPS A1 domain, revealing that it prefers ketoacid activation over amino acid activation, but only amino acids are loaded onto the PCP domain during thioesterification.
full_output.methodology: The study used NADH-coupled pyrophosphate release assays, in vitro reconstitution of NRPS modules, intact protein mass spectrometry, and molecular dynamics simulations to analyze the substrate specificity of the teicoplanin NRPS A1 domain.

full_output.paper_title: A dual-mechanism luminescent antibiotic for bacterial infection identification and eradication.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents TPA2PyBu, a novel dual-mechanism luminescent antibiotic that effectively targets both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including drug-resistant strains, with low resistance development. It operates by damaging bacterial membrane integrity and inducing DNA aggregation.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and evaluation of TPA2PyBu's antimicrobial activity, mechanism of action, and in vivo efficacy using various microbiological and imaging techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance in hospital wastewater in West Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes several antibiotic resistance genes in hospital wastewater in West Africa, including blaTEM, blaOXA-48, blaSHV, and mecA, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug-resistant bacteria and the importance of monitoring antibiotic resistance in environmental settings.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on antibiotic resistance in hospital wastewater in West Africa, utilizing PCR, sequencing, and statistical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of a novel SME-6 Carbapenemase in Serratia ureilytica in Germany.

blaSME-6.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel carbapenemase, SME-6, in a Serratia ureilytica isolate from Germany, which shows temperature-dependent resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and RT-qPCR were used to characterize the resistance mechanism.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant bacteria in drinking water from filtration plants in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, Pakistan, with a particular emphasis on beta-lactamase genes such as blaCTX-M, blaSHV, blaTEM, blaNDM, blaVIM, blaSPM, blaIPM, blaOXA-51, blaOXA-24, blaOXA-23, and blaOXA-58.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolation, identification using MALDI-TOF, and genotypic screening for beta-lactamase genes via PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Public health threat of antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes in Escherichia coli from human-chicken transmission in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of virulence genes papC, iss, and vgrG1 in E. coli isolates from both chickens and humans, highlighting the potential for zoonotic transmission and the public health risks associated with multidrug-resistant E. coli.
full_output.methodology: The study employed PCR for detection of virulence genes, antimicrobial susceptibility testing using disk diffusion, and phylogenetic analysis of the vgrG1 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance pattern of Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolate in Ethiopia. A systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: This study reveals high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Acinetobacter baumannii in Ethiopia, with significant resistance to various antibiotics, including carbapenems, cephalosporins, and aminoglycosides. The findings highlight the urgent need for improved antimicrobial stewardship and infection control measures.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 26 studies on antimicrobial resistance in A. baumannii clinical isolates from Ethiopia.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence genes and antibiotic resistance profiling of staphylococcus species isolated from mastitic dairy cows in and around Bahir dar, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple Staphylococcus species, including S. chromogenes, S. aureus, and S. hyicus, with high prevalence of virulence genes such as mecA, coa, icaD, and seb. All isolates showed resistance to penicillin, and many were multidrug-resistant.
full_output.methodology: PCR for virulence gene detection and disk diffusion for antimicrobial resistance profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of an outbreak of carbapenem resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in an intensive care unit during the COVID-19 epidemic.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) as the causative agent of an outbreak in an ICU during the COVID-19 epidemic. Whole genome sequencing revealed the presence of the intrinsic carbapenem resistance gene oxa-51 and bla genes, which conferred resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the CRAB isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Activity of imipenem/relebactam against KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae and the possible role of Ompk36 mutation in determining resistance: an Italian retrospective analysis.

full_output.key_findings: All IMI/REL-resistant KPC-Kp strains displayed a mutation in porin OmpK36, and the mutation p.Asp357fs was significantly correlated with resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and correlation analysis of mutations in ompK36 with resistance to IMI/REL.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the performance of various susceptibility testing methods for mecillinam against carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE), highlighting the importance of accurate methods for determining susceptibility in these resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study compared disc diffusion, Liofilchem MTS gradient strip, bioMérieux E-test, Sensititre broth microdilution, and VITEK 2 against agar dilution as the reference method for mecillinam susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: NDM-5-carried outer membrane vesicles impair the efficacy of antibiotics against bacterial infections.
full_output.key_findings: NDM-5-containing outer membrane vesicles (N-OMVs) were shown to degrade meropenem, protecting susceptible E. coli from antibiotic-induced death.
full_output.methodology: Extraction and characterization of OMVs, ELISA, proteomic analysis, HPLC, and in vivo infection model in Galleria mellonella.

full_output.paper_title: Colony morphotype variation in Burkholderia: implications for success of applications and therapeutics.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: loss of functional OmpR led to positive effects on CF lung epithelial adhesion, biofilm formation under high osmolarity, and motility. However, it had negative impacts on antibiotic sensitivity, osmotic stress tolerance, and virulence

ompR.notes: Mutation in ompR affects virulence and antibiotic sensitivity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the role of OmpR in colony morphotype variation (CMV) and its impact on virulence and antibiotic resistance in Burkholderia species, particularly in B. multivorans.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic analysis, mutagenesis, and sequencing were used to investigate the role of OmpR in CMV and its effects on virulence and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Combating Concomitant Bacterial and Fungal Infections via Codelivery of Nitric Oxide and Fluconazole.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel biomaterial with dual antibacterial and antifungal capabilities by combining nitric oxide (NO) and fluconazole release from the same interface. The material effectively reduces the viability of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, and shows significant antifungal activity against Candida albicans.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the fabrication of polymeric composites incorporating NO donor SNAP and antifungal drug fluconazole, followed by evaluation of their antibacterial and antifungal efficacy through in vitro assays.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli type I toxin TisB exclusively controls proton depolarization following antibiotic induced DNA damage.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies tisB and istR as key players in controlling proton depolarization and pH homeostasis in Escherichia coli following antibiotic-induced DNA damage, highlighting their role in persister cell formation and DNA damage response mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Flow cytometry, microscopy, and genetic mutants were used to analyze the role of tisB and istR in proton depolarization and pH homeostasis.

full_output.paper_title: Gallium nitrate inhibits multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolated from bloodstream infection by disrupting multiple iron-dependent metabolic processes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the roles of exbD, hemO, and basA in iron uptake in multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting their association with gallium nitrate's antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MIC testing, transcriptomics, and PCR to analyze the antibacterial effects of gallium nitrate and the role of iron uptake genes in A. baumannii.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes two rare ST592 Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, identifying the carbapenem resistance gene blaNDM-1, the trimethoprim resistance gene dfrA14, and the quinolone resistance gene qnrS1 in the XDR isolate KPZM16.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and assess resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Chlorogenic acid inhibits virulence and resistance gene transfer in outer membrane vesicles of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: Chlorogenic acid (CA) inhibits the virulence and resistance gene transfer in outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKp). CA reduces the production and protein content of KOMV-MEM, affects the proteome of OMVs, and downregulates the expression of resistance genes such as blaKPC, blaCTX-M-63, blaSHV-39, blaOXA-56, blaNDM-1, GyrA, GyrB, ParC, ParE, RmtB, MdtA, MdtC, MdtN, MdtP, TraI, and TraN.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis, animal experiments, and biochemical assays were used to evaluate the effects of CA on OMVs and resistance gene transfer in CRKp.
full_output.sample_size: n=3 for some experiments, n=5 for others, n=10 for survival studies

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antibacterial effects of Kelisha capsule (KLSC) on E. coli-induced diarrhea in mice, demonstrating its ability to reduce inflammation, restore intestinal barrier function, and disrupt E. coli cell membranes.
full_output.methodology: The study used HPLC for chemical characterization, animal models for in vivo experiments, and molecular dynamics simulations to explore the antibacterial mechanism of KLSC.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic interrogation of urban Superfund site reveals antimicrobial resistance reservoir and bioremediation potential.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 28 AMR genes within 8 classes of antibiotic resistance, including Rifamycin and Aminoglycosides, highlighting the Gowanus Canal as an environmental reservoir of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis using the MetaSUB CAP pipeline and MEGARES2 for AMR profiling.

full_output.paper_title: A mechanistic understanding of the effect of Staphylococcus aureus VraS histidine kinase single-point mutation on antibiotic resistance.

vraS.notes: The T331I mutation in the VraS histidine kinase increases resistance to vancomycin, methicillin, and daptomycin.

full_output.key_findings: The T331I mutation in the VraS histidine kinase enhances resistance to vancomycin, methicillin, and daptomycin by increasing autophosphorylation rate and catalytic efficiency.
full_output.methodology: Enzyme kinetics, microbiological, and transcriptomic analyses were used to evaluate the effects of the T331I mutation in VraS on antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm formation, methicillin resistance and SCCmec types among Staphylococcus aureus isolated from clinical samples from a tertiary care hospital, in Nepal.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene as a key determinant of methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates, with 78.3% of MRSA isolates carrying the gene. SCC mec type V was the most prevalent, highlighting the circulation of community-acquired MRSA in hospital settings.
full_output.methodology: PCR for mecA and SCC mec typing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and biofilm formation assessment using the tissue culture plate method.

full_output.paper_title: Taxonomic distribution of SbmA/BacA and BacA-like antimicrobial peptide transporters suggests independent recruitment and convergent evolution in host-microbe interactions.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes SbmA/BacA and BclA antimicrobial peptide transporters across bacterial species, highlighting their roles in resisting antimicrobial peptides and their taxonomic distribution.
full_output.methodology: Computational and experimental approaches, including phylogenetic analysis, sequence similarity networks, and functional assays in S. meliloti.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus lineages contribute towards poor patient outcomes in orthopaedic device-related infections.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and molecular characterization of 86 S. aureus isolates from patients with ODRIs, along with phenotypic assessments and statistical analysis of clinical outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Green Synthesis and Characterization of Silver Nanoparticles Using Anchusa Officinalis: Antimicrobial and Cytotoxic Potential.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AO-AgNPs) using Anchusa officinalis leaf extract, demonstrating effective antimicrobial activity against S. aureus, E. coli, and C. albicans at low concentrations. The nanoparticles also showed significant cytotoxic effects on cancerous cell lines.
full_output.methodology: The study used LC-MS/MS for phytochemical analysis, UV-Vis spectroscopy for nanoparticle characterization, and MIC assays for antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Performance and hypothetical clinical impact of an mNGS-based machine learning model for antimicrobial susceptibility prediction of five ESKAPEE bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated an mNGS-based machine learning model for antimicrobial susceptibility prediction of five ESKAPEE bacteria, showing high accuracy and reduced turnaround time compared to traditional culture-based methods.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized mNGS data combined with machine learning algorithms to predict antimicrobial susceptibility, validated against culture-based AST results.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus infections in a hospital in Salvador, Bahia: a descriptive study, 2021-2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the vanA gene as the predominant genotype among vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus isolates, highlighting its role in conferring resistance to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis were used to identify and characterize vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial, Quorum Sensing Inhibition, and Anti-Cancer Activities of Silver Nanoparticles Synthesized from Kenyan Bacterial Endophytes of Teclea nobilis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized from endophytic Streptomyces sp. KE4D and Bacillus safensis KE4K, demonstrating their antimicrobial, quorum sensing inhibitory, and anti-cancer activities. The AgNPs show strong antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains and inhibit quorum sensing in Chromobacterium violaceum. They also exhibit significant cytotoxic effects against breast and prostate cancer cell lines.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and identification of bacterial endophytes, synthesis of AgNPs using cell-free supernatants, and evaluation of their antimicrobial, quorum sensing inhibitory, and anti-cancer activities through various assays.

full_output.paper_title: Bioactivity of novel isoxazole-fused heterocycles: comprehensive antimicrobial, antioxidant activities, SwissADME predictions, molecular docking, and DFT analysis.
full_output.key_findings: Compounds 11a and 11b showed high antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli, Bacillus megaterium, Bacillus subtilis, and Trichoderma harzianum, with activity comparable to standard antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity testing, molecular docking, and DFT calculations.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium susceptibility to ivermectin by inhibition of eccD3, an ESX-3 secretion system component.
full_output.key_findings: Inhibition of the eccD3 gene in M. smegmatis led to increased susceptibility to ivermectin, suggesting that eccD3 is a potential target for enhancing the efficacy of ivermectin against mycobacteria.
full_output.methodology: In silico molecular docking analysis and CRISPRi-mediated gene inhibition followed by susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that Kiam wood extract (KWE) exhibits strong antimicrobial activity against Vibrio parahaemolyticus, effectively inhibiting bacterial growth, biofilm formation, and motility. KWE also enhanced the immune response and survival rate of Pacific white shrimp.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of Kiam wood extract against V. parahaemolyticus using microbiological assays, scanning electron microscopy, and in vivo trials.

full_output.paper_title: Alleviating penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae‑induced lung epithelial cell injury: mechanistic insights into effects of the optimized combination of main components from Yinhuapinggan granules.

full_output.paper_title: The Challenge of Bacterial Infections During Intensive Care Unit Stay After Heart Transplantation.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the significance of Gram-negative infections in heart transplant patients during ICU stay and identifies rectal colonization with multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria as a risk factor for infections. It also notes the protective effect of perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis (PAP) covering Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Observational prospective study analyzing infections in heart transplant patients, including microbiological testing and statistical analysis of risk factors.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of novel Mycobacterium tuberculosis leucyl-tRNA synthetase inhibitors with antibacterial activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel inhibitors of Mycobacterium tuberculosis leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LeuRS) with antibacterial activity, focusing on N-(5-benzyl-thiazol-2-yl)-2-(1-phenyl-1H-tetrazol-5-ylsulfanyl)-acetamide derivatives. full_output.paper_title: Genomic Characterization of NDM-1 Harboring Extensively-Drug Resistance Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolate From ICU-Admitted Patient With COVID-19.

full_output.paper_title: The ahpC c-54t compensatory mutation is not always a valid surrogate for isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular simulation-based investigation of thiazole derivatives as potential LasR inhibitors of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Warming is Associated With More Encoded Antimicrobial Resistance Genes and Transcriptions Within Five Drug Classes in Soil Bacteria: A Case Study and Synthesis.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a positive correlation between optimal growth temperature of soil bacteria and the number of encoded AMR genes, particularly for tetracycline and lincosamide/macrolide/streptogramin drug classes. Warming increased the transcription of AMR genes, especially those targeting lincosamide/streptogramin, beta-lactam, and phenicol/quinolone antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed soil bacterial genomes from the BV-BRC database and soil transcriptomes from a warming experiment in an Alaskan boreal forest using AMRFinder, DESeq2, and Salmon for AMR gene detection and expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Mobile phone bacterial contaminations, associated factors and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of bacteria isolates from health professionals' working in public health facilities of West Guji zone, Southern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that mobile phones of health professionals were contaminated with various bacteria species, with Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CONS) being the most prevalent. The bacteria showed high susceptibility to Sulphamethoxazole+Trimethoprim and resistance to tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving 240 mobile phones of health professionals, with microbiological analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, proteomics, and MIC testing were used to characterize nitroxoline's mechanism of action and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Development and characterisation of antimicrobial epoxy resin.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the development of an antimicrobial epoxy resin incorporating chlorhexidine digluconate (CHX), which exhibits significant antimicrobial efficacy against various pathogens including E. coli, S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, and C. albicans. The CHX-containing resin maintains its antimicrobial properties even after leaching and prolonged storage.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the preparation of epoxy resins with and without CHX, followed by evaluation of their antimicrobial efficacy through various assays including ToF-SIMS, water contact angle measurements, scratch resistance tests, optical transparency assessments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and etiological dynamics affected by tropical climate variability on year-round diagnosis of upper respiratory infections in companion rabbits with snuffles.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in gram-negative bacteria, particularly against penicillin, co-trimoxazole, and chloramphenicol. Multidrug resistance was prevalent among several bacterial groups, highlighting the need for region-specific antimicrobial stewardship in companion rabbits.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolation, Gram staining, biochemical tests, and Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, identification of virulence genes, and antibiotic resistance properties of Shiga-toxin producing Escherichia coli (STEC) strains isolated from ice cream and juice in sales centers.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of antibiotic resistance genes aadA1, tetA, and sul1 in STEC strains isolated from ice cream and juice samples, contributing to high resistance rates against ampicillin, tetracycline, and sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing to detect and characterize antibiotic resistance genes in STEC strains.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial action and mechanism of piscidin against Helicobacter pylori.
full_output.key_findings: Piscidin demonstrated potent antimicrobial activity against Helicobacter pylori without inducing resistance, suggesting its potential as a novel therapeutic agent.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics analysis, MIC testing, SEM, urease activity assay, qRT-PCR, and ATP assay were used to evaluate the antimicrobial effects and mechanisms of piscidin against H. pylori.
