full_output.paper_title: Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. allosunkii and lactis as emerging human uropathogens in elderly patients.
full_output.key_findings: Two L. delbrueckii isolates exhibited tetracycline resistance due to the presence of the tet(W) gene, which encodes a ribosomal protection protein. The study highlights the emergence of L. delbrueckii as a uropathogen in elderly patients, with most isolates showing susceptibility to various antibiotics except for intrinsic resistance to fosfomycin and metronidazole.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, MIC testing, and MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry were used to identify resistance genes and characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and characteristics of tigecycline- and carbapenem-resistant adeN-truncated Acinetobacter baumannii: a genomic epidemiological analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies adeN truncation as a key mechanism for tigecycline resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting its global prevalence and association with poor patient outcomes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR screening, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to investigate the prevalence and characteristics of adeN-truncated A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative effectiveness and safety of colistin-based versus high-dose ampicillin/sulbactam-based combination therapy for nosocomial pneumonia caused by carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: High-dose ampicillin/sulbactam-based combination therapy demonstrated superior outcomes compared to colistin-based therapy for treating nosocomial pneumonia caused by carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, with lower mortality, higher clinical success rates, and reduced kidney injury.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study comparing clinical outcomes of colistin-based and high-dose ampicillin/sulbactam-based combination therapies in patients with CRAB nosocomial pneumonia.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology of Salmonella Enteritidis human infections in the Netherlands, 2019 to 2023.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella Enteritidis isolates from the Netherlands, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, tetracycline resistance genes, and quinolone resistance proteins, as well as specific gyrA mutations associated with (fluor)quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella Enteritidis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Species and functional composition of cecal microbiota and resistance gene diversity in different Yunnan native chicken breeds: A metagenomic analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 1327 antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the cecal microbiota of six Yunnan native chicken breeds, revealing significant differences in ARG abundance and diversity between free-range and caged farming systems. Key ARGs included macB, evgS, tetA(58), bcrA, walK, and rpsA, which conferred resistance to multiple antibiotic classes.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and functional annotation of cecal microbiome samples from 108 chickens across six breeds.

full_output.paper_title: Providencia pseudovermicola sp. nov.: redefining Providencia vermicola and unveiling multidrug-resistant strains from diabetic foot ulcers in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple multidrug-resistant genes in Providencia pseudovermicola sp. nov., including bla CTX-M-14, bla CMY-6, bla NDM-1, qnrD1, aadA, armA, msrE, mphE, lnuF, rmtC, aac(6')-Ib10, sul1, aph(3')-Ia, qacEΔ1, and dfrA1, highlighting the significance of these genes in conferring resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and Biofilm-Inhibiting Effects of Baicalein Against Staphylococcus aureus in Prosthetic Joint Infections
full_output.key_findings: Baicalein exhibits strong antibacterial and biofilm-inhibiting effects against Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating bactericidal activity at concentrations above its minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC).
full_output.methodology: MIC and MBC determination, time-kill assay, biofilm inhibition and eradication assays, SEM, CLSM, and cytotoxicity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Potential pathogens drive ARGs enrichment during biofilms formation on environmental surfaces.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) such as sul1, sul2, ermF, and intI-1 that are enriched in biofilms on environmental surfaces, highlighting the role of potential pathogens in ARG dissemination.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing, quantitative PCR, and biofilm formation experiments were used to analyze ARGs and microbiota dynamics.

full_output.paper_title: The Slow Pandemic: Emergence of Antimicrobial Resistance in the Postadvent of SARS-CoV-2 Pandemic.

qacA.mechanism: confers resistance to quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs)
qacA.role_in_paper: discussed in the context of resistance mechanisms
qacA.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the emergence of antimicrobial resistance in the context of increased use of quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs) during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, highlighting the role of efflux pumps like qacA and qacE in conferring resistance to QACs in bacteria such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Enterococcus species.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of existing studies on QAC resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Population and pan-genomic analyses of Staphylococcus pseudintermedius identify geographic distinctions in accessory gene content and novel loci associated with AMR.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel chromosomal loci associated with antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus pseudintermedius, including the trimethoprim resistance gene dfRS1, the quinolone resistance determinant grlA_D84H, the lincosamide resistance gene lnuG, and the extended-spectrum beta-lactamase gene blaTEM-116.
full_output.methodology: Pan-genomic and pan-GWAS analyses of S. pseudintermedius isolates from North America and global collections, coupled with antimicrobial susceptibility testing and bioinformatics tools for gene annotation and correlation with resistance phenotypes.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic insights into the population structure, antimicrobial resistance, and virulence of Brachyspira hyodysenteriae from diverse geographical regions.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tva(A) and lnu(C) genes associated with tiamulin and lincomycin resistance in Brachyspira hyodysenteriae isolates from diverse geographical regions.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and ABRicate screening for antimicrobial resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Rational design of synthetic antimicrobial peptides based on the Escherichia coli ShoB toxin.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the ShoB toxin from the shoB-ohsC TA system in E. coli as a basis for designing synthetic antimicrobial peptides. Modified peptides showed rapid bactericidal action and limited resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study involved peptide synthesis, evaluation of antimicrobial activity, and assessment of proteolytic stability and resistance frequency.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of infective Streptococci recovered from local and imported mozzarella cheese from different markets in Baghdad.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified four Streptococcus species (Streptococcus thoraltensis, Streptococcus sanguinis, Streptococcus cremoris, and Streptococcus alactolyticus) in mozzarella cheese samples and determined their antibiotic susceptibility patterns, revealing high resistance to several antibiotics including imipenem, lincomycin, meropenem, methicillin, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: The study used culture, biochemical tests, VITEK technique, and disc diffusion method to identify and assess the antibiotic susceptibility of Streptococcus isolates from mozzarella cheese samples.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid detection of drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates for first-line antitubercular drugs by using a novel reporter mycobacteriophage.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a novel reporter phage phiFN for rapid detection of drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates for first-line antitubercular drugs. The phiFN phage uses the P furAma promoter and nanoluciferase (Nluc) reporter sequences to detect resistance to rifampin (RIF), isoniazid (INH), streptomycin (STR), and ethambutol (EMB).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a novel reporter phage phiFN incorporating the P furAma promoter and nanoluciferase (Nluc) to detect drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates through a rapid and sensitive assay.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Evaluation of Aquatic Antimicrobial Peptides Derived from Marine Metagenomes Using a High-Throughput Screening Approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three antimicrobial peptides (K-5, K-58, and K-61) with potent activity against aquatic pathogens, demonstrating their potential as alternatives to traditional antibiotics in aquaculture.
full_output.methodology: The study employs a machine-learning macro-model to predict antimicrobial peptides from marine metagenomes, followed by high-throughput screening using a cell-free protein expression system.

full_output.paper_title: An abundance of aliC and aliD genes were identified in saliva using a novel multiplex qPCR to characterize group II non-encapsulated pneumococci with improved specificity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the aliC and aliD genes in non-encapsulated pneumococci (NESp) using a novel multiplex qPCR assay, improving the specificity and efficiency of NESp detection and differentiation from other mitis-group streptococci.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a novel multiplex qPCR assay targeting pspK, aliC, and aliD genes, validated with DNA from various NESp isolates and non-pneumococcal mitis-group strains.

full_output.paper_title: Disruption of Pseudomonas aeruginosa quorum sensing influences biofilm formation without affecting antibiotic tolerance.

lasI.notes: The lasI gene is involved in the production of the QS signal molecule C12-HSL.

lasR.notes: The lasR gene is involved in the reception of the QS signal molecule C12-HSL.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that disruption of the lasI/R quorum sensing system in Pseudomonas aeruginosa leads to distinct autolysis phenotypes and altered biofilm formation, but does not affect antibiotic tolerance. The QS mutants exhibited increased biofilm mass but not live-cell numbers compared to the wild-type, and were equally susceptible to antibiotics as the wild-type.
full_output.methodology: The study compared wild-type and QS mutant strains (Δ lasI and Δ lasR ) of P. aeruginosa PA14, analyzing autolysis phenotypes, biofilm formation, and antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Toxic cultures: e-cigarettes and the oral microbial exposome.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that e-cigarette aerosol is metabolized by oral biofilms, leading to changes in metabolic pathways and biofilm architecture. Certain metabolites produced were linked to antimicrobial resistance and virulence amplification.
full_output.methodology: Combining untargeted metabolomics, metatranscriptomics, and fluorescent microscopy with human samples to analyze the impact of e-cigarette exposure on oral microbiota.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Burkholderia gladioli contamination in ultrasonic coupling agents and highlighted the importance of proper disinfection protocols to prevent healthcare-associated infections.
full_output.methodology: The study involved environmental hygiene sampling, strain identification, drug susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing to analyze Burkholderia gladioli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Bats as Hosts of Antimicrobial-Resistant Mammaliicoccus lentus and Staphylococcus epidermidis with Zoonotic Relevance.

salB.mechanism: confers resistance to lincosamides and class A streptogramins

qacA.mechanism: confers resistance to quaternary ammonium compounds

full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance genes in Mammaliicoccus lentus and Staphylococcus epidermidis isolated from bats, including mph(C), msr(A), dfrC, salB, tet(K), str, qacA, arsB, and cadD, highlighting their potential for horizontal gene transfer and environmental co-selection.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, whole genome sequencing, and gene detection were used to characterize resistance mechanisms in bat-derived bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Constructing Polymetallic Nodes in Metal-Organic Frameworks Enhance Antibacterial of Drug-Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a novel strategy for constructing polymetallic indium coordination node metal-organic frameworks (polyIn-BTB) that enhance antibacterial activity against drug-resistant bacteria by increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. PolyIn-BTB showed 87.0% and 92.0% antibacterial efficiency against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Escherichia coli, respectively, significantly higher than monometallic In-BTB.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized density functional theory (DFT) calculations, in vitro antibacterial assays, and in vivo wound healing models to evaluate the antibacterial efficacy of polyIn-BTB and monoIn-BTB.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and Antioxidant Properties of Carbon Quantum Dots from Avocado Peel
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial properties of carbon quantum dots (CQDs) derived from avocado peel against L. monocytogenes and P. putida, demonstrating significant antibacterial activity, particularly against L. monocytogenes. The CQDs showed varying levels of effectiveness depending on their surface functionalization and chemical characteristics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized CPC fractionation, XRD, FT-IR, and antimicrobial susceptibility tests to analyze the properties and effects of CQDs.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into the Antimicrobial Mechanisms of a Scorpion Defensin on Staphylococcus aureus Using Transcriptomic and Proteomic Analyses.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that BmKDfsin4, a scorpion defensin, affects multiple cellular processes in Staphylococcus aureus, including ribosome assembly, protein synthesis, amino acid biosynthesis, and cell wall synthesis, leading to bacterial growth inhibition and eventual death.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were used to examine the effects of BmKDfsin4 on S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Unveiling Berberine analogues as potential inhibitors of Escherichia coli FtsZ through machine learning molecular docking and molecular dynamics approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies berberine analogues, particularly ZINC000524729297 and ZINC000604405393, as potential inhibitors of E. coli FtsZ through computational and molecular modeling approaches.
full_output.methodology: The research employs machine learning, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate the binding affinity and stability of berberine analogues with E. coli FtsZ.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity, antibacterial and phytotoxic activities of intestinal fungi from Epitheca bimaculata.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified nine monomer compounds from intestinal fungi of Epitheca bimaculata, including citrinin, emodin, citreorosein, 8-hydroxy-6-methyl-9-oxo-9H-xanthene-1-carboxylic acid methyl ester, ergosterol, rubratoxin B, erythrol, flufuran, and 4-N-butylpyridine-2-carboxylic acid, which exhibited strong antibacterial and phytotoxic activities against various pathogens and weeds.
full_output.methodology: The study used ITS sequence amplification for fungal identification, filter paper disk method for antibacterial activity testing, and petri dish bioassay for phytotoxicity assessment.

full_output.paper_title: Pan-genome analysis of the Enterobacter hormaechei complex highlights its genomic flexibility and pertinence as a multidrug resistant pathogen.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a wide range of antibiotic resistance genes in the Enterobacter hormaechei complex, highlighting its multidrug-resistant nature and the role of mobile genetic elements in the dissemination of resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and resistance gene prediction using ResFinder v. 4.6.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating the Link between Efflux Pump Expression and Motility Phenotypes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Treated with Virulence Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that R-6 upregulates armR and mexAB-oprM, while R-2 affects mexEF-oprN expression. These efflux pumps are implicated in the resistance mechanisms of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq and β-galactosidase assays were used to analyze gene expression and efflux pump activity.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of CRISPR-Cas9, CRISPR-Cas12f1, and CRISPR-Cas3 in eradicating resistance genes KPC-2 and IMP-4.

full_output.methodology: CRISPR plasmids were designed and tested for their ability to eliminate KPC-2 and IMP-4 genes in E. coli through colony PCR, drug sensitivity testing, and qPCR analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Integrated 16S rRNA and metagenomic sequencing reveals the distribution of key antibiotic resistance genes in duck gut microbiota.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified key antibiotic resistance genes such as tetQ, tet32, tet37, vanR, vanG, and acrB in the duck gut microbiota, particularly in the hindgut, and highlighted their potential hosts including Bacteroides, Roseburia, Ruminococcus, and Blautia.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA gene sequencing and metagenomic analysis were used to characterize the gut microbiota and identify antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Biosynthesis and Fatty Acid- and Cation-Binding Properties of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Methylglucose Lipopolysaccharides.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the biosynthesis of Methylglucose Lipopolysaccharides (MGLP) in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, identifying key enzymes involved in methylation, glucosylation, and acylation processes. Mutants defective in these pathways show altered MGLP structures and growth characteristics.
full_output.methodology: Genetic disruption, complementation, and biochemical analysis of MGLP biosynthesis in M. tuberculosis and M. smegmatis.

full_output.paper_title: Study on extended-spectrum beta-lactamases genes and drug resistance in patients with urinary tract infection of enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli after bladder cancer surgery.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCTX-M-14 and bla-TEM as the main ESBL genes in ESBL-producing E. coli isolates from patients with urinary tract infections after bladder cancer surgery, with blaCTX-M-14 having the highest detection rate. These genes conferred high resistance to ampicillin and cefotaxime.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping and drug sensitivity testing were performed on E. coli isolates from patients with urinary tract infections after bladder cancer surgery.

full_output.paper_title: An anti-virulence drug targeting the evolvability protein Mfd protects against infections with antimicrobial resistant ESKAPE pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NM102, a small molecule that inhibits the Mfd protein, reducing bacterial resistance and evolvability. NM102 shows antimicrobial activity under nitric oxide stress conditions and effectively reduces bacterial load in vivo without host toxicity.
full_output.methodology: In silico screening, in vitro ATPase inhibition assays, ITC, molecular docking, and in vivo studies in insect and mouse models.

full_output.paper_title: Structure and mechanism of a mycobacterial isoniazid efflux pump MsRv1273c/72c with a degenerate nucleotide-binding site.

MsRv1273c.validation_method: ATPase activity assay, transport assay, growth curve analysis

full_output.key_findings: MsRv1273c/72c functions as an isoniazid efflux pump, demonstrating resistance to isoniazid through ATP hydrolysis and transport mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-EM structure determination, ATPase activity assays, transport assays, and growth curve analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Unraveling the molecular drivers of antibacterial prenylated (iso)flavonoids and chalcones against Streptococcus mutans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several prenylated phenolics, including isokanzonol V, gancaonin I, kanzonol C, and isobavachalcone, as having potent antibacterial activity against Streptococcus mutans. These compounds demonstrate varying degrees of efficacy, with some showing MIC values as low as 3.13 μg/mL.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity testing of prenylated phenolics against S. mutans using MIC and MBC measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Amphiphilic mPEG-PLGA copolymer nanoparticles co-delivering colistin and niclosamide to treat colistin-resistant Gram-negative bacteria infections.

mcr-1.encodes: protein that modifies colistin target lipid A
mcr-1.mechanism: confers resistance to colistin by modifying the bacterial membrane
mcr-1.validation_method: antibacterial activity against colistin-resistant clinical strains

mcr.mechanism: confers resistance to colistin by modifying the bacterial membrane
mcr.validation_method: antibacterial activity against colistin-resistant clinical strains

The research highlights the effectiveness of co-delivering colistin and niclosamide using mPEG-PLGA nanoparticles to overcome this resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed using MIC and time-kill curve assays against colistin-resistant Gram-negative bacteria carrying mcr-1 and mcr genes.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of a Natural Antibiotic's Properties Effective against Resistant Opportunistic Pathogenic Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a new antibiotic, A-312, produced by Streptomyces lateritius strain 312, which exhibits strong antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant strains of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: The antibiotic was isolated from the culture liquid and biomass of strain 312 using extraction methods, and its activity was evaluated using the well diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution status and influencing factors of antibiotic resistance genes in the Chaohu Lake, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified nine families of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in Chaohu Lake, with multidrug, bacitracin, polymyxin, macrolide lincosamide streptogramin (MLS), and aminoglycoside being the most abundant. Key genes included bacA, mexF, and mdtB, which were found to confer resistance to specific antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing was used to analyze the distribution and influencing factors of ARGs in Chaohu Lake.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Linezolid Resistance Genes optrA and cfr(D) in an Enterococcus saccharolyticus from Chicken.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first identification of optrA and cfr(D) in Enterococcus saccharolyticus from chicken feces in China, highlighting their presence in a new species and emphasizing the need for surveillance of resistance determinants in animal-associated bacteria.
full_output.methodology: PCR analysis, whole-genome sequencing, conjugation experiments, and stability testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Extended-Spectrum ß-Lactamases-Producing Escherichia coli Isolated from a Greek Food Testing Laboratory.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-55, bla SHV-12, and bla TEM-1B, in Escherichia coli isolates from food of animal origin in Greece. These genes were associated with resistance to third-generation cephalosporins and other beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, and plasmid analysis to identify and characterize ESBL genes in E. coli isolates from food samples.

full_output.paper_title: Persistence of Colistin Resistance and mcr-1.1-Positive E. coli in Poultry Despite Colistin Ban in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1.1-positive colistin-resistant E. coli strains in Japanese broilers despite the colistin ban, highlighting the persistence of colistin resistance in poultry.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: 231 cecal stool samples from five poultry farms

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Variant GTR(I)Staphylococcus aureus Isolated from Dairy Cow Milk Samples in the Alpine Grazing System of the Aosta Valley and Its Association with AMR and Virulence Profiles.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaZ gene as a key determinant of penicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from dairy cows in the Aosta Valley, with high prevalence in the CLR genotypic cluster.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, and molecular genotyping were used to analyze AMR genes and virulence factors in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a Potential High-Risk Clone and Novel Sequence Type of Carbapenem-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Metro Manila, Philippines.

full_output.paper_title: A multi-strategy antimicrobial discovery approach reveals new ways to treat Chlamydia.

fabH.mechanism: covalent inhibitor of fatty acid biosynthesis
fabH.validation_method: thermal proteome profiling, enzyme kinetics, intact protein mass spectrometry

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies c1 e as a potent antichlamydial compound that selectively inhibits Chlamydia FabH, the enzyme initiating fatty acid biosynthesis, through covalent binding to its active site.
full_output.methodology: Experimental compound library screening, thermal proteome profiling, enzyme kinetics, and mass spectrometry were used to identify and validate the mechanism of action of the antichlamydial compound c1 e.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm inhibition of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa using green-synthesized silver nanoparticles and colistin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the downregulation of quorum sensing (QS) genes lasI, lasR, rhlI, rhlR, pelA, and pslA in P. aeruginosa ATCC 27,853 and clinical isolate No. #354 upon treatment with AgNPs@CL, indicating reduced biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RT-qPCR to analyze the expression of QS-related genes in P. aeruginosa isolates following treatment with AgNPs@CL.

full_output.paper_title: Personalized inhaled bacteriophage therapy for treatment of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in cystic fibrosis.
full_output.key_findings: Phage therapy reduced sputum Pseudomonas aeruginosa levels and improved lung function in cystic fibrosis patients with multidrug-resistant infections.
full_output.methodology: Phage therapy was administered to nine patients with cystic fibrosis and multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections.

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that spatial entropy influences the maintenance and dissemination of plasmids, which are crucial for the spread of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Prokaryotes from low-entropy environments tend to carry more plasmids and ARGs, highlighting the role of spatial structure in microbial ecology and antibiotic resistance dynamics.
full_output.methodology: Combining mathematical modeling, experiments with E. coli metacommunities, and genomic analysis of prokaryotic genomes to investigate the impact of spatial entropy on plasmid persistence and dissemination.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-Resistant Burkholderia cepacia Complex Isolates Carrying bla (NDM-1) and bla (NDM-5) in Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia Patients and Contaminated Ventilator Tubing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaNDM-1 and blaNDM-5 as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in carbapenem-resistant Burkholderia cepacia complex (BCC) isolates from ventilator-associated pneumonia patients and contaminated ventilator tubing.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize blaNDM-1 and blaNDM-5 genes in BCC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: First Report of Complete Genome Analysis of Multiple Drug Resistance Proteus mirabilis KUST-1312 Isolate From Migratory Birds in China: A Public Health Threat.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 15 antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in the multidrug-resistant Proteus mirabilis KUST-1312 isolate, including bla-TEM-1B, sul2, and blaPER-1, highlighting the presence of multiple resistance mechanisms in this strain.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing and PCR analysis were used to identify and characterize the antimicrobial resistance genes in the P. mirabilis KUST-1312 isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetically Informative Mutations in Drug Resistance Genes of Human-Infecting Mycobacterium bovis.

pncA.evidence_note: The H57D mutation in the pncA gene is associated with the inherent PZA resistance of M. bovis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the pncA H57D mutation as a phylogenetically informative mutation conferring intrinsic pyrazinamide resistance in Mycobacterium bovis, highlighting its significance in distinguishing true resistance from false positives in drug resistance testing.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and mutation analysis of 165 M. bovis isolates from humans.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and Genomic Analyses of a Multidrug Resistant Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli Coharboring mcr-1, bla (TEM-176) and bla (CTX-M-14) Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a multidrug-resistant APEC isolate carrying mcr-1, bla(CTX-M-14), and bla(TEM-176) genes, which conferred resistance to polymyxin B and third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, WGS, and conjugation assays were used to analyze the resistance genes and their transferability.

full_output.paper_title: Wild Birds as Drivers of Salmonella Braenderup and Multidrug Resistant Bacteria in Wetlands of Northern Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes in bacterial isolates from wild aquatic birds in Northern Italy, including beta-lactamases (blaTEM, blaCMY-1, blaCMY-2, blaNDM, blaKPC), colistin resistance genes (mcr-2, mcr-3, mcr-4), tetracycline resistance genes (tetA, tetB, tetC, tetL, tetM, tetK), macrolide resistance genes (ermB, vatD, vgA, msrC), vancomycin resistance genes (vanC1, vanC2, vanM, vanG), sulfonamide resistance genes (sul1, sul2, sul3), aminoglycoside resistance genes (aac(3), aac(6')-Ib, aph(3')-Ia, armA, rmtB, rmtC, rmtF), and nitrofurantoin resistance genes (nfsA, nfsB).
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, whole genome sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to identify AMR genes and resistance profiles in bacterial isolates from wild aquatic birds.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem treatment options for metallo-beta-lactamase: drug screening and dose optimization of meropenem-based combinations against NDM- or IMP-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM and blaIMP genes in NDM- or IMP-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae strains, which conferred resistance to meropenem. Combination therapies with fosfomycin or colistin were effective against these strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, and in vitro PK/PD modeling were used to evaluate resistance mechanisms and optimal treatment regimens.

full_output.paper_title: Monitoring the Prevalence of Antimicrobial Resistance in Companion Animals: Results from Clinical Isolates in an Italian University Veterinary Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and multidrug resistance (MDR) in bacterial isolates from companion animals, with specific resistance patterns observed in ESKAPE group bacteria such as Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter spp.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method and analysis of clinical isolates from companion animals.

full_output.paper_title: Genotyping and antibiotic susceptibility of Salmonella strains collected from sheep and cattle samples in Algeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance in Salmonella strains from sheep and cattle in Algeria, with resistance to multiple antimicrobial classes, including sulfamethoxazole, trimethoprim, tetracycline, and ciprofloxacin. Notably, one colistin-resistant strain was detected.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was assessed using the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) method, and genetic relatedness was analyzed using pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE).

full_output.paper_title: Azithromycin represses evolution of ceftazidime/avibactam resistance by translational repression of rpoS in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Azithromycin represses the evolution of ceftazidime/avibactam (CZA) resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by translational repression of the rpoS gene, which reduces mutation frequency and resistance development.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis, ribosome profiling, and mutation frequency assessment.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of the 13-valent pneumococcal vaccine on Streptococcus pneumoniae serotypes and antibiotic susceptibility in children.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the majority of Streptococcus pneumoniae serotypes isolated from children in Xiamen were covered by the 13-valent pneumococcal vaccine. The isolated S. pneumoniae strains were highly resistant to erythromycin and tetracycline but remained susceptible to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed S. pneumoniae serotypes and antibiotic susceptibility in children vaccinated with the 13-valent pneumococcal vaccine and unvaccinated children.

full_output.paper_title: Postexposure Antimicrobial Drug Therapy in Goats Infected with Burkholderia pseudomallei.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of various antimicrobial drug regimens for postexposure prophylaxis against Burkholderia pseudomallei infection in goats. Combination therapy with four antimicrobial drugs showed significant efficacy in reducing infection and abscess formation compared to monotherapy or dual therapy.
full_output.methodology: The study used goats as a model to assess the impact of different antimicrobial drug regimens on B. pseudomallei infection following percutaneous inoculation.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Transmission and Divergence of Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcus faecium Sequence Type 80, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two subpopulations of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium ST80 (SC11-pop I and SC11-pop II) that diverged through insertion sequence-mediated recombination. SC11-pop II acquired additional antimicrobial resistance genes, including vanM, ant9Ia, aph3IIIa, arr, dfrF, ermA, ermC, ermT, lnuB, lsaE, fexA, optrA, and catA1.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to investigate the genetic diversity and transmission dynamics of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A Live Bacterial Screening Assay for Membrane-Active Antimicrobial Compounds Using Imaging Fluorescence Correlation Spectroscopy.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces an ITIR-FCS-based screening assay for membrane-active antimicrobial compounds, demonstrating its sensitivity in detecting sub-MIC effects on bacterial membrane dynamics. The method allows rapid assessment of antimicrobial activity within 30 minutes and generates dose-response curves in 1-2 hours.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized ITIR-FCS combined with image processing algorithms to analyze membrane dynamics of S. aureus exposed to various antimicrobial compounds, including EHG, BAC, CG, and PO.

full_output.paper_title: Platelet-rich plasma as a potential antimicrobial agent against multidrug-resistant bacteria in diabetic foot infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) against multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), MDR Klebsiella pneumoniae, and MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa. PRP showed variable antibacterial effects depending on the bacterial strain and incubation time, but no AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this study.
full_output.methodology: In vitro experimental study using Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion, broth microdilution, checkerboard synergy testing, and time-kill assays to assess the antibacterial activity of PRP against MDR bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance risk assessment and molecular basis of metconazole in Fusarium pseudograminearum.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a M151T mutation in FpCYP51B as a mechanism of metconazole resistance in Fusarium pseudograminearum, along with increased expression of FpCYP51 genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used protoplast transformation, DNA sequencing, and sensitivity testing to identify and validate the resistance mechanism.

full_output.paper_title: Xenopus laevis as an infection model for human pathogenic bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study established Xenopus laevis as a viable animal infection model for evaluating antimicrobial efficacy and identifying virulence genes in human pathogenic bacteria. It demonstrated that virulence gene deletion mutants of S. aureus and L. monocytogenes exhibit reduced virulence in Xenopus frogs.
full_output.methodology: The study used intraperitoneal injection of human pathogenic bacteria into Xenopus frogs to assess mortality, virulence, and antimicrobial efficacy. Bacterial virulence gene deletion mutants were tested for their impact on frog survival.

full_output.paper_title: Next-generation rifamycins for the treatment of mycobacterial infections.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the rpoB gene as a resistance mechanism against rifamycins in Mycobacterium abscessus, highlighting the importance of monitoring these mutations for effective treatment strategies.
full_output.methodology: The study involved in vitro assays, mouse models, and genetic analysis to evaluate the efficacy of rifamycin derivatives and characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of genetic determinants of antibiotic resistance in Helicobacter pylori isolates in Vietnam by high-throughput sequencing.

pbp1A.mechanism: mutations in the penicillin-binding protein motifs

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several mutations in 23S rRNA, gyrA, pbp1 A, and rdxA genes associated with resistance to clarithromycin, levofloxacin, amoxicillin, and metronidazole in H. pylori isolates from Vietnam.

full_output.paper_title: T cell toxicity induced by tigecycline binding to the mitochondrial ribosome.
full_output.key_findings: Tigecycline was found to inhibit mitochondrial translation and cause cytotoxicity in human T cells by binding to the mitochondrial ribosome, affecting T cell activation and proliferation.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of novel DdlA inhibitors in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa using virtual screening, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations.
full_output.key_findings: This study identified novel inhibitors of DdlA, a critical enzyme in peptidoglycan biosynthesis in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, using virtual screening, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations.
full_output.methodology: Virtual screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to identify and analyze potential DdlA inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a Bismuth-Doped Carbon Dot-Based Hydrogel for Targeted Treatment of Periodontitis
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a bismuth-doped carbon dot-based hydrogel (BiCD-Ber HA gel) that effectively targets Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg) and reduces periodontal inflammation. The hydrogel exhibits antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities, suppresses Pg virulence factors, and shows therapeutic potential in an in vivo periodontitis model.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro antimicrobial assays, SEM, confocal microscopy, and in vivo rat models to evaluate the effectiveness of the hydrogel.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro Evaluation of the Antibacterial Activity of the Combination of Avibactam and β-Lactams Against Highly Virulent Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC-2 and blaNDM as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in CRKP strains, highlighting their significance in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance and virulence genes in CRKP strains.

full_output.paper_title: Incidence, case-fatality rates and risk factors of bloodstream infections caused by Escherichia coli, Klebsiella species and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, England, April 2017 to March 2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the incidence, case-fatality rates, and risk factors of bloodstream infections caused by Escherichia coli, Klebsiella species, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa in England from April 2017 to March 2022. It found varying incidence rates and case-fatality rates among the three pathogens, with P. aeruginosa having the highest case-fatality rate. The study also highlighted the importance of managing urinary tract infections and urinary catheterization to reduce these infections.
full_output.methodology: The study used data from the UKHSA HCAI DCS on E. coli, Klebsiella spp., and P. aeruginosa bloodstream infections diagnosed by NHS acute trusts in England between 1 April 2017 and 31 March 2022. full_output.paper_title: Incidence and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of multi-drug resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains isolated from diseased Clarias gariepinus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae strains isolated from diseased Clarias gariepinus, showing resistance to multiple antimicrobial classes including penicillins, tetracyclines, nitroimidazole, and macrolides.
full_output.methodology: The study involved bacteriological examination, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Interdependence of plasma membrane nanoscale dynamics of a kinase and its cognate substrate underlies Arabidopsis response to viral infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CPK3 and group 1 REMs as key players in restricting PlAMV propagation in Arabidopsis, highlighting their interdependent roles in modulating plasma membrane dynamics during viral infection.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic mutants, transgenic lines, and advanced imaging techniques to analyze the role of CPK3 and REMs in viral propagation.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial profile, treatment outcomes, and determinants among adult patients with musculoskeletal infections admitted to Jimma Medical Center: A prospective observational study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Klebsiella pneumonia as the most common bacterial isolates causing musculoskeletal infections. These isolates showed high resistance rates to ceftriaxone, ceftazidime, and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a prospective observational approach with microbiological analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: A sonosensitive diphenylalanine-based broad-spectrum antimicrobial peptide.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a sonosensitive diphenylalanine-based peptide, FFRK8, which exhibits high broad-spectrum antibacterial efficiency against clinically isolated methicillin-resistant bacteria upon ultrasound activation. full_output.paper_title: DmdA-independent lag phase shortening in Phaeobacter inhibens bacteria under stress conditions.

full_output.paper_title: AMPCliff: Quantitative definition and benchmarking of activity cliffs in antimicrobial peptides.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, mutation analysis, and genomic comparisons were used to identify resistance genes and mutations in Pseudomonas aeruginosa ST463.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and genetic mechanisms of resistance of Ureaplasma isolates in North America between 2012 and 2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in 23S rRNA, rplD, parC, gyrB, and parE genes associated with erythromycin, tetracycline, and levofloxacin resistance in Ureaplasma isolates. The tet(M) gene was detected in tetracycline-resistant isolates, and specific mutations in parC and gyrB were linked to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to identify genetic mutations associated with antimicrobial resistance in Ureaplasma isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that MarA activates genes involved in LPS synthesis (lpxC, lpxL, rfaY) and represses pbpG, a cell wall remodelling enzyme, thereby coordinating cell envelope biology to enhance intrinsic antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics, electrophoretic mobility shift assays, β-galactosidase assays, in vitro transcription assays, and mutagenesis experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial impact of biosynthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles on uropathogenic Escherichia coli and in vivo assessment of physiological and histological alterations.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antibacterial effects of biosynthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) against uropathogenic E. coli. ZnO NPs showed significant antibacterial activity with MIC and MBC values of 3.2 mg/mL and 3.9 mg/mL, respectively. In vivo studies demonstrated the effectiveness of ZnO NPs in reducing bacterial load and improving hematological and biochemical parameters in infected rats.
full_output.methodology: In vitro disk diffusion and microtiter plate assays were used to determine the antibacterial activity of ZnO NPs. In vivo studies involved administering ZnO NPs to infected rats and assessing physiological and histological changes.

full_output.paper_title: From discovery to potential application: engineering a novel M23 peptidase to combat Listeria monocytogenes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes a novel M23 peptidase from Streptococcus thermophilus (StM23) and a chimeric variant (StM23_CWT) that exhibits broad-spectrum bacteriolytic activity against Listeria monocytogenes and other Gram-positive bacteria. The chimeric enzyme demonstrates enhanced tolerance to pH and salt concentrations, effective biofilm disruption, and surface decontamination capabilities.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics, structural analysis, turbidity reduction assays, electron microscopy, and safety evaluations in zebrafish, moth larvae, and human cell models.

full_output.paper_title: Eco-friendly biosynthesis of silver nanoparticles using marine-derived Fusarium exquisite: optimization, characterization, and evaluation of antimicrobial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the successful extracellular biosynthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using the marine-derived fungus Fusarium equiseti. The AgNPs exhibited strong antimicrobial activity against bacterial and fungal strains, including Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, with MIC values of 6.5 and 7.5 µg/mL, respectively. They also showed antifungal effects on Candida albicans and Fusarium solani, as well as antioxidant and cytotoxic activities against MCF-7 breast cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of biochemical and biophysical techniques, including UV-Vis spectroscopy, XRD, SEM, TEM, and FTIR, to characterize the synthesized AgNPs. Antimicrobial activity was assessed using a broth microdilution assay, while antioxidant and cytotoxic activities were evaluated using the DPPH radical scavenging assay and MTT assay, respectively.

full_output.paper_title: Point-prevalence surveys of hospital-acquired infections in 42 Chinese hospitals in Weifang, China: from 2015 to 2020.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB), methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), and carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) as the most frequent multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) in hospital-acquired infections (HAIs).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of hospital-acquired infections across 42 hospitals in Weifang, China, from 2015 to 2020, including data on pathogen isolation and antimicrobial use.

full_output.paper_title: Screening the Pandemic Response Box identifies novel ligands of the Staphylococcus aureus protein arginine kinase, McsB.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified six novel ligands for the Staphylococcus aureus protein arginine kinase, McsB, using thermal shift and cellular thermal shift assays. These ligands, particularly MMV1593539 and MMV1782355, showed significant stabilization of McsB. Additionally, MMV1634391 potentiated the activity of ciprofloxacin against S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: Thermal shift assays, cellular thermal shift assays, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to identify and characterize McsB ligands.

full_output.paper_title: Simultaneous detection of pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes with the open source, cloud-based, CZ ID platform.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Activity of Gloeophyllum striatum-Derived AgNPs with Ciprofloxacin and Gentamicin Against Human Pathogenic Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the synergistic activity of Gloeophyllum striatum-derived silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) with ciprofloxacin and gentamicin against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, showing enhanced antimicrobial and antibiofilm effects.

full_output.paper_title: Public Health Risk of Campylobacter spp. Isolated from Slaughterhouse and Retail Poultry Meat: Prevalence and Antimicrobial Resistance Profiles.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Campylobacter spp. isolates exhibited resistance to ciprofloxacin (41.6%), tetracycline (25.0%), chloramphenicol (16.6%), gentamicin (11.1%), ertapenem (5.6%), and erythromycin (2.8%). Multidrug-resistant strains were also identified.
full_output.methodology: The study used standardized microbiological methods (ISO 10272-1:2017) for Campylobacter detection and the Kirby–Bauer disc diffusion assay for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Antibacterial Effects of Plant Extracts and Essential Oils Against Drug-Resistant Bacteria of Clinical Interest.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial effects of plant extracts and essential oils against drug-resistant bacteria, highlighting the synergistic effects of essential oils with antibiotics against multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used microdilution assays and fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) analysis to assess the antibacterial activity of essential oils and plant extracts against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: From Microbial Ecology to Clinical Challenges: The Respiratory Microbiome's Role in Antibiotic Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The paper characterizes the respiratory resistome, highlighting the presence of multiple antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in respiratory pathogens, including beta-lactamases, macrolide resistance genes, aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, tetracycline resistance genes, and others. These genes contribute to multidrug resistance in respiratory infections.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of the respiratory microbiome to identify ARGs and their distribution in chronic respiratory diseases.

full_output.paper_title: Mutational Analysis of Colistin-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolates: From Genomic Background to Antibiotic Resistance.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and mutation detection using whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics tools.

full_output.paper_title: Bactericidal activity of mammalian histones is caused by large membrane pore formation.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized cryogenic transmission electron microscopy (cryoEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and various microbiological assays to analyze membrane permeability and antimicrobial synergy.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of a novel lytic bacteriophage Pv27 with biocontrol potential against Vibrio parahaemolyticus infections in shrimp.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolated and characterized a novel lytic bacteriophage, Pv27, which shows high lytic activity against Vibrio parahaemolyticus strains and has potential as a biocontrol agent. The genome of Pv27 was sequenced and analyzed, revealing no genes associated with antibiotic resistance, virulence, or lysogeny.
full_output.methodology: Phage Pv27 was isolated using the double-layer agar technique, characterized by transmission electron microscopy, and its genome was sequenced and analyzed for functional annotations and phylogenetic relationships.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two membrane-active peptides, TM8 and TM8-S, which enhance the efficacy of antibiotics against Gram-negative bacteria by permeabilizing bacterial membranes. These peptides do not encode known antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes or mutations but rather act as adjuvants to restore antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study uses peptide synthesis, MIC and MHC assays, liposome-based assays, and fluorescence measurements to evaluate the effects of peptides on bacterial membranes and antibiotic potency.

full_output.paper_title: REL/DPA/AVI method: a novel approach for rapid detection of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales directly from positive blood cultures based on optical density.
full_output.key_findings: The REL/DPA/AVI method was developed for rapid detection of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales directly from positive blood cultures. It showed high sensitivity and specificity for detecting class A, B, and D carbapenemases, with improved time efficiency compared to traditional methods.
full_output.methodology: The REL/DPA/AVI method utilized optical density measurements to identify carbapenemase types by monitoring bacterial growth in the presence of imipenem and specific inhibitors. PCR and DNA sequencing were used for preliminary identification of carbapenemase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial control and temporal dynamics of M. plutonius colonization in adult worker honey bees (Apis mellifera).
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the persistence of M. plutonius colonization in adult worker honey bees and evaluates the effects of antibiotic treatments (oxytetracycline, tylosin, and lincomycin) on reducing bacterial loads, though none eliminated the bacteria completely.
full_output.methodology: Experimental inoculation of adult bees with M. plutonius, qPCR for bacterial load quantification, and antibiotic treatment trials in laboratory and field settings.

full_output.paper_title: Observation of persister cell histories reveals diverse modes of survival in antibiotic persistence.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that growing persisters are predominant in post-exponential phase cell cultures exposed to ampicillin, exhibiting heterogeneous survival dynamics including continuous growth, fission with L-form-like morphologies, and post-exposure filamentation. Non-growing persisters were also observed, albeit in smaller fractions.
full_output.methodology: Single-cell time-lapse imaging using a microfluidic device (MCMA) to track persister cell dynamics under antibiotic exposure.

full_output.paper_title: The Burden of Antimicrobial Resistant Bacteremia in Ontario: A Population-Wide Analysis of Attributable Mortality From 110 Pathogen-Antibiotic Combinations.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that antimicrobial resistance was associated with a 10% relative increase in the risk of mortality among patients with bacteremia and 1.2 AMR attributable deaths per 100,000 population per year in Ontario, Canada.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed data from 83,962 bacteremia episodes across 30 pathogens, examining the association between antimicrobial resistance and 30-day mortality using proportional hazards models.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-wide association study and transcriptomic analysis reveal the crucial role of sting1 in resistance to visceral white-nodules disease in Larimichthys polyactis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies sting1 as a key gene involved in the resistance to visceral white-nodules disease in Larimichthys polyactis through genome-wide association study and transcriptomic analysis.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide association study (GWAS) and transcriptome sequencing were used to identify candidate genes associated with resistance to visceral white-nodules disease.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology of a novel Pandoraea pneumonica group caused severe bloodstream infection in Hainan, China, 2021-2024.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a novel cluster of Pandoraea pneumonica causing severe bloodstream infections in Hainan, China, with high resistance to meropenem, amoxicillin/clavulanate, gentamicin, and ceftazidime. Several potential resistance genes, including OXA-157, ceoB, MexB, MuxB, MexA, and OrpM, were predicted.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, pan-genome analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and characterize the novel P. pneumonica cluster.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical evaluation of personalized Helicobacter pylori treatment guided by PCR detection from fecal samples: a real-world study.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the clinical utility of PCR analysis of fecal samples for detecting antibiotic resistance in Helicobacter pylori, focusing on 23S rRNA and gyrA genes to guide personalized treatment.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective, observational study using PCR melting curve method to detect 23S rRNA and gyrA mutations in fecal samples.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of Neisseria gonorrhoeae susceptibility trends (MIC creep) from North India: A 15-years’ experience!
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the susceptibility trends of Neisseria gonorrhoeae to various antimicrobials over a 15-year period in North India, revealing high resistance levels to penicillin, tetracycline, and ciprofloxacin, but low resistance to ceftriaxone and azithromycin. No significant increase in MIC for ceftriaxone and azithromycin was observed.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using E-test strips and MIC-test strips, with results interpreted according to CDS and CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Gram-negative bacterial sepsis, antimicrobial susceptibility pattern and treatment outcomes at two neonatal intensive care units in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: A retrospective observational study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Klebsiella spp. as the most prevalent gram-negative bacteria causing sepsis in neonates, with high levels of multidrug resistance. It also highlighted the significant association between multidrug-resistant organisms and poor treatment outcomes.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study analyzing blood culture results and antimicrobial susceptibility testing data from two neonatal intensive care units in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

full_output.paper_title: Non-typhoidal Salmonella transmission reservoirs in Sub-Saharan Africa: a genomic assessment from a one health perspective.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella enterica strains, particularly S. Typhimurium ST313, associated with human reservoirs in sub-Saharan Africa. Resistance to ampicillin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, and chloramphenicol was prevalent in isolates from blood cultures.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic studies were conducted on Salmonella isolates from humans, livestock, and the environment in Ghana and Tanzania.

full_output.paper_title: D-Serine Can Modify the Wall Teichoic Acid of MRSA via the dlt Pathway.
full_output.key_findings: D-Serine modifies the wall teichoic acid of MRSA via the dlt pathway, reducing WTA synthesis and increasing susceptibility to polymyxins. The dlt operon genes (dltA, dltB, dltC, dltD) were identified as involved in this process.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing, quantitative real-time PCR, enzyme kinetic assays, WTA extraction, and in vivo mouse infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of Boronic Acids-Based β-Lactamase Inhibitors Through In Situ Click Chemistry.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes triazole-based β-lactamase inhibitors using in situ click chemistry, highlighting the effectiveness of KTGS in generating potent inhibitors against KPC-2 and AmpC β-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: Kinetic target-guided synthesis (KTGS) and enzymatic inhibition assays were used to screen and validate the inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Evaluation of Platelet-Rich Fibrin (PRF) and Concentrated Growth Factor (CGF) as Carriers for Antibiotics-In Vitro Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy of c-PRF and LPCGF as carriers for antibiotics, highlighting their potential as localized antibiotic delivery systems. c-PRF showed superior performance as a carrier for amoxicillin and clindamycin, while LPCGF was more effective with the amoxicillin-metronidazole combination.
full_output.methodology: Disk diffusion method was used to assess the antibacterial effects of antibiotics carried by c-PRF and LPCGF against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-Modal Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Fusidic Acid Derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: This study focused on the design and synthesis of novel fusidic acid (FA) derivatives with improved efficacy against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). The research involved computational methods, molecular dynamics simulations, and experimental validation to identify and characterize FA derivatives with enhanced antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study employed molecular dynamics simulations, scaffold decoration, virtual screening, and chemical synthesis to develop and evaluate novel FA derivatives. Experimental validation included in vitro testing of the synthesized compounds against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Loss of LasR function leads to decreased repression of Pseudomonas aeruginosa PhoB activity at physiological phosphate concentrations.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the loss of LasR function in Pseudomonas aeruginosa leads to increased PhoB activity at physiological phosphate concentrations, which is inhibited by phenazines and regulated by the CbrA-CbrB-Crc pathway.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, AP activity assays, qRT-PCR, and NanoString technology were used to investigate the relationship between LasR, PhoB, and other regulatory genes.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the efficacy of sulbactam combination therapy for monomicrobial and polymicrobial pulmonary infections caused by multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that sulbactam combination regimens, particularly with polymyxins, showed better microbiological efficacy against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii compared to monotherapy or other combinations.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective multicenter study analyzing the efficacy of sulbactam-based treatments in patients with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infections.

full_output.paper_title: Development of disk diffusion susceptibility test methods for Aerococcus spp. and updates to Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute MIC breakpoints.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on establishing disk diffusion susceptibility test methods and updating MIC breakpoints for Aerococcus spp., highlighting challenges in growth and susceptibility testing.
full_output.methodology: The study involved testing 174 isolates of Aerococcus spp. using broth microdilution and disk diffusion methods to determine MIC breakpoints and disk diffusion criteria.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) strains, with high resistance rates to amoxicillin, tetracycline, and enrofloxacin. It also noted the presence of high-risk sequence types ST131, ST117, and ST95, highlighting the potential public health implications of APEC in poultry.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR for virulence factor and phylogroup analysis, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing to determine resistance profiles of APEC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and molecular characterisation of multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolated from chicken meat.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM and sul 2 genes as key contributors to ampicillin and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim resistance in multidrug-resistant E. coli isolates from chicken meat.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion and PCR for detection of resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic relationship of a novel pleuromutilin derivative p-furoylamphenmulin against Mycoplasma gallisepticum in vivo in chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vivo activity of p-furoylamphenmulin against Mycoplasma gallisepticum, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing bacterial load and air sac lesions in chickens. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of p-furoylamphenmulin was 0.001953125 μg/mL, and the PK/PD analysis suggested a recommended dose of 62.64 mg/kg for three consecutive days.
full_output.methodology: PK/PD analysis, MIC determination, and in vivo efficacy testing in a chicken model.

full_output.paper_title: Antifungal agent tavaborole as a potential broad-spectrum serine and metallo-β-lactamases inhibitor.

tavaborole.mechanism: Competitive inhibition of β-lactamases through coordination with Zn2+ in NDM-5 and covalent bonding with serine residue in KPC-2
tavaborole.validation_method: Enzyme kinetic studies, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vivo efficacy tests

full_output.key_findings: Tavaborole was identified as a broad-spectrum inhibitor of serine and metallo-beta-lactamases, enhancing the efficacy of beta-lactam antibiotics against resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, enzyme inhibition assays, molecular docking, and in vivo mouse models were used to evaluate the synergistic effects of tavaborole with beta-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Adjunctive phage therapy improves antibiotic treatment of ventilator-associated-pneumonia with Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that adjunctive phage therapy enhances the effectiveness of antibiotic treatment for ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, leading to faster clinical improvement and reduced lung and organ injury.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a murine model of Pseudomonas aeruginosa-induced VAP and in vitro experiments with human primary alveolar epithelial cells to evaluate the efficacy of phage-antibiotic combination therapy.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility at intensive care units in Sudan, antibiogram development.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a local unit-specific antibiogram for intensive care units in Sudan, highlighting the high prevalence of Gram-negative bacteria with low antimicrobial susceptibility, particularly Klebsiella spp. and Acinetobacter spp. It also noted the low prevalence of MRSA and the high susceptibility of Gram-negative bacteria to colistin.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of microbiology culture and susceptibility test results from ICU patients over a one-year period.

full_output.paper_title: A decade of genomic and phenotypic adaptation of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various AMR genes and mutations in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates, including blaOXA-23, blaOXA-51-like, and several aminoglycoside resistance genes, contributing to extensive drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze AMR genes and mutations in A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of a novel polymyxin adjuvant against multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacteria through oxidative stress modulation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies A22 as a novel polymyxin adjuvant that enhances the efficacy of polymyxin B (PB) against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa DK2 and other Gram-negative bacteria. A22 reduces bacterial resistance development and shows minimal cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial and synergistic activities of A22 using in vitro and in vivo assays, including MIC testing, time-kill assays, and animal models.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-confirmation by using a machine learning model directly on routine automated susceptibility testing results.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a machine learning model to rapidly confirm extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production using minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) from routine antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) results. The model achieved high performance metrics, demonstrating potential to shorten time-to-detection of ESBL-producing bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized machine learning algorithms (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost) to predict ESBL-production based on MIC-values from AST data.

full_output.paper_title: A novel mutation of ramR involved in tigecycline resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, complementation experiments, and RT-qPCR were used to validate the role of the ramR mutation in tigecycline resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study compares the effectiveness of ceftriaxone and ceftaroline in combination with ampicillin or penicillin against Enterococcus faecalis, highlighting that ceftaroline-based combinations show better activity and synergy against borderline-PRASEF isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution and 24-hour time-kill assays to evaluate antimicrobial activity against E. faecalis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Flagellar motility and the mucus environment influence aggregation-mediated antibiotic tolerance of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in chronic lung infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that loss of flagellar motility, specifically through mutations in fliC, flgE, motAB, and motCD, increases antibiotic tolerance and aggregation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa under mucin-rich conditions. These findings highlight the critical role of flagellar motility in determining antibiotic tolerance and aggregate formation in chronic lung infections.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic mutants of P. aeruginosa, confocal microscopy, and MIC assays to investigate the effects of flagellar motility on antibiotic tolerance and aggregation in a mucin-rich environment.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in Salmonella enterica isolates from Mexico, including genes conferring resistance to aminoglycosides, beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, sulfonamides, tetracyclines, phenicols, and colistin. Notable genes include aph(4)-Ia, aadA, aph(3')-Ib, blaCTX-M-65, fosA3, qnrB19, sul1, tetA, and others.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in silico prediction of antibiotic resistance genes using the Resistance Gene Identifier (RGI) v6.0.3 integrated with the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD v3.2.9).

full_output.paper_title: A combined in silico and MD simulation approach to discover novel LpxC inhibitors targeting multiple drug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies compound P-2 as a potential lead inhibitor of LpxC, a key enzyme in lipid A biosynthesis, for combating multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: In silico methods including molecular docking, ADMET profiling, DFT calculations, and MD simulations were used to identify and validate compound P-2 as a LpxC inhibitor.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and laboratory indicators predicting coagulase-negative staphylococci as a cause of bloodstream infection among children below five years of age admitted at a tertiary hospital in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mecA as a gene conferring methicillin and oxacillin resistance in coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) isolated from bloodstream infections in children.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: In silico and in vitro comparative analysis of 79 Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaADC-25 as a prevalent cephalosporinase gene in 78 out of 79 A. baumannii isolates, contributing to resistance against multiple beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico analysis using ResFinder to identify antimicrobial resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance to oxyimino-cephalosporins conferred by an alternative mechanism of hydrolysis by the Acinetobacter-derived cephalosporinase-33 (ADC-33), a class C β-lactamase present in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAb).

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial profile and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of community and hospital-acquired urinary tract infections among UTI suspected geriatrics in Gondar town, Northwest Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of bacterial urinary tract infections (UTIs) among geriatrics in Gondar town, with Escherichia coli being the most common pathogen. High levels of resistance to several antibiotics were observed, including nalidixic acid, tetracycline, and ampicillin. Piperacillin-tazobactam and meropenem were found to be the most effective antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted urine cultures and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Fingolimod as a potent anti-Staphylococcus aureus: pH-dependent cell envelope damage and eradication of biofilms/persisters.
full_output.key_findings: Fingolimod exhibits potent bactericidal activity against Gram-positive bacteria, including S. aureus, E. faecalis, and S. agalactiae, with MICs ranging from 1.56 to 12.5 μg/mL. It effectively eliminates persisters, inhibits biofilm formation, and disrupts bacterial cell envelopes. Resistance development was minimal, and phospholipids, especially cardiolipin, reduced its antibacterial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: MIC assays, time-kill assays, biofilm inhibition, confocal microscopy, and whole-genome sequencing were used to evaluate Fingolimod's antibacterial activity and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: Clinical isolates from Shenzhen Nanshan People's Hospital

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, microbiology, and antimicrobial susceptibility profile of bacterial skin and soft tissue infections in pediatric patients with malignancies at a referral teaching hospital in Shiraz, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus as the most common pathogens causing bacterial skin and soft tissue infections (SSTIs) in pediatric oncology patients. It also found that E. coli was sensitive to ampicillin-sulbactam and colistin, while S. aureus was sensitive to chloramphenicol and cotrimoxazole.
full_output.methodology: The study used a descriptive cross-sectional design, analyzing data from 227 pediatric patients with malignancies. Bacterial cultures and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines.
