full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and sequencing were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in EIEC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A porin-like protein used by bacterial predators defines a wider lipid-trapping superfamily.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PopA, a porin-like protein from Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus, as part of a wider lipid-trapping superfamily. PopA forms a pentameric assembly that traps a lipid monolayer within its central chamber, distinguishing it from traditional porins.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis using X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM, and molecular dynamics simulations, alongside functional assays in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial effects and mechanisms of graphene oxide loaded on TiO(2)-nanotube-modified ti: an in vitro study.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that TNT-GO exhibits strong antibacterial activity against Porphyromonas gingivalis, likely through membrane disruption, oxidative stress, and phospholipid extraction mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized SEM, Raman spectroscopy, XRD, AFM, standard plate counting, MTT assay, fluorescence staining, SEM, TEM, LDH cytotoxicity assay, and ROS assay to evaluate the antibacterial effects and mechanisms of TNT-GO.

full_output.paper_title: Biological activities of optimized biosynthesized selenium nanoparticles using Proteus mirabilis PQ350419 alone or combined with chitosan and ampicillin against common multidrug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the antibacterial and antibiofilm activity of selenium nanoparticles (Se NPs) and a selenium/chitosan/ampicillin nanocomposite (Se/CS/AMP) against multidrug-resistant bacteria, including P. mirabilis, K. pneumoniae, and S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the biosynthesis of Se NPs using P. mirabilis PQ350419, optimization of synthesis conditions, and evaluation of antibacterial and antibiofilm activity through various assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that antibiotic administration significantly reduced Bifidobacterium abundance in very preterm infants, while increasing the abundance of Escherichia-Shigella and other genera. Sepsis was associated with altered microbiome trajectories, including lower Bifidobacterium and higher Escherichia-Shigella abundance.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA sequencing and quantitative PCR were used to analyze the gut microbiome of very preterm infants with and without sepsis.

full_output.paper_title: Different patterns of antimicrobial non-susceptibility of the nasopharyngeal carriage of Streptococcus pneumoniae in areas with high and low levels of PCV13 coverage.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates from areas with high PCV13 coverage had lower antimicrobial non-susceptibility rates compared to those from low coverage areas. High rates of resistance were observed to macrolides, clindamycin, and tetracycline, with 82.9% of isolates being multidrug-resistant.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed on 737 Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates using the micro-dilution method against 17 antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance genes circulating in Nigeria: a systematic review and meta-analysis from the One Health perspective.
full_output.key_findings: This study identified several antibiotic resistance genes circulating in Nigeria, including bla SHV, bla CTX-M, bla TEM, sul, tet, qnr, bla NDM, bla KPC, bla VIM, bla OXA, mec A, and erm. These genes were found in various bacterial species from human, animal, and environmental sources.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2015 and 2024.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of the risk of aerosol transmission of CRKP during bronchoscopy in the intensive care unit.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies KPC-2 as the resistance gene responsible for carbapenem resistance in CRKP isolates, highlighting the risk of aerosol transmission during bronchoscopy in ICU settings.
full_output.methodology: Sanger sequencing and MLST analysis were used to characterize CRKP isolates and identify the KPC-2 resistance gene.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial profile and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of urinary tract infection among diabetic patients at Bule Hora University Teaching Hospital, Southern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a 15.7% prevalence of bacterial urinary tract infections among diabetic patients, with E. coli being the most common pathogen. High resistance to ampicillin and amoxicillin-clavulanic acid was observed, and 43.6% of isolates were multidrug-resistant.
full_output.methodology: The study used urine culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Bithionol is ineffective in a mouse model of S. aureus implant-associated osteomyelitis despite potent in vitro activity.
full_output.key_findings: Bithionol showed potent in vitro activity against S. aureus, including against persister cells, but was ineffective in reducing bacterial load in a murine model of implant-associated osteomyelitis.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo experiments, including MIC, MBC, MBEC, checkerboard assays, and a murine IAOM model.

full_output.paper_title: Biological Studies of Silver Nanoparticles
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial and anti-biofilm activities of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized using different plant extracts. Tp-AgNPs showed the highest antibacterial and anti-biofilm efficacy against various bacterial strains, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized agar well diffusion assay, MIC/MBC determination, and biofilm inhibition assays to evaluate the antibacterial and anti-biofilm activities of AgNPs.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of polyphosphate-binding proteins in Escherichia coli uncovers targets involved in translation control and ribosome biogenesis.

rnr.notes: mutant failed to interact with polyP

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies YihI and Rnr as novel polyP-binding proteins in E. coli, highlighting their roles in translation control and ribosome biogenesis.
full_output.methodology: In vitro polyP-binding assays and genetic manipulation of E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: Population-based microbiological characterization of Nocardia strains causing invasive infections during a multiyear period in a large Canadian healthcare region.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the antimicrobial susceptibility of various Nocardia species complexes, highlighting resistance patterns to imipenem and ceftriaxone in certain complexes.
full_output.methodology: The study used MALDI-TOF MS and 16S rRNA gene sequencing for species identification and performed antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Massive culture-based approach for the screening of AmpC, ESBL, and carbapenemase producers from rectal swabs.

blaNDM.validation_method: modified carbapenem inactivation method and detection of carbapenemase-encoding genes

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a massive culture-based approach for the screening of AmpC, ESBL, and carbapenemase producers from rectal swabs, demonstrating improved specificity for detecting ESBL producers compared to conventional methods. It identifies various beta-lactamase genes, including bla CTX-M-1/2-like, bla CTX-M-8-like, bla CTX-M-9-like, bla SHV-like, bla TEM-like, bla GES-like, bla MOX, bla CIT, bla DHA, bla ACC, bla EBC, bla FOX, bla CMY-2, and bla NDM.
full_output.methodology: The method involves enrichment on MacConkey agar supplemented with ceftriaxone, followed by replica plating under selective pressures to differentiate between AmpC, ESBL, and carbapenemase producers. PCR and amplicon sequencing were used for gene detection and confirmation.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic features of three major diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli pathotypes in India.

qnrS1.validation_method: characterized as a non-conjugative plasmid encoding the quinolone resistance gene

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a variety of acquired antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli (DEC) strains from India, highlighting the prevalence of resistance to multiple antibiotic classes, including aminoglycosides, beta-lactams, sulfonamides, and tetracyclines. Key AMR genes include blaTEM-105, strB, strA, mphA, sul1, sul2, addA1-pm, tetA, tetB, blaCTX-M15, blaCTX-M27, and blaDHA-1. Additionally, mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining regions (QRDRs) of gyrA and parC were found to contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, bioinformatics analysis, and plasmid replicon analysis were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and mutations in DEC strains.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptomic profiling of ceftriaxone-tolerant phenotypes of Neisseria gonorrhoeae reveals downregulation of ribosomal genes - a pilot study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified downregulation of ribosomal genes and associated genes in ceftriaxone-tolerant Neisseria gonorrhoeae, suggesting a potential mechanism for bacterial survival under antibiotic stress.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis using RNA-Seq to compare gene expression between ceftriaxone-tolerant and control isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Purification and characterization of a novel antibacterial peptide against Clostridium perfringens.
full_output.key_findings: A novel antibacterial peptide, IP HG88, was identified and characterized from Bacillus velezensis HG88, which exhibits potent antimicrobial activity against Clostridium perfringens.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, peptide purification, and antimicrobial activity assays were used to identify and characterize the antibacterial peptide.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial resistance in human- and poultry-derived Campylobacter jejuni isolates from Hangzhou, China.

gyrA.evidence_note: The paper states that the T86I mutation in gyrA was predominant, detected in 91.5% (43/47) of isolates, and that strain J26 exhibited a rare gyrA Thr86Val (T86V) mutation while maintaining NAL and CIP resistance.

gyrA.notes: The T86I mutation was predominant, detected in 91.5% (43/47) of isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in Campylobacter jejuni isolates, including gyrA mutations (T86I and T86V) associated with quinolone resistance, tet(O) for tetracycline resistance, and various beta-lactamase genes (blaOXA-61, blaOXA-193, blaOXA-450, blaOXA-451, blaOXA-452, blaOXA-453, blaOXA-489) linked to beta-lactam resistance. Additionally, aminoglycoside resistance genes APH(3')-IIIa and ant(6)-Ia were found in some isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and gene detection using CARD and ResFinder databases.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents novel N-arylpyrrole derivatives with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against ESKAPE pathogens, MRSA, and Mycobacterium phlei. Compounds Vb, Vc, and Ve showed improved activity against MRSA compared to levofloxacin, while Vc exhibited potent anti-tubercular activity. The compounds also demonstrated significant antibiofilm and antivirulence properties.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized ligand-based drug design, molecular modeling, and in vitro antimicrobial testing to evaluate the synthesized compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic Inhibition of Metalloproteases by Tetracyclines During Infection by Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas.
full_output.key_findings: Tetracyclines inhibit the metalloprotease LasB, reducing inflammation and sensitizing Pseudomonas to immune cell killing, even in multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Computational modeling, biochemical assays, and in vitro and in vivo experiments with human neutrophils and a murine pulmonary model.

full_output.paper_title: Global analysis of the Hfq-mediated RNA interactome discovers a MicA homolog that affects the cytotoxicity, biofilm formation, and resistance to complement of Bordetella pertussis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CT_532 as a MicA homolog in Bordetella pertussis, which affects cytotoxicity, biofilm formation, and resistance to complement. Mutant analysis shows that the deletion of the first 22 nucleotides of CT_532 leads to reduced cytotoxicity and impaired biofilm production but increased resistance to complement.
full_output.methodology: RIL-seq, Northern blot, RT-qPCR, and mutant analysis were used to characterize the role of CT_532 in B. pertussis.

full_output.paper_title: Determining genotype and antimicrobial resistance of Salmonella Typhi in environmental samples by amplicon sequencing.

gyrA.notes: Detected in Hospital-4, Hospital-6, Hospital-7

parC.notes: Detected in Study-43

full_output.key_findings: The study identified fluoroquinolone-resistant S. Typhi strains through detection of gyrA mutations (S83Y, S83F, E84K) in wastewater samples using amplicon sequencing.
full_output.methodology: Amplicon sequencing and SNP detection in wastewater samples for genotyping and AMR gene profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Competitive exclusion approach using an E. coli live vaccine to protect broilers from colonization with ESBL-/ pAmpC- E. coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes two E. coli strains carrying the bla CTX-M-15 and bla CMY-2 genes, which confer resistance to cephalosporins and other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genetic characterization of E. coli strains and monitoring of colonization in broiler chickens.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial resistance of Salmonella enterica isolated from cattle farms in Inner Mongolia.

blaCMY-2.validation_method: PCR detection of drug resistance target genes

blaLAP-1.validation_method: PCR detection of drug resistance target genes

qnrA.validation_method: PCR detection of drug resistance target genes

aac(6').validation_method: PCR detection of drug resistance target genes

cat1.validation_method: PCR detection of drug resistance target genes

flor.validation_method: PCR detection of drug resistance target genes

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Salmonella enterica isolates from Inner Mongolia, including bla TEM-1, cmlA, tetA, tetB, tetM, aadA2, aph(3')-IIa, aacC4, aac(3)-IIa, sul1, sul3, oqxA, and oqxB, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, chloramphenicol, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides, sulfonamides, and quinolones.
full_output.methodology: PCR, WGS, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Punicalagin as a Key Bioactive Compound Responsible for the Antimicrobial Properties of Punica granatum L. Peel Extract against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Punicalagin was identified as a key bioactive compound in pomegranate peel extract with strong antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, showing a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 16 μg/mL.
full_output.methodology: Bioassay-guided fractionation, HPLC, LC-MS, and growth inhibition assays were used to identify and characterize the antimicrobial activity of punicalagin.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa Cryptic Prophage Endolysin Is a Highly Active Muramidase.

Pa GH19Lys.mechanism: cleaves the β-1,4 linkage between N-acetylmuramic acid and N-acetyl-d-glucosamine in peptidoglycan
Pa GH19Lys.validation_method: enzymatic activity assay, crystal structure determination

full_output.key_findings: Pa GH19Lys is a highly active muramidase that cleaves the β-1,4 linkage between N-acetylmuramic acid and N-acetyl-d-glucosamine in peptidoglycan, demonstrating potent lytic activity against Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Expression, purification, and enzymatic activity assays of Pa GH19Lys, along with crystal structure determination.

full_output.paper_title: Anticorrosion and antimicrobial performance of extracted and fractionated phytochemicals of terminalia bentzoe leaves.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the anticorrosion and antimicrobial properties of methanolic extract (ME), aqueous fraction (QF), and n-butanol fraction (nBF) of Terminalia bentzoe leaves. The nBF fraction exhibited the highest corrosion inhibition efficiency of 94.4% at 60 ppm. The antimicrobial activity of the fractions was assessed against various bacteria and fungi, with nBF showing the highest inhibition zones against Shigella and Candida.
full_output.methodology: The study involved extraction and fractionation of Terminalia bentzoe leaves, followed by electrochemical tests, surface analysis, and antimicrobial activity assessment using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion technique.

full_output.paper_title: AEPMA: peptide-microbe association prediction based on autoevolutionary heterogeneous graph learning.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel anti-Staphylococcus aureus peptide and an anti-Escherichia coli peptide using a computational framework called AEPMA, which predicts peptide-microbe associations.
full_output.methodology: AEPMA uses an autoevolutionary heterogeneous graph to predict peptide-microbe associations, incorporating similarity calculations and message passing mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: High-yield bioproduction of virus-free virus-like P4-EKORhE multi-lysin transducing particles as an antimicrobial gene therapeutic.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the development of a high-yield bioproduction system for virus-free virus-like P4-EKORhE transducing particles carrying a multi-lysin cassette, which effectively exhibits antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: The research involved constructing and optimizing a P4-EKORhE system for high-yield production of transducing particles, utilizing optical density measurements and mass spectrometry to evaluate the efficacy of the multi-lysin cassette.

full_output.paper_title: Development and application of a curcumin-cinnamon essential oil nanoemulsion agent against mycobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a curcumin-cinnamon essential oil (Cur-CEO) nanoemulsion with potent antimicrobial activity against mycobacteria, achieving MIC values of 2 µg/mL for M. smegmatis and 0.25 µg/mL for M. tuberculosis. The nanoemulsion demonstrated effectiveness in inhibiting both surface and airborne mycobacteria and showed good lung deposition characteristics.
full_output.methodology: The Cur-CEO nanoemulsion was prepared and optimized using ultrasonic treatment, and its antimicrobial activity was evaluated through MIC and MBC assays, along with assessments of membrane permeability and aerosol efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into the Enhanced Ceftazidime Hydrolysis by Ent385 AmpC β‑Lactamase from Multiscale Simulations.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the Ent385 AmpC β-lactamase as a key player in enhanced ceftazidime hydrolysis, revealing that Tyr150 acts as a base in the deacylation process, facilitating efficient antibiotic degradation.
full_output.methodology: Quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations were used to investigate the molecular mechanisms of ceftazidime hydrolysis by the Ent385 AmpC β-lactamase.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriophage infection drives loss of β-lactam resistance in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.key_findings: Bacteriophage infection leads to the loss of β-lactam resistance in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) through mutations in genes such as femA, mgrA, sarA, arlR, and spoVG.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, phenotypic analysis, and transcriptomic profiling were used to identify mutations and their effects on β-lactam resistance and virulence in MRSA.
full_output.sample_size: Three MRSA strains (MRSA252, MW2, and LAC) were studied.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic insights into the diversity, antimicrobial resistance and zoonotic potential of Campylobacter fetus across diverse hosts and geographies.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified five AMR genes in Campylobacter fetus, including tet(O), tet(44), ant(6)-Ib, aph(3′)-III, and lnu(C), which confer resistance to tetracyclines, streptomycin, amikacin, and lincomycin. These genes were detected in human and animal isolates from various geographic regions.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis using Abricate and AMRFinderPlus to detect AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, Identification, and Antibiogram Characteristics of Staphylococcus aureus From Dairy Cows Kept Under Extensive Management System, in the Uba DebreTsehay District of Southern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: Staphylococcus aureus isolates from dairy cows in the Uba Debretsehay District of Southern Ethiopia showed 100% susceptibility to amoxicillin-clavulanate, cefoxitin, ciprofloxacin, chloramphenicol, oxacillin, trimethoprim-sulphamethoxazole, and gentamicin, but 0% susceptibility to penicillin G and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method on 10 antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of Essential Oil of Algrizea minor Sobral, Faria & Proença (Myrtaceae) in Combating Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus: Antibacterial and Virulence Modulation Studies Conducted In Vitro and In Vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Algrizea minor essential oil (EOAM) exhibits synergistic effects with amoxicillin and oxacillin against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), reducing biofilm formation and enhancing the efficacy of hydrogen peroxide. EOAM also increased the survival of Galleria mellonella larvae infected with MRSA.
full_output.methodology: Chemical analysis, MIC determination, checkerboard method, kill curve, biofilm assays, hydrogen peroxide sensitivity, coagulase assay, hemolysis assay, and in vivo experiments with Galleria mellonella larvae.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid diversity in Klebsiella pneumoniae ST307 co-producing KPC plus NDM recovered during the COVID-19 pandemic.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the plasmid diversity in Klebsiella pneumoniae ST307 isolates co-producing KPC and NDM carbapenemases, identifying multiple resistance genes and plasmid types involved in carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, S1 nuclease-PFGE, and transcriptional analysis were used to characterize plasmid diversity and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci utilise antibiotic-enriched nutrients for intestinal colonisation.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) utilize increased nutrient availability and decreased microbial metabolites in antibiotic-treated gut microbiomes to promote their growth. Specific nutrients like monosaccharides, disaccharides, and amino acids were identified as critical for VRE growth.
full_output.methodology: Ex vivo faecal culture experiments, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and 1H-NMR spectroscopy were used to analyze changes in gut microbiome composition and metabolite profiles following antibiotic treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the prevalence of methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MR-CoNS) in Africa, highlighting the presence of mecA, mecA1, and mecC genes in various species such as Staphylococcus epidermidis, Staphylococcus haemolyticus, and Mammaliicoccus sciuri.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 65 studies from 16 African countries, employing PCR and whole-genome sequencing for gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Investigating the in-vitro antimicrobial activities of sorghum [Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench] phenolic extracts on liver abscess causing bacterial pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial effects of sorghum phenolic extracts on liver abscess causing bacterial pathogens, demonstrating significant inhibition of Fusobacterium necrophorum subspecies and Trueperella pyogenes, but not Salmonella enterica serotype Lubbock.
full_output.methodology: Phenolic compounds were extracted from sorghum and tested using broth macro-dilution and micro-dilution methods to determine antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Cross-border spread of a mosaic resistance (OXA-48) and virulence (aerobactin) plasmid in Klebsiella pneumoniae: a European Antimicrobial Resistance Genes Surveillance Network investigation, Europe, February 2019 to October 2024.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the cross-border spread of a mosaic plasmid carrying the OXA-48 carbapenemase and aerobactin virulence genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae across eight European countries.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis of K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Investigating the effects of dietary and management modifications on Salmonella enterica population in harvest-ready beef cattle.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that a high-starch diet may reduce Salmonella prevalence in cattle lymph nodes, potentially mitigating Salmonella risks in beef products. Most Salmonella isolates were pansusceptible, with only a few antibiotic-resistant strains identified, which were likely not persistent due to a lack of selective pressure.
full_output.methodology: The study used a double-blinded, randomized controlled feedlot study to evaluate the effects of dietary and feeding management changes on Salmonella prevalence and antibiotic susceptibility profiles in cattle.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of First-in-Class Inhibitors Targeting a Pathogen-Associated Aminoglycoside-Resistance 16S rRNA Methyltransferase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NpmA as a key mediator of aminoglycoside resistance through 16S rRNA methylation and reports the discovery of first-in-class inhibitors targeting a unique Y-shaped pocket in NpmA.
full_output.methodology: Virtual screening, docking, and in vitro methylation assays were used to identify and validate NpmA inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Machine learning-based prediction of antimicrobial resistance and identification of AMR-related SNPs in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies key SNPs associated with antimicrobial resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis using machine learning, highlighting mutations in rpoB, katG, gyrA, embB, and inhA linked to resistance against rifampicin, isoniazid, ciprofloxacin, and ethambutol.
full_output.methodology: The study employs machine learning algorithms and whole-genome sequencing data to predict antimicrobial resistance and identify AMR-related SNPs in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the Structural Design, Antibacterial Activity, and Molecular Docking of Newly Synthesized Zn(II) Complexes with NNO-Donor Carbazate Ligands.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial activity of Zn(II) complexes with carbazate ligands, demonstrating that complex (3) exhibited the highest antibacterial activity against cariogenic and anaerobic bacteria, particularly against S. mutans, S. sobrinus, and P. anaerobius.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and structural characterization of Zn(II) complexes, followed by in vitro antibacterial testing and molecular docking studies.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring Daptomycin Hypersensitivity in Enterococcus faecium: The Impact of LafB Mutation on Bacterial Virulence.

full_output.methodology: Protein expression, purification, biophysical characterization, in silico modeling, growth curve analysis, biofilm formation assay, and in vivo virulence assessment in a Galleria mellonella model.

full_output.paper_title: Combinatorial Effects of CPP-Modified Antimicrobial Peptides: Synergistic and Additive Interactions Against Pathogenic Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antimicrobial activity of three designed peptides—R44K S *, V31K S *, and R23F S *—engineered to incorporate an amyloidogenic fragment from the S1 protein of Staphylococcus aureus and cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) fragments. The results show that these peptides exhibit significant antibacterial activity, with combinations showing enhanced inhibitory effects and reduced minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs), suggesting synergistic or additive interactions.
full_output.methodology: The antimicrobial activity of the peptides and their combinations was assessed against various bacterial strains using a liquid medium and the checkerboard assay to determine synergistic responses.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, Antimicrobial Activities, and Model of Action of Novel Tetralone Derivatives Containing Aminoguanidinium Moiety.
full_output.key_findings: Compound 2D exhibits potent antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, with MIC values of 0.5/4 µg/mL and 1/4 µg/mL against S. aureus ATCC 29213 and MRSA-2, respectively. It disrupts bacterial membrane integrity and shows low hemolytic activity and cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, in vitro antibacterial activity testing, membrane permeabilization assays, and molecular docking studies.

full_output.paper_title: Dual-Mode Antibacterial Orthodontic Composite: Contact-Killing QACs and Sustained CHX Release via Large-Pore Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a dual-mode antibacterial orthodontic composite using QLMSN@CHX, which combines contact-killing QACs and sustained CHX release, effectively eradicating biofilms and maintaining mechanical properties.
full_output.methodology: Characterization of nanoparticles, antibacterial property analysis, and mechanical testing.

full_output.paper_title: An mRNA Vaccine Targeting the C-Terminal Region of P1 Protein Induces an Immune Response and Protects Against Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The mRNA-SP+P1 vaccine targeting the C-terminal region of the P1 protein induces humoral and cellular immune responses, providing protection against Mycoplasma pneumoniae, including partial cross-protection against the ST3 drug-resistant strain.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of the mRNA-SP+P1 vaccine in BALB/c mice through ELISA, flow cytometry, adhesion inhibition assays, and transcriptome analysis.

Iron limitation via deferiprone reduced ceftazidime MICs, suggesting a potential strategy to enhance antibiotic efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-wide antibiotic-CRISPRi profiling identifies LiaR activation as a strategy to resensitize fluoroquinolone-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies recF, recJ, efp, liaS, and spxA2 as genes involved in fluoroquinolone susceptibility in Streptococcus pneumoniae. Deletion of these genes affects the bacterium's sensitivity to fluoroquinolones, highlighting their roles in DNA repair, protein synthesis, and stress response.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide CRISPRi-seq screens, phenotypic validation, RNA-seq, and overexpression experiments were used to identify and characterize genes affecting fluoroquinolone susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial potential and chromatographic profiling of bioactive compounds from endophytic Streptomyces sp. strain MIRK71 isolated from Mirabilis jalapa (L.).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Streptomyces sp. strain MIRK71 as a potent producer of antimicrobial compounds with activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens. GC-MS and HPTLC analyses revealed 20 volatile organic compounds, some of which exhibited antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation of endophytic actinobacteria, molecular identification via 16S rRNA sequencing, antimicrobial screening using agar well diffusion, and chemical profiling via GC-MS and HPTLC.

full_output.paper_title: Innovo GenMax MTB-RIF/INH: a moderate-complexity automated NAAT for rapid simultaneous detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and rifampin/isoniazid resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the Innovo GenMax MTB-RIF/INH assay for the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and resistance to rifampin and isoniazid. It identifies specific genes involved in resistance mechanisms, including rpoB, katG, inhA, and ahpC.
full_output.methodology: The study uses sequencing of gene fragments (IS6110, rpoB, ahpC, inhA, and katG) to validate resistance findings.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and characterization of ESBL-producing diarrheagenic Escherichia coli from the poultry industry in Shanghai, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several beta-lactamase genes, including bla TEM-1B, bla CTX-M-55, bla OXA-10, and bla CTX-M-65, which confer resistance to various antibiotics in ESBL-producing diarrheagenic E. coli isolates from poultry farms in Shanghai, China.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Arenaria serpyllifolia as a Natural Antiviolaceum Agent: Phytochemical, Biological, and Molecular Approaches.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that Arenaria serpyllifolia extract exhibits strong antimicrobial activity against Chromobacterium violaceum, with a minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) of <5 mg/mL. The extract also showed significant antibiofilm and anti-quorum sensing (QS) effects, inhibiting violacein production by up to 91.6%. Molecular docking and MD simulations indicated that compounds like levoglucosan and guanosine have strong binding affinities to the CviR receptor, suggesting their potential as QS inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized GC-MS for chemical profiling, molecular docking, and MD simulations to evaluate the binding interactions of compounds in A. serpyllifolia extract with the CviR receptor, along with antimicrobial and QS assays.

full_output.paper_title: Adaptive laboratory-evolved MRSA with PPEF manifests cross-susceptibility to oxacillin and hypersensitivity to ciprofloxacin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the downregulation of several AMR genes, including blaZ, mecR1, kdpB, ble, pbp, and ermA, in PPEF-evolved MRSA-PR strains, leading to increased susceptibility to antibiotics such as oxacillin, ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, and imipenem.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing, qRT-PCR, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of bla(CTX-M-55)-carrying Escherichia coli in both ceftiofur-use and non-use pig farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla CTX-M-55 as the primary ESBL/AmpC β-lactamase gene responsible for ceftiofur resistance in E. coli from pigs and their farm environment in South Korea. Other genes like bla CMY-2, bla DHA-1, and mcr-1 were also found to contribute to resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed E. coli isolates from pig feces and farm environments using PCR and sequencing to identify resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies variations in the microbiota and inflammatory profiles of Pseudomonas aeruginosa-infected patients with bronchiectasis, highlighting the importance of microbiota diversity and geographical region in determining the effectiveness of inhaled antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized 16S rRNA sequencing, proteomics, and Olink analysis to characterize the microbiota and proteome of sputum samples from patients in the ORBIT-3 and ORBIT-4 trials.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance of non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli in a tertiary hospital in Niger: a prospective cross-sectional study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli (NFGNB), including carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii and P. aeruginosa, highlighting the urgent need for improved antibiotic stewardship and infection control measures.
full_output.methodology: Prospective cross-sectional study involving antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: A single-center investigation on serotypes, drug resistance and clinical significance of GBS isolates from pregnant and non-pregnant adults in Baoji, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates to erythromycin, azithromycin, levofloxacin, clindamycin, tetracycline, and chloramphenicol among GBS isolates, with serotypes Ib, III, and V being the most common.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 200 GBS isolates using antimicrobial susceptibility testing and serotyping methods.

full_output.paper_title: The challenge of multidrug resistance in hospitalized pediatric patients with urinary tract infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) among pediatric urinary tract infections (UTIs) in Lebanon, with a focus on resistance patterns in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella spp. It identifies risk factors for MDRO infections, including recent antibiotic use and a history of leukemia.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective chart review of pediatric UTI cases from two tertiary medical centers in Beirut, analyzing resistance patterns and risk factors for MDRO infections.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effects of modified triple antibiotic paste (mTAP) containing azithromycin (AZM) versus traditional triple antibiotic paste (TAP) in resolving periapical inflammation. mTAP showed comparable antibacterial effects to TAP but did not cause tooth discoloration. The study also analyzed the root canal microbiome using 16S rDNA sequencing, revealing changes in bacterial composition post-treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vivo and in vitro experiments, including micro-CT imaging, histological analysis, ELISA, and 16S rDNA sequencing to evaluate the effects of mTAP and TAP on periapical inflammation and root canal microbiota.

full_output.paper_title: Association between farm-level antimicrobial usage and antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli isolates from healthy swine in ten farms in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a positive association between farm-level antimicrobial usage and antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates from swine, highlighting the role of multidrug-resistant E. coli in complicating antimicrobial resistance on farms.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance rates in E. coli isolates from swine fecal samples using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion test and evaluated the association between antimicrobial resistance and farm-level antimicrobial usage.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin Sensitization in Pseudomonas aeruginosa is Contingent on Limited Metabolic Flux.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that Pseudomonas aeruginosa can be sensitized to vancomycin and other gram-positive antibiotics under nutrient-limited conditions. It also finds that certain resistance genes like catB7, fosA, and sul1 are present in strains that show increased sensitivity to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study uses MIC testing, efflux pump analysis, and carbon source supplementation experiments to explore the mechanisms of antibiotic sensitization in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance among ICU patients during the COVID-19 pandemic and its associated factors: a retrospective study using electronic medical records in two Vietnamese hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: High prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and multidrug resistance (MDR) was observed among ICU patients, particularly in Acinetobacter spp., Klebsiella spp., and P. aeruginosa. The study highlighted the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on AMR trends and identified various factors associated with AMR prevalence.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of electronic medical records, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and logistic regression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Higher-order epistasis drives evolutionary unpredictability toward novel antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the TEM-1 beta-lactamase and identifies multiple mutations that enhance resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics, emphasizing the role of higher-order epistasis in the evolution of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) activity.
full_output.methodology: Combinatorial mutant library screening, barcode sequencing, and fitness landscape analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of gold nanoparticles and γ-cyclodextrin polymer on physicochemical, antimicrobial, and antibiofilm properties of a novel schiff base derived from dialdehyde cellulose and camphor thiazole-imine.

full_output.key_findings: Quercetin-functionalized silver and copper nanoparticles (Qn@AgNPs and Qn@CuNPs) were synthesized and demonstrated potent antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus, with significantly lower MIC values compared to free quercetin and metal ions. full_output.paper_title: Prophage-encoded methyltransferase drives adaptation of community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pamA, a prophage-encoded adenine methyltransferase, as a key driver of increased skin abscess size in community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA). pamA enhances virulence by upregulating fnbA, a fibronectin-binding protein A, leading to increased biofilm formation and inflammation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic deletions, complementation, RNA-Seq, and proteomic analyses to validate the role of pamA and fnbA in CA-MRSA virulence.

full_output.methodology: Case report and literature review.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates from sternal bursitis in chickens, including beta-lactamases (blaTEM-1B, blaTEM-1A, blaTEM-1C, blaCTX-M-1, blaOXA-10), chloramphenicol resistance genes (catA1, cmlA1, floR), aminoglycoside resistance genes (aph(6)-Id, aph(3")-Ib, aadA1, aadA2b, aadA5, aadA9, aadA13, sat2), quinolone resistance gene (qnrS1), tetracycline resistance gene (tetA), sulfonamide resistance genes (sul1, sul2, sul3), and efflux pump genes (acrF, mdtM, ermE, qacE, qacL, terD, terW, terZ). Mutations in gyrA (p.S83L) and parC (p.E84G, p.S80I) were associated with quinolone resistance, and a mutation in glpT (E448K) was linked to fosfomycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and PCR were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates from sternal bursitis in chickens.

full_output.key_findings: Xeruborbactam in combination with meropenem shows potent activity against carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, including strains resistant to other β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations. Specific β-lactamases like blaIMP-23 and blaSPM-1 were identified as resistant to xeruborbactam.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, MIC determination, and genetic analysis of β-lactamases.

full_output.paper_title: Organism profiles and empirical treatments for periprosthetic joint infections.
full_output.key_findings: Gram-positive bacteria were the predominant pathogens associated with PJI, with high rates of methicillin resistance and multidrug resistance. The combination of vancomycin and meropenem is an empirical antibiotic regimen for culture-negative chronic PJI patients in this region, with the combination of linezolid and meropenem as an alternative. For patients with culture-negative acute postoperative PJI, vancomycin combined with ceftazidime is suggested as the preferred empirical therapy.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of pathogen profiles and antibiotic sensitivities of PJI patients treated at the center.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic Mechanisms of Phenothiazine Drugs: A Mini-Review of Advances in Cancer Treatment and Antibiotic Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: Phenothiazines demonstrate potential in cancer treatment by inducing cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, and modulating key signaling pathways. They also show antibacterial activity by targeting efflux pumps and restoring antibiotic susceptibility in multidrug-resistant pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Narrative review of preclinical studies on phenothiazines' applications in oncology and infectious diseases.

full_output.paper_title: Sugar phosphate-mediated inhibition of peptidoglycan precursor synthesis.

glmU.encodes: bifunctional enzyme that converts glucosamine-1P to UDP-GlcNAc
glmU.validation_method: in vitro biochemical assay, targeted metabolomics, genetic overexpression

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies GlmU as a critical target for antibiotic susceptibility in Vibrio cholerae, demonstrating that glucose-1-phosphate (G1P) competitively inhibits GlmU, leading to impaired peptidoglycan synthesis and increased susceptibility to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: In vitro biochemical assays, targeted metabolomics, genetic manipulation, and molecular modeling were used to validate the role of GlmU in glucose toxicity and peptidoglycan synthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Dietary impact on the gut resistome: western diet independently increases the prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes within the gut microbiota.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that a western diet independently increases the prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the gut microbiota without antibiotic exposure. Specifically, ARGs such as ErmG, CfxA2, tetQ, lnuC, and mefA were found to be significantly enriched in the gut microbiota of mice fed a western diet.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing, qPCR, and Biolog Phenotype MicroArrays were used to analyze the gut resistome and antibiotic resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Combatting virulent gut bacteria by inhibiting the biosynthesis of a two-component lanthipeptide toxin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes peptide boronic acid inhibitors targeting the serine protease CylA, which is essential for the maturation of the enterococcal cytolysin toxin. These inhibitors block cytolysin maturation and reduce hemolytic activity in C+ E. faecalis.
full_output.methodology: The study uses synthetic chemistry, enzymatic assays, and biochemical analyses to develop and evaluate peptide boronic acid inhibitors of CylA.

full_output.paper_title: Modulation of Gut Microbiota and Antibiotic Resistance Genes by Heat-Killed Enterococcus faecalis EF-2001 in High-Fat Diet-Induced Obesity Mice: A Shotgun Metagenomics Study.
full_output.key_findings: Heat-killed Enterococcus faecalis EF-2001 reduced the abundance of multidrug resistance genes, including bcrA, cdeA, and msbA, in high-fat diet-induced obese mice, suggesting a protective role against antibiotic resistance spread.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomics and bioinformatic analysis of gut microbiota and antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: First Detection of Rhodococcus equi in a Foal in Bulgaria-A Case Report.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first documented case of VapA-positive Rhodococcus equi infection in a foal in Bulgaria, highlighting the importance of early detection and targeted therapy for this intracellular pathogen.
full_output.methodology: Microbiological tests and PCR were used to confirm the presence of VapA-positive R. equi.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a Novel Antibacterial Function of Mammalian Calreticulin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies calreticulin as a novel antibacterial protein with activity against Gram-negative bacteria, including Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhimurium, and Pasteurella multocida, through mechanisms involving bacterial binding and aggregation.
full_output.methodology: Expression and purification of recombinant calreticulin, antibacterial activity assays, bacterial binding and aggregation assays, and in vivo evaluation in lambs.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating Host Defense Peptides: A Comparative Analysis of Synthetic Peptides and Recombinant Concatemers.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares the antimicrobial activity and structural characteristics of synthetic and recombinant host defense peptides (HDPs) produced in Lactococcus lactis. The recombinant forms showed improved antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity compared to their synthetic counterparts, with some demonstrating higher efficacy against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized chemical synthesis and recombinant production in Lactococcus lactis to generate HDPs, followed by evaluation of their antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and endotoxin-binding activities.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of a Potent Antimicrobial Peptide Through Rational Design: A New Frontier in Pathogen Control.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the design and characterization of a novel antimicrobial peptide, RKW, which shows broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens, including ESKAPE bacteria and fungi, with minimal inhibitory concentrations (MBC) ranging from 5 µM to 20 µM.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in silico design, circular dichroism spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, and antimicrobial assays to evaluate the properties and effectiveness of the peptide RKW.

full_output.paper_title: Resistome and Phylogenomics of Escherichia coli Strains Obtained from Diverse Sources in Jimma, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified CTX-M-15 and NDM-1 as the most prevalent beta-lactamase and carbapenemase genes in multidrug-resistant E. coli isolates from clinical and environmental sources in Jimma, Ethiopia. These genes contribute to resistance against multiple antibiotics, highlighting the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance in the region.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing, DNA microarray analysis, and multilocus sequence typing were used to characterize the resistome and phylogenomics of E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial-Resistant Staphylococcus spp. Harbored by Hedgehogs (Erinaceus europaeus) in Central Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of antimicrobial-resistant Staphylococcus spp. in hedgehogs, including the detection of the blaZ and mecA genes associated with beta-lactam resistance. Vancomycin-resistant strains were also found, but they lacked the vanA and vanB genes.
full_output.methodology: Molecular analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed on Staphylococcus isolates from hedgehogs.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence and Antibiotic Resistance Profiles of Staphylococcus aureus Isolated from Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Inhibitors-Associated Skin Lesions.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified S. aureus strains with high resistance to penicillins and tetracyclines, and characterized virulence genes such as clfA, clfB, and fib, which are associated with adherence and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of S. aureus strains, including antibiotic susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assays, and multiplex PCR for virulence and resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Mechanisms of Aminoglycoside-Induced Ototoxicity in Murine Auditory Cells: Implications for Otoprotective Drug Development.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the molecular mechanisms of aminoglycoside-induced ototoxicity, focusing on the roles of TMC1 and OCT2 in gentamicin uptake and the involvement of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway in ototoxicity. It also evaluates the effectiveness of STS and NAC in reducing gentamicin-induced ototoxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study used transcriptomic analysis, Western blotting, and GTTR uptake assays to examine the molecular mechanisms of gentamicin-induced ototoxicity in murine auditory cell lines.

full_output.paper_title: In Silico and In Vitro Evaluation of Quinolone-Triazole Hybrid Derivatives as Potential Antimicrobial Agents
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial activity of quinolone-triazole hybrid derivatives, identifying compounds 10-15 as potent inhibitors of bacterial growth with MIC values ranging from 0.24 to 1.9 μg/mL against various pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Computational analysis, molecular docking, and in vitro antimicrobial testing were used to evaluate the compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Study on Antibacterial Activity of Water Extract of Galla chinensis Against Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of Galla chinensis (GC) water extract against carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE) and found that it significantly inhibited bacterial growth and reduced the activity of carbapenemase genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution assays, qRT-PCR, and transcriptome analysis to evaluate the antibacterial activity of GC extract against CPE.

full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, gene expression analysis, and population genomics were used to investigate the genetic basis of ML resistance in P. ovis mites.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla KPC-2 and bla KPC-3 as the most common carbapenemase genes in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, highlighting their role in resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and network analysis were used to characterize the genetic relatedness and transmission patterns of CR Kp isolates.

full_output.key_findings: This study identifies four molluscan metabolite compounds (CMNPD7125, CMNPD22991, CMNPD4542, and CMNPD12265) with potential as KasA inhibitors in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, showing stable binding and favorable interactions through in silico screening and molecular dynamics simulations.
full_output.methodology: In silico screening, molecular docking, ADMET analysis, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/GBSA calculations were used to evaluate the potential of molluscan metabolites as KasA inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Population Structure, Genomic Features, and Antibiotic Resistance of Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli in Shandong Province and Adjacent Regions, China (2008-2023).

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the genetic and phenotypic characteristics of APEC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Evaluation of Tricyclic Antidepressants Against S. aureus and the Possible Pathways of the Mechanism of Action.
full_output.key_findings: Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) exhibit antibacterial activity against S. aureus, showing bactericidal effects and synergistic interactions with oxacillin (OXA). The mechanism involves reducing cell viability through actions on genetic material and inducing oxidative stress.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution, checkerboard, flow cytometry, fluorescence microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were used to assess antibacterial activity and mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: Seven clinical isolates of S. aureus, including four MRSA and three MSSA, along with the S. aureus ATCC 6538p strain.

full_output.paper_title: In Salmonella Typhimurium and Bacillus subtilis, Nucleoid-Associated HU Proteins Are N-Terminally Acetylated.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the N-terminal acetylation of HU proteins in Salmonella Typhimurium and Bacillus subtilis by the acetyltransferases Se NatB and Bs YfmK, respectively. It also demonstrates that the methionine sulfoxide reductases MsrA and MsrB restore the acetylation of oxidized HU proteins.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biochemical purification, in vitro acetylation assays, mass spectrometry, and genetic manipulation techniques to investigate the acetylation of HU proteins and the role of MsrA and MsrB in restoring acetylation.

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and AMR genes (AMGs) in fish-associated bacteria, highlighting the presence of various resistance mechanisms such as beta-lactamases, tetracycline resistance genes, and fluoroquinolone resistance genes. It emphasizes the role of horizontal gene transfer and the importance of monitoring AMR in aquaculture systems.
full_output.methodology: Literature-based analysis of AMR and AMGs in fish-associated bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Molecular Characterization of Antimicrobial-Resistant Bacteria from Vegetable Foods.

TEM.evidence_note: The paper mentions the presence of the TEM gene in 14 out of 76 β-lactam-resistant strains.

CTX-M IV.evidence_note: The paper mentions the presence of CTX-M IV in strains resistant to β-lactams, but does not explicitly state that CTX-M IV is an acquired AMR gene that confers resistance in its wild-type form. The paper also does not provide specific information about the mechanism or genetic context of CTX-M IV.

SHV.evidence_note: The paper mentions the presence of SHV in 3 strains (3.9%) among the 76 strains resistant/intermediate resistant to β-lactams subjected to molecular analyses.

CMY II.evidence_note: The paper mentions the presence of CMY II gene in 2 out of 76 β-lactam-resistant strains.

DHA.evidence_note: The paper mentions the presence of DHA in 3 strains (3.9%) among the 76 strains resistant/intermediate resistant to β-lactams subjected to molecular analyses.

tetA.evidence_note: The paper mentions the detection of tetA in 8 out of 22 tetracycline-resistant strains.

tetW.evidence_note: The paper mentions the detection of tetW in 4 out of 22 tetracycline-resistant strains.

sul-I.evidence_note: The paper mentions that 36% (4/11) of sulfonamide-resistant strains carried the sul-I gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in Enterobacteriaceae isolated from vegetables, including TEM, CTX-M IV, SHV, OXA, CMY II, DHA, tetA, tetW, sul-I, and qnrD, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, tetracyclines, sulfonamides, and quinolones.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and molecular analyses (PCR and sequencing) were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes in bacterial isolates from vegetables.

full_output.paper_title: From Antiretroviral to Antibacterial: Deep-Learning-Accelerated Repurposing and In Vitro Validation of Efavirenz Against Gram-Positive Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Efavirenz (EFV) showed significant synergistic activity with antibiotics against Gram-positive bacteria, restoring sensitivity to β-lactams in MRSA and enhancing effectiveness against MSSA and Enterococcus spp. EFV demonstrated binding to PBPs and WalK, suggesting potential as an antibacterial agent.
full_output.methodology: Computational docking and in vitro susceptibility testing were used to evaluate EFV's antibacterial activity and mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Trends in Colistin Resistance and Multidrug-Resistant Phenotypes Among Gram-Negative Bacilli: A Retrospective Analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies colistin resistance in various Gram-negative bacilli, with Klebsiella spp. showing the highest prevalence. Low levels of colistin resistance were observed in other species, emphasizing the need for continued surveillance and antimicrobial stewardship.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 23,143 Gram-negative bacilli isolates from a Romanian hospital, with antimicrobial susceptibility testing using broth microdilution.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the relationship between P-glycoprotein (P-gp) expression and drug sensitivity in cancer cell lines, demonstrating that P-gp content can predict drug response. It also shows that P-gp expression influences the accumulation of the fluorescent substrate calcein-AM over short timescales.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized siRNA transfection to modulate P-gp expression, followed by assessments of drug sensitivity, P-gp surface concentration, and calcein-AM accumulation using flow cytometry, western blot, and fluorescent imaging.

full_output.paper_title: South Tyrol (Italy) Pastinaca sativa L. subsp. sativa Essential Oil: GC-MS Composition, Antimicrobial, Anti-Biofilm, and Antioxidant Properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antimicrobial properties of the essential oil (EO) from Pastinaca sativa subsp. sativa, focusing on its effectiveness against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, as well as its antibiofilm and antioxidant activities.
full_output.methodology: The study used GC-MS for chemical analysis, Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion, MIC determination, NPN uptake assay, fluorescence-based viability assay, and biofilm inhibition assays to evaluate the antimicrobial and antibiofilm properties of the EO and its main constituents.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, Risk Factors, and Human Health Implications of Salmonella enterica and Campylobacter spp. in Vermont Backyard Poultry.

gyrA.notes: Frameshift at 734 leads to premature stop codon at 818.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella enterica isolates from Vermont backyard poultry, highlighting resistance to streptomycin, tetracycline, sulfonamides, and ampicillin, as well as quinolone resistance through specific mutations.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella enterica isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Amphiphilic nebramine analogs synergize with β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations, including cefepime-taniborbactam and meropenem-xeruborbactam against metallo-β-lactamase-carrying Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that amphiphilic nebramine analogs, particularly compound 4, enhance the efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics and β-lactamase inhibitor combinations against metallo-β-lactamase-carrying Pseudomonas aeruginosa by acting as outer membrane permeabilizers.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized checkerboard assays, time-kill kinetics, and MIC evaluations to assess the synergistic effects of nebramine analogs with β-lactam antibiotics and β-lactamase inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: An antisense peptide-conjugated peptide nucleic acid (PPNA) for peptidoglycan recycling inhibition reduces AmpC hyperproduction and β-lactam resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

nagZ.validation_method: mRNA levels decreased, AmpC production reduced

ampC.validation_method: mRNA levels decreased, MIC of ceftazidime reduced

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that targeting nagZ with a PPNA reduces AmpC hyperproduction and β-lactam resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, demonstrating the potential of antisense strategies to restore antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation using PPNA to target nagZ, measuring mRNA levels, AmpC production, and MICs of ceftazidime.

full_output.paper_title: Gentamicin induction of the gonococcal hicAB toxin-antitoxin-encoding system and impact on gene expression influencing biofilm formation and in vivo fitness in a strain-specific manner.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the hicAB toxin-antitoxin system in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, which is induced by sub-lethal gentamicin levels and influences biofilm formation and in vivo fitness in a strain-specific manner.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, EMSA, and biofilm assays were used to analyze gene expression and functionality of the hicAB system.

full_output.paper_title: Decoding the SCFA-CpxAR-OMP axis as a dietary checkpoint against antimicrobial resistance transmission across gut-environment interfaces.

mutations_found.validated_by: CRISPR validation of CpxAR in ARGs containment

cpxAR.notes: cpxAR downregulation leads to reduced conjugation efficiency
cpxAR.evidence_note: The paper shows that cpxAR downregulation leads to reduced conjugation efficiency and that butyric acids inhibit bacterial conjugation by downregulating cpxAR.

full_output.key_findings: High-fiber diets reduce the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) by suppressing conjugation-related promoters (trfAp and trbBp) and disrupting membrane function via the CpxAR-OMP pathway.
full_output.methodology: qPCR, transcriptomic analysis, conjugation assays, and SCFA treatments.

full_output.key_findings: Lactobacillus crispatus MV24 co-aggregates with Neisseria meningitidis, disrupting microcolony formation and increasing susceptibility to antimicrobial agents such as LL-37, hBD2, and cephalexin.
full_output.methodology: Live-cell microscopy, sedimentation assays, motility assays, and survival assays with antimicrobial agents.

full_output.paper_title: Functional and genomic analysis of Enterococcus phage A155: a potential agent for reducing VRE gut colonization.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolates and characterizes phage A155, which targets vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis (VR-Efs) V583. Phage A155 shows strong lytic activity against VR-Efs V583, effectively reducing its intestinal colonization in a mouse model. No antibiotic resistance genes or virulence factors were identified in the A155 genome.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, purification, and characterization were performed using standard microbiological techniques. Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to analyze the phage genome.

full_output.paper_title: An evaluation of the impact of abattoir processing on the levels of Campylobacter spp. and Enterobacteriaceae on broiler carcasses.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Campylobacter spp. isolates from broiler carcasses exhibited resistance to tetracycline (45%), nalidixic acid (41%), and ciprofloxacin (39%). Multidrug resistance was observed in 2.7% of isolates, with combined resistance to ciprofloxacin, erythromycin, and tetracycline in 1.6% of isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disc diffusion method according to EUCAST guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis in Fujian Province, Southeast China: a retrospective analysis of drug resistance screening and treatment outcomes, 2019-2024.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB) in Fujian Province, reporting a decline in RR rates from 6.3% in 2019 to 3.1% in 2024. RR-TB patients showed higher resistance to isoniazid and ofloxacin compared to rifampicin-sensitive TB. Key risk factors for unsuccessful treatment included male sex, age ≥45 years, high-risk group status, and occupation as farmer or worker.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of data from China's National Tuberculosis Information Management System, including drug susceptibility testing and statistical analysis of treatment outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: First regional consensus on the management of Helicobacter pylori infection in the Middle East.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the challenges of antibiotic resistance in Helicobacter pylori, particularly to macrolides and fluoroquinolones, emphasizing the need for routine antibiotic susceptibility testing and alternative therapies.
full_output.methodology: The paper is a consensus guideline developed by an expert panel using a Delphi method to reach agreement on the management of H. pylori infection in the Middle East.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro antimicrobial susceptibility of Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates across different regions of China in 2023.

mutations_found.validated_by: detection using PCR fluorescence probing kit

23S rRNA.notes: All isolates harbored the A2063G mutation.

full_output.key_findings: All Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates from China in 2023 were highly resistant to macrolides (erythromycin and azithromycin) due to the A2063G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene, but remained susceptible to tetracycline, doxycycline, and moxifloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using PPLO broth and microdilution susceptibility tests, with macrolide resistance-associated mutations detected via PCR fluorescence probing.

full_output.paper_title: Disulfide bonds are critical for stabilizing cell division, cell envelope biogenesis, and antibiotic resistance proteins in mycobacteria.

lamA.validation_method: expression in M. smegmatis and western blotting
lamA.genetic_context: required for stability of proteins involved in cell division and cell envelope biogenesis
lamA.evidence_note: LamA is required for disulfide bond formation in proteins involved in cell division and cell envelope biogenesis, but it does not confer resistance to antibiotics directly.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that disulfide bonds are critical for the stability of key mycobacterial proteins, including LamA, PstP, LpqW, and EmbB, which are involved in cell division, cell envelope biogenesis, and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Proteomics, bioinformatics, and genetic manipulation were used to analyze the role of disulfide bonds in mycobacterial proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of human exposures of cefepime-taniborbactam against cefepime-resistant Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a 7-day hollow fiber infection model.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of cefepime-taniborbactam against cefepime-resistant Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, identifying the presence of various beta-lactamase genes such as blaNDM-1, blaVIM-1, blaVIM-4, blaKPC-2, and blaOXA-48, which contribute to resistance against beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a hollow fiber infection model (HFIM) to assess bacterial kill and the potential for treatment-emergent resistance, along with broth microdilution for determining MIC values.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of mlstverse system for accurate subspecies identification and drug resistance prediction in Mycobacterium abscessus species.
full_output.key_findings: The mlstverse system accurately identifies Mycobacterium abscessus subspecies and predicts drug resistance to clarithromycin and amikacin based on genetic analysis.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis using mlstverse software combined with phenotypic drug susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Development of phenotypic and genotypic methods for the identification of NmcA β-lactamases in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacter spp. and Klebsiella aerogenes.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a double-disk synergy test and a loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay to detect NmcA β-lactamase producers in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacter spp. and Klebsiella aerogenes. The LAMP assay showed high sensitivity and specificity for detecting bla NmcA.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of phenotypic methods (double-disk synergy test) and genotypic methods (LAMP assay) to detect NmcA β-lactamase producers.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence signature of the endemic vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium clones in Denmark, 2015-2023.
