These genes are associated with various cellular functions such as surface adhesion, carbohydrate metabolism, biofilm formation, and host colonization.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the virulence profiles of dominant VREfm clones in Denmark.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of imipenem combined with dimercaptosuccinic acid in a murine sepsis model using Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

blaVIM-2.mechanism: chelation of zinc ions in the active site of the metallo-beta-lactamase
blaVIM-2.role_in_paper: studied as a target for inhibition by DMSA
blaVIM-2.genetic_context: blaVIM-2 gene was cloned into E. coli and expressed in P. aeruginosa
blaVIM-2.evidence_note: The paper describes the role of blaVIM-2 in conferring resistance to carbapenems through the production of a metallo-beta-lactamase, which hydrolyzes carbapenems. The study shows that DMSA can inhibit this enzyme by chelating zinc ions in its active site, thereby restoring imipenem activity against MBL-producing strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that combining imipenem with DMSA enhances the antibacterial activity against MBL-producing P. aeruginosa strains, including NDM-1, IMP-1, IMP-10, IMP-13, and VIM-2.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro MIC determination and in vivo murine sepsis models to evaluate the efficacy of imipenem combined with DMSA against MBL-producing P. aeruginosa strains.
full_output.sample_size: Six P. aeruginosa strains including PAO1, NDM-1, IMP-1, IMP-10, IMP-13, and VIM-2.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization and global relatedness of multidrug-resistant Salmonella Goldcoast ST2529.

bla_NDM-1.genetic_context: bla NDM-1 is located on an IncFII-type plasmid (contig 2) spanning 138,951 bp. This plasmid also carries other resistance genes, including ble MBL, qnrS1, floR, and two copies of tet (A).
bla_NDM-1.evidence_note: The paper states that the bla NDM-1 gene was confirmed through PCR and Sanger sequencing, and the conjugation assay proved successful, resulting in the acquisition of the transconjugant T67J, characterized by a conjugation efficiency of 9.329 × 10^-2.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the bla NDM-1 gene in a multidrug-resistant Salmonella Goldcoast ST2529 strain, which confers resistance to multiple beta-lactam antibiotics, chloramphenicol, tetracycline, and fluoroquinolones. The gene is located on an IncFII-type plasmid and was successfully transferred via conjugation.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, conjugation assay, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in the Salmonella Goldcoast strain.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic Efficacy of Monoterpenes in Nile Tilapia Infected With Edwardsiella tarda: A Phytogenic Alternative to Oxytetracycline.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that monoterpenes thymol and carvacrol, when added to the diet of Nile tilapia, significantly reduced mortality caused by Edwardsiella tarda, with the highest concentration (0.8 g kg−1) showing efficacy comparable to oxytetracycline.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the effectiveness of monoterpenes in reducing mortality and improving haematological parameters in Nile tilapia infected with Edwardsiella tarda.

full_output.paper_title: Extended spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales in live and dead birds from rural poultry farms and urban live bird markets of Bangladesh.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM, blaSHV, and blaCTX-M genes as the primary contributors to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) resistance in Enterobacterales from poultry in Bangladesh. ESBL-producing E. coli was the most prevalent species, with high resistance rates to multiple antibiotic classes.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to detect and characterize ESBL genes in Enterobacterales isolates from poultry fecal samples.

full_output.paper_title: Extracellular defense of bacteria against antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.key_findings: This paper reviews the extracellular defense mechanisms bacteria employ against antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), focusing on sequestration, degradation, and modification strategies. Key findings include the role of phospholipids, exopolysaccharides, lipopolysaccharides, capsules, and proteins in neutralizing AMPs, as well as the contribution of membrane vesicles and biofilms to collective resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study synthesizes existing literature and experimental data to describe bacterial mechanisms of AMP resistance, emphasizing extracellular defense strategies.

full_output.paper_title: Performance evaluation of plazomicin susceptibility testing of Enterobacterales on VITEK 2 and VITEK 2 Compact Systems.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the performance of the VITEK 2 AST-GN plazomicin test for determining minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) of Enterobacterales, showing high essential agreement and category agreement with the reference BMD method.
full_output.methodology: The study compared VITEK 2 AST-GN plazomicin results with BMD reference method results for 979 Enterobacterales isolates, assessing essential agreement, category agreement, and error rates.

full_output.paper_title: Probiotic potential and antimicrobial efficacy of a dairy isolate, Enterococcus faecium MBBL3.
full_output.key_findings: E. faecium MBBL3 exhibits antimicrobial activity against bovine mastitis pathogens, with Enterolysin_A showing strong molecular interactions with virulence-associated proteins.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, in-vitro antimicrobial assays, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Systematic Determination of the Impact of Structural Edits on Peptide Accumulation into Mycobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the impact of structural modifications, such as backbone N-alkylation and macrocyclization, on the accumulation of peptides into mycobacteria, revealing that macrocyclization generally enhances accumulation while N-alkylation shows context-dependent effects.
full_output.methodology: Utilized the PAC-MAN assay for live-cell analysis of peptide accumulation in mycobacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Mixed infections and heteroresistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis among multidrug-resistant tuberculosis in China: a genomic epidemiology study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified heteroresistance in 16.5% of MDR-TB isolates, with specific mutations in embB, gyrA, rpoB, and katG associated with resistance to ethambutol, fluoroquinolones, rifampicin, and isoniazid, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and statistical analysis of MDR-TB isolates from Shanghai, China.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial profile and antimicrobial resistance in diabetic foot ulcer infections: a 10-year retrospective cohort study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in diabetic foot ulcer infections, with notable resistance to extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBL), quinolones, and carbapenems. Gram-negative bacteria, particularly Enterobacterales and non-fermenters, were predominant, and multidrug resistance was observed in 16% of Pseudomonas sp. and 63.6% of Acinetobacter sp.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing microbiological and resistance patterns in diabetic foot infections.

full_output.paper_title: (p)ppGpp imposes graded transcriptional changes to impair motility and promote antibiotic tolerance in biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that (p)ppGpp levels in Pseudomonas aeruginosa increase gradually with stress severity, leading to extensive transcriptional changes that impair motility, promote biofilm formation, and enhance antibiotic tolerance, especially in biofilm conditions.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis, MIC testing, and motility assays were conducted to evaluate the effects of (p)ppGpp on gene expression and bacterial phenotypes.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, characterization and antibiogram of Staphylococcus aureus isolates from bovine and swine population in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates carrying the mecA and femA genes, as well as biofilm-associated icaA and icaD genes. High levels of multidrug resistance were observed, particularly against streptomycin and β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and molecular characterization.

full_output.paper_title: Fecal carriage of resistant Escherichia coli in livestock in Algeria: emergence of NDM and OXA-181.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of 3GC-resistant E. coli in livestock in Algeria, with the detection of various resistance genes including bla CTX-M, bla NDM-1, bla OXA-181, bla CMY, tet A, aac(6')-Ib, and intI1. These genes contribute to resistance against multiple antibiotics, highlighting the need for monitoring and control strategies.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize resistance genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a lytic phage and its efficacy against carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the lytic phage Pa_WF01, which specifically targets carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA). The phage exhibits robust lytic activity, wide pH and temperature stability, and shows therapeutic potential in a mouse model of CRPA infection.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, host range determination, TEM, genome sequencing, and in vivo therapeutic evaluation in a mouse model.

full_output.paper_title: Uncovering hidden threats: prevalence, antibiotic resistance and virulence gene profiles of Escherichia coli strains isolated from Testudines and their aquatic habitats.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic resistance genes in E. coli isolates from Testudines and their aquatic habitats, including mcr-1, mcr-2, mcr-4, bla TEM, bla SHV, qnrA, qnrD, eaeA, virF, stx1, and stx2. These genes confer resistance to colistin, cephalothin, ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, and nalidixic acid, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant E. coli in wild reptiles and their environments.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection and sequencing were used to identify antibiotic resistance and virulence genes in E. coli isolates from Testudines and sediments.

These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as tetracycline, cefoxitin, aztreonam, and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: Genotypic analysis using ResFinder and phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing via broth microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: Breastfeeding and the milk resistome shape the establishment and transmission of antibiotic resistance genes in the infant gut microbiome.

sdrM.validation_method: metagenomic sequencing and linear regression analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the quinolone resistance gene sdrM as potentially transmitted from breastmilk to the infant gut microbiome, especially under maternal antibiotic use.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and statistical analysis of ARGs in infant, maternal, and breastmilk samples.

full_output.paper_title: Role of the gut microbiome in frequent gut colonization with extended-spectrum β lactamase-producing Enterobacterales among Peruvian children.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that rarely colonized children had significantly lower abundance of bla CTX-M genes compared to frequently colonized children, indicating a potential link between gut microbiome composition and resistance gene prevalence.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis of stool samples to assess gut microbiome and antibiotic resistance gene profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Phage and enzyme therapies in wound infections: From lab to bedside.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the use of phage and phage-derived enzymes as alternatives to antibiotics for treating antibiotic-resistant wound infections, highlighting their mechanisms, applications, and challenges.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature and studies on phage and enzyme therapies for wound infections.

full_output.paper_title: Global spread and antimicrobial resistance of Aeromonas hydrophila in aquatic food animals: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM and tetA as the most prevalent antimicrobial resistance genes in Aeromonas hydrophila isolates from aquatic food animals, with high prevalence rates observed in both Africa and Asia.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2020 and 2024.

full_output.paper_title: Biogenic silver nanoparticles from chamomile incorporated in hydrogels for high transparent non-infectiveness contact lenses.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and characterization of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using chamomile extract, which were incorporated into hydrogels for contact lenses. The AgNPs demonstrated antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus epidermidis, and Staphylococcus aureus, with notable inhibition zones and minimum inhibitory concentrations.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of AgNPs from chamomile extract, their incorporation into pHEMA hydrogels, and evaluation of their antimicrobial efficacy through MIC, MBC, and IZ assays.

full_output.paper_title: Protracted outbreaks of VIM-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a surgical intensive care unit in France, January 2018 to June 2024.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaVIM-2 and blaVIM-4 as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in VIM-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA-VIM) during prolonged outbreaks in a French surgical intensive care unit. These genes were detected in both patient and environmental isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial resistance gene screening using the Abricate pipeline and ResFinder database.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of antimicrobial resistance in Enterococcus spp. Isolated from the skin microbiota of channel catfish (Ictalurus punctatus) in Southeastern United States.

lsa(A).encodes: lincosamide and streptogramin A resistance determinant

efrB.encodes: rifamycin, fluoroquinolone, and macrolide resistance determinant

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Enterococcus spp. isolated from the skin microbiota of channel catfish, including aac(6')-Iid, aac(6')-Ii, efmA, msr(C), lsa(A), efrA, efrB, emeA, and dfrE, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as aminoglycosides, macrolides, fluoroquinolones, and disinfectants.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in Enterococcus spp. isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Persistence phenotype of adherent-invasive Escherichia coli in response to ciprofloxacin, revealing high-persistence strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NRG857c as a high-persistence strain of adherent-invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC) with a persistence level 200-fold higher than LF82. The high-persistence phenotype of NRG857c is not related to the presence of a multi-resistance plasmid or the htrA gene.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the persistence phenotype of AIEC strains using time-killing curves and MIC measurements, and evaluated the role of the htrA gene and plasmid in persistence.
full_output.sample_size: 2 AIEC reference strains, 4 clinical isolates, and 2 non-AIEC E. coli pathotypes

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing characterization of silver-resistant bacteria from the outfall of wastewater treatment plants and effluent-receiving rivers.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the sil and pco operons as key contributors to silver resistance in bacteria isolated from wastewater treatment plants and effluent-receiving rivers. These operons, along with other heavy metal resistance genes, were found to be prevalent in the isolates, highlighting the environmental dissemination of silver resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and PCR were used to characterize silver-resistant bacteria and identify resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of a piliated and multidrug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 35B-ST156 clone in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of a multidrug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 35B-ST156 clone in Japan, characterized by resistance to beta-lactams, macrolides, and co-trimoxazole due to specific genetic mutations and gene acquisitions.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in the 35B-ST156 isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the X998_03220 gene, encoding the H-NS protein, as a significant predictor of resistance to multiple antibiotics in Staphylococcus aureus, highlighting its potential role in AMR mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Machine learning models were trained using WGS data, including gene, SNP, and k-mer features, to predict AMR phenotypes in S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Quantifying the effects of antibiotic resistance and within-host competition on strain fitness in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates how antibiotic resistance and within-host competition influence the fitness of Streptococcus pneumoniae strains, revealing that within-host competition increases clearance rates and reduces establishment rates of serotypes, and that antibiotic resistance can impose fitness costs in the absence of antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study uses survival analyses on a longitudinal dataset of pneumococcal carriage in infants to quantify the effects of within-host competition and antibiotic resistance on strain fitness.

full_output.paper_title: Heterofunctional Cationic Polyester Dendrimers as Antibacterial Agents: The Role of Internal and External Charges.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents two families of cationic polyester dendrimers with internal and/or external charges, showing superior antibacterial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The second-generation dendrimer (G2-(PA-NH3+ )9 -(β-Ala-NH3+ )12 ) exhibited bacteriostatic and bactericidal activity at 10-21 μM and enhanced Escherichia coli sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of cationic polyester dendrimers, antibacterial activity assessment via MIC and MBC assays, and cytotoxicity evaluation using the Alamar Blue assay.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitory efficacy, production dynamics, and characterization of postbiotics of lactic acid bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial activity of postbiotics from five lactic acid bacteria (LAB) strains, identifying their efficacy against various Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens. It highlights the potential of these postbiotics as natural preservatives in food safety.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized broth microdilution, agar well diffusion, and enzymatic susceptibility tests to assess the antimicrobial activity of postbiotics from LAB strains.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative proteomics analysis of MRSA under different experimental conditions.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies differentially expressed proteins in MRSA strains ST398 and JE2 under varying experimental conditions, highlighting changes in metabolic pathways such as arginine, purine, and glycine-betaine biosynthesis, as well as stress response mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun proteomics combined with label-free quantification (LFQ) using LC–MS/MS analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Decoding Proteus mirabilis biofilms: expression of selected virulence genes and association with antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence and expression of virulence genes (ureC, mrpA, speA, and rsbA) in Proteus mirabilis strains from both urine and non-urine specimens, highlighting their association with multidrug resistance (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) phenotypes.
full_output.methodology: PCR and qPCR for gene detection and expression analysis, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer method.

full_output.paper_title: Identifying Modulators of the Post-Antibiotic Effect.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rfaE as a gene whose deletion enhances the post-antibiotic effect (PAE) of LpxC inhibitors CHIR-090 and LPC-058. Deletion of rfaE increases the PAE by 2-4-fold, likely due to increased stability of the LpxC enzyme.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput chemical-genetic screen of the E. coli Keio collection, followed by validation through PAE measurements, MIC testing, and protein turnover analysis using SILAC.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and Antibiofilm Activity of 8-Hydroxyquinoline Derivatives Against Mycobacterium and Staphylococcus Species.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated 8-hydroxyquinoline derivatives for their antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against Mycobacterium and Staphylococcus species, identifying HQ-2 as the most effective compound with significant activity against various strains.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of 8-hydroxyquinoline derivatives, antimycobacterial and antibiofilm activity assays, and cytotoxicity evaluations.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes Esc(1-21) analogs with site-specific isopeptide bonds, focusing on their antimicrobial activity, membrane permeabilization, biofilm eradication, hemolytic activity, cytotoxicity, and proteolytic stability. The most promising analog, Esc(1-21)ε20, shows comparable or improved antimicrobial activity, lower cytotoxicity, and greater resistance to enzymatic degradation compared to the parent peptide.
full_output.methodology: Peptide synthesis, antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity assays, membrane permeabilization studies, hemolytic assays, cytotoxicity assessments, and plasma stability testing.

full_output.paper_title: Bioprospecting of six polyphenol-rich Mediterranean wild edible plants reveals antioxidant, antibiofilm and bactericidal properties against Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the antibiofilm and bactericidal properties of six wild edible plants against Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), highlighting their potential as natural alternatives to combat antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study combined analytical chemistry, plant biochemistry, and microbiology to evaluate the antioxidant, antibiofilm, and bactericidal properties of plant extracts against S. aureus and MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Anti-staphylococcal activity, antibiotic-resistance modulation effects and action of Harungana madagascariensis (Hypericaceae) fruit extracts on the antioxidant system of multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial potential of Harungana madagascariensis fruit extracts and their effects on the antioxidant system of multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. The hexane extract showed excellent activity against S. aureus isolates, while the dichloromethane/methanol extract enhanced the activity of several antibiotics against MDR S. aureus. The extracts also affected the antioxidant system of S. aureus by inhibiting catalase activity and inducing lipid peroxidation.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed using the micro-dilution method, and the effect on the antioxidant system was evaluated by measuring catalase activity and lipid peroxidation levels.
full_output.sample_size: 14 clinical MDR isolates and a reference strain

full_output.paper_title: The in vitro evaluation of synergistic effects of ciprofloxacin and berberine hydrochloride against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the synergistic effects of ciprofloxacin and berberine hydrochloride against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, demonstrating that the combination showed synergistic activity against PAO 1 and improved bactericidal effects against both susceptible and resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution, checkerboard assays, time-kill kinetics, and biofilm assays to assess the antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of ciprofloxacin and berberine hydrochloride.
full_output.sample_size: 10 clinical isolates and the standard strain PAO 1

full_output.paper_title: Diversity and antibiotic sensitivity of uropathogens from a regional hospital in Rwanda.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance among uropathogens, with very high resistance frequencies (above 70%) against amoxycillin, cotrimoxazole, trimethoprim, aztreonam, and fosfomycin. Resistance to fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, and cephalosporins varied between 40-60%. High levels of cross-resistance were observed for drugs of the same class. Resistance to potentiated penicillins, meropenem, cefoxitin, and nitrofurantoin were less than 30%.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted a hospital-based cross-sectional study analyzing urine samples using dipstick urinalysis and urine culture, followed by antibiotic sensitivity testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: A systematic review and meta-analysis on the prevalence of extended-spectrum beta-Lactamase-Producing Klebsiella Pneumonia in Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: This study found that the prevalence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (ESBL-KP) in Nigeria is 47.3%. The most common ESBL genes identified were blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCTX-M, and blaOXA, with prevalence rates of 55%, 41%, 54%, and 57%, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on the prevalence of ESBL-KP and their encoding genes in Nigeria.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Colistin Susceptibility in Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Isolates Using Broth Microdilution, MICRONAUT-MIC-Strip, and VITEK MS.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated colistin susceptibility in 194 carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates using broth microdilution, MICRONAUT-MIC-Strip, and VITEK MS. It found that 11.8% of the isolates were colistin resistant, and no mcr-1-5 genes were detected. The MALDIxin test did not identify mutations responsible for lipid A modification-related colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution, MICRONAUT-MIC-Strip, and VITEK MS to evaluate colistin susceptibility in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.

full_output.key_findings: Carrimycin (CAM) showed potent activity against Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) in vivo, with significant reduction in bacillary load and improved immune response. CAM exhibited synergy with clofazimine and ethambutol against MAC in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, intracellular activity assays, in vivo efficacy studies in BALB/c mice, and synergy testing using checkerboard assays.
full_output.sample_size: 15 clinical isolates and 2 reference strains of MAC

full_output.paper_title: Rapid screening for carbapenemase-producing carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales: clinical implementation of an immunochromatographic test using broth-enriched rectal swabs.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates an immunochromatographic test (ICT) for detecting carbapenemases in rectal swabs, showing that the ICT after 6 hours of incubation has a sensitivity of 65% and specificity of 97.5% for detecting CP-CRE, offering a rapid and cost-effective alternative to traditional methods.
full_output.methodology: The study used an immunochromatographic test (ICT) on broth-enriched rectal swabs, comparing its performance to the GeneXpert Carba-R PCR assay and culture methods.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a significant increase in antimicrobial resistance among bloodstream infection (BSI) pathogens, including extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing organisms, multidrug-resistant (MDR), and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) bacteria. Notably, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa showed alarming increases in resistance rates.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of blood culture data and antimicrobial susceptibility testing results from a tertiary care hospital in Nepal over a 10-year period.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization, Antibiogram, and Virulence Gene Profiling of Proteus vulgaris Isolated From Cattle With Bovine Respiratory Disease in Bangladesh.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of virulence genes rsbA and luxS in Proteus vulgaris isolates from cattle with bovine respiratory disease in Bangladesh. All isolates showed resistance to penicillin, erythromycin, ampicillin, and tetracycline, while being susceptible to ceftriaxone and levofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the antimicrobial potential of Boehmeria rugulosa wood extract, particularly the 70% aqueous ethanol extract, which shows significant antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, Bacillus cereus, and Escherichia coli. The extract contains various volatile and non-volatile phytochemicals with antimicrobial properties.
full_output.methodology: The study used GC–MS analysis to identify volatile compounds and in-vitro antimicrobial assays to evaluate the antibacterial efficacy of different solvent extracts of B. rugulosa wood.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiome-mediated colonization resistance to carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in ICU patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaKPC-2 and blaNDM-1 as carbapenem resistance genes in CRKP isolates, highlighting their role in resistance to meropenem.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and microbiome analysis were used to characterize resistance mechanisms and microbial interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Hfq balances energetic efficiency and antibiotic persistence in Acinetobacter baumannii.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: disrupted proton motive force along with lower metabolic activity and reduced intracellular ATP

hfq.notes: Mutations in hfq affect antibiotic persistence.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that mutations in the hfq gene, specifically the F39A mutation, result in intermediate cefepime persistence in Acinetobacter baumannii. The wild-type hfq gene is associated with normal susceptibility, while its deletion leads to increased persistence.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, persistence assays, and molecular biology techniques were used to analyze the effects of hfq mutations on antibiotic persistence.

full_output.paper_title: Investigating the molecular transmission dynamics of bla(NDM) in antibiotic-selective environments.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the blaNDM-shble gene and its mobility via IS Aba125 in Vibrio cholerae and Escherichia coli, showing that the copy number of IS Aba125 affects the stability and expression of the resistance gene.
full_output.methodology: Genome engineering, MIC testing, and in vivo experiments in a rabbit model.

full_output.paper_title: ST11 carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae integrates virulence plasmid fragments into the chromosome via insertion sequence.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the integration of virulence plasmid fragments into the chromosome of ST11 carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting the role of IS26 and ISKpn1 in this process. It characterizes blaKPC-2 and rmpA2 as key genes involved in resistance and virulence.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, Sanger sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the genetic elements and their integration mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic application of a jumbo bacteriophage against metallo-β-lactamase producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a jumbo phage, vB_PaerM_AttikonH10, which shows broad host range and effective lytic activity against metallo-β-lactamase (MBL)-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates. The phage demonstrated synergistic effects with amikacin in reducing bacterial load in a murine thigh infection model.
full_output.methodology: The study involved phage isolation, purification, and characterization, along with in vivo pharmacokinetic and efficacy assessments in a murine thigh infection model.

full_output.paper_title: IITR00803: a benzoxazole-nitrothiophene small molecule with broad-spectrum antibacterial potential.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IITR00803, a novel small molecule with broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against enteric pathogens, including Salmonella and E. coli. It demonstrates bactericidal activity, prevents biofilm formation, and does not induce stable resistance development in vitro.
full_output.methodology: The study involved chemical screening, MIC determination, efflux pump analysis, membrane potential assays, and in vivo testing in C. elegans.

full_output.paper_title: gltB encoding glutamate synthase is involved in persister and biofilm formation and virulence in Staphylococcus aureus.

gltB.notes: Deletion of gltB leads to increased susceptibility to ampicillin, norfloxacin, and rifampicin.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that gltB, which encodes the large subunit of glutamate synthase in Staphylococcus aureus, is involved in persister formation, biofilm formation, and virulence. The ΔgltB mutant exhibited increased susceptibility to antibiotics, heat, carbon starvation, and oxidative stress, along with reduced virulence in mice.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic knockout and complementation techniques, along with antibiotic susceptibility testing, biofilm assays, and virulence assessments in a murine model.

full_output.paper_title: LC-MS/MS metabolomics unravels the resistant phenotype of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several carbapenemase genes (bla KPC-2, bla KPC-3, bla NDM-1, bla NDM-5, bla NDM-7, bla OXA-48, and bla OXA-181) in carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) isolates, highlighting their role in carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and metabolomics analysis using LC-MS/MS were employed to characterize resistance mechanisms in CPE isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Archaeasins: A New Class of Antimicrobial Peptides from Archaea
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 12,623 archaeal peptides with potential antimicrobial activity, termed archaeasins, which demonstrate significant antimicrobial activity against multiple bacterial pathogens, including drug-resistant strains. Some archaeasins, such as archaeasin-73, show efficacy comparable to established antibiotics like polymyxin B in preclinical models.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a deep learning model (APEX 1.1) to predict antimicrobial activity in archaeal proteomes, followed by experimental validation through synthesis and testing of selected peptides against bacterial pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Pyrazolopyridine pyrimidone hybrids as potential DprE1 inhibitors, design, synthesis and biological evaluation as antitubercular agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyridine-linked pyrimidin-4-one derivatives as potential antitubercular agents, showing significant activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv with MIC values of 3.12 µg/mL and 12.5 µg/mL for compounds 8 and 14, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were evaluated for anti-tubercular activity using the Microplate Alamar Blue Assay (MABA) and analyzed through molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and phenotypic characterization of six multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter pittii isolates.

blaOXA-72.evidence_note: The blaOXA-72 gene was identified in the plasmid pAP290R and was shown to confer carbapenem resistance when transferred to a carbapenem-susceptible A. baumannii strain.

blaOXA-272.evidence_note: The blaOXA-272 gene was identified in the genomic analysis of A. pittii isolates and was associated with carbapenem resistance.

blaOXA-255.evidence_note: The blaOXA-255 gene was identified in the genomic analysis of A. pittii isolates, and it was found to confer carbapenem resistance.

blaADC-21.evidence_note: The gene blaADC-21 is mentioned in the context of conferring resistance to cephalosporins, and it is part of the ampC cephalosporinase family. The paper states that all isolates carried at least two genes conferring β-lactam resistance: a variant of ampC cephalosporinase (ADC) and a variant of OXA-type β-lactamase.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple beta-lactamase genes, including blaOXA-72, blaOXA-272, and blaOXA-255, which confer resistance to carbapenems. Additionally, other resistance genes such as blaADC-245, blaADC-150, and others were found to confer resistance to cephalosporins. Efflux pump genes like adeF, abaQ, and abeS were associated with resistance to fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines. The gene lpsB was linked to colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, plasmid transfer experiments, and MIC testing were used to identify and validate AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic profiling of cefotaxime-resistant Haemophilus influenzae from Norway and Sweden reveals extensive expansion of virulent multidrug-resistant international clones.

ftsI.mechanism: amino acid substitutions in the transpeptidase region leading to reduced susceptibility to beta-lactam antibiotics
ftsI.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and classification of rPBP3 stages

HI_1132.mechanism: amino acid substitutions in the transpeptidase region leading to reduced susceptibility to beta-lactam antibiotics
HI_1132.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and classification of rPBP3 stages

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the expansion of multidrug-resistant Haemophilus influenzae clones with cefotaxime resistance, primarily due to mutations in the ftsI gene encoding penicillin-binding protein 3 (PBP3). These mutations lead to cross-resistance to multiple beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and classification of rPBP3 stages based on amino acid substitutions in PBP3.

full_output.paper_title: Deep-Learning Driven Identification of Novel Antimicrobial Peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three novel antimicrobial peptides (AMP1, AMP2, and AMP3) using a deep learning-driven pipeline. AMP3 exhibits the broadest antibacterial spectrum and effective membrane-disruptive activity.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a deep learning pipeline combining HydrAMP and AMPlify to identify and validate novel antimicrobial peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Mycoplasma genitalium from nucleic acid amplification test specimens, Nunavut region of Inuit Nunangat, Canada, 2020-2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in mtrR, 23S rRNA, gyrA, and parC genes associated with azithromycin and moxifloxacin resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Mycoplasma genitalium.
full_output.methodology: PCR and Sanger sequencing were used to detect mutations in target genes for antimicrobial resistance prediction.

full_output.paper_title: Tracking Enterobacteria, microbiomes, and antibiotic resistance genes from waste to soil with repeated compost applications.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes including bla CTX-M, bla TEM-1B, bla SHV-12, qnr A, qnr B, aac(6')-Ib, sul 1, sul 2, intI 1, and intI 2 in Enterobacteria from composts and raw waste, highlighting their persistence and potential spread in tropical soils.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, and qPCR to identify and quantify AMR genes in raw waste, composts, and soils.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequencing of Salmonella in poultry from China reveals the presence of bla(NDM-5) in different serotypes.

blaNDM-5.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and conjugation experiments

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM-5 in Salmonella isolates from poultry in China, highlighting its presence in various serotypes and its potential for horizontal transfer.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and their genetic environments.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in ClpC1 or ClpX subunit of caseinolytic protease confer resistance to ilamycins in mycobacteria.

clpC1.notes: Mutations in clpC1 confer resistance to ILE and ILF in mycobacteria.

clpX.notes: Mutation in clpX confers resistance to ILE and ILF in mycobacteria.

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in clpC1 and clpX confer resistance to ilamycins (ILE and ILF) in mycobacteria. Specific mutations such as F80I, F80V, F80L, F80C, F2L, F2C, M1-FERF-F2, Q17R, H77D, L88R, L88P, F5I, F80S, and P30H were identified as responsible for resistance.
full_output.methodology: Gene editing, MIC testing, and molecular docking were used to validate the resistance mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: Various mycobacterial strains were analyzed, including Mtb, Mab, Mmr, and Msm.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and Anticancer Activities of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Probio87 Isolated from Human Breast Milk.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial and anticancer activities of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Probio87, highlighting its strong acid and bile tolerance, efficient mucin adhesion, and broad carbohydrate utilization. It demonstrated potent antimicrobial activity against several pathogens, including Candida albicans, and showed selective inhibition of L. iners without affecting L. crispatus. Additionally, Probio87 exhibited anticancer effects on cervical cancer cells, reducing proliferation and inducing apoptosis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro tests to assess the probiotic properties of Probio87, including acid and bile tolerance, mucin adhesion, antibiotic susceptibility, and antimicrobial activity. Anticancer effects were evaluated through cell viability assays, angiogenesis arrays, and pathway analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Potential Use of Cefiderocol and Nanosilver in Wound Dressings to Control Multidrug-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial efficacy of cefiderocol and nanosilver against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting that while cefiderocol was effective against reference strains, multidrug-resistant A. baumannii strains were resistant to both cefiderocol and silver forms. The combination of cefiderocol and nanosilver showed variable efficacy depending on the strain and concentration.
full_output.methodology: The study used disk diffusion method on Mueller-Hinton agar to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of cefiderocol and nanosilver against reference and multidrug-resistant strains of P. aeruginosa, E. coli, and A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Anti-Bacterial and Anti-Fungal Properties of a Set of Transition Metal Complexes Bearing a Pyridine Moiety and [B(C6F5)4]2 as a Counter Anion.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and characterization of six novel metal(II) complexes with the general formula [MPy6][B(C6F5)4]2 (M = Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn). These complexes exhibited broad-spectrum antibacterial and antifungal activities, with complex 6 showing exceptional antibacterial activity against Streptococcus pyogenes and complexes 5 and 6 demonstrating high antifungal activity against Candida albicans.
full_output.methodology: The complexes were synthesized and characterized using elemental analysis, FT-IR, 11B-NMR, 1H-NMR, EPR, TGA, and UV-Vis spectroscopy. Their antimicrobial activities were evaluated using agar well diffusion and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) assays.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular and virulence differences of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from blood.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaKPC-2 gene as a key factor in carbapenem resistance among Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from blood, highlighting the diversity of resistance mechanisms and plasmid profiles among the strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and plasmid analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and virulence factors of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A ptsH mutation suppresses growth defects and antibiotic sensitivity in a cpgA mutant defective in metabolite proofreading.

full_output.methodology: The study used a checkerboard assay to evaluate the synergistic effects of meropenem and sulbactam against CRAB isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance to colistin in neonates: epidemiological insights and public health implications in Nigeria - a mini review.

mcr-1.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

mcr-10.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The review identifies an increasing trend of colistin resistance in Gram-negative bacteria in neonates in Nigeria, highlighting the presence of mobile colistin resistance (MCR) genes such as mcr-1 and mcr-10 in clinical isolates.
full_output.methodology: Narrative mini-review synthesizing literature, systematic reviews, and global and national reports on colistin resistance in neonates.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance profile of Escherichia colis trains isolated at the main hospital in Dakar retrospective study over 10 years.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights a concerning resistance profile of Escherichia coli to commonly used antibiotics, particularly beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, and aminoglycosides, with a marked increase in multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains and carbapenem resistance over the 10-year period.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective, cross-sectional study analyzing antimicrobial susceptibility testing data from E. coli isolates over 10 years.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a novel aminoglycoside nucleotidyltransferase ANT(3"))-Ic from Citrobacter telavivum S24.

ant(3\"))-Ic.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + disk diffusion
ant(3\"))-Ic.evidence_note: The ant(3"')-Ic gene is located on the chromosome of C. telavivum S24. The gene was cloned into E. coli DH5α and tested for resistance using disk diffusion.

ant(3\")-Ic.mechanism: modifies aminoglycoside antibiotics by adding a phosphate group, reducing their efficacy

full_output.key_findings: A novel aminoglycoside resistance gene, ant(3"))-Ic, was identified in Citrobacter telavivum S24, encoding the ANT(3"))-Ic protein, which confers resistance to streptomycin and spectinomycin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, cloning, expression, purification, and enzymatic activity assays were performed to characterize the ant(3"))-Ic gene.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, crystal structure, DFT calculations, in-vitro and in-silico studies of novel chromone-isoxazoline conjugates as antibacterial and anti-inflammatory agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the synthesis and biological evaluation of novel chromone-isoxazoline hybrids, demonstrating their antibacterial and anti-inflammatory activities. Some compounds showed promising efficacy against various bacterial strains, including Bacillus subtilis, Salmonella enterica, Escherichia coli, and Klebsiella aerogenes. The anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated through 5-LOX enzyme inhibition, with compound 5e showing the strongest activity.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized through 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition and characterized using spectroscopic techniques. Antibacterial activity was assessed via disk diffusion and microdilution assays, while anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated through 5-LOX enzyme inhibition.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization and antibiotic susceptibility of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in immunocompromised cancer patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of femA, mecA, and PVL genes in MRSA isolates from cancer patients, with PVL being a significant factor in patient outcomes.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Functional insights into Streptomyces isolates containing both clavulanic acid-like and carbapenem biosynthetic gene clusters.

ceaS2.mechanism: part of the CA-like BGC involved in early stages of CA biosynthesis

cpe.mechanism: required for a later step in the CA biosynthetic pathway

cmmE.mechanism: homologous to those present in carbapenem producers

cmmM.mechanism: homologous to those present in carbapenem producers

cmmI.mechanism: involved in MM 4550 biosynthesis and regulation

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that Streptomyces pratensis and related environmental isolates contain both clavulanic acid-like and carbapenem biosynthetic gene clusters. The CA-like BGC contributes to β-lactamase inhibitory activity, while the MM 4550-like BGC is associated with potential β-lactam antibiotic activity. Early intermediates in the CA biosynthetic pathway, such as deoxyguanidinoproclavaminic acid and guanidinoproclavaminic acid, were found to be responsible for the observed β-lactamase inhibitory activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RT-PCR analysis, bioassays, HPLC, and metabolomics to characterize the biosynthetic gene clusters and their associated activities in Streptomyces isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Enzyme-mediated aminoglycoside resistance without target mimicry.

aac(3)-Ia.evidence_note: The paper describes AAC(3)-Ia as an aminoglycoside acetyltransferase that confers resistance to gentamicin and sisomicin through acetylation. The enzyme was tested in Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli.

aac(3)-XIa.source: AAC(3)-XIa was identified in 2015 from Corynebacterium striatum
aac(3)-XIa.evidence_note: The paper states that AAC(3)-XIa provides resistance to kanamycin B, tobramycin, dibekacin, gentamicin, sisomicin, and fortimicin.

AAC(3)-Ia.validation_method: antibiotic susceptibility testing and enzymatic assays
AAC(3)-Ia.evidence_note: The paper states that AAC(3)-Ia provides resistance to gentamicin, sisomicin, and fortimicin.

AAC(3)-XIa.validation_method: antibiotic susceptibility testing and enzymatic assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AAC(3)-Ia and AAC(3)-XIa as aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes that do not use target mimicry, binding aminoglycosides in a non-canonical boat conformation. These enzymes confer resistance to several aminoglycosides, including gentamicin, sisomicin, and others.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, enzymatic assays, and antibiotic susceptibility testing in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring mutational possibilities of KPC variants to reach high level resistance to cefiderocol.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic characterisation, virulence factors, and multi-drug resistance of Escherichia coli strains isolated from faeces of feral pigeons (Columba Livia forma urbana).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several virulence genes in E. coli strains isolated from feral pigeons, including stx1, eaeA, katP, lpfA O157/OI−141, lpfA O157/OI−154, tir, iha, and stx2. High resistance to imipenem, tetracycline, and doxycycline was observed.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify virulence genes and resistance patterns in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Bio-guided discovery of antibacterial metabolites from Penicillium chrysogenum.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two new metabolites, 15-deoxy-15-amino-citreohybridonol (6) and chrysogenotoxin (7), along with five known compounds. Compound 6 showed broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, while compound 7 exhibited potent bactericidal activity against Gram-negative bacteria. Molecular docking studies indicated that compounds 4, 6, and 7 could act as inhibitors of the NDM-1 β-lactamase.
full_output.methodology: The study involved bio-guided isolation, NMR spectroscopy, and molecular docking studies to evaluate the antibacterial activity and potential mechanisms of action of the isolated compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Hijacking the Electron Train: Menaquinone-Binding Antimicrobial Peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the role of menaquinone (MK) as a target for antimicrobial peptides, highlighting the importance of MK biosynthesis genes menA and menB in resistance to LysE and other MBAMPs.
full_output.methodology: The study includes genetic analysis, mutagenesis, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of MK biosynthesis genes in resistance to antimicrobial peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic characterisation and prevalence of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales in a tertiary care centre in Bihar India.

blaNDM.validation_method: modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM) and EDTA-modified carbapenem inactivation method (eCIM)

blaOXA-48.validation_method: modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM) and EDTA-modified carbapenem inactivation method (eCIM)

blaIMP.validation_method: modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM) and EDTA-modified carbapenem inactivation method (eCIM)

blaKPC.validation_method: modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM) and EDTA-modified carbapenem inactivation method (eCIM)

blaVIM.validation_method: modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM) and EDTA-modified carbapenem inactivation method (eCIM)

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the prevalence of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) in Bihar, India, highlighting the dominance of Class B carbapenemases (blaNDM, blaOXA-48, blaIMP, blaKPC, blaVIM) and the co-expression of Class A and Class B carbapenemases in E. coli and K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic detection of carbapenemases using modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM) and EDTA-modified carbapenem inactivation method (eCIM), along with combined disc tests for class differentiation.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and expression of a novel antimicrobial peptide Gloverin and its antibacterial effect against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: A novel gloverin CpGlv was identified, expressed, and purified, exhibiting antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus by increasing cell membrane and wall permeability and inhibiting biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Sequence alignment, recombinant expression in E. coli, MIC determination, SEM, and biochemical assays were used to assess the antibacterial activity of CpGlv.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of Eravacycline against carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacilli and associated risk factors for non-susceptible infections from a tertiary hospital in fujian, China from 2021 to 2024.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes, including bla KPC, bla CTXM−10, bla CTXM−9, bla CTXM−14, bla CTXM−1, bla OXA−23, armA, ant(3”)-I, aac(6)-Ib, rmtB, bla NDM−5, bla NDM−1, bla NDM−4, and bla NDM−13, which confer resistance to various antibiotics in carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to characterize resistance genes, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using broth microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of porcine intestinal Lactobacillus salivarius and antimicrobial potential of its biosurfactant.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolated a biosurfactant-producing Lactobacillus salivarius strain from the ileum of PCV2-infected piglets. The biosurfactant showed significant antimicrobial activity against E. coli and S. suis, and antiviral activity against PCV2.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation of L. salivarius from PCV2-infected piglets, characterization of its biosurfactant, and evaluation of its antimicrobial and antiviral activities using various assays.

full_output.paper_title: Use of Subtherapeutic Tylvalosin Against Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae: Implications For Respiratory Microbiome Dysbiosis and Swine Lung Health.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of subtherapeutic tylvalosin on Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae infection in pigs, highlighting the impact on respiratory microbiome and lung health, but no AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Experimental infection of pigs with M. hyopneumoniae, assessment of clinical signs, seroconversion, lung lesions, and microbiota analysis via 16S rRNA sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of daphnetin combined with tobramycin on Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm infection in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that daphnetin combined with tobramycin effectively reduced Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm formation in vitro and in vivo, demonstrating a synergistic antibacterial effect.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial effects of daphnetin and tobramycin using microdilution, crystal violet staining, colony counting, and electron microscopy in vitro, and in vivo using a rabbit joint infection model.

full_output.paper_title: A Review on the Degradation of Antibiotic Resistance Genes During Composting of Livestock Manure.

ermB.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

tetM.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

tetW.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The review discusses the degradation of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) during composting of livestock manure, highlighting the effectiveness of aerobic composting in reducing ARGs through high-temperature elimination, reduction in host bacterial abundance, and inhibition of horizontal gene transfer.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature and studies on the degradation of ARGs during composting processes.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance patterns of Campylobacter jejuni isolated from retail raw chicken meat in Jordan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-61, blaOXA-184, tet(O), and gyrA as key resistance genes in Campylobacter jejuni isolates from Jordanian chicken meat, with high prevalence rates of resistance to β-lactams, tetracycline, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in C. jejuni isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of teicoplanin protein-binding variability and clinical utility of its free serum concentration measurement.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the variability in teicoplanin (TEIC) protein-binding and the importance of measuring free serum TEIC concentrations for optimal therapy. It found that free TEIC concentrations vary significantly among patients and are not accurately predicted by existing models, emphasizing the need for individualized dosing strategies.
full_output.methodology: The study measured free serum TEIC concentrations using HPLC and evaluated their correlation with clinical outcomes in patients with various underlying diseases.

full_output.paper_title: Cefiderocol-resistant pathogens in German hospital wastewater: a reservoir for multidrug resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes, including bla NDM−1, bla VIM−1, bla OXA−48, and bla KPC−2, in cefiderocol-resistant isolates from German hospital wastewater, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant pathogens with diverse resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and resistance profiles in cefiderocol-resistant isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Tracking of multidrug-resistant pathogen clones in Ghana: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: This study identified several multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial clones in Ghana, including E. coli ST155, ST617, and ST10, K. pneumoniae ST152 and ST17, S. pneumoniae ST802, and S. aureus ST152 and ST121. These clones show high prevalence and are associated with resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting genetic characterisation of MDR clones from Ghana using MLST and WGS.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Natural Products as Inhibitors of Shikimate Dehydrogenase from Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus: Kinetic and Molecular Dynamics Simulations, and Biological Activity Studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified phloridzin, rutin, and caffeic acid as potent inhibitors of Shikimate Dehydrogenase (SaSDH) from Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), with IC50 values of 140, 165, and 240 µM, respectively. Caffeic acid showed an MIC of 12 mM against MRSA.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic activity assays, inhibition screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to evaluate the inhibitory effects of natural product derivatives on SaSDH.

full_output.paper_title: Finding the Missing IMP Gene: Overcoming the Imipenemase IMP Gene Drop-Out in Automated Molecular Testing for Carbapenem-Resistant Bacteria Circulating in Latin America.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the IMP-18 allele as a carbapenemase gene that was not detected by automated qPCR but was confirmed by whole-genome sequencing. A tailored qPCR assay was developed to detect IMP-18 and other alleles, improving the detection of carbapenem-resistant bacteria in Latin America.
full_output.methodology: Tailored qPCR and whole-genome sequencing were used to detect and characterize the IMP-18 gene in carbapenem-resistant isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Nanopore Sequencing-Driven Mapping of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes in Selected Escherichia coli Isolates from Pigs and Poultry Layers in Nigeria.

oqxB.evidence_note: oqxB was identified as an ARG associated with diaminopyrimidine resistance and Nitrofurantoin resistance in E. coli isolates.

mdtG.role_in_paper: identified as a gene associated with phosphonic acid resistance
mdtG.evidence_level: supported by detection in multiple isolates
mdtG.evidence_note: The mdtG gene was retrieved to predict resistance to phosphonic acid among three isolates by command line and one by EPI2ME application.

mdtM.evidence_note: The mdtM gene was identified as an ARG associated with resistance to Lincosamide in the study.

mdtE.evidence_note: The gene mdtE was identified in the context of Fluoroquinolone, Macrolide, Lincosamide, Rifamycin, Glycylcycline, Nucleoside, and Aminocoumarin resistance in E. coli isolates.

acrR.encodes: repressor of the multidrug efflux complex AcrAB-TolC

acrR.notes: mutation in the promoter region of acrR leads to increased resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 95 antimicrobial resistance genes in 10 E. coli isolates from pigs and poultry in Nigeria, including genes such as qnrS1, qnrS10, qnrS15, kdpE, cmlA1, MIR-14, sul3, dfrA12, blaEc15, blaACT58, and blaEc18, which confer resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Nanopore sequencing combined with command line and EPI2ME analyses were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics and Potential of KSL, KSL-W, and Dadapin-1 Antimicrobial Peptides for Preventing Infections of Orthopedic Prosthetic Devices: Identifying the Most Robust Candidate.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of KSL, KSL-W, and Dadapin-1 against various bacterial strains associated with orthopedic infections, highlighting KSL-W as the most effective peptide in terms of antibacterial potency and stability.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed through MIC, MBC, and MBIC determinations in both undiluted and diluted MHB II media, along with statistical analysis of the results.

full_output.paper_title: Development of an Antibacterial Poly(Lactic Acid)/Poly(ε-Caprolactone)/Tributyl Citrate Film Loaded with Staphylococcus aureus Bacteriophages Using a Sodium Alginate Coating.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the Staphylococcus aureus bacteriophage PBSA08, demonstrating its strong bacteriolytic efficacy against S. aureus and its potential as a biocontrol agent in food packaging applications.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluates the mechanical and barrier properties of PLA/PCL/TBC films, investigates the rheological properties of SA coatings, and assesses the antibacterial efficacy of phage-loaded films against S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Antimicrobial Activity of BrSPR20-P1 Peptide and Silver Nanoparticles Against Pathogenic Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the synergistic antimicrobial activity of BrSPR20-P1 peptide and silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) against pathogenic bacteria, revealing that their combination exhibited enhanced antibacterial efficacy, particularly against Gram-positive bacteria like S. aureus and MRSA, with reduced resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a checkerboard assay to determine the fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) and assessed the antibacterial activity of P1 and AgNPs through bacterial growth inhibition, time-killing studies, and morphological analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Ammonium Catecholaldehydes as Multifunctional Bioactive Agents: Evaluating Antimicrobial, Antioxidant, and Antiplatelet Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial, antioxidant, and antiplatelet activities of water-soluble quaternary ammonium acylhydrazones derived from catecholaldehyde. Compounds 9a, 10b, and 11a showed high antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Additionally, these compounds exhibited significant antioxidant and antiplatelet properties.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of acylhydrazones followed by evaluation of antimicrobial, antioxidant, and antiplatelet activities using MIC, MBC, CV assay, and platelet aggregation tests.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal Dissemination of Pandrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae ST392KL27 in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Mexico.
Impact of Dietary Inputs on Carbapenem Resistance Gene Dynamics and Microbial Safety During Bioconversion of Agri-Food Waste and Anaerobic Digestate by Hermetia illucens Larvae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of carbapenem resistance genes (bla VIM, bla OXA-48, bla GES, and bla KPC) in Hermetia illucens larvae and frass, primarily associated with legume-based diets. These genes were not detected in young larvae or in diets containing onion or digestate.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR (qPCR) was used to detect and quantify carbapenem resistance genes in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from different diets and samples of H. illucens larvae and frass.

full_output.paper_title: Quorum-Sensing C12-HSL Drives Antibiotic Resistance Plasmid Transfer via Membrane Remodeling, Oxidative Stress, and RpoS-RMF Crosstalk.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that C12-HSL enhances antibiotic resistance plasmid transfer in E. coli through membrane remodeling, oxidative stress, and RpoS-RMF crosstalk. Deletion of rpoS or rmf significantly reduces conjugation efficiency.
full_output.methodology: The study used E. coli MG1655 and its derivatives, along with conjugation assays, qPCR, and microscopy to investigate the role of C12-HSL and the genes rpoS and rmf in plasmid transfer.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of Ethanolic Extracts of Origanum majorana, Salvia officinalis, and Ribes nigrum Against Digestive Pathogens: Polyphenolic Composition and In Vitro Assessment.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of ethanolic extracts from Origanum majorana, Salvia officinalis, and Ribes nigrum against digestive bacterial pathogens. Ribes nigrum showed the strongest antimicrobial effect against Yersinia enterocolitica with a MIC of 0.002 μg/μL. Salvia officinalis was effective against Enterobacter cloacae, and Origanum majorana showed activity against Yersinia enterocolitica and Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.methodology: The study used HPLC-DAD-ESI-MS for polyphenolic profiling and agar well diffusion and broth microdilution methods for antimicrobial activity assessment.

full_output.paper_title: From Hermetia illucens Pupal Exuviae to Antimicrobial Composites: Metal Nanoparticles Synthesized by Laser Ablation in Sustainable Chitosan Matrices.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the antimicrobial efficacy of silver and copper nanoparticles synthesized in chitosan matrices, with silver composites showing a MIC of 0.006 g/L and copper composites showing a MIC of 0.003 g/L against Escherichia coli and Micrococcus flavus. A synergistic effect between the metal nanoparticles and chitosan was observed, particularly with chitosan derived from Hermetia illucens pupal exuviae.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was evaluated using agar diffusion and microdilution assays, with physico-chemical characterization performed via UV-vis spectroscopy, TEM, and FTIR.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting Bacterial Adenylate Kinase mRNA with a Chimeric Antisense Oligonucleotide for Rational Antibacterial Drug Development.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies adenylate kinase (ADK) mRNA as a viable target for antibacterial drug development using a chimeric antisense oligonucleotide (pVEC-ASO1). pVEC-ASO1 effectively inhibits the growth of Staphylococcus aureus by targeting ADK mRNA, demonstrating a bactericidal effect with a 50% minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC50) of 500 nM. The ASO shows low toxicity to mammalian cells, making it a promising candidate for antibacterial drug development.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bioinformatics, in vitro experiments, and molecular biology techniques to evaluate the effectiveness of pVEC-ASO1 in targeting ADK mRNA and inhibiting bacterial growth.

full_output.paper_title: When the Last Line Fails: Characterization of Colistin-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Reveals High Virulence and Limited Clonal Dissemination in Greek Hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high prevalence of virulence genes such as basD, pld, csuE, and bap in colistin-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates, highlighting their role in pathogenicity and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: High Prevalence of Virulence and bla(OXA) Genes Encoding Carbapenemases Among Acinetobacter baumannii Isolates from Hospitalised Patients in Three Regions of Poland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-40, blaOXA-23, and ISAba-blaOXA-51 genes as prevalent carbapenemase genes in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from Poland, contributing to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance and virulence genes, disc-diffusion method for antibiotic resistance, and biofilm formation assay.

full_output.paper_title: Exploration of Phosphoproteins in Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and Antimicrobial Resistance Analysis of an ST25 Streptococcus suis Strain Isolated from a Human in Zhejiang Province, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the tetracycline resistance gene tet(O) and the macrolide resistance gene erm(B) in an ST25 Streptococcus suis strain isolated from a human in Zhejiang Province, China.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the strain's resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Potential of Bee-Derived Products: Insights into Honey, Propolis and Bee Venom.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the antimicrobial potential of bee-derived products such as honey, propolis, and bee venom, highlighting their chemical compositions and mechanisms of action against various pathogens.
full_output.methodology: This paper reviews existing literature on the antimicrobial properties of bee products, focusing on their chemical compositions and biological activities.

full_output.paper_title: Case Report of Toxic Shock-like Syndrome Associated with Mixed Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus halichoeri and Dermatophilus spp. Infection in a Dog.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of genes for enterotoxin H (seh), protein A (spa), toxic shock syndrome toxin TSST-1 (tst), and methicillin resistance (mecC) in a Staphylococcus aureus isolate from a dog with toxic shock-like syndrome.
full_output.methodology: PCR and bacterial culture were used for gene detection and identification.

full_output.paper_title: In Vivo Emergence of Podovirus Resistance via tarS Mutation During Phage-Antibiotic Treatment of Experimental MSSA Endocarditis.

tarS.notes: Mutations in tarS were identified as the likely genetic basis for in vivo podovirus resistance.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, comparative genomics, RNA-seq, and phage susceptibility testing were used to analyze the resistance mechanism.
full_output.sample_size: 2 clones (16C02 and 16C12) were analyzed for mutations in tarS.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activity of Pediococcus pentosaceus strains against diarrheal pathogens isolated from pigs and effect on paracellular permeability of HT-29 cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the tetM gene in Pediococcus pentosaceus SMFM2016-YK1, which confers tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing was performed to identify genes related to antimicrobial activity and resistance.

full_output.methodology: The study uses molecular biology techniques including gene cloning, mutagenesis, protein purification, nuclease assays, and bioinformatics to characterize Vc OLD and Oad1.
