full_output.methodology: Molecular detection of the CTX-M gene using PCR with specific primers and analysis of antibiotic resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance of coagulase-negative Staphylococcus isolated from the external ear canal of healthy cats in Talca, Chile, South América preliminary results.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance in 55.5% of CoNS strains, primarily to oxacillin, with one strain showing multidrug resistance (MDR) to clindamycin, erythromycin, oxacillin, and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial cultures, MALDI-TOF identification, and Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion testing were used to assess antimicrobial susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: One health approach on zoonotic multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from Egyptian cattle, horses, and humans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM and TetA(A) genes in multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Egyptian cattle, horses, and humans, indicating resistance to amoxicillin-clavulanic, ceftriaxone, cefotaxime, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and sequencing were used to identify resistance genes in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Public health impact of multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica serovars identified via MALDI-TOF MS in cattle from Abakaliki abattoirs, Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica serovars, including Enteritidis and Typhimurium, in cattle from Abakaliki abattoirs, Nigeria. These isolates showed resistance to ampicillin, tetracycline, and erythromycin, but were susceptible to ciprofloxacin and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: The study used MALDI-TOF MS for identification and Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that Streptococcus agalactiae associated with bovine mastitis in China showed high resistance rates to sulfonamides, aminoglycosides, and β-lactams, with lower resistance to chloramphenicol and quinolones.
full_output.methodology: Meta-analysis of 33 studies published between 2004 and 2024, focusing on the prevalence and antimicrobial resistance of S. agalactiae in bovine mastitis cases.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the antimicrobial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic properties of five ethnomedicinal plants, with Rosemary showing the strongest antibacterial and antifungal activity. The findings highlight the potential of these plants as natural sources of bioactive compounds for therapeutic applications.
full_output.methodology: Phytochemical analysis, antimicrobial screening using agar well diffusion, antioxidant activity assessment via DPPH assay, and cytotoxicity testing on cancer cell lines.

full_output.paper_title: Poly(imidazolium ester) antibiotic forms intracellular polymer-nucleic acid biomolecular condensates and fight drug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a biodegradable poly(imidazolium ester) (PIE), P8, with broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria. full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and optimization of PIEs, evaluation of antimicrobial activity through MIC testing, investigation of membrane translocation and nucleic acid phase separation using microscopy techniques, and in vivo testing in murine infection models.

mutations_found.mutation_type: Mutations in the PBP2x protein can result in low-affinity PBP2x variants, reducing the efficacy of the β-lactam antibiotics and contributing to antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
mutations_found.origin: The mutations T338A/G/P within the conserved SXXK (STMK) motif, and K547G/T adjacent to the KXG (KSG) motif were introduced.

full_output.key_findings: This study identifies five clinically relevant mutations in the PBP2x protein of Streptococcus pneumoniae (T338A, T338G, T338P, K547G, K547T) that reduce susceptibility to beta-lactam antibiotics. Glucozaluzanin C is identified as a potential inhibitor that binds effectively to these mutant forms of PBP2x.
full_output.methodology: The study uses machine learning-based virtual screening, density functional theory analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify and validate natural inhibitors targeting mutant PBP2x in Streptococcus pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Weekly azithromycin for 48 weeks impacts nasopharyngeal microbial prevalence and Streptococcus pneumoniae serotypes in children with HIV-associated chronic lung disease.
full_output.key_findings: Azithromycin treatment reduced nasopharyngeal colonization of certain bacteria in children with HIV-associated chronic lung disease during treatment but had no long-lasting effects after treatment cessation.
full_output.methodology: Randomized controlled trial analyzing nasopharyngeal samples using nanofluidic qPCR for 94 S. pneumoniae serotypes, 12 bacterial species, and eight respiratory viruses.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, antimicrobial resistance, and public health risk assessment of zoonotic bacterial pathogens in raw cattle meat from three zonal cities in Tigray, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in zoonotic bacterial pathogens isolated from raw cattle meat, including resistance to Vancomycin, Erythromycin, and Amoxicillin in E. coli and Salmonella isolates.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolation, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and questionnaire surveys were conducted to assess resistance profiles and practices.

full_output.paper_title: Exploration of Human Skin Phageome to Reveal Endolysins and Novel Antimicrobial Peptides for Therapeutic Applications.
full_output.key_findings: This study identified 968 endolysins and 37 novel antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) from the human skin phageome, highlighting their potential as therapeutic agents against antibiotic-resistant pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of 1564 human skin microbiome samples, followed by identification and characterization of endolysins and AMPs using computational and experimental approaches.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-guided in silico design of a methionine aminopeptidase-derived multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies methionine aminopeptidase (MAP) as a conserved and immunogenic vaccine target for Neisseria gonorrhoeae, with epitopes showing high conservation across 48 clinical isolates and no homology to the human proteome.
full_output.methodology: Computational workflows including AlphaFold2 modeling, epitope prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to identify and validate MAP as a vaccine candidate.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, in vitro antimicrobial activity, and in silico studies of 1-aminoalkyl-2-naphthols.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis of two 1-aminoalkyl-2-naphthol derivatives, 1-(dimethylaminomethyl)naphthalen-2-ol (2) and 1-(piperidin-1-ylmethyl)naphthalen-2-ol (3), which exhibit potent antibacterial and antifungal activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens. Compound 3 showed strong activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa MDR1 with an MIC of 10 µg/mL and against Staphylococcus aureus MDR strains with an MIC of 100 µg/mL. Compound 2 displayed superior antifungal activity against Penicillium species compared to griseofulvin.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of compounds followed by antimicrobial testing using disk diffusion and broth dilution methods, alongside molecular docking studies to predict mechanisms of action.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents an electroless biocide amphiphilic coating of [Sn(tetra dentate ligand cephradine)Cl] that protects brass alloy in artificial seawater contaminated with bacteria. The coating exhibits enhanced antibacterial activity compared to native cephradine, effectively preventing biofilm formation and microbiologically induced corrosion.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized electroless plating techniques, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy to evaluate the effectiveness of the organotin coating in preventing microbial corrosion of brass alloys.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the Rtc system in E. coli as a key player in mediating heterogeneity in responses to ribosome-targeting antibiotics, revealing a potential form of heteroresistance. It highlights the role of RtcA and RtcB in repairing damaged RNA, thereby enabling cells to maintain translational capacity and survive antibiotic stress.
full_output.methodology: The study combines a computational model of Rtc-regulated RNA repair with experimental validations, including single-molecule RNA-FISH and Raman microspectroscopy to measure ribosome concentrations.

full_output.paper_title: Food Safety Threats: Molecular Surveillance, Antibiogram and Virulence Profiling of Biofilm Forming Enterococcus faecalis in Bangladeshi Restaurants.

blaTEM.validation_method: PCR detection of blaTEM gene in 81.48% of isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM as a prevalent gene encoding beta-lactamase in Enterococcus faecalis isolates from Bangladeshi restaurants, indicating resistance to penicillin.
full_output.methodology: PCR and disc diffusion test for antimicrobial susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Cefiderocol and Moxifloxacin Have Additive and Synergistic Activity Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa Including an Isolate of the 2023 Keratitis Outbreak.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that cefiderocol and moxifloxacin exhibited synergistic and additive activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa keratitis isolates, including an isolate from the 2023 keratitis outbreak. The combination was particularly effective against sheen-negative isolates, while sheen-positive isolates showed reduced responsiveness.
full_output.methodology: The study used time-kill and E-test assays to determine the minimum inhibitory concentrations and drug interactions of cefiderocol and moxifloxacin against P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Hyperforin potentiates polymyxin B against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens via membrane disruption, biofilm eradication, and oxidative stress.
full_output.key_findings: Hyperforin enhances the antibacterial activity of polymyxin B against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens by increasing membrane permeability, eradicating biofilms, and inducing oxidative stress.
full_output.methodology: In vitro assays including fractional inhibitory concentration index, time-kill kinetics, biofilm eradication, membrane integrity assays, and reactive oxygen species measurement.

full_output.paper_title: Shikonin-copper coordination nanoparticles for enhanced antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents shikonin-copper coordination nanoparticles (SCu NPs) as a novel antimicrobial agent with enhanced antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against Staphylococcus aureus. SCu NPs showed improved efficacy compared to shikonin (SK) alone, with lower minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC).
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of SCu NPs using shikonin as a chelator and stabilizer, followed by characterization using various analytical techniques and evaluation of antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Upregulation of metallophore-related genes of community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus enhances pathogenicity in BALB/c mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several metallophore-related genes, including sbnC, sbnI, cntA, hlgC, sspB, and pknB, which were upregulated during infection and associated with increased pathogenicity of community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) in BALB/c mice.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RNA-seq and RT-qPCR to analyze gene expression changes in CA-MRSA during infection in a mouse model.
full_output.sample_size: Six BALB/c mice in the infection group and six in the control group.

full_output.paper_title: Phytochemical Profiling of Ferula varia Extract and Its Antibiofilm Activity Against Streptococcus mutans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several phenolic compounds in Ferula varia extract, including chlorogenic acid, gallic acid, and isoquercitrin, which exhibited significant antibiofilm activity against Streptococcus mutans. The extract inhibited biofilm formation in a dose-dependent manner, with 100% inhibition at 5 mg/mL.
full_output.methodology: Chemical profiling using LC-UV-ESI-MS/MS, determination of total phenolic and flavonoid content, and evaluation of antibiofilm activity using a crystal violet assay.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Effects of Curcumin and Antibiotics Against Drug-Sensitive and Multidrug-Resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that curcumin exhibits intrinsic antimicrobial activity against both drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) and synergizes with first- and second-line antibiotics to enhance bacterial clearance. It also shows that curcumin improves immune responses and reduces neuroinflammation in TB-infected mice.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo models to assess the antimicrobial activity of curcumin against Mtb, its synergistic effects with antibiotics, and its impact on macrophage-mediated bacterial clearance and immune responses.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of 2,7-Naphthyridines as Targeted Anti-Staphylococcal Candidates with Microbiota-Sparing Properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates 2,7-naphthyridine derivatives as targeted anti-staphylococcal agents with microbiota-sparing properties, identifying compound 10j as having potent activity against Staphylococcus aureus with low cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, antimicrobial activity testing, molecular modeling, and cytotoxicity assessments were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Vesicle-Mediated Transfer of CTX-M β-Lactamase Genes and Proteins Confers Ampicillin Resistance in Escherichia coli.

blaCTX-M-15.validation_method: functional assays demonstrating beta-lactamase activity within OMVs and protection of susceptible E. coli from ampicillin-induced killing

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from CTX-M-15-producing E. coli carry both the CTX-M-15 beta-lactamase gene and active beta-lactamase enzymes, leading to ampicillin resistance in susceptible E. coli.
full_output.methodology: OMVs were isolated, characterized, and tested for beta-lactamase activity and their ability to confer ampicillin resistance in susceptible E. coli using disc diffusion and microtiter assays.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activity of Manuka Honey, Either Alone or in Combination With Topical Antibiotics, Against Bacteria Commonly Found in Equine Ulcerative Keratitis.
full_output.key_findings: Manuka honey exhibits in vitro antibacterial activity against bacteria causing equine ulcerative keratitis, including methicillin-resistant strains. It enhances the antibacterial effect of certain antibiotics like tetracycline, chloramphenicol, and fusidic acid, while slightly reducing the effect of ofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Microdilution assays, disk diffusion, and E-tests were used to evaluate the antibacterial activity of manuka honey and its combination with antibiotics.
full_output.sample_size: Eight bacterial strains from equine corneal ulcers and two reference strains

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of Phage Cocktails Against Biofilms Formed by Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibiotic resistance genes such as bla NDM-1, bla KPC, bla OXA-48, bla CTX-M-1, and bla TEM in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. It also detected biofilm formation genes including fimH, mrkA, matBecp in K. pneumoniae and algD, PslD, PelF in P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: PCR was used to detect antibiotic resistance and biofilm formation genes in the bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiology and epidemiology of enteroaggregative Escherichia coli isolated from UK residents in England, 2016-2023: what are the risks to public health?
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) isolates from the UK, highlighting significant resistance to fluoroquinolones, beta-lactams, macrolides, sulfonamides, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and in silico analysis of AMR genes were conducted on EAEC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Higher valency vaccines' impact on antimicrobial resistance rates in Streptococcus pneumoniae causing invasive disease: a retrospective analysis based on national reference laboratory data, Belgium, 2018 to 2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the association between antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and non-PCV13 serotypes in PCV15 and PCV20 in Belgium from 2018 to 2023. It found that PCV15-non-PCV13 and PCV20-non-PCV15 serotypes were more frequently associated with resistance to certain antibiotics, while others showed susceptibility. The implementation of PCV20 may lead to a larger decrease in overall IPD incidence and AMR rates compared to PCV15.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 8,123 IPD isolates from the Belgian National Reference Centre for invasive S. pneumoniae, including serotyping and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of VITEK REVEAL fast antimicrobial susceptibility testing to antibiotic disk diffusion for gram-negative bloodstream infections.
full_output.key_findings: The VITEK REVEAL system showed a categorical agreement of 94.8% with disk diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing of gram-negative organisms, with improvements to 97.0% after adjudication with broth microdilution. It significantly reduced the time to result for AST by at least 23 hours compared to standard-of-care disk diffusion.
full_output.methodology: The study compared the VITEK REVEAL AST system with disk diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing of gram-negative bloodstream infections, analyzing 150 monomicrobial blood cultures and 2,309 organism-antibiotic combinations.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic surveillance reveals global spread of macrolide-resistant Bordetella pertussis linked to vaccine changes.

23S rRNA A2047G.mechanism: mutation in 23S rRNA gene leading to macrolide resistance
23S rRNA A2047G.validation_method: molecular assays confirming the presence of the mutation in all resistant isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the 23S rRNA A2047G mutation as the primary cause of macrolide resistance in Bordetella pertussis, with a significant increase in resistance rates post-2020. The MT28-ptxP3-MRBP lineage became dominant, showing a transmission advantage in older age groups.
full_output.methodology: Genomic surveillance, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to evaluate the spread and resistance mechanisms of B. pertussis.

full_output.paper_title: Genome analysis of Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae strain APPFJLYC01 reveals multidrug resistance and high virulence potential.

tet34.mechanism: Ribosomal protection protein - confers resistance by protecting ribosomes from tetracycline binding

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 10 antibiotic resistance genes in the Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae strain APPFJLYC01, including genes conferring resistance to multiple antibiotic classes such as β-lactams, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides, and macrolides.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis were used to identify antibiotic resistance genes and virulence factors in the strain APPFJLYC01.

full_output.paper_title: Assembly and inhibition of transferable TMexCD1-TOprJ1 efflux pump.

tmexCD1-toprJ1.validation_method: expression in E. coli and MIC testing

TMexD1.notes: Mutations in TMexD1 affect tigecycline resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the transferable TMexCD1-TOprJ1 efflux pump, demonstrating its role in tigecycline resistance through structural and functional analyses.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-EM, bacterial genetics, and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: CarbaDetector: a machine learning model for detecting carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales from disk diffusion tests.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces CarbaDetector, a machine learning model that improves the detection of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) using disk diffusion test results. It achieves high sensitivity and specificity, reducing unnecessary confirmatory testing.
full_output.methodology: The model was developed using inhibition zone diameters from disk diffusion tests and validated on external datasets.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of antibiotic resistance, Staphylococci carriage and biochemical parameters of intensive care unit patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic-resistant Staphylococcus strains, including S. aureus, S. hominis, S. epidermidis, and S. haemolyticus, showing resistance to several antibiotics such as levofloxacin, erythromycin, tetracycline, oxacillin, clindamycin, and fusidic acid.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 100 ICU patients, including biochemical parameters and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of Staphylococcus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence and emerging cephalosporin resistance of penicillinase-producing Neisseria gonorrhoeae in Meizhou, China (2022-2024).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM−1 and bla TEM−135 as the main β-lactamase genes in penicillinase-producing Neisseria gonorrhoeae (PPNG) isolates in Meizhou, China. bla TEM−135 was associated with reduced susceptibility to cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, plasmid typing, and molecular analysis of bla TEM genes.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antibiotic resistance of Mycoplasma hominis and Ureaplasma urealyticum in Chongming District, Shanghai, China from 2020 to 2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates of Mycoplasma hominis (MH) and Ureaplasma urealyticum (UU) to certain antibiotics, with josamycin, methomycin, and strong bacteriocins showing high activity against both pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study analyzing prevalence and antibiotic resistance profiles of MH and UU through PCR testing and antibiotic resistance assays.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Peptide Glucosyltransferase Inhibitors With Comprehensive Coverage Across Clostridioides difficile Toxin B Sub-Types.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes several peptides (LSB5, SB2, SB5, SB6) that inhibit the glucosyltransferase activity of Clostridioides difficile toxin B (TcdB) by directly competing with the toxin's molecular targets, Rho proteins.
full_output.methodology: Solid-phase peptide library screening, computational evaluation, in silico optimization, and in vitro glucosyltransferase assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and virulence profiling of waterfowl-derived Salmonella in Sichuan from 2021 to 2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in waterfowl-derived Salmonella isolates, including aac(6')-Iaa, bla_OXA-1, bla_CTX-M-65, catB3, sul2, fosA3, lnu(F), dfrA17, and cfr. These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics, highlighting the multidrug resistance profile of the isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (MIC) were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Potential of Banana peel extract powder as a promising alternative to antibiotics for treating Salmonella Gallinarum infection in broiler chicks.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effect of banana peel extract powder (BPP) on Salmonella Gallinarum infection in broiler chicks, showing that BPP supplementation modulated immune-related gene expression (IL6 and MHC class IIβ), improved gut health, and reduced Salmonella Gallinarum counts.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR for gene expression analysis, histopathological examination, and in vitro antibacterial assays to evaluate the effects of BPP on Salmonella Gallinarum infection.

full_output.paper_title: Interfering Transposable Elements: ISXoo15 Transposase as a First-in-Class Antibacterial Target Against Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IS Xoo 15 transposase as a novel antibacterial target for J9, a pyrimidine-substituted pleuromutilin derivative, which shows potent anti-Xoo activity and targets the transposase to inhibit bacterial virulence and pathogenicity.
full_output.methodology: ABPP, RT-qPCR, mutagenesis, complementation, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to validate the interaction between J9 and IS Xoo 15 transposase.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid acquisition of daptomycin resistance in a Corynebacterium striatum osteoarticular infection: case report and discussion on antimicrobial resistance.

pgsA.notes: The G147D mutation introduces a premature stop codon in the active site of the PgsA enzyme, abolishing phosphatidylglycerophosphate synthase activity.
pgsA.evidence_note: The pgsA gene, which encodes phosphatidylglycerophosphate synthase involved in the synthesis of phospholipid acids in the bacterial membrane, harbored a G147D mutation.

mltG.notes: The T102A substitution affects peptidoglycan synthesis by acting as an elongation terminator.

ftsI.notes: The A370D substitution affects cell division and peptidoglycan synthesis.

full_output.key_findings: A case of chronic T11-T12 spondylodiscitis in a paraplegic patient led to the isolation of a daptomycin-resistant Corynebacterium striatum strain (CORY-2) after 14 days of daptomycin monotherapy. Whole-genome sequencing revealed a nonsense mutation in pgsA (G147D) likely responsible for daptomycin resistance, along with mutations in mltG (T102A) and ftsI (A370D) possibly contributing to increased beta-lactam MICs.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (MICs) using E-test strips and broth microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization of Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates from cancer patients: resistance profiles, virulence factors, and sequence typing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in K. pneumoniae isolates from cancer patients, including genes conferring resistance to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, tobramycin, levofloxacin, and carbapenems. Key resistance genes included sul1, sul2, dfrA1, dfrA12, dfrA14, dfrA27, aadA16, aadA2, aph(3')-Ia, aph(3'')-Ib, aph(6)-Id, aph(4)-Ia, ACC(3)-IId, ACC(3)-IIV, AAC(6')-Ib-cr, QnrS1, QnrB17, QnrB20, QnrB4, CTX-M, SHV, TEM, DHA-1, LAP-2, bla_kpc-1, bla_ndm-5, and bla_oxa-10.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing was used to analyze the resistance genes and virulence factors in 105 K. pneumoniae isolates from cancer patients.

full_output.paper_title: Network analysis of antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus aureus: characterization of hub genes and their functional implications.

mecA.mechanism: target replacement

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hub genes involved in antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus aureus, including mecA, fosB, arlR, mepA, mgrA, arlS, and msrA2, which are associated with mechanisms such as efflux pump regulation, target protection, and target replacement.
full_output.methodology: The study used network analysis and functional enrichment to identify and characterize hub genes involved in antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characterization of an invasive, hyper-aerotolerant Campylobacter jejuni strain causing bacteremia in a pediatric leukemia patient.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel invasive, hyper-aerotolerant Campylobacter jejuni strain, CNH-HAT-1, which exhibits resistance to penicillins and cephalosporins due to the presence of the beta-lactamase gene blaOXA-61 with a G250A mutation in the major outer-membrane protein PorA.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Is CepA from Klebsiella pneumoniae a biocide pump? Evidence suggests a metal efflux function.

cepA.validation_method: expression in E. coli and metal transport activity verification

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the function of CepA from Klebsiella pneumoniae, concluding it primarily acts as a heavy metal transporter rather than a biocide efflux pump.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MIC assays, ethidium accumulation assays, and ICP-MS to analyze the role of CepA in metal and biocide resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii at a hospital in Botswana: detecting a protracted outbreak using whole genome sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenemase genes bla OXA-23 and bla NDM-1 in all 19 ST1 isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii, along with biocide resistance gene qacE, highlighting the presence of extensively drug-resistant strains in a hospital outbreak in Botswana.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing was used to analyze clinical and environmental isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and track the outbreak.

full_output.paper_title: Engineered Mycoplasma pneumoniae targeting dual-species bacterial biofilms: a novel strategy against infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the engineering of a Mycoplasma pneumoniae strain, CV8_HAD, which secretes biofilm-disrupting enzymes (PelAh, PslGh, A1-II', and Dispersin B) to effectively degrade dual-species biofilms of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.methodology: The CV8_HAD strain was generated by introducing genes encoding biofilm-degrading enzymes into the genome of an attenuated M. pneumoniae strain using transposon mutagenesis. Expression and secretion of the enzymes were confirmed by western blot analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic insights into Bordetella pertussis evolution and macrolide resistance in Yiwu, China.

23S rRNA.validation_method: genomic analysis comparing resistant and sensitive isolates
23S rRNA.evidence_note: The A2037G substitution in the 23S rRNA gene was strongly associated with macrolide resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a high prevalence of macrolide resistance in B. pertussis isolates from Yiwu, China, with over 90% of isolates showing resistance. Key resistance mechanisms include a point mutation in the 23S rRNA gene and nonsynonymous mutations in the efflux pump genes oprM and opmD.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and comparative genomic analysis were used to identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug resistant hypervirulent ST307 clone from genomic surveillance of extended spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae species complex in East Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes, including blaCTX-M-15, blaTEM-1D, aac(6')-Ib-cr, aadA16, strB, qnrS1, sul2, sul1, catII.2, tet(A), dfrA14, arr-3, and mphA, in ESBL-KpSC isolates from East Africa, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize AMR genes and virulence factors in ESBL-KpSC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Hitchhiking genes and boundaries of AmpC amplicons during amoxicillin resistance development in E. coli.

ampC.validation_method: gene duplication and amplification observed in all evolved strains

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that ampC gene amplification in E. coli is not restricted to a fixed genomic hotspot and often involves hitchhiking genes. Loss of sugE or epmA significantly reduces the rate of amoxicillin resistance adaptation. IS1A frequently serves as an endpoint of ampC duplicons.
full_output.methodology: Experimental evolution with gene deletion mutants and whole-genome sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Selective antimicrobial photodynamic therapy of clinical isolates from patients with infected diabetic foot ulcers using a small cationic chlorin.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that aPDT with IC-H-Me2+ and KI effectively inactivates biofilms from clinical isolates of diabetic foot ulcers, achieving up to 15 log CFU/mL reduction in viability without harming human cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used aPDT with IC-H-Me2+ and KI, along with biofilm formation and dispersal assays, to evaluate the efficacy against clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prolonged exposure to teixobactin generates cross-tolerance to other cell wall-targeting antimicrobials in Enterococcus faecalis.

liaR.mechanism: regulator of cell envelope stress response

liaS.mechanism: part of the LiaFSR two-component system

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the cell envelope stress response, mevalonate pathway, Epa biosynthesis, and carbon metabolism genes that contribute to teixobactin tolerance in Enterococcus faecalis, with specific emphasis on liaF, epaM, mvaD, and hprK.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC and MBC assays, complementation experiments, and β-galactosidase reporter assays were used to validate the role of identified genes and mutations in teixobactin tolerance.
full_output.sample_size: Six TXB-tolerant mutants from three E. faecalis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and dynamic roles of tandem acyl carrier proteins in aryl polyene biosynthesis in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ApeE and ApeF as critical acyl carrier proteins in the biosynthesis of aryl polyenes in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, with ApeE acting as the primary starter ACP and ApeF facilitating malonyl-group transfer.
full_output.methodology: NMR spectroscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, in vitro enzymatic assays, and isothermal titration calorimetry.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of synonymous mutations in the bla(TEM-3) gene on gene expression and Escherichia coli fitness.
full_output.key_findings: Synonymous mutations in the blaTEM-3 gene increase ceftazidime resistance in Escherichia coli, likely due to epigenetic factors affecting gene stability.
full_output.methodology: Asymmetric competition assays, E-tests, sequencing, and cell-free transcription experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Silent spread of mcr-9 in ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae clinical isolates, Jimma, Ethiopia.

mcr-9.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the silent mcr-9 gene in ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae clinical isolates from Ethiopia, highlighting its presence on IncHI2 plasmids despite susceptibility to colistin.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted on the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative assessment of annotation tools reveals critical antimicrobial resistance knowledge gaps in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various AMR genes and mutations in Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting knowledge gaps in existing annotation tools and databases for accurate resistance prediction.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized machine learning models and comparative analysis of annotation tools to assess AMR gene detection and resistance prediction accuracy.

full_output.paper_title: Funnel-based antimicrobial resistance monitoring in Italy: the FUN-IT study.
full_output.key_findings: The study utilized funnel plots and other statistical process control methods to analyze antimicrobial resistance (AMR) trends in Italy, focusing on pathogens such as carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter spp. (CRAS), vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VRE-faecium), and others. It identified regional variations and systemic increases in AMR, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic.
full_output.methodology: Statistical Process Control (SPC) methods, including funnel plots, Z-score charts, and chi-squared control charts, were employed to monitor AMR trends in Italy from 2015 to 2023.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive study of community acquired Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children in Baoding, China, 2023.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified macrolide resistance mutations A2063G and A2064G in the 23S rRNA gene of Mycoplasma pneumoniae, which were prevalent in 93.2% of the cases.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based identification of M. pneumoniae and macrolide resistance mutations.

full_output.paper_title: New resistance threat in difficult-to-treat resistance Pseudomonas aeruginosa co-producing AFM and KPC carbapenemases: plasmid dynamic transfer and global phylogeography perspective.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla AFM-2 and bla KPC-2 as critical resistance genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, highlighting their role in carbapenem resistance and the potential for plasmid-mediated spread in hospital settings.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid conjugation experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence and regional evolution of Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC)-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST11 in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaKPC-2 as the predominant carbapenemase gene in KPC-KP ST11, often co-occurring with resistance genes for aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, and fosfomycin. It highlights the role of plasmids in the spread of these resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, cgMLST, and phylogenetic studies were used to characterize the resistance genes and evolutionary trajectories of KPC-KP ST11 in China.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology, antimicrobial resistance, and virulence determinants of Enterococcus faecium bloodstream isolates: a 7-year study in Shandong, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA as a key vancomycin resistance gene in E. faecium bloodstream isolates and highlighted the role of pilA and pilB in biofilm formation and environmental survival.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, biofilm formation assay, and MLST were used to analyze E. faecium isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Design and characterization of anti-microbial novel herbal nanofiber scaffolds for the management of periodontal diseases.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel herbal nanofiber scaffold named Ashvakatri, which effectively inhibited periodontal pathogens such as Aggregabacter actinomycetemcomitans, Porphyromonas Gingivilis, Fusobacterium spp., and Prevotella intermedia. The nanofiber demonstrated sustained drug release and antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized electrospinning to fabricate nanofibers, analyzed their physicochemical properties, and assessed antimicrobial efficacy through in vitro experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study develops a computational framework integrating genomic, microbiological, and patient mobility data to identify asymptomatic carriers of antimicrobial-resistant organisms, demonstrating that multimodal data improves the accuracy of detecting carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) carriers.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a stochastic agent-based model (ABM) combined with hospitalization records, electronic health records, clinical culture results, and whole-genome sequencing data to infer CRKP colonization probabilities and evaluate targeted isolation strategies.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence and Antibiotic Resistance Profiles of Proteus mirabilis Strains Isolated From Broiler Chickens: Implications for Poultry and Public Health.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM and blaDHA genes in P. mirabilis isolates from broiler chickens, which confer resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics. High resistance rates were observed against chloramphenicol and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, while all isolates were susceptible to meropenem and cefepime.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, PCR for virulence genes and beta-lactamase-encoding genes, and biofilm formation assessment.

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the resistance mechanisms of Acinetobacter baumannii, focusing on beta-lactamases (bla OXA-23-like, bla OXA24/40-like, bla OXA-51-like, and bla NDM-1), lipid A modifications (pmrCAB, lpxA, lpxC, lpxD, and mcr-1), fluoroquinolone resistance (gyrA, parC, and qnr), antifolate resistance (sulI, sulII, dfrA1, dfrA12, and dfrA14), fosfomycin resistance (fosA, abaF, and abpr), aminoglycoside resistance (aadB(ant2")Ia and aph(3')-Via), and efflux pumps (AdeABC, AdeIJK, AdeFGH, OqxAB, CraA, AmvA, AbaQ, AbeD, ArpAB, catA1, catA2, catB11, catB3, catB8, cmlA5, craA, abrp, tet(A), tet(X3), tet(X4), and tet(X6)).
full_output.methodology: The paper is an integrative review analyzing existing literature on resistance mechanisms and therapeutic strategies for multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution of DNA gyrase cleavage sites across the Streptococcus pneumoniae genome: relation to transcription and methylation at GATC sites.

parC.notes: The ParCS79F mutation was found in the resistant mutants and is associated with levofloxacin resistance.

gyrA.notes: The GyrA mutations S81F, S81Y, and E85K were found in the resistant mutants and are associated with levofloxacin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that methylation of GATC sites reduces gyrase cleavage and supercoiling activity, potentially increasing resistance to fluoroquinolones in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide mapping of gyrase cleavage sites using Topo-Seq, chromosomal fragmentation analysis via PFGE, and in vitro gyrase activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Preclinical evaluation of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum as a probiotic alternative against multidrug-resistant avian pathogenic Escherichia coli in chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the probiotic potential of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ATS1 against multidrug-resistant avian pathogenic E. coli (APEC) in chickens, demonstrating its ability to improve growth performance, enhance immune response, reduce tissue colonization, and lower mortality.
full_output.methodology: The study involved in vitro adhesion and survival assays, in vivo supplementation trials, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Current Trends in Antibiotic Resistance Patterns of Pathogens in Urinary Tract Infections in Children in Karaganda, Kazakhstan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates among uropathogens, particularly Escherichia coli, Enterococcus faecalis, and Staphylococcus epidermidis, to commonly used antibiotics such as amoxicillin and erythromycin. E. coli and E. faecalis showed sensitivity to amikacin, while E. faecalis and S. epidermidis were sensitive to ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing antibiotic resistance patterns in uropathogens using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of Pathogens of Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Hospitalized Patients: A Retrospective Study From 2010 to 2020.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates to ceftriaxone in Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli, and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) was resistant to penicillin but sensitive to vancomycin, linezolid, cotrimoxazole, and tigecycline.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of sputum cultures and drug susceptibility tests from AECOPD patients.

full_output.paper_title: Beyond antibiotic resistance: evidence for resistance-nodulation-cell division (RND) efflux pumps as virulence determinants.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the role of RND efflux pumps, particularly AcrAB-TolC, as virulence determinants in various Gram-negative pathogens, showing that their inactivation reduces virulence in animal and cell models.
full_output.methodology: Genetic inactivation and deletion studies, along with animal and cell culture models, were used to assess the role of RND efflux pumps in virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Global epidemiological insights on the antimicrobial resistance of Enterococcus faecium and a genomic analysis framework.

cfr.mechanism: confers resistance to linezolid, chloramphenicol, florfenicol, and pleuromutilins

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies vanA and vanB as the most prevalent vancomycin resistance genes, along with aac(6')-I, aph(3')-IIIa, and ant(6)-Ia for aminoglycoside resistance. It also detects optrA, poxtA, and cfr for linezolid resistance. Mutations in PBP5 (M485A) are associated with penicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of 21,058 Enterococcus faecium genomes using AMRFinderPlus and ABRicate for resistance gene identification.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Klebsiella oxytoca isolated from backyard broiler chickens and their contacts with antimicrobial resistance genes of Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Klebsiella oxytoca isolates from backyard broiler chickens and human contacts, including ermB, blaTEM, blaCTX-M1, sul1, tetA, gyrA, blaOXA-48, and mcr-1, indicating widespread multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and gel electrophoresis were used to detect antimicrobial resistance genes in Klebsiella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating eravacycline's efficacy against pediatric carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in China: a 6-year study.
full_output.key_findings: Eravacycline (ERV) showed significant in vitro activity against pediatric carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) isolates, with varying susceptibility based on carbapenemase types, sequence types, and age groups. bla KPC-2 showed the lowest susceptibility (64.3%), while bla NDM-1 showed the highest (97.4%).
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using MIC Test Strips and whole genome sequencing for resistance gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Persister Cells in Acinetobacter baumannii: Overview of Molecular Mechanisms and Removal Strategies.
full_output.key_findings: The review discusses various molecular mechanisms involved in the physiology of persister cells in Acinetobacter baumannii, including toxin/antitoxin systems, second messengers, SOS response, and membrane changes. It highlights the role of specific genes such as abkB, relB, hicA, zeta, and ppk in persister formation and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature and experimental studies on molecular mechanisms of persister cells in Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of Salmonella enterica serovars from poultry in Egypt: a comprehensive genetic analysis of ESBLs, MCR, integron and other resistance genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella enterica isolates from poultry in Egypt, including bla TEM, bla SHV, bla CTX-M, bla OXA-10, bla CMY-2, mcr-1, and intI 1. These genes were associated with resistance to various antibiotics, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Monitoring of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes and Susceptibility Profiles in Bacterial Isolates From Animal-Origin Meat.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes, including bla_KPC, bla_NDM, bla_OXA-48, bla_SPM, bla_VIM, bla_TEM, bla_SHV, bla_CTX-M, and mcr-1, in bacterial isolates from animal-origin meat samples. These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics, including carbapenems, beta-lactams, and polymyxins.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to detect resistance genes in bacterial isolates from meat samples.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance is widespread among intestinal and extra-intestinal Bacteroides fragilis strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that both intestinal and extra-intestinal B. fragilis strains possess comparable resistance gene profiles and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, suggesting that intestinal strains serve as a reservoir of clinically relevant resistance determinants.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, antimicrobial susceptibility testing via E-test, and microbial genome-wide association study (mGWAS) were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in B. fragilis.

full_output.paper_title: Associations of diet, race, and other environmental factors with antimicrobial resistance genes in the gut bacterial communities of pregnant women and 3-month-old infants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in the gut microbiomes of pregnant women and 3-month-old infants, highlighting the impact of factors such as mode of delivery and infant diet on ARG composition and diversity.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR to detect and quantify ARGs in stool samples from pregnant women and infants.

full_output.paper_title: Inactivation of cAMP receptor protein (MSMEG_6189) increases isoniazid susceptibility in Mycobacterium smegmatis via altered oxidative phosphorylation, elevated ROS production, and loss of ahpC expression.
full_output.key_findings: Inactivation of Crp1 in Mycobacterium smegmatis increases isoniazid susceptibility through upregulation of katG1 and loss of ahpC expression.
full_output.methodology: qRT-PCR, peroxidase activity staining, and zone inhibition assays.

full_output.paper_title: Precision therapy guided by genotypic antibiotic resistance for Helicobacter pylori eradication: A prospective, randomized controlled trial.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the 23S rRNA gene associated with clarithromycin resistance and in the gyrA gene associated with levofloxacin resistance in Helicobacter pylori, guiding precision therapy for eradication.
full_output.methodology: Genotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing using real-time PCR to detect resistance mutations in H. pylori.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical predictors of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pyogenic liver abscess and nomogram construction: A retrospective analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies risk factors for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial liver abscesses, including age ≥ 60, diabetes, malignancy, lower C-reactive protein levels, and prolonged prothrombin time. It constructs a nomogram for predicting the risk of such infections.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical and microbiological data from 268 patients with Gram-negative pyogenic liver abscesses.

Multiple resistance genes, including bla NDM-1, acrAB-tolC, and various beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, and sulfonamide resistance genes, were identified and validated.

full_output.paper_title: Metabolic control of porin permeability influences antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that porin permeability in E. coli is dynamically regulated by changes in periplasmic H+ and K+ concentrations, influencing antibiotic resistance. Key findings include the role of the Kch potassium channel in controlling porin permeability and the impact of metabolic states on antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized single-cell imaging, flow cytometry, molecular dynamics simulations, and genetic manipulations to investigate the regulation of porin permeability and its effect on antibiotic resistance.

These nanoparticles demonstrate significant antimicrobial activity against various bacterial isolates, including multidrug-resistant strains, through mechanisms such as disruption of bacterial cell wall synthesis and inhibition of key target proteins like Penicillin-Binding Proteins (PBPs) and KPC-2 carbapenemase.

full_output.paper_title: Histidinol dehydrogenase (HisD): a critical regulator of Staphylococcus aureus virulence and a promising target for antivirulence therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies histidinol dehydrogenase (HisD) as a critical regulator of Staphylococcus aureus virulence. Deletion of hisD reduces hemolytic activity, biofilm formation, and virulence gene expression, while its inhibition by pixantrone suppresses virulence without affecting bacterial growth.

full_output.paper_title: Bovine Mastitis-Derived Bacillus cereus in Inner Mongolia: Strain Characterization, Virulence Factor Identification, and Pathogenicity Validation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several virulence genes in Bacillus cereus isolates from bovine mastitis, including nheA, nheB, entFM, nheC, cytK, hblA, hblC, hblD, bceT, and ces. These genes were universally present or highly prevalent in the isolates, indicating their significance in the pathogenicity of B. cereus.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacological Intervention for Refractory Biofilm Infection After Hemipelvic Replacement Surgery: Multidisciplinary Management of a Case of Giant Cell Tumor of Bone.
full_output.key_findings: The case report details the successful management of a refractory biofilm infection following hemipelvic replacement surgery in a patient with a giant cell tumor of bone. The infection involved methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis, extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The treatment included targeted antibiotic therapy, surgical debridement, and optimization of vancomycin trough concentrations.
full_output.methodology: The methodology involved empirical and targeted antibiotic therapy, surgical debridement, and therapeutic drug monitoring.

full_output.paper_title: Flavomycin inhibits plasmid-mediated conjugative transfer of antibiotic resistance genes by disrupting energy metabolism and pilus assembly.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating the role of microplastics and wastewater in shaping Vibrio spp. and antibiotic resistance gene abundance in urban freshwaters.

full_output.paper_title: High colonization by multidrug-resistant and virulent Staphylococcus aureus genotypes among critically ill patients in the COVID-19 pandemic in a Brazilian hospital.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology, genetic dynamics, and transmission of the mcr-1 gene in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the mcr-1 gene, which confers resistance to colistin, and analyzes its genetic dynamics, transmission, and association with bla NDM gene in China.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, sequencing, and bioinformatics tools were used to study the mcr-1 gene and its genetic context.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotype-First Diagnostic Framework for Tracking Fluoroquinolone Resistance in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: This study developed a phenotype-first diagnostic framework for tracking fluoroquinolone (FQ) resistance in E. coli without the need for sequencing. The framework uses standard laboratory techniques to monitor MIC trajectories, collateral resistance, and biofilm formation, providing actionable insights for empirical treatment strategies and antimicrobial stewardship.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MALDI-TOF MS, CLSI-interpreted AST, growth-curve analysis, and crystal-violet biofilm assays to evaluate FQ resistance and collateral resistance in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic Characterization of Virulence Factors in Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase (ESBL)-Producing Escherichia coli Strains from Chickens in Hungary.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a variety of virulence genes associated with ExPEC pathotypes, including UPEC, APEC, and NMEC, in ESBL-producing E. coli strains from chickens in Hungary. These genes were linked to colonization, iron acquisition, and toxin production, highlighting the zoonotic potential of these strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify virulence genes and pathotype markers in 87 ESBL-producing E. coli isolates from chickens.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Phenotypes and Genotypes of Escherichia coli Isolates from Artisanal Minas Frescal Cheeses from the Federal District, Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates from artisanal Minas Frescal cheese, including sul1, sul2, tetA, tetB, blaCTX-M, blaTEM, blaSHV, and clmA, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug-resistant strains in dairy products.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was assessed using disk diffusion, and resistance genes were detected using PCR with specific primers.

full_output.paper_title: Viable, Multi-Drug-Resistant Bacteria Recovered from E-Liquids Used with Commercial Electronic Cigarettes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified viable, multidrug-resistant bacteria in e-liquids, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Bacillus spp., which showed resistance to penicillin, tetracyclines, and phenicols. The e-liquids also demonstrated antibacterial activity against certain bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: Culture-based methods, Sanger sequencing, and Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion assay were used to identify and assess the antimicrobial susceptibility of bacteria isolated from e-liquids.

full_output.paper_title: Characterisation of Plasmid-Associated Antimicrobial Resistance Genes in Coastal Marine Enterobacterales from the Central Adriatic Sea: De Novo Assembly and Bioinformatic Profiling.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified nine clinically relevant antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in plasmid-like assemblies from marine Enterobacterales, including blaKPC, blaTEM, aacA4, folP, and tetA, highlighting the potential for horizontal gene transfer in coastal environments.
full_output.methodology: The research employed Illumina-based whole genome sequencing, de novo assembly, and bioinformatics tools to identify and characterise antimicrobial resistance genes in plasmid-like sequences from marine Enterobacterales.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance: A concise update

full_output.methodology: Review of recent literature and case studies on antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: A Nine-Year Review of Acinetobacter baumannii Infections Frequency and Antimicrobial Resistance in a Single-Center Study in Salerno, Italy.

full_output.methodology: Bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed using the VITEK2 system and MALDI-TOF MS.
